author: visormatt
description:
Free/local TTS still reads as robotic; evaluate whether a paid, off-box provider is enough better than the pinned ship voice to justify the cost and the privacy tradeoff. Providers under test: ElevenLabs (https://join.elevenlabs.io/tts/text-to-speech) and Fish Audio (https://fish.audio/) — head-to-head against Piper, with macOS say staying in the tree as the rehearsal-only reference (so effectively 4 voices, 3 real contenders).

Context (applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/NARRATION.md):
- Ship voice is SETTLED for Season 1: Piper en_US-hfc_male-medium (DEFAULT_PIPER_VOICE in narrate/backends/piper.ts is frozen — repinning means re-rendering every published episode). This bake-off therefore targets a Season 2 / future-content decision, not a mid-season swap.
- ElevenLabs row in the backend table: paid, sends data off box, 'Not evaluated — needs an API key'. Fish Audio is not yet in the table — add a row (paid, off-box, OpenAudio models) when its backend lands.
- Off-box matters: narration text describes unreleased work, and 'nothing leaves your box' is a product claim. Backends record sendsDataOffBox per take so this stays checkable.
- Evaluation method precedent (Piper vs macOS say): render the same script through every backend, A/B on phone speakers (not headphones), and corroborate with measured loudness range (say: 0.2 LU flat; Piper: 2.1 LU).
- Pronunciation lexicon (narrate/lexicon.ts) must be re-checked per backend: entries are only removable after hearing the new backend read the written form.

Deliverable: a GO/NO-GO verdict per provider recorded in NARRATION.md (backend table + a decision note), plus working --backend elevenlabs and --backend fish-audio options either way so the comparison is reproducible.
title: Narration TTS bake-off: ElevenLabs and Fish Audio vs the pinned Piper voice

author: visormatt
description:
## Why this is a separate plan

`packages/react-router-shadcn` was deliberately excluded from the base audit ([OT 0f0528ff](../plans/0f0528ff-13dd-45c9-8f41-75547ecba3b3)) as vendored primitives. Owner's call: we *install and control* these files, so they deserve a standard too — but a **different** one, because they are structurally unlike an authored component.

## What makes shadcn different (measured 2026-07-30)
- **154** component files. **66** use `React.forwardRef`. **125** are **multi-export** (e.g. `Card` + `CardHeader` + `CardTitle` + `CardContent` + `CardFooter`).
- They type props via `React.ComponentProps<...>` / cva `VariantProps`, **not** a hand-written `FooProps` interface.
- Our copies have **already diverged from upstream**: PascalCase filenames (`Button.tsx`, `Card.tsx`) and compound components in `index` folders (`Accordion/`, `AlertDialog/`), vs the registry's kebab-case single files. A `components.json` exists but no longer matches our layout.

**Implication:** the base primitive shape (single `export const Foo` + single `export interface FooProps` + the six ordered markers) does **not** cleanly apply. Stamping the template on a compound cva primitive would be wrong. So step one is deciding what 'conform' *means* here.

## Central design question (the first task, human-gated)
Define a **primitive/compound variant** of the standard that fits cva + forwardRef + multi-export reality. Candidate dimensions to standardize instead of the 6-marker body:
- Consistent export style + ordering; consistent props typing (`ComponentProps`/`VariantProps` convention); `cn` import + variant (`cva`) placement; file/folder naming (single file vs `index` folder threshold); one-primitive-family-per-file.
- Whether the markers apply at all (maybe only to any genuinely-authored logic components living in the package), or a reduced marker set.

## Upstream re-sync tradeoff (decide explicitly)
Because our filenames/structure already diverge from the shadcn registry, `shadcn` CLI re-sync is **already** a manual merge. The plan must decide: do we keep pretending we can re-sync (and cap divergence), or declare these files fully owned and drop the registry contract? That decision sets how far 'conform' can go.

## Scope note / clarifying '+ vendored'
'Vendored' = code sourced from outside rather than hand-authored (shadcn is the main example). Generated/build output (`dist/**`, `__generated__/**`) and `__tests__/**` stay **permanently** excluded from every component audit — they're artifacts, not source. This plan pulls **only shadcn** back into scope, under its own variant ruleset.

## Strategy
Design the shadcn variant + re-sync policy (HUMAN GATE) → extend the ESLint rule + audit script with a 'primitive' profile → pilot on a few simple single-export primitives → bulldoze the compound/forwardRef families in batches → flip enforcement on for the package + document the ownership/re-sync policy. Reuses the enforcer infrastructure built in OT 0f0528ff.
summary: Follow-up to the primitive-shape audit (OT 0f0528ff): the shadcn package was scoped OUT as vendored, but we install and control it, so hold it to a standard too. First define what 'conform' means for multi-export / forwardRef / cva primitives (the base template doesn't map), then extend the enforcers with a primitive profile and roll it out.
title: Bring react-router-shadcn into the component-shape standard

author: visormatt
description:
## Where this starts

`packages/openthrottle-showroom/src/episodes/` holds 24 typed episodes. Four have a `flow.ts` — `01-what-is-openthrottle`, `03-first-plan`, `05-connect-ot-mcp`, `21-dashboard-tour`. The other **20 have beats and narration but nothing that can be recorded**: `src/runner/run.ts --flow <id>` resolves `../episodes/<id>/flow.ts` and exits when it is absent, and nothing in the test suite notices the gap — `video-validate` checks narration against the format spec, never whether the episode can be filmed.

The reason the other 20 were not written is now gone. Plan `050c43a1-8b00-485d-adce-86bda5bb7a19` (COMPLETED, PR #457 open on `openthrottle/loop-plan-showroom-snapshot`) replaced the hand-written fiction with a **windowed, sanitized snapshot of the real dev database** — 221 plans, 1,437 tasks, 1,195 output chunks, 126 conversations, 4,900 task tags, 2,549 work sessions, 366 skill-usage events, embeddings included — loaded idempotently alongside the stable `d0d0d0d0-` hero rows, with per-episode `dataRequirements` asserted at the end of the seed. Episodes 07, 09, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19 and 21 already carry requirements on that branch. The workspace on camera is now a used workspace, which is the thing the flows were waiting for.

**This plan depends on PR #457 landing** (or is worked on a branch stacked on it). Nothing here is authorable against `main`'s eight tables of fiction.

## What this plan is not

It is not permission to invent picture. `AGENTS.md` in the package is explicit: the beat's `action` field is the literal flow step, and porting a script is transcription, not interpretation — *if a flow needs a step the script does not describe, the script is wrong.* Every flow authored here transcribes beats that already exist. Where a beat cannot be transcribed because the app has no such control, the finding goes into `production.blockedOn`, not into a flow that pretends.

## The four shapes, because they are not one job

Grouped by what the camera points at, since the work per group is genuinely different:

- **Read-only app** (04, 07, 08, 13-second-half, 19) — navigate and dwell over snapshot rows. Cheapest, and the group to prove the loop with.
- **Mutating app** (06, 09, 10, 14) — types into forms and saves, like 03 already does. These dirty the demo database, so take 2 is not take 1 and there is currently no convention for that.
- **Shell / typeset surface** (02, 16, 22, 13-first-half, L2) — the subject is a terminal, so they run against `surfaces/shell.ts` the way 05 does, never a screen recording.
- **Agent replay** (11, 12, 15, 17, 18) — a live model call is non-deterministic in content and duration, so these record against pre-baked rows. 15 additionally needs a run that reads as `IN_PROGRESS` on camera, which the seed deliberately forbids.
- **Long form** (L1 ~11 min, L2 ~10 min) — composites, deliberately last.

## Known landmines, found while scoping

- **The snapshot has no notes and no tags table.** Exported tables are `plan_tags` / `task_tags` / `tag_action_rules` / `rule_applications` (5 rows) — no `notes`. Episode 10 is entirely notes, and 04's fourth beat opens one. Episode 09's payoff is the rule-applications list.
- **`projects.jsonl` is one row.** 04 beat 5 navigates to `/projects` and opens a seeded project; L1 adds a project.
- **Every imported run is coerced to `COMPLETED`** at load, on purpose — the stale-run sweep reconciles a heartbeat-less `IN_PROGRESS` run mid-take and flips the badge between takes. 15-kill-runaway-run needs the opposite.
- **07 is blocked in the app**, by its own `blockedOn`: `/search` redirects to `/dashboard` in a production build. 21 works around this with the header commander; 10's fifth beat and 13's third both go through search too.
- **16 is blocked in the app**: worktree state is CLI-only today.
- **20-generators assumes a generator UI.** `generators._index.tsx` and `generators.$generatorId.tsx` exist, so this is probably fine — but "the option form renders" and "run it; the created file paths list out" need confirming against a real build before a flow claims them.
- **18's fourth beat is the browser network panel.** That is devtools, not the app, and Playwright cannot put it in frame — it needs a typeset surface or a rewritten beat.

## Definition of done

Every registered episode either has a `flow.ts` that records end to end and passes `video-scan`, or has a non-empty `production.blockedOn` naming the app gap that stops it — and a test fails if an episode is in neither state.
summary: Author the missing 20 flow.ts modules against the sanitized snapshot workspace, after an honest per-episode recordability audit, with mechanical gates so a flowless or drifted episode fails a test rather than a take.
title: Showroom: a recordable flow for every Season 1 episode

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Every so often a chat turn "hangs": the backend stalls, no further deltas arrive, and no terminal `done` chunk is ever published. The server's `runStream()` `for await` loop blocks indefinitely, so the turn never persists and never emits a terminal chunk; the client stays `isStreaming: true` forever (`pendingAssistantId` never clears) and the composer is stuck. Today the only exit is the manual Stop button, and there is **no retry** anywhere in the chat UI. These hangs are the kind we could simply have interrupted and recovered from with a retry.

## Locked decisions
- **Timeout posture: idle-only.** Fire only when no chunk has arrived for N seconds — safe for legitimately long CLI agent runs that keep emitting output; catches true stalls. No aggressive wall-clock cap on the orchestrator (CLI backends keep their own wall-clock as a last resort).
- **Recovery: auto-retry once, then manual.** On a retryable timeout, silently re-run the turn once; if it stalls again, surface the error + a manual Retry button.

## Current architecture (verified)

Streaming spine: `submitTurn()` → `intent=start` POST to `/resources/conversation-stream` → `startConversationStream` mutation → `ConversationStreamService.start()` → fire-and-forget `runStream()` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts:211`) → `for await (const chunk of backend.stream(backendRun))` → `publishChunk()` → in-process PubSub topic `conversation:<id>:stream` → `conversationStreamChunkAdded` subscription → `useConversationStream` hook (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useConversationStream.tsx`) → `reduceStreamChunk` (`packages/react-router-chat/src/conversation-stream.ts`) → `useAgenticChatTurn` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useAgenticChatTurn.tsx`). Chunk shape `{ id, conversationId, messageId, delta, done, error, kind, metadataJson, sortOrder }`.

Existing timeout/abort inventory:
- Per-conversation `AbortController` + `cancel()` **exist** in the service (line 115/177), driven today only by the user's Stop button — no timer.
- **CLI backends already self-terminate**: claude/codex/grok/cursor-agent/opencode wrap their subprocess in idle + wall-clock timeouts via `resolveAgentTimeouts()` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/cursor-agent/teardown.ts`; `idleMs` default 120_000 env `OPENTHROTTLE_AGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `wallClockMs` 900_000, `graceMs` 5_000) + SIGTERM→SIGKILL teardown.
- **Gap 1 — HTTP/OpenAI backend is unbounded**: `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/openai.ts` → `chat-completions/stream.ts` only forwards `options.signal`; a mid-stream silent endpoint hangs the iterator.
- **Gap 2 — no orchestrator backstop**: `runStream()` trusts each backend to terminate; any wedged backend hangs the turn with no terminal chunk.
- **Gap 3 — no retry**: grep for `watchdog|stall|retry|setInterval` across the chat hooks + `react-router-chat/src` returns nothing. `StreamState` carries no last-activity timestamp for a client watchdog.

Surfaces sharing the path: the global header chat wraps `useAgenticChatTurn` via `useHeaderChatController`; the admin app has its own copy under `applications/openthrottle-admin/app/routes/resources.conversation-stream.tsx`. A separate, lower-priority legacy single-shot path (`packages/react-router-chat/src/hooks/useChatTurnFetcher.tsx`, `intent=send-agent-message`) also has no timeout. Reference pattern for timeout+abort+kill already implemented for the (unrelated) Ralph driver path in `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/engine/index.ts` (`runDriverAsync`).

## Approach

1. **Server orchestrator idle-timeout backstop** in `runStream()` — the single choke point covering ALL backends including the unbounded HTTP one. Race the backend iterator against an idle timer (reset on each chunk); on expiry call the existing `controller.abort()` AND break the loop so a backend that ignores its signal still terminates. Persist whatever streamed, then publish a terminal `done` chunk carrying a clear timeout message + a machine-readable retryable marker.
2. **HTTP/OpenAI backend idle timeout** to match the CLI backends' `resetIdle()` behavior, using the shared `resolveAgentTimeouts()`.
3. **Retryable terminal-chunk contract** propagated through the shared reducer/types so the client can distinguish "timed out — retry" from a fatal error.
4. **Client auto-retry-once + watchdog** in `useAgenticChatTurn`: remember the last `(message, fields)`, track last activity, auto-resubmit once on a retryable terminal chunk (or a client-side stall if the subscription dies), guarded against loops; expose a manual Retry after.
5. **Manual Retry UI affordance** + **header/admin parity** + **tests** + **config/docs/validation**.

Reuse the existing `resolveAgentTimeouts()` env knobs (or add a chat-scoped alias) for consistency; keep defaults conservative so healthy long CLI runs are unaffected.
summary: Add a high-level idle timeout to the streaming chat turn so a hung backend always terminates and publishes a terminal error chunk, then auto-retry the turn once (manual Retry after) so users recover from stalls without a stuck composer.
title: Chat turn idle-timeout backstop + auto-retry recovery for hangers

author: visormatt
description:
# Onboarding flow + dashboard "Get Started" checklist

## Why
New users landing in `openthrottle-developer` see a data-dense dashboard (queue health, PR stats, contributions heatmap) but no guided path to their first success. We're smoothing out the basics; this plan turns that into a real, wonderful first-run experience. The centerpiece is a **dismissable "Get Started" checklist** shown on the dashboard route that nudges users toward the handful of actions that make the product click.

## Scope
Target app: `applications/openthrottle-developer`, dashboard route (`app/routing/dashboard`). Reuse existing conventions rather than inventing new ones.

### Anchor deliverable — dashboard Get Started checklist
- A card/panel on `/dashboard` listing the key first-run steps as a checklist with per-step completion state and clear CTAs (deep links) into each destination.
- **Dismissable**, and stays dismissed (persisted). Also auto-hides once all steps are complete. A way to bring it back (e.g. from settings/help) is a nice-to-have.
- Completion is **derived from real state** where possible (e.g. GitHub token present, ≥1 workspace repo, ≥1 plan, ≥1 CLI configured), not just "I clicked the button".

### Candidate checklist steps (finalize in design task)
1. Connect your GitHub token (already has `DashboardGithubTokenEmptyState` signal).
2. Add a workspace repository (workspace onboarding: add-folder / clone-repo).
3. Configure an agent CLI (driver discovery).
4. Create your first plan (and/or task).
5. Run your first task / kick off a plan run.

## Conventions to follow (do not reinvent)
- Component shape: one component per file, generator scaffold section comments (`Hooks/Setup/Handlers/Markup/Life Cycle/🔌 Short Circuit`), `data/data.copy.ts` for copy, `data.ts` for lists. Scaffold via `@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component`.
- UI from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; headings via `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global` (`GlobalHeading`), matching `DashboardIntroduction`.
- Dismiss/persistence: use the established `atomWithStorage` (versioned) Jotai pattern (see `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/data/atom.chat-toolbar.ts` and `app/global/data/atom.config.ts`) rather than raw `localStorage`.
- Route stays a thin adapter; grid/checklist live in `app/routing/dashboard/components` (route-primitive-shape R4, per `DashboardContentGrid`).
- Tests: Vitest + `component` (not `screen`), `userEvent`; render-level assertions.

## Design decisions to lock before build
- **Persistence scope of "dismissed":** client-only (localStorage atom, per-browser) vs server-side per-user preference. Start client-only unless we want cross-device; note the tradeoff.
- **Where completion state comes from:** which loader data already exposes these signals vs new resolvers needed.
- Empty/loading/error states and how the checklist coexists with the existing `DashboardIntroduction` + content grid.

## Out of scope (for now)
- Multi-step modal wizard / product tour overlays.
- Server-persisted onboarding progress model (revisit if client-only proves insufficient).
- Onboarding for other apps (admin/email/website).

## Validation
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint typecheck test` green; render-level tests for the checklist (visible steps, completion, dismiss hides + stays hidden).
- Live-verify on the dashboard route with a permissioned user (fresh users have zero perms → render-level Vitest).
summary: Build a first-run onboarding experience for openthrottle-developer, anchored by a dismissable "Get Started" checklist on the dashboard route that drives new users to their first meaningful actions (connect GitHub, add a workspace repo, create a plan, run a task, configure a CLI).
title: Developer app onboarding flow + dashboard "Get Started" checklist

author: visormatt
description:
# Goal

Get the user *onto* `/plans/:planId` as fast as the plan row can be read, and let the expensive per-tab data stream in behind skeletons. Today the route's single `PlanDetailIndexLoader` awaits everything before React Router renders anything, so time-to-first-paint equals the slowest field in the query.

The route file itself is fine as-is (it is a thin loader + Provider + action switch, ~180 lines). This plan does not restructure it for size — it changes **when** its data arrives.

# Current shape (verified 2026-08-26)

`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx:64` awaits `Promise.all([PlanDetailIndexLoader, loadEnabledEditors])` and returns 10 fully-resolved keys. `PlanDetailIndexLoader` (`app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx.graphql`) selects, in one round trip:

| field | consumer | cost signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan(id)` (`PlanDetails`) | header, toolbar, run-config seed, meta title | one row + tags/hooks — cheap, **critical** |
| `tasksByPlanId` (`PlanTaskRow`) | Tasks tab, tab counter `(x/y)`, Details requirements | one indexed query — **critical** |
| `workspaceRepositories` (`PlanRunConfigRepositoryFields` incl. `checkouts.inspection.git.currentBranch`) | Configuration tab + branch seeding | resolver doc: *"snapshots refresh on view past the 15-minute TTL"* → `git` subprocesses per checkout (`repository-inspection.service.ts` `execFileAsync('git', …)`). Prime suspect for the worst case. |
| `planOutputStreamChunks(input: { planId })` | Output tab | **no `limit` passed** — server defaults/caps it (`plan-output-stream.resolver.ts:75`), but the client should ask for a bounded tail |
| `planRunsByPlanId(limit: 10)` + `metrics.recentPlanRunsMetrics(limit: 25)` | Details tab run transparency, toolbar stale badge | join-heavy; metrics walks `taskRunMetrics` |
| `ruleApplications`, `workArtifactsByPlan` | Output tab — **currently commented out in `PlanTabOutput.tsx`** | dead weight in the critical path right now |
| `skillTagVocabulary { tags }` | toolbar tag-add popover only | whole vocabulary |
| `workspaceSettings.profile.enabledEditors` (separate doc, own catch) | toolbar deep links | already isolated, still awaited |

Secondary problem: because it is one query, **any** of those failing takes the whole plan page down. Per-region boundaries fix that too.

# Target shape

`loader` returns:

- **awaited**: `plan`, `tasks` (plus the existing `planId`-missing short circuit).
- **naked promises** (RR8 Single Fetch streams them; precedent: `app/routes/dashboard._index.tsx:52-84` and `DashboardDeferredCard.tsx`): `enabledEditors`, `ledger` (`ruleApplications` + `workArtifactsByPlan`), `outputChunks`, `runHistory` (`planRunsByPlanId` + `recentPlanRunsMetrics`), `tagVocabulary`, `workspaceRepositories`.

Each promise gets its own `Suspense` + `Await` + `errorElement` region with a skeleton shaped like the real content.

# The three hard parts (do not hand-wave these)

1. **`PlanRunConfigStoreProvider` currently needs `repositories` at mount** (`PlanRunConfigStoreProvider.tsx:52` seeds `workflowBranchAtom` via `resolveDefaultRunBranch({ repositories })`). Deferring repositories means seeding without them, then back-filling once resolved — **only if the user has not edited the branch** — and making Run/Queue read as "resolving workspace…" (disabled) rather than validation-failed while pending. Enqueue must never fire with an empty branch.
2. **`usePlanOutputStream(planId, snapshot)`** takes the loader snapshot synchronously and merges live `planOutputChunkAdded` deltas. With a deferred snapshot, deltas can arrive *before* the snapshot — merge must dedupe by chunk `id` and order by `iteration`/`createdAt`.
3. **`usePlanLifecycleRevalidation`** revalidates on every plan/task notification. Fresh promises on each revalidation would re-suspend every region → skeleton flash on a running plan. Deferred regions must retain their last resolved value while the next promise is pending.

# Non-goals

- No server/schema changes. `limit`/`offset` already exist on `ListPlanOutputStreamChunksInput`; inspection-snapshot caching stays as-is (a separate concern — see `agentic-utils-cache-hardening` if it proves to be the real cost).
- No visual redesign of the tabs, no splitting of the route file for line count.
- Do not re-enable the commented-out rule-applications / linked-artifacts blocks in `PlanTabOutput.tsx`; just stop paying for their data on the critical path.

# Validation

Per `developer-app-validation-gates`: `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build` on `openthrottle-developer`. Live verification against the built isolated server on `:6021` with the seeded `developer-e1e878@atlasworks.example` user (has admin perms).
summary: Split applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx's one-shot loader into a small critical query (plan + tasks) plus per-region deferred promises streamed through Await/Suspense boundaries, so navigating to a plan paints the header, toolbar and tabs immediately and only the genuinely slow regions (workspace repositories with git inspection, run history/metrics, output chunks, rule/artifact ledger, tag vocabulary) show a skeleton. Includes flash-suppression across lifecycle revalidation and route prefetch on intent.
title: Fast plan-detail route: stream the heavy tabs, paint the shell first

author: visormatt
description:
# Repositories route: nested table + toolbar + pagination

## Problem

`/settings/repositories` renders `RepositoriesSection` → a `<ul>` of `RepositoryCard`, one card per repository, each card containing an inner `<ul>` of checkouts with three inline `<Form>` action buttons apiece. This reads fine at 2–3 workspaces and degrades badly past ~10: no search, no sort, no pagination, and every checkout's full action set is always expanded on screen.

Every other list route in openthrottle-developer already converged on the same shape — `XxxToolbar` + `XxxTable` (shadcn `DataTable`) + `OpenThrottlePagination`, all state in search params, loader does filter/sort/slice. See `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects._index.tsx` as the canonical exemplar. Repositories is the outlier.

## Goal

Bring `/settings/repositories` in line with that pattern, while representing the repository → primary checkout → worktree hierarchy that a flat table would flatten away.

## Decisions (settled with the owner)

1. **Row grain: one row per checkout, nested.** Not one row per repository. But the rows are not flat — a repository's `kind: 'primary'` checkout is the parent row and its `kind: 'worktree'` checkouts nest beneath it as indented, expandable child rows. This is real data, not a derived guess: `RepositoryCheckoutObject.kind` is `'primary' | 'worktree'` and `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/repositories/repository-checkouts.service.ts` genuinely writes `'worktree'` via `recordWorktreeCheckout` (`kind: data.kind ?? 'primary'` on the ordinary create path).
2. **Table only — retire the cards.** No `view=table|card` toggle. `RepositoryCard.tsx` and its test are deleted. The rich per-repository view already exists at the detail route `settings.repositories.$repositoryId._index.tsx`.

## Shape of the change

**Pagination unit is the parent row.** Paginate over primary checkouts (parent rows); a parent always carries its worktree children with it so a group is never split across a page boundary. `totalCount` = number of parent rows after filtering.

**Search** matches across repository name, checkout `displayName`, `filesystemPath`, `normalizedRemoteUrl`, and current branch. A child match pulls its parent in (and auto-expands that group), so searching a worktree branch name never yields an orphan row.

**Sort** at minimum: repository name, last updated, checkout count. Children sort within their parent group, never globally.

**Row actions** (refresh checkout, apply editor config, remove) move from three always-visible buttons into a single per-row actions menu. They stay `<Form method="post">` submissions against the existing `action` intents — no behavior change, no new mutations, no GraphQL/schema changes, no codegen. `settings.repositories._index.tsx.graphql` is untouched.

**`DataTable` needs sub-row support.** `packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/DataTable.tsx` currently wires only `getCoreRowModel`. Nesting requires optional `getSubRows` + `getExpandedRowModel` + expansion state. This must be strictly additive — every existing caller (`ProjectsTable`, `PlansTable`, `SkillsTable`, `RulesTable`, `NotesTable`, `QueuesTable`, `PersonasTable`, `PullRequestsTable`, `ScheduleTable`, and the settings tables) passes neither prop and must render byte-identically.

## Non-goals

- No server-side pagination. Loader-side filter/sort/slice over `workspaceRepositories`, same as Projects does today.
- No changes to the repository detail or edit routes.
- No changes to `AddFolderDialog`, `CloneRepoDialog`, `AddFolderResult`, `DirectoryPicker`, or the picker/browse flow — those keep working exactly as they do now, above the table.
- No GraphQL schema, resolver, or migration work.

## Conventions

- Scaffold components with the generator, do not hand-write: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=settings/repositories --name=RepositoriesTable,RepositoriesToolbar,RepositoryRowActions`.
- Keep the generated `// Hooks / Setup / Handlers / Markup / Life Cycle / 🔌 Short Circuit` section comments even when empty.
- Components export only the component + its props interface; lists/copy live in the nearest `data/` (`data.copy.ts`).
- No new TS enums — `as const` objects. No `as` casts. Alphabetized props/keys. `component` not `screen` in tests, `userEvent` not `fireEvent`.

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`, plus `pnpm nx run react-router-shadcn:test` for the `DataTable` change. Then `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:dev` and exercise the route by hand: expand/collapse, search hitting a worktree, sort, page 2, and each of the three row actions.
summary: Replace the card list on /settings/repositories with a RepositoriesTable (nested primary checkout → worktree rows), RepositoriesToolbar (search + sort), and OpenThrottlePagination, matching the Projects/Skills/Rules route pattern. Retire RepositoryCard.
title: Repositories route: nested table + toolbar + pagination

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

`packages/openthrottle-showroom/src/fixtures/demo-content.ts` seeds 8 tables of hand-written fiction; the developer app reads ~30. Measured against the dev database on 2026-08-27, the gap is an order of magnitude on every surface (tasks 5194 vs 16, work ledger 4558/4087/4216 vs 0, conversations 376/121 vs 0, tags 5697+928 vs 0, …) and most episode surfaces render empty states. Episodes 07, 09, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19 and 21 cannot be recorded honestly against the current seed.

An earlier revision of this plan proposed a deterministic PRNG-generated background calibrated to the measured distributions. **That approach is dead.** Generated fiction has to imitate a real workspace; we already have a real workspace. This repo is open source and the workspace is expected to eventually be exposed publicly as a read-only "watch us build it" instance, so the content itself is not the secret — credentials, personal data and machine details are.

## Approach: export → sanitize → commit → load → verify

1. **Export** the last `n` days (default 30; ~208 plans, ~1,400 tasks measured 2026-08-27) of the real dev database by walking the FK graph (restored in migration 099) from time-windowed root tables (`plans`, `agent_conversations`, `scheduled_agent_job_runs`, `daily_stats`, `skill_usage_events`). Parents of windowed rows always come along (users, projects, repositories, tags); children come along within the window. Embedding vectors export with their rows — episode 07 works for free because the embedded text is unchanged. Output is JSONL per table in FK-topological order.
2. **Sanitize best-effort, fail loud where it counts.** A committed column manifest classifies every exported `(table, column)` as `keep | scrub | drop`; an unclassified column (i.e. any new migration) fails the export naming the table and column — schema drift breaks the export, not the take. Deny-listed tables (`mcp_connector_connections`, anything credential-adjacent) never export. A secret detector (known key shapes + high-entropy strings) stops the export on a hit rather than silently redacting. Identity scrub (emails, home paths, machine names) applies inside free text. Free text is otherwise **kept** — accepted residual risk: recordings are reviewed carefully before publishing, nothing goes live automatically.
3. **Commit** the sanitized snapshot to the package. Refreshing it is a PR, so leak review is code review, and the existing `scan/rules.ts` leak rules run over the snapshot itself in CI.
4. **Load** the snapshot idempotently into the demo database alongside the existing hand-authored hero rows (which keep their `d0d0d0d0-` ids and byte-identical content — existing flows deep-link them). Imported rows keep their real ids: a re-export is stable, and a deep link shown on camera can later match the public instance. Timestamps are rebased to the existing minute-offset-from-seed-time convention so the snapshot stays visually fresh.
5. **Verify like an E2E suite.** Each episode declares `dataRequirements` asserted against the freshly seeded database; a missing row names the video it breaks. The videos become a byproduct of a passing run.

## Out of scope (deliberately)

Hosted deployment of the platform and the public read-only guest instance are separate future plans. This plan must not block on them, but the column manifest and deny list built here are their first draft.

## Non-negotiables carried forward from PIPELINE.md

Demo database name contains `demo`; seed idempotent under re-run and `--reset`; every seeded run stays `COMPLETED` (stale-sweep reconciles `IN_PROGRESS` runs and changes badges between takes); output chunk timestamps strictly increasing and unique per plan.
summary: Replace hand-written demo fiction with a time-windowed, sanitized snapshot of the real dev database, loaded deterministically for recordings and asserted per episode like an E2E suite.
title: Showroom demo fixture: sanitized snapshot of the real workspace

author: visormatt
description:
# Roadmap proposals — 2026-08

First run of this monthly job (no prior `🔁 Roadmap proposals:` plan exists in any status).

## Where the last 30 days actually went

189 non-merge commits, ~100 PRs, 97 of the last 100 PRs merged. Directory churn (git diff --dirstat, 30-day window): ~25% in `packages/` (react-router-shadcn, react-router-chat, agentic-utils, nestjs-repositories), ~15% in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/` (settings, plans, skills), ~6% in `openthrottle-server/src/graphql`, plus a heavy `docs/` + infra tail. Themes, by commit volume:

1. **Public-launch & onboarding push** — leak audit (#290), Apache-2.0 open-core relicense (#238/#253), Docker one-command bootstrap (#296), Postgres volume reset (#292), landing-page rebuilds (#364/#369/#374), onboarding UI everywhere (#354, #362, #366, #372).
2. **Skills platform** — usage tracking end-to-end (#277), agentic-hooks (#312), foreign-workspace injection (#349), DB-backed tags (#352), detail routes/pagination (#358).
3. **Agent-CLI/chat stack** — drivers registry (#220/#248), per-model enablement + favorites (#340), streaming backends (#251), chat-wiring consolidation (#335).
4. **Convention enforcement** — component/route primitive-shape gates (#263/#278/#319), pre-Hooks props unpack (#353), GraphQL field alphabetization (#318), warn-mode test-coverage guard (#325) and four unit-spec backfill PRs (#327/#328/#331/#333).
5. **Scheduled agent jobs** — generic cron jobs (#266), run metadata (#281), run detail/edit (#270), ten recurring Job_* audit prompts (#377) — of which this job is one.

## Comparison with the living roadmap

The living roadmap is plan `ce7e2773-3c71-4e8f-8229-11355d021723` (cited, not modified). Month's effort maps cleanly onto its themes — mostly **Self-Host & Operate** (launch prep, onboarding, bootstrap) and **Open Interfaces / The Substrate** (developer-app UI, conventions). Notable: the roadmap's Now/Next/Later sections are empty (last updated 2026-06-19), so an effort-vs-stated-priorities gap analysis is only possible at the theme level right now; keeping those sections current would make future runs of this job sharper.

## Method notes and limitations

- `semantic_search` returned zero chunks for every query this run — the vector index appears unpopulated or query embedding is unavailable. Dedupe was done instead against the full PENDING/IN_PROGRESS plan list, the 🌟 Features and Bug Tracker backlog tasks, and session memory of ~80 historical plans.
- The perception of a "large backlog of DONE-but-unmerged plans" is mostly stale: only 3 PRs are open (#317 dependabot, #313 typed skill args, #307 nx-sync gate). The real residue of the pipeline is post-merge bookkeeping (ledger artifacts, plan statuses) — which proposal 1 addresses.

## Considered and rejected

- **Kill or park `vscode-openthrottle`** — it received almost no investment this month (12 file-touches out of ~thousands) while carrying an open audit-remediation plan (808a8b6d), but the roadmap explicitly names the VS Code extension under Open Interfaces, and one quiet month against a stated strategic surface is not enough evidence to propose deletion. Revisit next run if it stays idle.
- **Chat-surface consolidation** — real duplication signal (#335 plus repeated wiring fixes), but an open plan already owns it (chat-surface consolidation, d246beb9 per prior planning); duplicate, dropped.
- **Nx GCS cache migration** — already filed as 🚀 Pre-launch plan aec1b0b2; duplicate, dropped.
- **Generalize registry-driven settings sections** — the Appearance regroup (#379) introduced the pattern and an in-flight plan (2498ad1d, /settings/workspace) is actively extending the settings surface; too early to call it a missing abstraction rather than a pattern still proving itself.

Three proposals follow as tasks, ordered by leverage.
summary: First monthly roadmap-proposals run. Three large proposals from 30 days of activity: (1) merge-driven work-ledger + plan-status reconciliation, (2) a real browser E2E suite in CI against a production build, (3) converge the four setup/bootstrap paths into one idempotent, self-verifying engine with a doctor mode.
title: 🔁 Roadmap proposals: 2026-08

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The scheduled-job detail route [`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/scheduled-jobs.$jobId.tsx`](applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/scheduled-jobs.$jobId.tsx) lists runs in `ScheduledJobRunsTable` but leaves you with almost nothing actionable: a run row shows status / trigger / started / finished / exit code and a truncated `errorMessage`. There is no way to open a run, no logs, no duration, and no way to cancel a stuck run. There is also **no edit route** — a job can only be created, toggled, run-now, or deleted, so the first configuration is effectively permanent.

Two deliverables:

1. **Run detail view** — click a run → full metadata + its live/historical logs + cancel.
2. **Job edit/update route** — change a job's prompt/schedule/driver/etc. after creation.

## What already exists (reuse, don't rebuild)

- **Update path is 90% built.** `updateScheduledAgentJob(input: UpdateScheduledAgentJobInputType!)` exists in `schema.gql` (line 3676), the `updateScheduledAgentJob` mutation doc + generated `UpdateScheduledAgentJobDocument` already live in [`scheduled-jobs.$jobId.tsx.graphql`](applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/scheduled-jobs.$jobId.tsx.graphql), `ScheduledJobForm` already takes `action: 'create' | 'update'` + a `job` prop, and `parseScheduledJobForm` already emits partial-patch fields. **No server work for edit** — only a route that wires them together.
- **Log console is reusable.** `QueueJobLogConsole`, `useQueueJobLogs`, and the `resources.queue-job-logs.tsx` loader (queries `queueJobLogs`, subscribes `queueJobLogTail`) are keyed by `queueName` + BullMQ `jobId`. Each run exposes `bullmqJobId` — so a run-detail view can embed the same console.
- **Cancel exists but is unused:** `cancelScheduledAgentJobRun(runId: ID!): ScheduledAgentJobRunObject!` (schema line 3696).

## Data model facts (constraints)

- `ScheduledAgentJobRunObject` fields (schema line 1874): `id, scheduledAgentJobId, bullmqJobId, status, driverId, model, trigger, exitCode, errorMessage, startedAt, finishedAt, createdAt`. **No output/log field on the run** — logs come from BullMQ via `bullmqJobId`.
- `bullmqJobId` is **null before the run is enqueued** — the run-detail logs section must handle that gracefully.
- There is currently **no single-run query** — only `scheduledAgentJobRuns(scheduledAgentJobId, limit)`. A run-detail route needs either a new `scheduledAgentJobRun(runId)` server query (preferred: supports refresh/deep-link) or to filter the existing list client-side.
- The run's logs are keyed by the **scheduled-agent-jobs BullMQ queue name** — identify that constant server-side and thread it into the loader (do not hardcode a guess).

## Recommended approach

Dedicated nested run-detail route `scheduled-jobs.$jobId.runs.$runId.tsx` that reuses `QueueJobLogConsole`/`useQueueJobLogs`, plus a `scheduled-jobs.$jobId.edit.tsx` route reusing `ScheduledJobForm`. Add the missing `scheduledAgentJobRun(runId)` server query so the run detail can load/refresh directly. Surface "Edit" from the detail header and make run rows link to the run detail.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning the queues console.
- New log storage — logs stay in BullMQ.
- Retention/pagination changes to the runs list beyond linking rows.

## Validation

Per CLAUDE.md: after any GraphQL change run server `dev` to regen `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel`, commit generated output. Gate each task with `lint` + `typecheck` + `test` (Vitest: `component` not `screen`, `userEvent`). Live-verify needs a permissioned user (settings:read) — render-level Vitest for authed pages.
summary: Add a per-run detail view (metadata + live/historical logs + cancel) and an edit/update route for scheduled agent jobs in openthrottle-developer.
title: Scheduled jobs: run detail view + job edit route
