author: visormatt
description:
## Evidence

Sampled the last 40 `continuous-integration.yml` runs: 24 success / 7 failure / 9 cancelled — a ~23% red rate on completed runs, and **4 of the 7 failures were pushes to `main`**, so `main` itself is intermittently red. All 7 failures land in the `🧠 NX lint,typecheck,test affected (shard N/3)` step; nothing else in the pipeline failed on its own.

Failure inventory (job logs pulled with `gh run view --log --job`):

| run | branch | shard | cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32201836604 | loop-plan-recharts-shapes | 1, 3 | `Editor.ssr.test.tsx` timed out at 5000ms (took 6318ms) |
| 32202185453 | loop-plan-mcp-followups | 3 | `Failed to resolve entry for package "@openthrottle/nestjs-openthrottle-mcp"` |
| 32201752646 | **main** | 1, 2 | generator timeouts **+** the same resolve-entry failure |
| 32200754295 | **main** | 1, 2 | generator timeouts + `Editor.ssr` timeout + the same resolve-entry failure |
| 32199870395 | **main** | 1, 2, 3 | all three shards red |
| 32198879567 | loop-plan-ci-shard | — | same family |
| 32181037247 | **main** | 1 | `watch.test.ts` + 5 × `generators/react/generator.*.test.ts` timeouts |

### Root cause A — the 5000ms default testTimeout

`grep -rn testTimeout` over the whole repo returns **nothing**: no project sets it, so every Vitest suite runs on the 5000ms default. Three repeat offenders exceed it under CI load while passing locally:

- `tools/generators` → `src/generators/react/generator.{component,hook,story,util}.test.ts` and `generator.test.ts` — these execute real Nx devkit generators over a tree; up to 5 files timed out in a single run.
- `packages/react-router-editor` → `src/components/__tests__/Editor.ssr.test.tsx` — `await import('../Editor')` pulls the editor module graph; measured at 6318ms against a 5000ms budget. Note the test already mocks `@monaco-editor/react`, so the cost is the remaining graph, not Monaco itself.
- `src/data/__tests__/watch.test.ts` → `watchWorkspace` — chokidar fs-event timing.

This class got *more* visible right as `09f34d98` (free-tier repricing) and `97a3210a` (3-way sharding) landed — the last three CI-perf commits on `main` each went red. Sharding did not introduce the slowness; it raised per-box CPU contention enough to push already-marginal suites past a budget with no headroom. The fix is a real timeout budget, not a revert.

### Root cause B — `exports` → gitignored `dist`, `main` → `src`

`packages/nestjs-mcp-developer/package.json` (package name `@openthrottle/nestjs-openthrottle-mcp`) declares:

```
"main":    "./src/index.ts",
"module":  "./src/index.ts",
"types":   "./src/index.ts",
"exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/src/index.js", ... } }
```

Vite/Vitest honor `exports` over `main`, and `dist` is gitignored (`.gitignore:14`). Its own test file `src/nestjs-mcp-developer.service.test.ts` imports the package **by name** (`import * as packageEntry from '@openthrottle/nestjs-openthrottle-mcp'`) to assert the entry contract — so the suite can only resolve if `dist/` exists on the box. The `test` targetDefault in `nx.json` depends on `^build` (dependencies' build), never on a *self* build, so `dist/` exists only when some other project scheduled onto that shard pulled this package through `^build`. Round-robin shard assignment therefore decides pass/fail: the identical failure surfaced on shard 3 once and shard 2 twice. This is a deterministic defect that CI has been masking, not a flake.

`packages/nestjs-agentic-workflow` carries the **identical** `exports`→dist / `main`→src mismatch. Its only self-referential import currently sits in a README, so it is a latent landmine rather than an active break — fix it in the same pass.

Both packages already carry a `publishConfig` block that rewrites `exports`/`main`/`types` to the built shape at publish time, so pointing the dev-time `exports` at `./src/index.ts` (matching `main`) costs nothing at publish and matches the source-first convention the rest of the workspace uses.

## Scope

Fix both root causes, add a guard so class B cannot reappear silently, then re-measure the red rate. Explicitly **not** in scope: reverting the sharding work (it is not the cause), and blanket `retry: N` on Vitest (that would hide class A rather than fix it).
summary: Shipped both CI failure classes that were turning `continuous-integration.yml` ~23% red (including on `main`). Class B: `@openthrottle/nestjs-openthrottle-mcp` `exports.import` now points at `./src/index.ts` (sibling `nestjs-agentic-workflow` already had that split; no rewrite needed). Guard: `scripts/check-package-entrypoints.ts` fails on Vite-resolved exports→gitignored-dist plus a self-import, warns otherwise; wired into CI shard 1 and `check:local`. Class A: workspace Vitest `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout` is 15s via `createBaseVitestConfig` (plus literals in the 11 configs that do not depend on `@tools/dotfiles`). Repeat-offender suites sped up (generator sub-suites ~9×, Editor.ssr 87×, watch.test ~2×). Deviations: did not rewrite all `exports` to src (would break the compiled CJS server); inverted the guard error/warn split because 39 packages have import→dist as the workspace norm. Draft PR: https://github.com/OpenThrottle/monorepo/pull/401. Follow-up: sample ≥20 completed CI runs after merge to confirm the red rate dropped; record the squash on the work ledger then.
title: 🩺 CI stability: kill the two failure classes turning pipelines red

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx` is the main chat surface. In a long thread the composer, `ChatComposerToolbar` and send/stop controls scroll out of view — the user has to scroll to the bottom to type, and loses the model/mode/permission controls while reading.

## Why it happens today (verified)

The developer app uses a **single page-level scroll container**, not a bounded chat column:

- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalLayout.tsx:83` — the content wrapper is `flex max-h-screen w-full max-w-full flex-col overflow-auto` and is the ref passed to `useScrollContainerRestoration`. This is the element that actually scrolls.
- `packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/Sidebar/SidebarInset.tsx` — `main` is `relative flex w-full flex-1 flex-col`, no `min-h-0`.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx:140` — `GlobalScreen className="flex flex-1 flex-col"`; the thread/composer column is `_index.tsx:160`, the composer wrapper is `_index.tsx:173` (`mx-auto w-full max-w-3xl`).
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatThread.tsx:134` — the thread *already* declares `flex min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto`, but it never becomes its own scroll region because no ancestor in the chain has a definite height with `min-h-0`, so the column grows and the outer container scrolls instead.

So the composer is a normal in-flow block inside the page scroller — it scrolls away by construction.

## Two candidate approaches

**A. Sticky composer (low blast radius, recommended v1).** Wrap the `ChatComposer` region in a `sticky bottom-0 z-10` container inside the existing page scroller, with a `bg-background` (or gradient/blur fade) backdrop so messages don't bleed through. Nothing about the global layout, scroll restoration, or other routes changes. `sticky` positions against the scroll container, so it stays correct with the sidebar inset and is far safer than `fixed` on mobile.

Wrinkle: the composer + toolbar subtree lives behind `<Suspense><Await>` (`_index.tsx:179`) with `HomeComposerSkeleton` as the fallback, and `HomeComposer` renders `ChatThread` and `ChatComposer` as **siblings** in one fragment (`HomeComposer.tsx:132-162`). The sticky wrapper has to sit around the composer only, which means either lifting `ChatThread` out of `HomeComposer` into the route, or introducing the sticky wrapper inside `HomeComposer`. Prefer the former — it also gives the skeleton the same sticky frame.

**B. Bounded chat column (architecturally cleaner, wider blast radius).** Give the route a real viewport-height column so `ChatThread` becomes the only scroll region and the composer is naturally the last, non-scrolling row: add `min-h-0` down the chain (`SidebarInset`, `GlobalScreen`, the route column) and switch the layout wrapper to a definite height (`h-screen`/`h-dvh` + `overflow-hidden`) for chat-shaped routes. This changes `GlobalLayout` for every route and interacts with `useScrollContainerRestoration` and the search-param scroll-reset behaviour already fixed in PR #279 — it needs its own verification pass across routes.

Ship A; record B as the follow-up if/when other routes want an app-shell layout.

## Mobile

The user explicitly asked whether this should apply on mobile too. Starting recommendation — **yes, apply it on mobile as well**, because a bottom-docked composer is the expected chat pattern on phones and the problem is strictly worse on a short viewport. Conditions:

- Use `sticky`, never `fixed` — `fixed` fights the iOS visual viewport when the software keyboard opens.
- The app already sets `viewport-fit=cover` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/root.tsx:339`), so the sticky bar needs `pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)]` or it sits under the home indicator.
- Consider `interactive-widget=resizes-content` in the viewport meta so the keyboard resizes the layout viewport rather than overlaying it.
- Keep the toolbar's vertical footprint small on mobile (it is a wrapping row of controls) so a docked bar doesn't eat half the screen — collapse-behind-a-trigger is in scope to evaluate, not necessarily to build.

Task 2 makes this a decision with evidence rather than an assumption; if mobile turns out to be bad, gate the sticky behaviour at `md:` and say so.

## Out of scope

- The header `ChatDialog` chat surface (it is already a bounded dialog column).
- Any redesign of `ChatComposerToolbar` contents.
- Approach B / the global app-shell layout refactor.

## Constraints

- Components come from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; keep the generated section comments and one-component-per-file rules.
- Existing route tests: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/__tests__/_index.test.tsx` and `_index.deep-link.test.tsx` must stay green.
- Don't regress `ChatThread`'s auto-scroll behaviour (event-driven, anti-jitter) or the scroll-restoration hook.
summary: Keep the composer, toolbar and send controls always reachable on `/` by pinning them to the bottom of the scroll container instead of letting them scroll away in long threads — on desktop first, with a deliberate decision (and safe-area handling) for mobile.
title: Pin the home chat composer + toolbar to the bottom of the viewport

author: visormatt
description:
Explore & ship a curated MCP **connectors** catalog with a connect flow, surfaced under `/settings/mcp` in `openthrottle-developer`.

## Context / gap
OpenThrottle today exposes *its own* tools **as** an MCP server (`packages/openthrottle-mcp`, `applications/openthrottle-server/src/modules/mcp-developer`). It has **no** concept of the platform *connecting to external* MCP servers (GitHub, Slack, Notion…) that agents could later consume. This plan adds the first vertical slice: a curated catalog + connect/enable flow.

## Locked decisions (2026-07-31)
- **Baseline** = curated **top ~10** connectors seeded across **3 registry/host providers**: (1) Anthropic connector directory, (2) the official MCP registry, (3) vendor-hosted remote MCP. Live registry tools returned nothing in-session, so Task 1 curates from known connectors rather than a live pull.
- **Scope** = **catalog + connect flow**: browse → connect (store credential / OAuth reference, mirroring `settings.keys`) → enable/disable. **No agent-run wiring** in this plan (explicit follow-up).
- **Route** = **`/settings/mcp`** (`settings.mcp._index.tsx` + `settings.mcp.$connectorId.tsx`).

## Proposed top-10 (finalized in Task 1)
GitHub, Linear, Notion, Slack, Atlassian (Jira/Confluence), Sentry, Google Drive, Figma, Stripe, Postgres/Supabase — each tagged with its source provider + auth type (OAuth vs token) + remote transport config.

## Key patterns to follow
- Flat routes (`settings.mcp.*.tsx`) + companion `.graphql` docs + `__tests__`; logic/components under `app/routing/settings/`.
- Credential storage mirrors the service-account-credential flow in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.keys.tsx` and its server resolvers.
- Code-first GraphQL in `openthrottle-server` (Result/ListResult types; never break fields, `@deprecated`); regenerate `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` + codegen.
- Generators first (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=...`), one component/file, keep section comments, no TS enums (`as const`).
- Authed pages need permissions → prefer render-level Vitest (repo memory: developer-app-live-verify-auth-permission).

## Out of scope (future plans)
Wiring enabled connectors into live agent runs / drivers; per-connector tool allow-lists; org-vs-user connection scoping beyond the baseline.
summary: Curated top-10 MCP connectors catalog (seeded across 3 registry/host providers) with a connect + enable/disable flow, surfaced at /settings/mcp in openthrottle-developer. No agent-run wiring in this plan.
title: MCP connectors catalog + connect flow under /settings/mcp

author: visormatt
description:
## Purpose

Smoke-test the plan → task → execution loop with work that is impossible to get subtly wrong. No repo code is touched; the only side effect is one new file on the user's desktop.

## Scope

- Three echo tasks, one joke each. Each task must `echo` its joke so the joke text appears in the run log.
- One final task that writes all three jokes to `/home/demo/Desktop/jokes.txt`.

## Jokes (fixed, so runs are reproducible)

1. Why do programmers prefer dark mode? Because light attracts bugs.
2. There are two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation, naming things, and off-by-one errors.
3. I told my manager the build was flaky. He said "so is my resolve." We shipped anyway.

## File format

`/home/demo/Desktop/jokes.txt`, plain UTF-8, trailing newline:

```
1. Why do programmers prefer dark mode? Because light attracts bugs.
2. There are two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation, naming things, and off-by-one errors.
3. I told my manager the build was flaky. He said "so is my resolve." We shipped anyway.
```

## Non-goals

- No changes anywhere under the repo working tree.
- No commits, no PR, no ledger artifacts — this is a throwaway smoke test.

## Done when

- All three jokes appear in the run output.
- `/home/demo/Desktop/jokes.txt` exists and contains exactly the three numbered lines above.
summary: A deliberately trivial smoke-test plan: three tasks each echo one joke to stdout, then a fourth task collects all three and writes them to ~/Desktop/jokes.txt.
title: 🧪 Test: echo three jokes and write them to the desktop

author: visormatt
description:
# Generic scheduled agent jobs

## Why
Every recurring agent job today requires a bespoke, code-defined queue + processor + `*-repeatable.service.ts` (there are 5 cron services). There is **no way for a user to create a scheduled agent job at runtime**: no persistence, no create-repeatable mutation (only `repeatableJobs` list + `removeRepeatableJob`), and the only agent worker (`PlansProcessor`) is hardwired to the Ralph orchestrator + a single Cursor iteration runner.

We want a **generic** scheduled job: give it a **prompt + provider/model/settings**, pick a **cron schedule**, and it runs on BullMQ's built-in repeatable machinery — one shared queue, no new queue per job — usable with any agent framework/CLI.

## Approach (locked)
- **Runner primitive lives in `openthrottle-drivers`** — that's our choke point and most of it already exists (`ALL_DRIVERS`/`getDriver`, `AgentDriver.buildShellCommand`, `DriverInvocationConfig`, `runDriverAsync`/`runDriverSync` engine across claude/codex/cursor/grok/opencode). The design must **inventory what already exists there first** and extend/expose a single provider-agnostic "run once with {prompt, driverId, model, settings, cwd, signal, onChunk}" entrypoint rather than reinventing invocation in the server.
- **Server adds ONE generic queue + processor** (modeled on `PlansProcessor`: heartbeat, AbortSignal cancellation, output logging, stalled recovery) that decodes `{scheduleId, prompt, driverId, model, settings}` and calls the drivers entrypoint. Decoupled from Ralph/plans.
- **BullMQ repeatable jobs** provide the scheduling (reuse `REPEATABLE_JOB_OPTIONS`; evaluate legacy `repeat` vs newer `upsertJobScheduler`). No dedicated queue per user job.

## Net-new
- Persistence for user-defined schedules (no table exists today).
- A create/update/delete/enable/run-now GraphQL surface (only list/remove repeatables exist).
- Reconciliation between persisted schedules and BullMQ schedulers.
- A generic driver-invocation worker (current one is Ralph/Cursor-specific).
- Developer UI to author schedules (prompt + provider/model/settings + cron) and view run history/live logs.

## Design-first
Task 1 is an architecture design doc (under `docs/`) that must resolve: the drivers-package entrypoint API, the generic queue payload + naming, persistence schema (schedule + runs), legacy `repeat` vs `upsertJobScheduler`, DB↔BullMQ reconciliation, where run output/logs live (reuse `queueJobLogs`/work-ledger?), role-slicing, and the GraphQL contract. Implementation tasks follow the doc.

## Key anchor files
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/{types,drivers,registry,engine}/index.ts`
- `packages/nestjs-bullmq/src/modules/nestjs-bullmq.module.ts`, `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/repeatable-job.options.ts`
- Reference services: `.../queues/doc-ingestion/doc-ingestion-repeatable.service.ts` (env-driven cron), `.../queues/work-ledger-sweep/work-ledger-sweep-repeatable.service.ts`
- Reference worker: `.../queues/plans/plans.processor.ts`; enqueue path `.../graphql/plans/plan-enqueue.service.ts`
- Dynamic-queue caveat: `.../graphql/queues/queues.service.ts` `createQueue` makes a producer-only queue (no processor) — a generic job needs a statically-registered processor.
summary: Design-first feature: let users create scheduled agent jobs from a prompt + provider/model/settings that run on a cron schedule via BullMQ's built-in repeatable jobs, WITHOUT a dedicated queue per job. The provider-agnostic run-once primitive stays in openthrottle-drivers (the choke point — runDriverAsync/engine already exists); the server adds one generic queue + processor, persistence, reconciliation, GraphQL, and a developer UI.
title: Generic scheduled agent jobs — prompt + provider on a schedule, no new queue per job

author: visormatt
description:
## The symptom

Open the checkout picker in a workspace with real branch names and the row text runs past the right edge of the popover. Observed on `/plans/<id>` with the icon-only trigger open: the `nativeapps` row's branch `claude/nx-upgrade-plan-ce8b01` extends beyond the popover boundary. The selector is otherwise good — this is a containment bug, not a redesign.

## Why it happens (both places, same mistake)

**The row** — [ChatCheckoutSelectorRow.tsx:110](packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatCheckoutSelectorRow.tsx:110). The branch is rendered as:

```
<span className="text-muted-foreground flex shrink-0 items-center gap-1 text-xs">
```

`shrink-0`, no `max-w-*`, no `truncate`. The label column next to it is `min-w-0 flex-1` and correctly truncates, but flexbox cannot shrink the branch to make room, so the row's intrinsic width simply exceeds its container. And the container does not clip: `CommandItem` ([CommandItem.tsx:29](packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/Command/CommandItem.tsx:29)) is `relative flex items-center` with **no** `overflow-hidden` and no `min-w-0`, and the popover is a fixed `w-96` (384px) — [ChatCheckoutSelector.tsx:163](packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatCheckoutSelector.tsx:163). Overflow, visibly.

**The trigger** — [ChatCheckoutSelectorTrigger.tsx:99](packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatCheckoutSelectorTrigger.tsx:99). Identical shape: the button is capped at `max-w-56` (224px), the label truncates, the branch span is `shrink-0`. A long branch pushes the button past its own max-width. This is invisible in the screenshot only because the plan-detail tabs row passes `minimal`, and minimal mode renders no branch at all — so the trigger bug is a chat-composer bug that has simply not been screenshotted yet. Fix both or it reappears.

## The non-obvious part: truncation direction

Plain `truncate` is end-ellipsis, and for branch names that is the wrong half. The two names on screen are `visormatt/bootstrap-service-accounts` and `claude/nx-upgrade-plan-ce8b01`; every branch in this workspace shares a short author/tool prefix (`visormatt/`, `claude/`, `openthrottle/`) and differs in its tail. `claude/nx-upgrade-pl…` and `claude/nx-upgrade-pr…` are not tellable apart, which defeats the whole reason the branch is on the row.

So the fix is not "add `truncate`". It is: give the branch a shrink budget, truncate it in a direction that preserves the tail, and put the full string somewhere reachable. There is no middle-truncation helper in the workspace today; the nearest prior art is `shortenFilesystemPath` ([repository-identity.ts:100](packages/react-router-chat/src/utils/repository-identity.ts:100)), which solves the same problem for paths and is the shape to follow.

## Scope

In scope: `ChatCheckoutSelectorRow`, `ChatCheckoutSelectorTrigger`, and whatever shared helper the truncation needs. Both are consumed by chat's composer and — via `PlanCheckoutSelector` — by the plan-detail tabs row, so one fix covers every surface.

Explicitly **not** in scope, checked and already correct:

- `PlanRunProvenanceCell` ([:69](applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/components/PlanRunProvenanceCell.tsx:69)) — icon `shrink-0`, text `truncate`. Fine.
- `PlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector` ([:166](applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/components/PlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector.tsx:166)) — same correct pattern.
- `IdeRepositorySelector` — renders no branch.
- The row's `qualifier` line already truncates and needs nothing.

## Related

- OT `d72565fd` (PENDING) — checkout-selector search tightening. Same components, different concern; don't merge them.
- OT `5ff2cb43` (DONE, PR #473) — the `minimal` trigger mode this plan has to keep working.

## Verification reality

jsdom has no layout engine, so no test can assert "does not overflow". Tests must assert the markup contract — the branch element carries its shrink/max-width classes and the full value is present as a title/accessible name — and the visual proof comes from a live pass in the developer app against a genuinely long branch. Plan on the running app for the last task, not on Vitest.
summary: The branch affordance in ChatCheckoutSelectorRow and ChatCheckoutSelectorTrigger is `shrink-0` with no width cap and no truncation, so a real-world branch name overflows the w-96 popover and the max-w-56 trigger. Give the branch a shrink budget and a truncation that keeps the distinguishing tail, with the full value reachable on hover.
title: Checkout selector: a long branch name must not break the layout

author: visormatt
description:
Port `docs/marketing/scripts/04-mental-model.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

This is the only Season 1 short that teaches a vocabulary rather than a click-path: plan, task, note, project. The risk the script itself names is that it degenerates into four definitions read aloud, so the on-screen action column carries the weight and each term must be SHOWN. That makes it structurally different from every flow recorded so far - it crosses four routes (`/plans/:id`, `/notes`, `/notes/:id`, `/projects`, `/projects/:id`) in 54 seconds, where 01, 03 and 21 each stay on one surface.

## The gate: beat 0:41 describes UI that does not exist

The script's 0:41 beat is "Back to the plan; show its project badge". `app/routing/plans/components/PlanDetailRouteHeader.tsx` renders the title, status badge, author -> assignee, tags and created/updated dates. There is no project anywhere on the plan header.

The data is already loaded: `app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx.graphql` selects `projectRelation { ...ProjectDetails }`, `project` and `projectId` on the plan. So this is a rendering gap, not a data gap, and it is cheap either way.

This is the same class of defect the pilot caught - a script claiming a commit-link view the app does not have - and it is exactly why the publish checklist exists. It must be decided before the flow is written, because the flow is a transcription of the script and a flow may not invent a step the script does not describe.

## What already exists and needs no work

- Routes: `/notes` (`NotesTable`, `NoteCard`), `/notes/:noteId`, `/projects` (`ProjectsTable`, `ProjectsStats`, `ProjectsToolbar`), `/projects/:projectId` (`ProjectTasksTable`).
- Fixture: `tests/demo/fixtures/demo-content.ts` already seeds two projects (`atlas-api`, `atlas-web`) and four notes whose voice fits the "something you learned" narration - "429 vs 503", "Antimeridian", "Tile cache invalidation", "Deploys and the tile cache". `scripts/seed-demo.ts` writes both.
- Plan `d0d0d0d0-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1`-linked plan (fixture id `01`, "rate limiting") already carries `projectId` -> `atlas-api`, so the plan->project relationship the 0:41 beat needs is seeded.
- Runner verbs: `highlight`, `navigate`, `dwell`, `scrollTo`, `zoomTo` are all implemented in `runner/actions.ts`.

## Constraints

- Selectors must be the same hooks the Maestro E2E flows use. The app must not grow a second parallel set of test hooks.
- The 9:16 strategy varies BY BEAT here rather than by flow: the plans and notes tables are wider than the portrait crop window and want `fit`, while a single note card and a single project row are legible cropped. This is the first flow where that is true, so expect `regionOfInterest` to do more work than in `03-first-plan`.
- 91 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; any rewrite of the 0:41 row must re-validate it.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.
summary: Port docs/marketing/scripts/04-mental-model.md to a recorded demo flow, and settle the project-badge beat the app does not render.
title: Build the 04-mental-model screencast flow

author: visormatt
description:
# Auto-run DB migrations on dev/start (Nx gate)

## Problem
On the Docker side, migrations are guaranteed by `Dockerfile.Migrations` (a one-shot init service the server `depends_on` with `service_completed_successfully`). There is **no equivalent guarantee for local dev/start** — `pnpm run database:migrate` is a manual step, so a developer can boot `openthrottle-server` against a stale schema after pulling new migrations. We want the monorepo dev/start flow to ensure all pending migrations are applied first.

## Current state (verified)
- **Runner already exists and is idempotent**: `scripts/openthrottle-database-migrations.ts` uses a `schema_migrations` ledger; it reads applied filenames, applies only pending ones (each migration + ledger insert in one transaction), and bootstraps the ledger when a schema-carrying DB has an empty ledger. It exports `runMigrations`, `PgMigrationStore`, `MigrationStore`/`MigrationSource` ports — already unit-testable with fakes. Root script: `database:migrate` = `POSTGRES_HOST='localhost' tsx --env-file .env ./scripts/openthrottle-database-migrations.ts`.
- **The ledger read IS the cheap "pending?" check** — no separate mechanism needed; running the runner on every boot is safe and fast when up to date.
- **Nx gate pattern already exists**: `openthrottle-server` `dev` target has `dependsOn: [{ target: 'ensure-worktree', projects: 'monorepo' }, '^dev']`. `monorepo:ensure-worktree` is a `cache:false` `nx:run-commands` target (`./scripts/ensure_worktree.sh`, `cwd: {workspaceRoot}`). This is the exact shape to mirror.
- **Server targets that boot against Postgres**: `dev` (PROCESS_ROLE=all), `dev-api` (api), `worker` (worker), `start`. `dev-api`/`worker` currently depend only on `^dev`/`^build`; `start` only on `^build`.
- **Root `start` flow**: `start` = `start:docker` (`database:start`) + `start:openthrottle` (`nx run-many -t start -p openthrottle-developer openthrottle-server`). `dev` does NOT start the DB.
- The `monorepo` project is defined via the root `package.json` `nx.targets` block; that's where the new target goes.

## Decisions (locked)
- **DB-not-up behavior: reachability preflight + wait, then fail fast.** Poll Postgres for readiness for a short window (covers the race where `database:start` was just issued); if still unreachable, exit non-zero with a clear message pointing to `pnpm run database:start`. The gate does NOT own container lifecycle (no auto `docker compose up`).
- **Scope: server targets only.** Gate `openthrottle-server` `dev`, `dev-api`, `worker`, `start`. The server is the only process that touches Postgres directly; the developer app inherits the gate via `^dev`/run-many when booted together. No changes to the root npm `start` scripts.
- **Reuse the existing runner** as the single source of truth — do not build a second migration mechanism.
- **Docker path unchanged** — `Dockerfile.Migrations` + the compose `migrations` init service remain authoritative for container installs; this plan is dev/start-only and must not duplicate or conflict with it.

## Approach
Add a `cache:false` `monorepo:ensure-migrations` target (mirroring `ensure-worktree`) that runs a small preflight-and-migrate script: resolve the Postgres URL (same resolution the server uses), retry-connect for a bounded window, then call the exported `runMigrations`; on timeout print guidance and exit 1. Wire it into the four server targets, ordered AFTER `ensure-worktree` (worktree self-heal can repair a stale `.env`, which is where Postgres connection settings come from).

## Key gotcha to guard
Env/DB-target parity: the gate must migrate the **same** Postgres the server will connect to. Root `database:migrate` uses root `.env` + `POSTGRES_HOST=localhost`; the server reads `applications/openthrottle-server/.env`. If those point at different DBs the gate would migrate the wrong one. A task explicitly verifies parity and makes the target resolve the server's DB.

## Out of scope
- Docker/compose migration wiring (already handled).
- Any change to migration file format or the ledger schema.
- Auto-starting Postgres/Redis containers from the gate.
summary: Guarantee all pending SQL migrations are applied before openthrottle-server boots in dev/start, via a new cache:false monorepo:ensure-migrations Nx target (reachability preflight + wait, then fail fast) wired into the server dev/dev-api/worker/start dependsOn — mirroring the existing ensure-worktree gate. Docker path (Dockerfile.Migrations init service) stays authoritative for containers and is unchanged.
title: Auto-run DB migrations on dev/start (Nx gate)

author: visormatt
description:
## Symptom

On `http://localhost:6020/schedule/:jobId/edit` (route `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/schedule.$jobId.edit.tsx`), editing the **Prompt** field and saving appears to succeed (redirects to the detail page) but the prompt value is not persisted. All other fields (name, driverId, cronPattern, model, timezone, timeoutMs, cwd, settingsJson) save correctly.

## Root cause

The bug is server-side, NOT in the edit route or client form.

Data flow on save:
1. `schedule.$jobId.edit.tsx` action parses the form (`parseScheduleForm`) — `prompt` is present and included in `patch`.
2. It sends `UpdateScheduledAgentJobDocument` with `input` containing `prompt` (the mutation input type `UpdateScheduledAgentJobInputType` DOES declare `prompt` — see `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.input.ts:70-73`).
3. Resolver `updateScheduledAgentJob` (`scheduled-agent-jobs.resolver.ts:119-135`) forwards `const { id, ...rest } = input; this.service.update(id, rest)` — `rest` still contains `prompt`.
4. **`ScheduledAgentJobsGraphqlService.update()` drops it.** In `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs-graphql.service.ts`:
   - The `UpdateArgs` interface (lines 50-59) has NO `prompt` field.
   - The `update()` method's call to `this.jobsService.updateJob(id, { ... })` (lines 129-141) never passes `prompt`.

So `prompt` is silently discarded before it reaches the repository. The underlying `ScheduledAgentJobsService.updateJob` (nestjs-repositories) uses `merge`, and its `UpdateScheduledAgentJobInput` DOES support `prompt` — the repository layer is fine.

## Fix

In `scheduled-agent-jobs-graphql.service.ts`:
1. Add `readonly prompt?: string;` to the `UpdateArgs` interface.
2. Pass `prompt: args.prompt,` in the `updateJob({...})` call inside `update()`.

Both must be added — `undefined` fields are already a no-op patch in `updateJob` (merge skips undefined), so this correctly leaves prompt unchanged when not supplied.

## Verification / regression guard

- Add a server-side unit test asserting `ScheduledAgentJobsGraphqlService.update()` forwards `prompt` to `jobsService.updateJob` (mirror existing tests in the graphql-service spec if present).
- Manual: edit a job's prompt at `/schedule/:jobId/edit`, save, reload — prompt reflects the new value.

## Notes / non-issues
- The edit route intentionally strips `enabled` (`const { enabled: _enabled, ...patch }`) because enablement has its own `setScheduledAgentJobEnabled` mutation and `UpdateScheduledAgentJobInputType` has no `enabled` field. Not part of this bug.
- No schema/codegen change needed — `prompt` already exists on the GraphQL input type; this is purely the internal server mapping.
summary: Editing a scheduled job's prompt on /schedule/:jobId/edit never persists because the server-side GraphQL service omits `prompt` from its update mapping.
title: Fix: prompt silently dropped on scheduled-agent-job update

author: visormatt
description:
## CLOSED — superseded by OT cf8469de-7c57-40d6-9dea-aad241dd3ce3 (COMPLETED)

Duplicate of the "Squash 'workspace is out of sync' (@nx/js:typescript-sync gate)" plan, which shipped the fix: committed `nx.json` `sync.disabledTaskSyncGenerators: ["@nx/js:typescript-sync"]` (keeps `analyzeSourceFiles` / affected edges intact), a one-time reconcile of real tsconfig-reference drift, and a non-gating `check:tsconfig-refs`. Root cause matches (non-interactive shells have no TTY so `applyChanges` refuses; the generator injects phantom RR cross-refs — nrwl/nx#36297 — so `nx sync` is never safe here). No separate work needed.

---

## Problem

Running any Nx target (`typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, …) in a **non-interactive shell** — CI, agent/headless sessions, `setup_worktree.sh` provisioning — hard-fails before the task runs with the `@nx/js:typescript-sync` "workspace is out of sync" error. `nx.json` sets `sync.applyChanges: true`, but that only auto-applies in interactive shells; non-interactive runs refuse and exit non-zero, forcing a recurring uncommitted `disabledTaskSyncGenerators` workaround. (Full original problem statement + constraints preserved in OT cf8469de.)
title: Stable fix for the nx sync "workspace out of sync" hard-fail in non-interactive shells

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

Builds directly on **f599b238** (onboarding empty-states). Today the rich `GlobalFeatureOnboarding` "teach-me-fast" block only renders when a list is **empty AND unfiltered** (`isNewUser`). Once a user has any Rules / Schedule jobs / Plans, that onboarding content vanishes — there's no way to re-read "what is this, what's it for, how do we use it."

We want the **same onboarding content** to remain reachable when the list is populated, surfaced inside a `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal` built on our base modal (`GlobalModal` → shadcn `Dialog`), driven consistently by `?modal=onboarding` across all three routes. A single copy object per feature drives BOTH the inline empty-state block AND the modal — no duplicated copy.

## Current state (verified 2026-08-15, on branch openthrottle/loop-plan-onboarding-empty-states)

- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalFeatureOnboarding.tsx` — presentational `Card` block. Props: `{ className?, content: GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent }`. Renders eyebrow/icon + title + tagline, "What it is", "How we use it internally", "What you could use it for", numbered "Quick start", and CTA(s). Exported from the package barrel along with the `GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent` / `GlobalFeatureOnboardingLink` types and `GLOBAL_FEATURE_ONBOARDING_SECTION_COPY`.
- `GlobalModal.tsx` — thin wrapper over shadcn `Dialog`/`DialogContent`, open-state bound to a URL search param via `useUrlSyncedOverlay({ param, openValue })`. `DialogContent` is already `max-w-5xl max-h-svh overflow-y-auto`.
- `GlobalMetricsInfoModal.tsx` + `GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger.tsx` — the reference pattern: a trigger sets `modal=<KEY>` (URL is the single source of truth; trigger and dialog share no React state), a modal wraps `GlobalModal`. Both hang a `.key` off the component.
- `useUrlSyncedOverlay.tsx` — hook returning `{ open, onOpenChange, setOpen }`; `setOpen(true)` sets the param preserving others, close deletes it. Scroll-preserving by default.
- Routes render onboarding inline gated on `isNewUser` (empty && !filtered): `rules._index.tsx`, `plans._index.tsx`, `schedule._index.tsx`. Header components: `RulesIntroduction`, `PlansIntroduction`, `ScheduleIntroduction` (Schedule's was added in f599b238). Copy objects: `RULES_ONBOARDING`, `PLANS_ONBOARDING`(via plans `data.copy.ts`), schedule `data.copy.ts` onboarding const.

## Design decisions (locked)

1. **One shared modal param value: `modal=onboarding`**, identical across Rules / Schedule / Plans. Each page renders at most one onboarding modal, so the value is unambiguous per-page and consistent across the app. Export a single `GLOBAL_FEATURE_ONBOARDING_MODAL` constant (`{ param: 'modal', value: 'onboarding' }`) from the package and use it in both the modal and the trigger — no stringly-typed drift.
2. **New primitive `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal`** in `react-router-ui-global`: `props { content: GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent; className? }`. Internally `<GlobalModal param="modal" value="onboarding">` wrapping the onboarding content. Hang `.key = 'onboarding'` off it, matching the existing convention.
3. **Dialog-aware rendering, single-sourced markup.** Add ONE optional prop to `GlobalFeatureOnboarding`: `renderAs?: 'block' | 'dialog'` (default `'block'`, preserving today's behavior). In `'dialog'` mode it (a) drops the outer `Card`/`CardContent` chrome (the `Dialog` surface is already the card), and (b) renders its title/tagline row using shadcn `DialogTitle`/`DialogDescription` so Radix's required-accessible-title invariant is satisfied without duplicating a header. All body sections + CTAs stay identical. This keeps the teaching markup in ONE component; the modal is a thin shell.
4. **New primitive `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger`** (mirrors `GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger`): a labeled button (default label e.g. "How it works" — expose a `label?` prop, default from package copy) that calls `setOpen(true)` on `modal=onboarding`. URL is the source of truth; trigger and modal need no shared state.
5. **Wiring per route.** Each route renders `<GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal content={X_ONBOARDING} />` unconditionally (cheap; only mounts a Dialog that's closed unless the param is set), and each `Introduction` header renders a `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger`. The existing inline `isNewUser` block is unchanged. Net effect: empty+unfiltered → inline pitch (as today); populated/filtered → same pitch on demand via the header trigger + `?modal=onboarding`.
6. **No GraphQL / schema / codegen** changes. Purely presentational + URL state.

## Out of scope

- Auto-opening the modal on first visit, or any "seen it" persistence/preference. v1 is trigger-driven only.
- Fanning the trigger+modal out to routes beyond Rules / Schedule / Plans (Prompts, Queues, Personas, …) — a follow-up, same as f599b238's rollout follow-up.
- Restyling the underlying `GlobalModal` / base Dialog.

## Validation

- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint,typecheck,test` green; `pnpm nx run react-router-ui-global:lint,typecheck,test` green.
- Package unit tests: `GlobalFeatureOnboarding renderAs="dialog"` emits an accessible `DialogTitle` and no `Card`; `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal` renders its content only when `?modal=onboarding`; trigger sets the param.
- Route render tests: with a populated list the header trigger is present and `?modal=onboarding` reveals the onboarding content (assert on a stable test-id + CTA href); the inline empty-state path still works when empty+unfiltered.
- Live dev-server screenshot of one route showing the modal open over a populated list.
title: Onboarding-in-a-modal: surface the FeatureOnboarding pitch via a modal=onboarding GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal when lists are populated

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Let a user invoke a skill directly from the skill detail route (`/skills/:slug`) in the **openthrottle-developer** app. Add a **"Run now"** button to the skill detail header (mirroring the schedule detail route's Run-now affordance) that opens a **"Run skill" modal**. The modal offers the basics to launch a run: pick an **agent (CLI backend) + model**, an optional free-text **Arguments** field, and a **Run** action that composes the invocation and streams the result live.

This is the v1 (interactive) slice. Structured, typed argument fields parsed from SKILL.md are a separate follow-up plan (see the companion "Parse & render structured skill arguments" plan).

## Decisions locked

- **Arguments:** single free-text "Arguments" input for v1. The invocation message is composed as `/<slug> <args>` (args trimmed; omitted entirely when empty). Structured/typed argument fields are the follow-up plan.
- **Run mechanism:** interactive **streamed conversation** via the existing `startConversationStream` path — no new server mutation. Output streams live in a conversation view; user is navigated there on Run.

## Current-state findings (from codebase exploration)

- **Skill detail route:** `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx`. Loader is **filesystem-based** (`readSkillFileBySlug` → `{ content, editable, entry }`); the action only reads/writes `SKILL.md`. There is **no run/invoke plumbing and no model discovery** in this route today — both must be added.
- **Detail component:** `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/components/SkillDetail.tsx`. Header row (`flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4`) has a `<div className="flex-1" />` spacer at ~line 129, then `<SkillDetailEditControls>`. The Run-now button goes just before the edit controls.
- **Skill entry shape:** `RepoSkillEntry` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/agents/data/repo-skills-registry.ts`) — `slug`, `summary`, `source`, `tags`, `layout`, `disableModelInvocation`, `provenance`, etc. Frontmatter parser (`packages/openthrottle-skills/src/parse-skill-frontmatter.ts`) only knows `name`/`description`/`disableModelInvocation`/`tags`. **No structured arguments exist.**
- **Agent + model picker:** unified grouped picker in `@openthrottle/react-router-chat` — `ChatModelPicker` (two-column: left rail = provider/CLI group ≈ agent, right = searchable model list), `ChatComposerModelControl`. State primitives in `@openthrottle/react-router-chat-state`: `buildModelGroups`, `decodeChatOption` (`modelId` → `{ backend, baseUrl, model }`), `capabilitiesForChatOption`, `chatToolbarStateAtom`. App wiring reference: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/HomeComposer.tsx` + `app/routing/home/demo/useHomeComposer.tsx`.
- **Model discovery loader:** `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/models.server.ts` (local endpoints + agent CLIs + driver×endpoint), with `app/routing/home/demo/chat-options-cache.ts` and `app/routing/home/demo/chat-model-option.ts`.
- **Run execution:** resource route `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/resources.conversation-stream.tsx` (action `intent=start` → `StartConversationStreamDocument`). Turn hook: `app/routing/home/demo/useAgenticChatTurn.tsx` (`submitTurn`). Live tokens via `conversationStreamChunkAdded` subscription. Mutation input `StartConversationStreamInput` (schema.gql ~4557): `message!`, `backend`, `baseUrl`, `modelId`, `repositoryId`, `permissionMode`, `reasoning`, `serviceTier`, `persist`, `personaId`, `conversationId`, `fileMentions`.
- **Dialog pattern to mirror:** `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/components/AddHookDialog.tsx` — controlled (`open`/`onOpenChange`), local form state, reset-on-open, computed `submitDisabled`, parent owns the mutation. `ScheduleForm.tsx` already assembles prompt + driver + model inputs.

## Key gotchas / constraints

- **CLI backends require `repositoryId`** in prod (`decoded.backend !== 'openai'`). The dialog must resolve a repository to run against. Decide the default: the skill's own repo/workspace vs. the currently selected workspace checkout. Surface a repository/checkout picker if none can be inferred, and disable Run until one is chosen for CLI backends.
- **`openai` backend requires `modelId` + `baseUrl`;** CLI backends take `backend` (+ optional `modelId` override). Reuse `decodeChatOption` to derive the right payload rather than reconstructing it.
- Skill detail loader is filesystem-only today — adding model discovery means calling the same shared discovery path used by the home composer (reuse `chat-options-cache` / `models.server`, don't duplicate).
- Reuse the existing chat-toolbar Jotai atom / `buildModelGroups` so the picker matches the rest of the app; don't fork a second model-state source.
- Authed developer-app pages need permissions; live smoke needs a permissioned user. Follow render-level Vitest convention for the dialog/button.

## Conventions (must follow)

- Generators first: scaffold the new component(s) with `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=skills --name=RunSkillDialog`. Keep the generated section comments; one component per file; props interface exported. Static copy/lists in the nearest `data/` (`data.copy.ts`).
- UI from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` (`Dialog`, `Button`, `TextArea`, etc.). No new enums (`as const`), avoid `as`/`any`, `import type`, explicit return types, `const`, alphabetize where order is irrelevant.
- Codegen: any new/changed `.graphql` documents → run `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel` and commit `__generated__`. Prefer reusing the existing `StartConversationStreamDocument` (no schema change needed).
- Validate: `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck,lint,test` and a `dev`/`build` integration check for the source-first chat packages.

## Out of scope (→ follow-up plan)

- Typed/structured argument fields parsed from SKILL.md frontmatter or metadata.
- A dedicated durable "skill run" record / detail page (this v1 reuses conversation streaming).
title: Run a skill from the /skills/:slug detail route (interactive stream)

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

On `/skills`, the source filter (`All`, `OpenThrottle`, `External`, `Personal`) renders as four detached, individually-bordered buttons. They read as four unrelated CTAs sitting next to the Search field and the two `Manage …` buttons, not as one mutually-exclusive control. The user wants them presented as a single button group (segmented control).

## Why it is not already segmented

The markup is already correct — `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/components/SkillsToolbar.tsx` uses `ToggleGroup type="single" variant="outline"` with four `ToggleGroupItem`s. The *presentation* is the gap:

- `packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/ToggleGroup/ToggleGroup.tsx` hard-codes `flex items-center gap-1` on the root — items are spaced apart.
- `packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/ToggleGroup/toggleGroupItemVariants.tsx` gives every item `rounded-md` and `variant: outline` a full `border border-input` — so each item is its own pill with its own four borders.

Nothing overlaps or collapses the shared edges, so the group cannot look attached no matter what the consumer passes.

## Approach

Add an **opt-in** `attached` presentation to the shared `ToggleGroup`, then adopt it in `SkillsToolbar`. Opt-in rather than changing the default, because there are 9 other `ToggleGroup` consumers whose spaced layout is deliberate (theme toggle, calendar layout switcher, queue charts, appearance motion field, rules toolbar, log consoles) — a default change would be an unreviewed visual change across the app.

Shape: `ToggleGroup` already owns `size`/`variant` context for its items; `attached` joins them by the same mechanism — the root supplies `gap-0` + rounded/border collapsing so items square their inner corners and share one border edge, and the outer corners stay rounded. Follow the pattern already proven in `ButtonGroup.tsx` (`[&>*:not(:first-child)]:rounded-l-none [&>*:not(:first-child)]:border-l-0 [&>*:not(:last-child)]:rounded-r-none`), which is the repo's existing answer to exactly this problem and is verified by `packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/__tests__/ButtonGroup.test.tsx`.

## Explicitly out of scope

- The `Filter by slug…` input + `Search` button pairing, and the two `Manage …` buttons — same screenshot, different controls.
- Migrating `RulesToolbar` (or any other consumer) to `attached`. Note it as an obvious follow-up once the prop exists; do not change it here.
- Any change to filter behavior, URL params, or `filter-skills-by-source`.

## Verification

`ToggleGroup` lives in a source-first package with no `build` target, so validate it with `lint` / `typecheck` / `test` and use `openthrottle-developer` as the integration check. Finish with a live look at `/skills` — a jsdom test can assert the classes but cannot tell you whether the seam looks right.
summary: Give the shared ToggleGroup an opt-in attached/segmented presentation and adopt it for the All / OpenThrottle / External / Personal source filter on /skills.
title: Skills source filter as a segmented button group

author: visormatt
description:
## Symptom
Chats via the "sonnet claude-code" backend in the developer chat UI intermittently fail with the terminal error: "The response timed out after 150s with no activity." Observed 3x in a row (8/10/26, ~1:23–2:16 PM). Reproduction just after showed healthy 8s turns, so this is intermittent/latency-triggered, not a hard break.

## Root cause
Two idle timers guard every turn and they measure DIFFERENT signals:
- CLI backend idle — packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/claude/claude.ts:155 — 120s, resets on ANY stdout byte from `claude`.
- Server backstop idle — applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts:272 (withIdleTimeout) — 150s (resolveChatIdleTimeoutMs = agent idle 120s + 30s margin), resets ONLY when the backend YIELDS a mapped chunk.

The user sees the SERVER 150s message, not the CLI's own "idle timeout". That is only possible when `claude` emits stdout continuously (keeping the 120s CLI timer alive) while producing nothing the server counts as a chunk for 150s straight.

mapClaudeEvent (packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/claude/events.ts:169) maps to NULL for:
- system/hook_started + system/hook_response (plugin SessionStart hooks — warp + vercel, 4 hooks, re-run every headless turn)
- system/status
- rate_limit_event

So during (a) slow/hanging startup hooks or (b) slow first-token / rate-limited API responses, `claude` is alive and emitting these null-mapped events; the CLI 120s idle never fires but the server 150s chunk-based idle does — killing a live turn. Empirically confirmed by reproducing the scrubbed-env spawn: a captured turn contained system/hook_*, system/status, and a rate_limit_event, plus heavy cache_creation_input_tokens (~28.6k) that lengthens time-to-first-token.

## Contributing amplifier
The claude backend spawns with the host's real HOME (ALLOWED_ENV_KEYS in claude.ts:35), so every chat turn re-runs the user's enabled plugin SessionStart hooks (warp@claude-code-warp + vercel@claude-plugins-official, verified in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json) and injects a large Vercel CLAUDE.md — pure overhead on the critical path before the model answers.

## Fix direction
1. (Primary/code) Make the server idle backstop measure real backend liveness, not just mapped chunks. Either: emit a lightweight keepalive/status chunk (done:false) for currently-null system/*/rate_limit_event events so the server timer advances in lockstep with the CLI's stdout timer; OR reset withIdleTimeout on any raw stdout activity from the backend iterator. Add a regression test alongside packages/react-router-chat/src/__tests__/conversation-stream.test.ts (which asserts the 150s message) covering: null-mapped-but-alive stream must NOT trip the backstop.
2. (Mitigation/env) Server env knobs for headroom: OPENTHROTTLE_CHAT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS (e.g. 300000), OPENTHROTTLE_AGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS.
3. (Mitigation/isolation) Spawn headless `claude` with a dedicated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/HOME that does not load user plugins, so chat turns stop re-running startup hooks and injecting plugin context every turn.

## Timeout math reference
DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000, DEFAULT_CHAT_IDLE_MARGIN_MS=30000 → server backstop 150000ms. Defined in packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/cursor-agent/teardown.ts.

## Note on scope
This blind spot is shared by all spawned CLI backends (grok/codex/cursor/opencode) that route through the same withIdleTimeout — any backend whose "alive" signals map to null is vulnerable. Fix should be evaluated at the orchestrator level, not only in the claude mapper.
summary: Server-side chat idle backstop (150s) aborts claude CLI turns that are still alive because it only resets on *mapped* chunks, while null-mapped liveness events (system/hook_*, system/status, rate_limit_event) keep the CLI's own 120s stdout-based idle alive. Fix: make server idle measure real backend activity; reduce per-turn plugin-hook overhead from spawning with real HOME.
title: Chat idle backstop aborts live claude turns (150s "no activity") — idle timers measure different signals

author: visormatt
description:
On `/settings/keys`, `SettingsKeysIntroduction` currently inlines operational help under the page heading: the **One-time secret** list item, the **Rotation** list item, and the **Human JWT sessions … AUTH.md** paragraph.

Keep the remaining header on the page — `GlobalHeading` “Keys” plus the long-lived bearer-token intro (`ot_sa_<prefix>_<secret>` / `Authorization` header). Move the three help bits into a **new generated modal**. Add a trigger on that remaining header (the `GlobalHeading` children slot, same placement as `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger` on Plans/Schedule/Repositories) so the help stays reachable without crowding the page.

This is Keys-specific operational help, not the shared empty-state onboarding pitch — do **not** reuse `GlobalFeatureOnboarding`. Scaffold a dedicated modal.

## Current source

- Route (thin): `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.keys.tsx` → `SettingsKeysIntroduction`
- Copy lives inline in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/SettingsKeysIntroduction.tsx` (lines ~46–83)
- Docs link: `MCP_DEVELOPER_AUTH_DOC_HREF` in `routing/settings/utils/settings-docs-links.ts`
- Existing create-credential UI is a separate local-state `Dialog` (`SettingsKeysForm` / `createDialogOpen`) — the help modal must not share that state

## Approach

1. **Generate** the modal with `@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=modal` (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false`, `application=openthrottle-developer`, `folder=settings`). Suggested name: `SettingsKeysHelpModal`.
2. After scaffold, **align with `GlobalModal` + URL sync** (`?modal=keys-help` via `useUrlSyncedOverlay` / `GlobalModal param="modal"`), matching `DashboardDailyStatsModal` and `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal`. Do not leave the generator’s older `Modal` + hand-rolled `searchParams` as the final shape. Pick a modal key that will not collide with `onboarding` or the create-credential dialog.
3. **Copy out of the component.** Add `SETTINGS_KEYS_COPY` (or similar) to `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts`: remaining intro, one-time secret title+body, rotation title+body, JWT/sessions paragraph, AUTH.md link label, trigger label, modal title. Components import constants; specs assert against the same constants — no duplicated literals.
4. **Slim the introduction.** Header keeps title + bearer-token paragraph. Render the trigger as `GlobalHeading` children. Mount the modal from the introduction (or the route) so `?modal=keys-help` works on this page.
5. **Preserve** the AUTH.md link (`data-testid` on the docs anchor) inside the modal body.
6. **Tests:** introduction still shows heading + remaining intro; moved copy is absent until the modal is open; trigger click (or `?modal=keys-help`) shows One-time secret, Rotation, Human JWT copy, and the docs link. Use `component` + `userEvent`.
7. **Validate:** `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint` / `:test` for the touched files.

## Out of scope

- Create/revoke credential flows (`SettingsKeysForm`, table, toolbar)
- Shared `GlobalFeatureOnboarding` wiring
- Copy rewrites beyond moving existing strings into `data.copy.ts`
title: Settings → Keys: move help copy into a header-triggered modal

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

Foreign-workspace skill injection is a flag users flip often, but today it is buried: /settings/repositories -> click a repo -> Edit -> scroll to a bare Switch -> Save changes. Four navigations for a boolean.

The index query already selects `foreignSkillInjectionEnabled` on every checkout, so the state is on the client and simply is not rendered.

## Scope decisions

- The toggle is REPOSITORY-LEVEL, rendered on depth-0 parent rows only. The DB column is per-checkout, but `updateRepository` deliberately flips every one of the user's checkouts for a repository together (applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/workspace-settings/workspace-folders.service.ts:851-866). Worktree child rows show an "inherited" marker. NO SERVER CHANGES.
- The form makeover targets `RepositoryEditForm` only (not the detail card).
- Keep the Card shell and the React Router `<Form>`; this is a presentation pass, not a migration to Formik.

## Key reuse

- `SettingsAgentsAgentToggle.tsx` + `resources.agent-enabled.tsx` are the exact precedent for a fetcher-backed optimistic inline toggle.
- `UpdateRepositoryDocument` is already generated (from the edit route's .graphql), so the new resource route needs no .graphql sibling.
- The service guards each repo-level field on `!== undefined` and only calls `repositoriesService.update` when the patch is non-empty, so a flag-only mutation is explicitly supported.

## Verification

- `pnpm nx test openthrottle-developer`
- `pnpm nx typecheck openthrottle-developer && pnpm nx lint openthrottle-developer`
- `pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict && pnpm run audit:route-shape:strict`
- Manual: flip a toggle, confirm it sticks after revalidation, confirm the detail badge agrees, confirm `.agents/skills` / `.claude/skills` appear in the target checkout and `git status` there stays clean.
summary: Add an inline, repository-level Skill Injection toggle to the /settings/repositories table and give RepositoryEditForm a visual pass. Frontend-only; no server changes.

author: visormatt
description:
Port `docs/marketing/scripts/09-tags-and-rules.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

The routes are all real — `/rules` (`rules._index.tsx`), `/rules/new` (`rules.new.tsx`), `/rules/:ruleId/edit` — and so is the ledger the closing beat wants. The problem is timing: the short is built on immediate cause and effect, and the feature is eventually consistent.

## Gate 1: the cold open promises a toast that does not exist (beat 0:00)

"Plan detail; add the tag `needs-review` to the plan; **a rule fires and a toast shows**. — I added one tag. Something just happened on its own."

Rules are evaluated by `queues/plan-rules/plan-rules.processor.ts`, a BullMQ worker: one job is one full evaluation pass over a plan, loading the owner's enabled rules, running the evaluator, dispatching matched actions and reconciling the ledger. Nothing in that path pushes a toast to the browser. Adding a tag revalidates the plan; the rule's effect lands later, out of band.

This is the short's hook — the first three seconds the format spec says retention is decided in — so it cannot be quietly softened. Options:

- Re-time the beat: add the tag, hold, and let the injected task appear on the plan when the pass completes. Honest, teaches the real mental model ("something happened on its own" is *more* true if it happens without a click), and needs `waitFor` on the injected task rather than a fixed dwell.
- Open on the aftermath: start on a plan that already carries the tag and the injected task, then rewind to show why. Safest to record, weakest hook.
- Make rule application surface a live notification. Real product work, well beyond a screencast plan, and it should be its own plan if it is wanted.

## Gate 2: the rule form is not "two choices" (beat 0:25)

"Click **New rule**; pick a tag; pick an action. — Making one is two choices. The label to watch, and what to do."

`RuleForm.tsx` submits `title`, `tagAll` (multi-select, one hidden input per tag), `actionType`, **`actionPayloadJson`**, `status`, `environment`, `tagAllow` and `enabled`. `RuleFormActionSection` drives the action type; `RuleFormMatchSection` drives the tag match.

Two problems for camera. First, `actionPayloadJson` is raw JSON — typing a JSON blob on screen is the opposite of "two choices", and leaving it empty may not produce a rule that does anything visible. Second, the available action types are `inject-task` and `availability-exception` (see `summarizeRuleAction` in `app/routing/rules/utils/formatters.ts`); only `inject-task` has a visible effect on a plan, so the short is really about that one.

The narration can stay at "two choices" if the flow only touches two fields and the rest are prefilled — but that has to be verified on screen, not assumed.

## Gate 3: the rule-applications list is on the plan, not on /rules (beat 0:50)

The script's closing beat is "Hold on the rule-applications list" with no navigation in the action column, arriving from 0:42 which is on a plan. That works out, but only by accident: `ruleApplications(planId: ID!)` is plan-scoped, and `PlanRuleApplications` renders inside `PlanTabOutput.tsx` — the plan's **Output tab**. The flow needs an explicit beat to open that tab, and the script's action column should say so.

## Gate 4: the fixture has to make a rule able to fire at all

Three fixture preconditions, none currently guaranteed:

- The tag must be in the vocabulary. `PlanTagChips` offers a `<select>` of `skillTagVocabulary`, not a free-text field — you cannot type `needs-review` if it is not an option.
- The plan owner must resolve. The processor resolves the owner from `plan.author` → users row, and "a plan whose author has no user row has no rules and is skipped". The demo runs as `GITHUB_USER=atlas-ada`, so that user must exist with enabled rules attached.
- The worker evaluates with `environment=null`, so an environment-qualified rule will never match on this path. The seeded rule must be unqualified.

## What already exists and needs no work

- `/rules` renders `RulesStats`, `RulesToolbar`, `RulesTable` and a `RulesIntroduction` onboarding empty state — check which of those is on screen, since an empty-state pitch in frame changes what the beat says.
- The upsert and delete mutations are wired through the route action, so creating a rule on camera genuinely persists.
- `PlanRuleApplications` has a stable `data-testid="PlanRuleApplications"` hook.

## Constraints

- 74 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; re-timing the cold open and adding an Output-tab beat will move it. Re-validate against `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` and the `short` budget in `docs/marketing/format.json`.
- Selectors must be the same hooks the Maestro E2E flows use. The app must not grow a second parallel set of test hooks.
- No `sleep` verb exists and none should be added — `waitFor` on app state, `dwell` for narration pacing only. This flow needs that discipline more than any other, because it genuinely waits on a worker.
- The rules list and the applications ledger are both wide tables; expect `portraitStrategy: 'fit'` on those beats, as in 04.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.
summary: Port docs/marketing/scripts/09-tags-and-rules.md to a recorded flow, and settle the cold open: rules fire in a BullMQ worker, so no toast appears when a tag is added.
title: Build the 09-tags-and-rules screencast flow

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

`packages/openthrottle-showroom/src/narrate/narrate.ts` renders **one TTS request per sentence**, concatenates the clips, measures loudness once across the take, and applies that single gain to every clip. Per-sentence was chosen so a re-record of one line does not invalidate a whole take, and `narrate/render-cache.ts` later exploited it so a one-word edit only re-buys the sentences that changed.

The cost of that choice is tonal: the model never sees more than one sentence, so it has no run-on context, no paragraph-level arc, and it re-picks pitch and pace at every full stop. NARRATION.md's own bake-off measured loudness range (LRA) as the proxy for prosody — that is exactly the axis a whole-take render should move.

Fish Audio's `POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts/stream/with-timestamp` returns an SSE stream where each event carries `audio_base64`, `content`, `chunk_seq`, `chunk_audio_offset_sec`, and an `alignment` object with **word-level** `segments` (`text`, `start`, `end`, relative to chunk start) plus `audio_duration`. That is the missing piece: with word timings we no longer need one file per sentence to know where each sentence starts — we can render one take and slice it.

The premise this plan takes as given: caching is nice, but at Fish's pricing (~$15/M UTF-8 bytes; a full 24-script Season 1 pass ≈ $0.17) the savings are noise, while consistent tone across a take is the thing that actually shows up in the video.

## Settled before the work starts

These are decisions, not open questions:

- **Fish Audio is the default backend.** Done in task 0 — `narrate.ts` defaults to `fish-audio`, and NARRATION.md, `docs/marketing/pipeline.md`, `publishing.md` and `catalogue-rebuild.md` say so. Piper is the on-box path (`--backend piper`), required for any text not going into a published episode. macOS `say` stays a rehearsal backend.
- **ElevenLabs is out of scope.** `backends/elevenlabs.ts` is left exactly as it is — no `renderTake`, no comparison renders, no edits beyond a stale comment already corrected. It won the 2026-08 listen and was not adopted; Fish won on cost, pay-as-you-go billing, open-weight escape hatch, and having a word-timestamp endpoint at all.
- **The currently pinned Fish voice is the voice.** `DEFAULT_FISH_AUDIO_VOICE` in `backends/fish-audio.ts`. A swap is expected within days, so no task may hardcode or assume the id — read the constant, and let every take keep recording the voice it used.
- **Season 1 is unshipped, so Season 1 is the testing ground.** The old "frozen on Piper, repinning means re-rendering everything published" rule protected published episodes; nothing is published. It starts applying at publication. Until then the plan iterates on the real 24 scripts, and re-rendering the season is a ~$0.17 pass.

## What changes

- `TtsBackend` gains an **optional** whole-take capability alongside `render`. Backends that do not implement it (Piper, macOS `say`, ElevenLabs) keep the per-sentence path untouched.
- Fish Audio implements it against the with-timestamp endpoint.
- Word timings are mapped back onto sentence boundaries, and the take is sliced into the same `NNN-<beat>.wav` files with the same `timings.json` shape, so `assemble/timeline.ts` and `assemble/captions.ts` are unchanged.
- The loudness rule from NARRATION.md gets simpler on this path, not different: one measurement per take, one gain — the take already exists as a single file, so measure it, apply the gain, then slice.
- The render cache moves to take granularity rather than being deleted.

## What must not change

- `timings.json` shape and the per-sentence `.wav` file layout; downstream stages are not rewritten for this.
- `backends/elevenlabs.ts`.
- Captions keep using the **written** form, not the spoken (lexicon-substituted) form.
- The privacy line, now that the default path is off box: hosted backends render script text intended for publication. Season 1 narration is written to be published, so it qualifies. Drafts, experiments and anything not going into an episode render through `--backend piper`, explicitly.

## The unknown worth answering first

Fish's `chunk_length` (100–300 chars, default 300) means the service internally re-chunks long text. If prosody resets at those seams, the tonal win is smaller than the hypothesis assumes and `chunk_length` becomes a tuning knob rather than a detail. Listen at a seam on a >300-character take before building the slicing logic.
summary: Render a whole narration take in ONE Fish Audio request and derive segment timings from the returned word timestamps, instead of one request per sentence. The hypothesis is tone: a model that sees the whole script reads it as one continuous performance, where per-sentence rendering resets prosody at every full stop. Trades away the per-sentence render cache, which at ~$0.17 per season pass is an acceptable loss. Season 1 is unshipped and is the testing ground.
title: Whole-take narration with word timestamps (Fish Audio stream-with-timestamp)
