Still deferred from 82aa63e8 (do not sneak in): client RHF/shadcn binding; native zod v4 (`zod/v3` compat path); MCP tool wiring (already on generated Input schemas except the v3 nesting note in `skill-availability.ts`).

## Remaining hand-rolled GraphQL FormData (developer)

High-value clones of the tag-action pattern (generated `*InputSchema` already exists):

- `routing/projects/actions/projectId.ts` — add/remove project tag (same as plan/task tags).
- `routes/notes.create.tsx`, `routes/notes.$noteId.tsx` — `CreateNoteInput` / `UpdateNoteInput`.
- `routes/projects.$projectId.edit.tsx` — `UpdateProjectInput`.
- `routes/prompts.create.tsx`, `routing/prompts/actions/promptId.ts` — `CreateCustomPromptInput` / `UpdateCustomPromptInput` (labels CSV).
- `routing/skills/utils/skill-availability-action.ts` `readRuleInput` — `SkillAvailabilityRuleInputSchema` + `lists` (MCP already uses this schema).
- `routing/plans/actions/planId.ts` leftovers: `setPlanStatus`, `updateTaskStatus`, `saveRunConfig`, `saveJobRunHooks`, `runPlan` / enqueue (mix of omit+inject, JSON preprocess, number coerce). `DetachHookInputSchema().parse({ hookTaskId: formData.get(...) })` is still a hand get.
- Settings: `routing/settings/actions/workspace.ts` + repo edit + `keys.ts` + `settings.mcp.$connectorId.tsx` — `AddWorkspaceFolderInput`, `CloneRepositoryInput`, `UpdateWorkspaceProfileInput`, `ConnectMcpConnectorInput`, credential inputs. Today they share `optionalTrimmedString`; delete that helper when unused.
- Queues: `routing/queues/actions/queueId.ts` `CleanQueueInput` (`confirm` boolean + `state`); `queues.$queueId.$jobId.tsx` already uses `RetryJobInputSchema().parse` on constructed objects — candidate for parseFormData if those fields come from the form.
- Rules / rollout: `rules.new.tsx`, `rules.$ruleId.edit.tsx`, `UpsertTagActionRuleInput`; `settings.rollout.*` + `rollout-typed-config.ts` — `CreateRolloutFlagInput` plus JSON variation blobs.

Lower priority / keep special-cased:

- Auth login in `root.tsx` / `auth._index.tsx` — not GraphQL Input types.
- Commander / search jump in `root.tsx` — UI navigation, not mutations.
- `skills.$slug.tsx` write-to-filesystem — local FS, not GraphQL.
- `resources.agent-*` resource routes — small boolean/string toggles; adopt only if a matching Input schema exists.
- `packages/react-router-chat` conversation-stream FormData — shared package; `AgentsRunChatTurnInputSchema` is already used in `utils.agents-chat.ts` after hand reads — follow-up candidate, separate from app actions.
- File upload decompose.

## Remaining (admin)

Admin never imported `parseFormData`. Same GraphQL Input schemas are generated in `openthrottle-admin` `app/__generated__/schemas.ts`:

- `routing/users/actions/userId.ts` + `users._index.tsx` — assign/remove role, update user.
- `routing/roles/actions/roleId.ts` + `roles._index.tsx` — add/remove permission, create/update role.
- Skip login in `root.tsx`.

Email/website: no comparable mutation FormData surface found.

## Duplicate Zod to retire when touching skill availability

`packages/nestjs-repositories/.../skill-availability.schemas.ts` `skillAvailabilityRuleInputSchema` duplicates the generated GraphQL input. Server-side Nest validation is a different layer than route FormData — only unify if we explicitly want one schema; do not block UI adoption on it.

## Success criteria

- New GraphQL-backed route actions use `parseFormData` + generated `*InputSchema()` (or a tiny composed `z.object` for non-input variables). No new `formData.get` + `typeof === 'string'` + trim helpers.
- Existing `optionalTrimmedString` / `readRuleInput` / project-tag hand parsers are gone or documented as non-GraphQL exceptions.
- Tests assert blank required fields fail via the schema (same style as the #357 action specs).
- Do not change GraphQL wire shapes or action result keys unless a given task explicitly normalizes onto `ActionResult` from react-router-utils.
title: Adopt parseFormData + generated Zod across remaining actions

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm.tsx` has all the right *information* and none of the right *shape*. One entity — an editor — is fragmented across three stacked blocks that each re-enumerate the same three editors:

1. `WorkspaceEditorMultiSelect` — a combobox dropdown for a fixed set of **three** options. The user must open a popover to discover what OpenThrottle even supports.
2. `WorkspaceEditorPresenceHints` — a separate "On this machine" bullet list restating those editors with a detected/not-detected line.
3. `WorkspaceEditorAffiliateLinks` — a third block of "Don't have Cursor yet?" paragraphs, again per editor.

So "is Cursor on? is it installed? where do I get it?" requires reading three disjoint lists and mentally joining them. The fix is a join in the UI: **one row (card) per editor**, carrying its toggle, its presence badge, and its acquisition link together.

Secondary gaps worth closing in the same pass:

- `editorPresence.scannedAt` and `editorPresence.trusted` are fetched by the loader and thrown away. `trusted` is the signal that separates "we probed the host and did not find it" from "we are guessing"; it should be visible, quietly.
- The Save button is always enabled, even with zero changes, and there is no dirty indicator.
- `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_OPTIONS` carries only `{ label, value }` — no icon, no one-line description, no docs link — so every surface that renders an editor invents its own presentation.

## Invariants that must survive (non-negotiable)

- **Presence never gates.** A `NOT_FOUND` editor must still be enableable and still submit; the save button must never disable because of detection. This is the whole point of commit f27d2c55 and is asserted by an existing test.
- **`UNKNOWN` renders no claim.** A containerized server cannot see the user's filesystem; silence stays the correct output.
- **A failed presence probe is invisible.** The loader already `.catch(() => null)`s it; the redesigned form must degrade to "no badges", never to a broken layout or an error.
- The form still posts `intent=updateProfile` with `worktreeRoot`, `contactDisplayName`, `contactEmail` hidden alongside `enabledEditors[]`, because the shared action tolerates no partial payload.
- The single FTC affiliate disclosure stays exactly one, page-level — not repeated per card.

## Target shape

A responsive grid (1 col mobile / 2–3 col at `md`) of editor cards inside the existing `OpenThrottleFieldset`. Each card:

- editor mark + label ("Claude Code", "Cursor", "Visual Studio Code")
- a one-line description of what OpenThrottle writes for it
- a presence `Badge` — `Detected` (success-ish) / `Not detected` (muted) / nothing at all for `UNKNOWN` or a failed probe
- a `Switch` for enablement, with the card itself selectable (whole-card click target, selected state via ring/border, `aria-pressed` semantics or a real label-wrapped switch)
- a "Get Cursor" affiliate link inline, shown when an affiliate URL exists — most valuable precisely on a not-detected card

Below the grid: the FTC disclosure, the `scannedAt`/`trusted` footnote, the action error, and a dirty-aware Save.

## Available primitives (use these, do not hand-roll)

`packages/react-router-shadcn`: `Badge`, `Card` (+ `CardHeader`/`CardContent`/`CardFooter`), `Switch`, `Tooltip`, `Separator`, `Label`, `Button`, `Empty`, `InlineErrors`. `packages/react-router-ui`: `OpenThrottleFieldset` (keep it — it is the section chrome for the whole settings page).

## Constraints

- Generators first: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=app/routing/settings/components --name=...`. Keep the generated section comments, even empty.
- One component per file; lists/copy live in `routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts`, editor metadata in `routing/settings/config/workspace-editors.ts`.
- No `as` casts, no enums, `import type` for types, explicit return types, alphabetized props/keys.
- Tests use `component` (not `screen`) and `userEvent`.
- Component line cap is checked **after** prettier runs.

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`, `:build`, then a live visual pass at `/settings/workspace` against the built server with the seeded `developer-e1e878@atlasworks.example` user (that user has admin; a fresh user has zero perms and cannot reach the page).
summary: Rebuild SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm from a dropdown + three stacked footnote blocks into one per-editor card grid that carries selection, presence, and the affiliate CTA on the same row.
title: Editor integration settings: design + layout refresh

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

The `/settings/workspace` route in `applications/openthrottle-developer` (route module: `app/routes/settings.workspace._index.tsx`) renders five stacked sections and has two concrete problems plus knock-on layout debt:

1. **"Repositories that will be configured" is very long and not useful.** `SettingsWorkspaceEditorTargets` renders one table row per repository × enabled editor pairing (`buildWorkspaceEditorTargets` in `app/routing/settings/utils/workspace-editor-targets.ts` does a `flatMap` cartesian expansion). With N repos and M editors the table is N×M rows, each repeating the repo name and filesystem path, and each row carries its own per-repo Apply form even though the action only takes `repositoryId` (not an editor) — so the same repo shows the identical Apply button M times.
2. **The "Editor integration" section is crammed.** `SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm` stacks the `WorkspaceEditorMultiSelect`, `WorkspaceEditorPresenceHints`, and `WorkspaceEditorAffiliateLinks` in one tight `space-y-2` block inside a single Label group — three distinct concerns (selection, detection hints, referral CTAs + FTC disclosure) visually mashed together.
3. The other sections (`SettingsWorkspaceApplyEditors`, `SettingsWorkspaceApplyResults`, `SettingsWorkspaceWorktreeRootForm`, `SettingsWorkspaceProfileForm`, `SettingsWorkspaceIntro`) should adapt as needed so the page reads as one coherent refresh.

## Hard constraints

- **NO server-side changes.** Do not touch `openthrottle-server`, the GraphQL schema, resolvers, or migrations. The loader keeps using `GetWorkspaceSettingsDocument` + `GetEditorPresenceDocument` exactly as-is (including the presence-failure-swallowing split), and the action keeps the exact same intents and payload shapes: `updateProfile` (always full payload: worktreeRoot + contact fields + enabledEditors) and `applyEditorConfig` (optional `repositoryId`). The full-payload hidden-input pattern across the three forms is a deliberate invariant — preserve it.
- Client-side files only, under `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/**` and the route module. `app/routing/settings/actions/workspace.ts` and the utils' action-facing behavior stay put (reshaping `buildWorkspaceEditorTargets`' output type for display is fine; it is UI-only and `@public`-tagged for Knip, keep tags coherent).
- Use `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` components; use `@tools/generators` (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component ...`) before hand-writing any NEW component. Keep the generated section comments in edited components.
- Copy lives in `app/routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts` (`WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_COPY`) — no inline strings.
- Load the `frontend-design` skill for the visual pass; keep both light/dark themes working.

## Direction (agent has latitude within this)

- **Targets:** group by repository — one row/card per repo showing display name, path, and the enabled editors as compact badges, with ONE per-repo Apply button (submitting `repositoryId` exactly as today). Consider collapsing beyond ~5–8 repos (scroll area or show-all toggle) so the section stays skimmable. Keep both empty states (no repos → link to /settings/repositories; no editors → hint) and the row-level busy state keyed off `navigation.formData`.
- **Editor integration:** keep the fieldset, but separate selection / presence hints / affiliate links into visually distinct sub-blocks (e.g. hints inline next to options or as a compact row of badges; affiliate links + FTC disclosure demoted to a quiet footer). Presence hints stay strictly advisory and display-only, UNKNOWN still renders nothing.
- **Rest of page:** tune section rhythm (the flat `space-y-8` stack), make Apply-all + its disabled reason and results feel attached to the targets section they act on, and keep worktree root + contact forms visually consistent with whatever fieldset treatment the refresh lands on.

## Validation

Per developer-app gates: `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`, `:build` (sequentially, not parallel). Update the route test (`app/routes/__tests__/settings.workspace._index.test.tsx`) and any component tests; use `component`-scoped queries and `userEvent`. Finish with a headless visual verification (seeded developer-e1e878@atlasworks.example against a built server) and screenshots in light + dark.
summary: UI-only refresh of the /settings/workspace route in openthrottle-developer: replace the long repositories × editors cartesian table with a grouped-by-repository view, give the crammed Editor integration section breathing room, and adapt the remaining sections (apply/results, worktree root, contact) to the refreshed layout. Zero server-side changes.
title: Refresh /settings/workspace UI: group editor targets, decompress Editor integration

author: visormatt
description:
Port `docs/marketing/scripts/10-notes.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

**This plan opens BLOCKED.** The notes half of the short is recordable today. The search half — which is the entire payoff and the whole reason the short exists — is not.

## Gate 1: notes are not in the semantic index (beats 0:32, 0:41, 0:50)

The short's promise is "search for the symptom, months later" → "There it is. And your agents query the same index before they start work."

`search._index.tsx.graphql` runs `search(input:)` and reads back `chunks` whose fields are `planId`, `planTitle`, `taskId`, `taskTitle`, `source`, `sourcePath`, `sourceRepo`, `sourceSha`. There is no `noteId`. The schema's own `getDocument` description enumerates the backing tables: *"UUID from plan_embeddings, task_embeddings, or documentation_embeddings"*. The migrations in `databases/migrations/` create `plan_embeddings` (004), `task_embeddings` (005), `documentation_embeddings` (020), `code_embeddings` (052) and `custom_prompt_embeddings` (037). **There is no note_embeddings table**, and `scripts/seed-demo.ts` truncates `task_embeddings, plan_embeddings` without ever writing a note embedding.

So the note will not come back from `/search`, and the closing claim that agents query the same index for notes is not true today. Recording it would put a false product claim on camera — the thing the publish checklist exists to prevent.

Two ways forward, and the first is real product work that deserves its own plan rather than being smuggled into a screencast:

- Index notes. A `note_embeddings` table, ingestion on note create/update, a `note` source in the search resolver and a note branch in the results UI. This is the feature the short is selling; if the channel wants this short, the product needs this.
- Re-cut the short around what notes actually do today — captured, listed, readable, linkable — and drop the search payoff. That is a materially weaker video and the title ("capture context your agents can actually find") stops being accurate, so it likely wants a new script rather than an edit.

## Gate 2: notes have no title (beats 0:08 and 0:18)

The script separates "type a title" from "type two sentences of body text". `NoteForm.tsx` renders a single `Label htmlFor="content"` over one `content` field; `notes.create.tsx` submits `{ input: { content: parsed.data.content } }`; and `CreateNoteInput` in `notes.create.tsx.graphql` is `{ content: String!, author: String }`. There is no title anywhere. `NotesTable` derives its row label from the content itself via `notePreviewLabel`.

Two beats collapse into one, and eight seconds of the script's runtime have nothing to show.

## What already exists and needs no work

- `/notes` (`NotesTable`, `NoteCard`), `/notes/create` (`NoteForm`) and `/notes/:noteId` all render, and `NoteCard` renders Markdown so a note with structure reads well in frame.
- `scripts/seed-demo.ts` already inserts `DEMO_NOTES` — four fictional notes whose voice fits "something you learned": "429 vs 503", "Antimeridian", "Tile cache invalidation", "Deploys and the tile cache". The 04 plan already vetted these on camera and found "429 vs 503" the strongest.
- `/search` renders and is exercisable; it is the *contents* of the index that are wrong for this short, not the route.

## Constraints

- 68 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; collapsing the title beat and re-cutting the payoff will move it substantially. Re-validate against `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` and the `short` budget in `docs/marketing/format.json`.
- The script's frontmatter says `blockedOn: []`, which is wrong and is a deliverable of this plan.
- Notes render free-form user content, which per the 04 plan's scan task is one of the pipeline's higher-risk leak surfaces. Only ever record the fictional seeded notes.
- A flow may not invent a step the script does not describe, and a script may not describe UI that does not exist.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.
summary: Port docs/marketing/scripts/10-notes.md to a recorded flow. Blocked: notes have no title field and are not in the semantic index, so the short's search payoff cannot happen.
title: Build the 10-notes screencast flow

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Let OT Agents run against **OpenRouter** — one API key, hundreds of models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, Qwen, …) behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`.

Today OT's model surface is **local-only**: `discoverModels` port-scans `localhost` for OpenAI-compatible servers (`ModelProvider = 'lmstudio' | 'ollama'`), and the only non-CLI chat path (`openAiConversationBackend` → `streamChatCompletion`) hardcodes `apiKey: process.env.LLM_API_KEY ?? 'not-needed'` with no per-provider auth, no attribution headers, and no remote catalog. Nothing in the repo mentions OpenRouter (`grep -ri openrouter` → 0 hits).

## Why this shape

OpenRouter is **not an agent CLI** — it is a gateway. So it does NOT get a `defineDriver` module. It lands at three existing seams:

1. **Remote model catalog** — a sibling to `utils/model-discovery/` that reads `GET /api/v1/models` instead of probing ports. The existing local types are deliberately local (`ModelEndpoint` carries `host`/`port`), so remote providers get their own type + GraphQL query rather than a widened `ModelProvider` union.
2. **Chat backend** — OpenRouter speaks the OpenAI wire protocol, so `streamChatCompletion` already covers it *once it can carry a per-request API key and headers*. That is the one real code change on the completion path.
3. **Agent-CLI drivers** — `DriverEndpointConfig` + `capabilities.supportsCustomBaseUrl` already exist for pointing `codex` and `opencode` at a non-default OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Extending that from "discovered local endpoint" to "authenticated remote provider" is additive. `claude` and `cursor` speak proprietary wire protocols (`supportsCustomBaseUrl: false`) and are **out of scope** — do not fake it.

## Non-goals (v1)

- No per-user API keys — v1 is an operator-level `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` on the server env. Per-user/BYO-key credential storage is a follow-up plan.
- No new driver id, no `ALL_DRIVERS` entry.
- No OpenRouter-specific routing features (provider preferences, `:floor`/`:nitro` variants, fallback arrays) beyond passing a model slug through.

## Constraints

- The API key is **server-side only**. It must never reach a browser bundle, a GraphQL response, or a loader payload.
- Every CLI flag or env var claimed in task 8 must be verified against that CLI's own `--help` / config docs at implementation time — never from memory (`packages/openthrottle-drivers/AGENTS.md`).
- Unconfigured must degrade cleanly: with no key set, OpenRouter simply does not appear in the picker; nothing throws, nothing blocks the composer.
- GraphQL is code-first — after resolver changes, boot the server, then `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel` and commit `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` plus all `__generated__` output.

## Key files

- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/model-discovery/` — local discovery core (sibling for remote)
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/types/model-discovery.ts` — `ModelEndpoint`, `DiscoveryResult`
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/chat-completions/stream.ts` — hardcoded `LLM_API_KEY`
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/openai.ts`, `registry.ts`
- `packages/nestjs-model-discovery/` — SWR-cached Nest wrapper + config namespace
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts` (`DriverEndpointConfig`), `src/drivers/{codex,opencode}.ts`
- `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/config/chat-capabilities.ts`, `src/utils/chat-discovery-options.ts`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/models.server.ts`

## Reference

- https://openrouter.ai/docs/quickstart — base `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions`, `GET /api/v1/models`, optional `HTTP-Referer` / `X-Title` attribution headers, slug ids like `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`.

## Related

- a55b76ba (token-usage surfacing) — task 9 feeds it
- 7393edc6 (model-discovery SWR caching) — task 5 reuses that cache
- 9a995913 (chat model picker rail) — task 7 extends that UI
- cf9b36a1 / ce1e1e94 (driver + local-endpoint discovery) — the seams task 8 widens
summary: Add OpenRouter (openrouter.ai) as a first-class remote model provider: a remote model catalog alongside local discovery, an authenticated OpenAI-compatible chat backend, and (where each CLI actually supports it) OpenRouter-backed agent-CLI driver runs.
title: OpenRouter as a model provider for OT Agents

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

After nuking the repo, Docker images, and volumes and re-running `./scripts/setup.sh` on a second machine, the generated `.demo-workstation.local` was missing `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`. The file must ALWAYS contain all six fields:

- `OPENTHROTTLE_ADMIN_URL`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_BOOTSTRAP_USER_EMAIL`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_BOOTSTRAP_USER_PASSWORD`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_URL`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN`

## Root cause

The six fields come from two bootstrap scripts writing the same git-ignored file via `scripts/local-secrets-file.ts` `upsertLocalSecrets`:

- `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts` writes the 4 non-token fields **unconditionally** (lines 128-133) — these always appear.
- `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts` writes the 2 token fields **only in the mint-and-print branch** (`mintBootstrapCredential`, `upsertLocalSecrets` at line 148). It does NOT write the file in the other two `provisionAccount` branches:
  - **Skip branch** (`mintBootstrapCredential`, `activeCount > 0`, lines 119-129): service account already has an active credential -> returns `skipped`, no file write. Because only a bcrypt hash is stored, the plaintext token cannot be re-derived, so the file legitimately cannot be repopulated with the existing value.
  - **Env-provided branch** (`upsertBootstrapCredentialFromEnv`): when `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` / `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN` is already set in the environment, the credential is upserted from that env value but the file is never written.

The observed asymmetry (worker token present, MCP token absent) means on the affected box the `openthrottle-mcp` service account already had an active credential when setup ran (Postgres named volume survived a `docker compose down` without `-v`, OR `database:bootstrap-service-accounts` ran twice — e.g. once during an earlier `server:dev` boot and once from `setup.sh`, OR `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` was set in `.env` from the Cursor MCP config), so it hit a non-mint path while `workflow-ralph` was freshly minted.

## Goal

Make bootstrap self-healing so `.demo-workstation.local` ends up with all six keys after `./scripts/setup.sh`, regardless of which `provisionAccount` branch each account takes — plus a loud final invariant that fails setup if any field is missing, and a documented recovery path for the box that is broken right now.

## Design decisions to lock before implementing

1. **Skip branch recovery.** When the env var is unset AND the target key is absent from `.demo-workstation.local` but an active credential already exists, the old plaintext is unrecoverable. Preferred fix: treat this as "need a usable token" and self-heal by rotating (revoke existing active credential(s) + mint a fresh one), then write the new value to the file. This is safe for local bootstrap accounts. Confirm rotate-vs-warn with the owner before implementing.
2. **Env-provided branch.** When the token comes from the environment, that plaintext IS known, so write it into the file so the durable copy stays complete.
3. **Final invariant.** Add a verification step (either at the tail of the service-account script or a small standalone check wired into `setup.sh`) that asserts all six keys are present and non-empty, failing loudly with remediation guidance otherwise.

## References

- `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts`
- `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts`
- `scripts/local-secrets-file.ts`
- `scripts/setup.sh` (steps 4 and 4b)
- `scripts/verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh`, `AUTH.md` runbook (from the stale-in-session OT MCP plan)
title: Guarantee all six .demo-workstation.local fields on every setup

author: visormatt
description:
## Symptom

In a chat thread every tool card and every folded tool group renders `name` as its header (see the group header "name · 10 actions" with ten child rows all titled "name"). Expanding a row shows the truth: the arguments payload is `{"name": "view_file", "parameters": {…}}` — the real tool is `view_file`. The header is repetitive and carries zero information.

## Root cause

`packages/react-router-chat/src/turn-events.ts` derives the tool name by key-sniffing:

```ts
const extractToolName = (toolCall: unknown): string => {
  if (!isRecord(toolCall)) return 'tool';
  const name = Object.keys(toolCall).find(
    (key) => key !== 'toolCallId' && key !== 'hookAdditionalContexts',
  );
  return name === undefined ? 'tool' : name.replace(/ToolCall$/, '');
};
```

That heuristic was written for the cursor-agent shape (`{ toolCallId, readToolCall: {…} }`, where the first non-reserved key IS the tool). Every other driver in `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/*/events.ts` emits a different shape, and the heuristic misreads all of them:

| driver | metadata shape | header today | should be |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cursor-agent | `toolCall: { toolCallId, readToolCall: {…} }` | `read` ✅ | `read` |
| gemini | `toolCall: { name, parameters }` | **`name`** | `view_file` |
| antigravity | `toolCall: { name, parameters }` / result `{ error, name, output, status }` | **`name`** | `view_file` |
| claude | `metadata.name` (no `toolCall` key at all) | **`tool`** | `Read` |
| opencode | `metadata.tool` + `metadata.toolPart` | **`tool`** | the part's tool |

So four of five backends render a useless header; only cursor-agent is accidentally correct. Same defect hits `toolLabelFromMetadataJson`, used for the one-line activity marker, and it flows through both the live stream (`turn-events.ts`) and the persisted path (`map-persisted-messages.ts`) since both go through `parseChunkMetadata`.

Secondary: the antigravity/gemini call payload is double-wrapped — `toolCall: { name, parameters: payload.tool_info }` where `tool_info` is itself `{ name, parameters }` — which is why the expanded Arguments block shows `name`/`parameters` twice.

## Direction

1. Drivers emit a canonical, explicit `metadata.toolName` (string) at the chunk boundary — the client should never have to guess.
2. The client prefers explicit fields (`toolName`, then `name`/`tool`) and keeps the key-sniff only as a legacy fallback for already-persisted cursor-agent conversations. Old rows must keep rendering correctly.
3. Rendering stays as-is otherwise: mono, truncating, `event.name` in `ChatToolCall` and `activeToolOf(...).name` in `ChatToolCallGroup`.

## Files

- `packages/react-router-chat/src/turn-events.ts` (`extractToolName`, `normalizeMetadata`, `toolLabelFromMetadataJson`)
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatToolCall.tsx`, `ChatToolCallGroup.tsx` (display only)
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/{claude,cursor-agent,gemini,antigravity,opencode}/events.ts`
- Tests: `packages/react-router-chat/src/__tests__/turn-events.test.ts`, `map-persisted-messages.test.ts`, and the per-driver event tests

## Done when

A thread run against each driver shows real tool names (`view_file`, `Read`, `edit`, …) on both the group header and every child card, with no `name`/`tool` placeholders for any driver that reports one, and persisted (reloaded) conversations render identically to live ones.
summary: Tool-call headers in chat threads render the literal string "name" (or the generic "tool") because the client sniffs the first key of the toolCall payload instead of reading the tool name. Make each driver emit a canonical toolName and make the client prefer it.
title: Chat tool cards: show the real tool name, not "name"

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

On the openthrottle-developer dashboard index (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/dashboard._index.tsx`), add a new card that lists the **3 most-recent agent conversations** ("chats") with per-chat hotlinks and a small footer of quick links to other useful spots.

## Context (verified in repo)

- The dashboard is a streamed grid: the loader returns two naked promises (`core`, `githubStats`) and each card renders inside `React.Suspense` + `Await`. New cards follow the same pattern.
- Conversations already have a server helper: `callListAgentConversations(request, { limit, offset, status })` in `app/global/utils/utils.agents-chat.ts`, backed by `ListAgentConversationsDocument` (already codegen'd — no new GraphQL needed).
- List-item shape `AgentConversationListItem` (from `@openthrottle/react-router-chat`): `{ id, status, title | null, updatedAt }`. Titles can be null → need a fallback label ("Untitled chat").
- The chat surface is the home route `/` (`app/routes/_index.tsx`). Opening a specific conversation is **client-only today** via `turn.restore({ conversationId })` — there is NO URL param to deep-link a chat. The `useConversationList` sidebar hook posts to `/resources/agent-conversations`.
- Existing "useful spots" links live in `WORKSPACE_FULL_JUMP_LINKS` (`~/routing/navigation/data/workspace-jump-links`), used by the (currently deprecated) `DashboardQuickNavigation`.

## Design decisions

1. **Data**: fetch the 3 most-recent conversations server-side in the dashboard loader via `callListAgentConversations(request, { limit: 3 })`, exposed as its own deferred promise (own `Await` boundary so it never blocks the activity chart, mirroring `githubStats`). Degrade gracefully via `errorElement` and an empty-state.
2. **Per-chat hotlink**: add a `?conversationId=<id>` deep-link so the card can link into a specific chat. Home `_index.tsx` reads the param on mount and calls `turn.restore({ conversationId })`. Card links to `/?conversationId=<id>`.
3. **Footer quick links**: "View all chats" (`/`), "New chat" (`/`), plus 2–3 curated useful spots reused from `WORKSPACE_FULL_JUMP_LINKS` (e.g. Plans, Queues, Pull Requests) — no bespoke link list.

## Conventions

- Generator-first: scaffold the component with `@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component` (keep section comments, one component/file, props interface, copy in nearest `data/data.copy.ts`).
- shadcn primitives from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; `Link` from `react-router`.
- Render-level Vitest tests (`component` not `screen`, `userEvent`). Show relative time for `updatedAt`.
- No codegen expected (reusing `ListAgentConversationsDocument`); if any GraphQL doc changes, run the codegen flow and commit `__generated__`.

## Out of scope

- Real-time updates of the card, pagination, rename/delete from the card.
summary: Add a DashboardRecentChatsCard to the openthrottle-developer dashboard index that lists the 3 most-recent agent conversations and hotlinks to each chat plus a few useful destinations.
title: Dashboard: Recent Chats card (3 most-recent conversations + hotlinks)

author: visormatt
description:
## What

With `recharts@3.10.1`, the data shapes in `SimpleBarChart` and `SimplePieChart` do not render:

- **Bar**: Recharts emits one `.recharts-bar-rectangle` group per datum, each containing an empty `.recharts-inactive-bar` group and **no** `rect`/`path`.
- **Pie**: `.recharts-pie` contains an empty layer and zero `path` elements.

Everything around them works — the SVG surface sizes correctly (512x256), axes render with the right scale and tick labels, grid, legend and tooltip are all fine. So the charts look plausible while the data is invisible.

`SimpleLineChart` and `SimpleAreaChart` are **unaffected** (1 curve path and 2 area paths respectively).

## Why it went unnoticed

jsdom cannot exercise Recharts geometry — the ResizeObserver no-op means no measurement, so no shapes. The package's 225-file / 472-test Vitest suite passes green. This was only visible once the components rendered in a real browser, via `applications/openthrottle-workbench` (plan c84d753c, task 56d7df54).

## Reproduce

```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-workbench:dev
```

Open `Components/SimpleBarChart → Default` and `Components/SimplePieChart → Default`, then inspect:

```js
document.querySelectorAll('.recharts-bar-rectangle path, .recharts-bar-rectangle rect').length; // 0
document.querySelector('.recharts-pie').outerHTML; // empty layer
```

The affected stories carry a `⚠️ KNOWN ISSUE` block pointing here.

## Not yet established

Root cause is open. Candidates worth checking in order:

1. **Version regression.** The catalog pins `recharts: ^3.6.0` and resolution landed on 3.10.1. Try pinning 3.6.x and see whether the shapes return — that would isolate it to a Recharts change.
2. **Component misuse.** Both failing components pass a `fill`/shape through in a way Line and Area do not. `SimpleBarChart` passes `fill={`var(--color-${valueKey})`}` and a `radius` tuple; check these against the Recharts 3.10 API.
3. **React 19 interaction.** The workspace is on React 19.2.4; confirm Recharts 3.10.1 supports it fully.

## Done when

- Bars and pie sectors render in the workbench for the existing stories, with no story changes required.
- The fix is verified in the browser (not only by unit tests, which cannot see this).
- Whatever regression guard is practical is added — note that a jsdom assertion cannot cover it, so this may mean pinning a version with a comment rather than a test.
- The `⚠️ KNOWN ISSUE` blocks are removed from `SimpleBarChart.stories.tsx` and `SimplePieChart.stories.tsx`.

## Related

Also documented while building the stories, and NOT a bug: `ChartContainer` wraps Recharts' `ResponsiveContainer`, which sets `width`/`height: 100%` **inline** — so sizing it with a `className` is silently ignored and it measures to zero. It needs a sized parent. This is already noted on the `Chart` stories.
summary: RESOLVED — NOT A BUG. Root cause is requestAnimationFrame starvation in the hidden browser tab used to inspect the workbench, not recharts and not the components. Recharts animates chart geometry from t=0 via rAF; browsers never fire rAF when document.visibilityState is 'hidden', so Rectangle/Sector stay zero-sized and return null. SimpleBarChart and SimplePieChart render correctly unmodified once rAF runs (verified by screenshot under an rAF shim). The report's claim that Line/Area were unaffected was also wrong — they are equally starved, they just emit paths that draw zero length (stroke-dasharray "0px N px"), so counting DOM nodes reported them healthy. No code fix made; disabling animation or pinning recharts would have degraded working code. Shipped: the misleading KNOWN ISSUE blocks removed, and the rAF/hidden-tab trap documented in applications/openthrottle-workbench/AGENTS.md.
title: Recharts 3.10.1: Bar and Pie shapes do not render

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

While designing plan d3a30314 (layer OT curated skills into foreign workspaces), a fact-finding pass found that skill-sync's docs and some code describe an OUTDATED world:

- `skills/skill-sync/README.md:20` and `skills/skill-sync/SKILL.md` frame Cursor as *drift* (`.cursor/skills` = something to catch) and imply Grok/others have no skill concept.
- Current reality (verified Aug 2026): **Cursor 2.4+** reads Agent Skills (SKILL.md) from `.cursor/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, and global `~/.claude/skills` / `~/.codex/skills`. **Grok Build CLI** reads SKILL.md from `.grok/skills` / `~/.grok/skills`, plus `.claude/` and the AGENTS.md family. **Codex** reads `.codex/skills` + `.agents/skills`. So `.agents/skills` + `.claude/skills` are near-universal in-repo targets.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/agents/data/discover-repo-skills.server.ts` `LAYOUT_SCAN_TARGETS` only enumerates `agents` / `claude` / `opencode` layouts (with `repo-skills-registry.ts`'s `SkillRegistryLayout`), so the Developer app's skill-layout scan under-reports what tools actually read.

## Goal

Make the docs and the code-encoded layout registry a faithful, current picture of per-CLI skill discovery, so downstream design (d3a30314) and the Developer UI aren't reasoning from stale claims.

## Scope

1. AUDIT current per-CLI skill discovery (all five: claude/codex/opencode/cursor/grok) against primary sources and the repo, and produce the exact list of stale assertions + intended edits before touching anything.
2. Fix skill-sync docs (README.md, SKILL.md) — the consumer list, the Cursor-drift framing, and the per-tool dir table — to reflect current discovery and the `.agents/skills` + `.claude/skills` near-universal targets (and note per-tool global dirs).
3. Update the code-encoded layout registry (`LAYOUT_SCAN_TARGETS` / `SkillRegistryLayout`) to include the layouts tools now read (cursor/codex/grok where applicable), with tests; adjust the CI SSOT gate (`scripts/check-agent-assets-ssot.sh`) only if the added layouts require it.
4. Sweep for other stale references and reconcile; run check:local for affected projects.

## Non-goals

- The foreign-workspace injection feature itself (that is d3a30314). This plan only corrects the description of current state.
- Changing skill-sync's fan-out targets/behavior beyond what a faithful current-state description requires.
summary: Reconcile skill-sync docs and the code-encoded skill-layout registry with current CLI reality: Cursor 2.4+ and Grok Build CLI now read the SKILL.md standard (and several CLIs read `.agents/skills` / `.claude/skills` in-repo plus per-tool global dirs). Fix the stale 'Cursor = drift / Grok = no skills' framing and the incomplete LAYOUT_SCAN_TARGETS so docs and the Developer app's skill-layout scan match how tools actually discover skills. Discovered while designing plan d3a30314 (foreign-workspace skill injection).
title: Correct stale skill-discovery docs & layout state (Cursor/Grok/Codex now read SKILL.md)

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

BullMQ 5.81 narrowed `Queue.client` to its internal `IRedisClient` interface (only the Redis commands BullMQ itself uses). Two server sites reach *past* the queue onto that shared connection for raw Redis commands BullMQ no longer types:

- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/health/health.service.ts` — `client.ping()` for the Redis health check.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/plans/plan-cancel-channel.service.ts` — `publish()` / `psubscribe()` / `duplicate()` + `pmessage` for the plan-cancel pub/sub fast path (Channel 2 of OT plan 2ab62876).

**Short-term fix already shipped:** a widening helper `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/bullmq-redis-client.ts` (`getQueueRedisClient` / `duplicateQueueRedisClient` + `QueueRedisClient` type) re-widens the narrowed client to the raw commands via two documented `eslint-disable consistent-type-assertions` casts. This restores `openthrottle-server:typecheck`/`lint`/`test` to green but leaves the control-plane pub/sub + health ping coupled to BullMQ's connection and dependent on an untyped escape hatch.

## Goal (long-term / option 3)

Stop borrowing BullMQ's queue connection for control-plane work. Use a dedicated, properly-typed Redis client (ioredis) for:
1. The Redis health-check ping.
2. The plan-cancel pub/sub channel (publisher + duplicated subscriber connection).

Then delete `bullmq-redis-client.ts` and both `consistent-type-assertions` disables.

## Constraints / notes

- `@openthrottle/nestjs-redis` today is Keyv/`@keyv/redis`-based (for the Apollo cache) — it does NOT expose a raw ioredis client. Either extend it to provide a shared injectable ioredis client, or introduce one. Prefer extending `nestjs-redis` so connection config (host/port/tls/auth via `redisConfig()`) stays in one place.
- ioredis is currently only a transitive dep (via bullmq); adding a direct ioredis client means declaring it as a direct dependency where used.
- Reuse the existing `redisConfig()` from `packages/nestjs-redis/src/config/nestjs-redis.config.ts` for connection settings; keep TLS/auth parity with the cache client.
- Preserve current runtime semantics: health ping stays best-effort (`unconfigured` when `REDIS_HOST` unset); plan-cancel stays best-effort with the durable `plan_runs.cancel_requested_at` marker as the guaranteed fallback (see the doc comment in `plan-cancel-channel.service.ts`).
- Wire graceful shutdown for any new long-lived connections (mirror `disconnectRedisCaches` / the subscriber `quit()` on `onApplicationShutdown`).
- Keep `plan-cancel-channel.service.test.ts` green (currently mocks `plansQueue.client`); update mocks to the new injected client.

## Definition of done

- Health ping and plan-cancel pub/sub use a dedicated typed Redis client, not `plansQueue.client`.
- `bullmq-redis-client.ts` and both eslint-disable casts are removed.
- `openthrottle-server:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test` all green; graceful shutdown covered.
title: Decouple control-plane Redis from the BullMQ queue connection

author: visormatt
description:
# Promote HeroDotMesh + HeroSoundArcs → react-router-ui-global

## Why
`HeroDotMesh` and `HeroSoundArcs` are two polished, dependency-light canvas backdrops living privately inside `applications/openthrottle-website`. We want them reusable across apps, so promote them into `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global` (the home of `GradientMesh`, the existing precedent for a promoted decorative background) as **`GlobalAnimationMesh`** and **`GlobalAnimationWaves`**. While moving them, expose the currently-locked tunables as typed props so consumers can iterate on the look without editing package internals.

## Current shape (source of truth)
- Components: `applications/openthrottle-website/app/routing/home/demo/HeroDotMesh.tsx`, `HeroSoundArcs.tsx` — thin `aria-hidden` `<canvas>` wrappers that delegate to a hook. Only `enabled` (+ `n`/`distributionStart`/`distributionEnd` for the arcs) are exposed today.
- Hooks: `app/routing/home/demo/useDotGridMesh.ts`, `useSoundArcs.ts` — all DOM/canvas work; SSR-safe; honor `prefers-reduced-motion`; pause via IntersectionObserver; pointer-reactive. They read tunables directly from `LANDING_DOT_MESH` / `LANDING_SOUND_ARCS`.
- Util: `app/routing/home/demo/build-sound-arcs.ts` (+ test) — pure geometry builder for the arc stack.
- Data/tunables: `LANDING_DOT_MESH` and `LANDING_SOUND_ARCS` (+ the `SOUND_ARC_STACK` sub-object) in `app/routing/home/demo/data.landing.ts`.
- CSS: `.landing-dot-mesh` mask-image gradient in `app/styles.css` (lines ~88-95) — fades the lattice toward the hero's lower edge.
- Consumers: `LandingHero.tsx` (`<HeroDotMesh />`), `download.tsx` (`<HeroDotMesh />`), `LandingClose.tsx` (`<HeroSoundArcs distributionEnd={-1} distributionStart={1} n={21} />`).
- Tests: `__tests__/HeroDotMesh.test.tsx`, `__tests__/HeroSoundArcs.test.tsx`, `utils/__tests__/build-sound-arcs.test.ts`.

## Target
- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalAnimationMesh.tsx` + `GlobalAnimationWaves.tsx`, exported from `src/index.ts`.
- Package-local hooks `useGlobalAnimationMesh` / `useGlobalAnimationWaves` + `utils/build-sound-arcs.ts` (internal — not part of the public `index.ts` unless there's a reason to expose them).
- Package-local default-config constants (the package must NOT import website data), mirroring the `GradientMesh` pattern where `DEFAULT_COLORS` etc. live beside the component.
- Website consumes both from `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global`; the old files and now-unused `LANDING_DOT_MESH` / `LANDING_SOUND_ARCS` / `.landing-dot-mesh` CSS are deleted.

## Key design decisions
1. **Props surface (the "expose valuable options" ask).** Follow `GradientMesh`: each component takes `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`-style passthrough plus every tunable as an optional prop with a sensible package default.
   - `GlobalAnimationMesh`: `enabled`, `className`, `color`, `spacing`, `dotRadius`, `dotAlpha`, `dotGlow`, `lineAlpha`, `lineGlow`, `idleAmplitude`, `repelForce`, `repelRadius`, `maxDisplace`, `spring`, `damping`, plus an optional `mask`/`maskImage` control for the lower-edge fade.
   - `GlobalAnimationWaves`: `enabled`, `className`, `n`, `distributionStart`, `distributionEnd`, `noise`, `seed`, `colorStart`/`colorMid`/`colorEnd`, `gain`, `idleAmplitude`, `lineWidth`, `attack`, `release`, `speed`, `speedGain`, `velocityRef`, `waveCycles`, `samples`.
   - Refactor the hooks to accept a single fully-typed config object and default each field internally (so passing nothing reproduces today's look exactly). Preserve the effect dependency arrays so prop changes re-init the canvas.
2. **CSS mask.** The `.landing-dot-mesh` mask-image belongs with the component now, not in website CSS. Make it a default inline style on `GlobalAnimationMesh` (overridable via prop) so the component is self-contained.
3. **No new external deps.** The package already carries `@paper-design/shaders-react` (GradientMesh) and `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; the canvas hooks are pure DOM. The website does NOT currently depend on `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global` — that workspace dep must be added (use the link-workspace-packages flow, not a hand-edit).
4. **Naming.** `HeroDotMesh`→`GlobalAnimationMesh`, `HeroSoundArcs`→`GlobalAnimationWaves`, `useDotGridMesh`→`useGlobalAnimationMesh`, `useSoundArcs`→`useGlobalAnimationWaves`; keep `buildSoundArcs`/`build-sound-arcs`. Update `data-testid`s to the new names and the tests that assert them.

## Validation
No GraphQL change → no codegen. Gate with `pnpm nx run react-router-ui-global:lint,typecheck,test` and, as the integration check for source-first packages, `pnpm nx run openthrottle-website:typecheck,lint,test,build`. Verify the landing hero + `/download` + the self-host close section still render the animations (browser preview).

## Constraints
- Follow OpenThrottle component conventions: one component per file, keep the `// Hooks / Setup / Handlers / Markup / Life Cycle / 🔌 Short Circuit` section comments, components export only the component + props interface, `@public` JSDoc on the exported components so Knip keeps them.
- `as const` objects (no enums), no `as` casts / `any`, explicit return types, `import type` for type-only imports, alphabetized props.
summary: Move the landing hero's two canvas animations out of openthrottle-website into the shared @openthrottle/react-router-ui-global package, renamed GlobalAnimationMesh (dot lattice) and GlobalAnimationWaves (sound arcs). Move their hooks, the build-sound-arcs util, and the tunable constants along with them. While relocating, promote the currently-hardcoded tunables to typed component props (following the GradientMesh precedent) so the animations can be iterated on per-consumer. Rewire the website to consume from the package and delete the originals.
title: Promote HeroDotMesh + HeroSoundArcs to react-router-ui-global as GlobalAnimationMesh / GlobalAnimationWaves

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

OpenThrottle needs a distribution surface. The product is visual (a dashboard, plans, live agent runs) and the story is fast ("0 to 60"), so short screencasts are the right medium. The constraint is explicit: **this will not scale on human effort, and there is no on-camera presenter.** So the format must be faceless screencasts, and the production must be automatable — ideally a target you can run.

## The core idea: demos as code

We already have a Maestro Web E2E harness for `openthrottle-developer` at `applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/e2e/` (config.yaml, `helpers/login.yaml`, flows under `flows/`, an idempotent `scripts/seed-user.sh`, and a documented set of Maestro Web selector gotchas in its README). A demo video is structurally the same artifact as an E2E flow: a deterministic, seeded, scripted click-path through the real app.

So: **one flow definition per video**, and the pipeline is

```
seed deterministic demo data
  → drive the app (scripted flow)
  → capture video (1920x1080@60 or 1080x1920 for Shorts)
  → TTS narration from a committed script
  → ffmpeg: mux + bumper + captions + music bed
  → upload-ready mp4 + title/description/tags
```

### Honest assessment of "can these just be Maestro flows?"

**Partly — Maestro is the right driver, but it is not a recorder.** Specifics:

- `maestro record` is Android/iOS only. **Maestro Web (Beta) has no video capture.** So Maestro alone cannot produce the mp4.
- Maestro Web has no visible mouse cursor, no easing/pacing control, and no way to hold on a frame — all of which are what make a screencast readable rather than a jittery robot.
- Maestro Web's selector model is quirky in ways already burned in (`id:` beats `data-testid`, controlled inputs can't be cleared, no `${VAR}` in the `url:` header, one shared browser per run).

Two viable recording paths, and Task 3 is a **spike to pick one**:

- **(A) Maestro + external screen capture.** Keep the exact flow YAML we already write; record the Chromium window with `ffmpeg -f avfoundation` on macOS. Cheapest, single source of truth for flows, but macOS-only, non-headless, non-CI, and you inherit Maestro's cursor/pacing gaps.
- **(B) A dedicated Playwright "screencast runner."** Playwright's `recordVideo` gives deterministic headless capture at a fixed viewport, plus a synthetic cursor overlay, easing, dwell-on-frame, zoom/pan, and step→narration-cue timestamps. Costs a second driver, but it is CI-able, cross-platform, and produces genuinely watchable output.

**Recommendation going in: (B) for recording, Maestro stays the correctness gate** — and both share the same seed script, the same test user, and the same `data-testid`/`id` selectors, so the app never grows two competing sets of hooks. The demo flows then also act as a second smoke suite: if a video fails to record, a user-facing path broke.

## Format spec: "0–60"

- **Shorts (the workhorse):** ≤60s, 9:16 (1080x1920), hard cut in at 0s with the payoff on screen, one idea per video, ends on the same 2-second outro card. Also exported 16:9 for the main feed where it reads.
- **Long-form (rare):** 5–12min, 16:9 — setup and the full idea→plan→tasks→commit narrative.
- Every video: committed narration script, committed flow, generated captions (YouTube needs them for silent autoplay), consistent lower-third title card.

## Season 1 backlog

Two long-form:

- **L1 — "OpenThrottle in 10 minutes: idea → plan → tasks → shipped commit."** The flagship. The whole loop end to end.
- **L2 — "Setup from scratch"** — clone → `./scripts/setup.sh` → `pnpm run start` → `localhost:6020`, plus `pnpm run setup:mcp-instructions`.

Twenty-two 60-second shorts, grouped:

**Getting started**
1. What is OpenThrottle in 60 seconds
2. 0–60: boot the entire stack with one command
3. Your first plan in 60 seconds
4. Plans vs tasks vs notes vs projects — the mental model
5. Connect the OT MCP to Claude Code in 60 seconds

**The planning substrate**
6. Turn a PRD into a plan + tasks
7. Semantic search across every plan you've ever written
8. Promote a task into its own plan
9. Tags & rules: automate what happens when work gets labeled
10. Notes: capture context your agents can actually find

**Execution**
11. Ralph: run a plan one task at a time
12. Watch an agent run stream live
13. `Plan-Id` / `Task-Id`: every commit traced back to why it exists
14. Scheduled agent runs — put work on a cron
15. Kill a runaway agent run
16. Worktrees: parallel agents that don't step on each other

**Interfaces & developer experience**
17. Chat with any CLI (Claude, Codex, OpenCode) from the dashboard
18. Local models with Ollama — nothing leaves your box
19. Skills: teach your agents your house rules
20. Generators: stop hand-writing components
21. The dashboard tour in 60 seconds
22. Self-host on one box with `docker compose`

Ordering for release: 1 → 3 → 2 → L2 → 11 → 5 → 21 → then the rest, roughly two per week. Publish the pilot (Task 10) before automating the tail — prove one video is watchable before building the factory around it.

## Risks / open questions

- **Demo data realism.** Screencasts of an empty app are worthless. Needs a dedicated, deterministic demo seed (distinct from the E2E seed user) with plausible plans/tasks/notes and pre-baked agent-run output.
- **Live agent runs are non-deterministic and slow.** Videos 11/12/14 probably need a recorded/replayed run rather than a live model call, or a heavily pinned local model.
- **Secrets on screen.** Recording the real app risks leaking tokens, emails, repo names. Needs a redaction/scrub checklist before publish, and the demo seed should contain only fictional data.
- **Upload automation is deliberately last.** Manual upload until the pipeline earns trust; YouTube Data API automation only after.
summary: Stand up the @OpenThrottleAI YouTube channel around a "0–60" format (mostly 60-second videos, two longer onboarding pieces), and build a faceless, repeatable production pipeline where each video is a scripted browser flow (Maestro/Playwright over the real openthrottle-developer app) recorded to video, narrated by TTS, and assembled with ffmpeg.
title: 🎥 OpenThrottle YouTube "0–60": video backlog + automated screencast pipeline

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

`skill-sync` is the only OpenThrottle-authored infra skill without the `ot-` prefix used by `ot-plans`, `ot-postgres`, `ot-claude-loop`, `ot-onboarding`, `ot-workflow-orchestration`. Rename the skill to **`ot-skill-sync`** and update every reference so nothing (scripts, CI, docs, DB rows, downstream install commands) points at the old slug.

## Scope of references found (grep `skill-sync`, 2026-08-23)

**Executable paths — break if missed:**
- `scripts/setup.sh:22`, `scripts/setup_worktree.sh:7` → `./skills/skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh`
- `scripts/check-agent-assets-ssot.sh:20-24` (the `--check` drift gate wired to `monorepo:check-agent-assets-ssot`)
- `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml:288-293`
- `.github/workflows/test-coverage-audit-scheduled.yml:60-62`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts:29` (user-facing command string shown in the UI)

**Skill itself:** `skills/skill-sync/{SKILL.md,README.md,scripts/{sync,cleanup,common}.sh}` — frontmatter `name:`, headings, self-referential install/run paths, and the `.gitignore` marker strings in `common.sh:38-39` (`# Start/End 🔄 Managed by OpenThrottle skill-sync`) which must stay in sync with the existing block in `.gitignore:86-90`.

**Docs:** `AGENTS.md` (48, 52, 61), `CONTRIBUTING.md:196`, `docs/README.md:27`, `docs/Skills.md` (5, 7, 14-15, 19, 22, 35, 58, 63), `docs/monorepo/agent-editor-folders.md` (5, 15, 47, 52-56, 104, 119, 125, 133-134), `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md` (5, 13, 64, 102-125), `docs/monorepo/skill-usage-telemetry-scope.md` (104, 127 — historical telemetry tables; annotate rather than rewrite history), `skills/README.md` (71, 86, 107), `skills/AGENTS.md:24`, `skills/ot-onboarding/SKILL.md` (131, 142), `.agents/rules/commands/openthrottle.mdc:36`, `applications/openthrottle-developer/README.md:70`, `applications/openthrottle-developer/docs/repo-skills-discovery-design.md` (5, 111, 143).

**Code comments / tests:** `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/{parse-skill-frontmatter,walk-agent-assets-on-disk,discover-skill-dirs}.ts` + `__tests__/walk-agent-assets-on-disk.test.ts`, `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/workspace-settings/openthrottle-repo-skill-paths.ts`, `tools/workflows/src/utils/__tests__/job-run-hooks-runner.test.ts:90`, developer app `agents/components/AgentsSkillsRegistry.tsx:74`, `agents/data/{repo-skills-registry.ts,discover-repo-skills.server.ts}` + both `discover-repo-skills*.test.ts`, `skills/data/write-skill-file.server.ts`.

**Database (slug-keyed):** `project_skills.slug = 'skill-sync'` (unique per project, tags seeded by `databases/migrations/094_...sql:40`). A pure disk rename would orphan the old row (`orphaned_at`, migration 093) and drop its tags — needs a forward migration. Audit sibling slug-keyed data too: `tasks.skill_slug` (migration 071), skill availability rule sets, and `skill_usage_events` rows.

## Constraints / gotchas

- Generated trees (`.agents/skills/skill-sync`, `.claude/skills/skill-sync`) are gitignored symlinks — the rename must leave **no stale symlink**; run `cleanup.sh` then `sync.sh`, and confirm `sync.sh --check` is clean on a fresh checkout.
- `.gitignore` marker text is load-bearing: if the marker changes, the old block must be migrated in the same commit or the managed block is duplicated/orphaned.
- Historical migrations (094) are immutable — add a new forward migration, never edit.
- `npx skills add openthrottle/monorepo --skill skill-sync` is the **public** install command (README + SKILL.md, public mirror). Renaming breaks downstream repos that already installed it under the old name; call this out in the PR body and in `docs/Skills.md`.
- Skill-name/slug-keyed telemetry: usage rows recorded under `skill-sync` stay under the old name unless migrated — decide migrate-vs-leave explicitly.

## Definition of done

`grep -rI 'skill-sync' --exclude-dir={node_modules,.git,.nx}` returns only intentional historical/annotated mentions; `bash skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh --check`, `pnpm nx run monorepo:check-agent-assets-ssot`, and `pnpm run check:local` all pass; the Skills UI shows one `ot-skill-sync` row with its tags intact and no orphaned `skill-sync` row.
summary: Renamed skill-sync → ot-skill-sync across disk, scripts, CI, docs, UI, and DB (migration 103). Breaking: install with --skill ot-skill-sync. PR https://github.com/OpenThrottle/monorepo/pull/423
title: Rename the skill-sync skill to ot-skill-sync

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

Today every PR is validated against the `main` it branched from, then merged with no re-validation. That is the classic semantic-conflict hole: two PRs that are individually green can break `main` together. A merge queue closes it by building each entry against `main` + the entries ahead of it, and only fast-forwarding when that build is green.

The plumbing is already half-built and currently inert:

- `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml:30` already declares `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]`.
- `docs/monorepo/NX.md:27` explicitly records the state: *"The `merge_group` trigger is still wired but inert — there is no merge queue enabled."*
- Line 245 of the workflow reasons about shard behavior with the note "No merge queue on this plan, so the ready PR is the gate" — that comment becomes wrong the moment the queue is on.

So this plan is mostly **configuration + verification + doc/agent-workflow reconciliation**, not a workflow rewrite. The hard parts are the traps, listed below.

## Current repo state (measured, 2026-08-18)

Two overlapping protection surfaces on `main`, which is itself something this plan must reconcile:

- **Classic branch protection** (`/branches/main/protection`): `required_status_checks.contexts = ["ci-success"]`, `strict: false`, `require_code_owner_reviews: true`, `required_approving_review_count: 0`, `enforce_admins: false`.
- **Ruleset `main` (id 14604876)**, enforcement `active`: rules `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `required_linear_history`, `pull_request` with `allowed_merge_methods: ["rebase"]` and `required_approving_review_count: 0`. **No** `required_status_checks` rule, **no** `merge_queue` rule, no bypass actors.
- Repo merge settings: `allow_squash_merge: true`, `allow_rebase_merge: true`, `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_auto_merge: true`, `delete_branch_on_merge: true`, `squash_merge_commit_title: PR_TITLE`, `squash_merge_commit_message: COMMIT_MESSAGES`. Repo is **public**.

`ci-success` is the only required context, and it is a stable non-matrix job (`continuous-integration.yml:520`) that already aggregates the 3 build shards. That is exactly the shape a merge queue wants — no work needed there.

## The traps (why this is a plan and not a checkbox)

1. **Every required check must fire on `merge_group`, or the queue stalls.** A required context whose workflow has no `merge_group` trigger simply never reports inside the queue; GitHub waits out `check_response_timeout_minutes` and dequeues the PR. Right now only `ci-success` is required and only `continuous-integration.yml` has the trigger, so we are safe *today* — but `secret-scan.yml`, `openthrottle-docker.yml`, `terraform-validate.yml`, and `vercel-deploy.yml` are all PR-triggered and none carry `merge_group`. Anyone who later marks one required silently arms a stall.
2. **`required_linear_history` + `allowed_merge_methods: ["rebase"]` constrain the queue's own merge method.** The queue has an independent merge method (`MERGE`/`SQUASH`/`REBASE`); `MERGE` is incompatible with linear history. Whichever we choose has to preserve conventional-commit titles and the `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers that the OT work ledger and traceability depend on.
3. **The merged SHA is not the PR branch SHA.** Queue entries build (and merge) a rewritten commit. Any agent flow that assumes "the SHA I pushed is the SHA on `main`" — notably `record_artifact` of the merged squash on the work ledger — must read the SHA back from `main` after the merge lands, not from the local branch.
4. **`gh pr merge` stops being synchronous.** With a queue on, merging enqueues; the actual merge happens minutes later and can *fail out of the queue*. Ralph loops, the `github-pull-request` skill, and any "merge then continue" automation need to either use `--auto` and stop waiting, or poll to completion.
5. **CI runs roughly double** (PR run + merge-group run, and the existing `push: main` trigger fires a third time after the fast-forward). Free on a public repo — see `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` — but the `push: main` run is now largely redundant re-validation of a commit the queue just validated, and is worth an explicit keep/drop decision rather than drift.
6. **Concurrency.** `continuous-integration.yml:56` groups on `github.ref` with `cancel-in-progress` for everything except `refs/heads/main`. Merge-queue refs are `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-N-<sha>` — unique per entry, so cancellation is a no-op in practice, but the reasoning in that comment block needs to be checked and restated rather than assumed.
7. **`nx affected` base resolution inside the queue.** `nrwl/nx-set-shas` derives `NX_BASE` from the last successful run on the default branch. Its behavior on a `merge_group` event must be confirmed empirically, not assumed — a wrong base means the queue build silently checks *less* than the PR build did, which is a green-but-untested failure mode this repo has explicitly designed against elsewhere (`changes` job fails closed, partitioner self-validates).
8. **The `changes` doc-only gate already handles it.** `continuous-integration.yml:124` short-circuits every non-`pull_request` event to `run/deps/graph=true`, so merge-group entries always run the full build. Verify, don't change.

## Scope

In: queue configuration on `main`, `merge_group` correctness of the CI workflow, required-check hygiene across the other workflows, an end-to-end live validation, docs, and the agent-workflow changes in trap 3/4.

Out: adopting Nx Cloud DTE (unrelated, still not adopted — `docs/monorepo/NX.md`), changing the sharding factor, and enabling any currently cost-gated workflow.

## Definition of done

A PR merged through the queue on `main`; a `merge_group` CI run visible in Actions and reporting `ci-success`; conventional-commit title and `Plan-Id:`/`Task-Id:` footers intact on the resulting `main` commit; a documented rollback; and `docs/monorepo/NX.md` no longer claiming the trigger is inert.
summary: Turn on a GitHub merge queue for `main` and make `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` a correct, trustworthy `merge_group` gate — including the agent workflows (auto-merge, work-ledger SHA capture) that change shape once merges stop being instantaneous.
title: 🔀 Enable GitHub merge queues on Continuous Integration

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`openthrottle-mcp` runs as a **long-lived stdio child** of the MCP client (Claude/Cursor), launched once at session start via `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh`. If it launches with an empty/invalid `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, the client still connects and lists tools — but **every authenticated tool call 401s** for the rest of the session. It looks connected; it is dead. Recovery requires provisioning/fixing the token AND a client reconnect — and in the 2026-08-05 session the `/mcp reconnect` control was repeatedly unavailable ("MCP controls aren't available right now"), so the stale process could not be relaunched from the UI. Net: many wasted turns diagnosing, and OT writes only succeeded via a one-off stdio-fallback launcher.

Root symptom seen: `.mcp.json` passes `"OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN": "${OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}"`; when the launching shell doesn't export it, that interpolates to empty, and the process was already running before the token was valid — so it held an empty token even though `.env` had a valid one.

## Already done (partial mitigation — track to merge)

On branch `fix/ot-mcp-token-placeholder-selfload` (draft PR pending):
- `run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` now does a **launch-time auth preflight**: refuses to start (loud banner + `exit 1`) when the token is unset or the server rejects it, so the client surfaces "failed to start" instead of silently connecting broken. Opt-out `OT_MCP_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1`.
- Fixed a false-pass bug: the server answers auth failures with **HTTP 200 + an `errors` array** (with `"path":["listSources"]`), so a naive `grep "listSources"` passed a bad token. Both the preflight and `verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh` now decide on the body (`errors` ⇒ rejected).

## Residual gaps this plan must close

1. **Mid-session staleness.** The preflight only runs at launch. A token valid at boot but rotated/revoked later still 401s until the next relaunch — inherent to a long-lived stdio process. Need detection/refresh (periodic re-check, per-request token resolution, or a self-heal).
2. **Reconnect reliability.** When the client's reconnect control is unavailable, there's no in-band way to recover. Investigate a reliable relaunch path and/or a `whoami`/auth-status signal the client can act on.
3. **Prevent empty-token-at-launch.** Guarantee the launcher resolves a valid token before exec (it self-loads from `.env`, but ordering/placeholder edge cases remain), and align `.mcp.json` env handling so an unset shell var can't silently become an empty bearer token.

## Goal

Make it impossible to operate against a stale/broken MCP without a loud, actionable signal, and provide a reliable recovery path — covering launch-time (done), mid-session, and prevention.

## Key references
- `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` (launcher + new preflight), `scripts/verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh`
- `.mcp.json` env block (`${OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}` interpolation), `.cursor/mcp.json.example`
- Auth: `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/auth/get-auth-token.ts` (resolution order: per-request store → env), `packages/openthrottle-mcp/docs/AUTH.md`
- Server returns HTTP 200 + `errors` (UNAUTHENTICATED) on bad token
- Prior findings: openthrottle-mcp auth config shadowing; OT MCP stdio fallback; OT MCP health-check first
title: Stable fix for the stale in-session openthrottle-mcp (connected but silently 401ing)

author: visormatt
description:
## Origin
While bulk-linking plans to repositories (2026-08-28) we found MCP `get_plan` returns plans WITHOUT `runConfigJson`, forcing a direct-GraphQL workaround. Question raised: 'why is the MCP not using our generated GraphQL approach?' Investigation answer: **it is** - the premise inverts.

## Findings (mapped 2026-08-28)
1. packages/openthrottle-mcp is fully on `defineCodegen` (`packages/openthrottle-mcp/codegen.ts`, output `src/__generated__/`, Nx `codegen-graphql` target wired into build/dev). Zero handwritten query strings; tools import generated `*Document` symbols + generated Zod input schemas (e.g. `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/tools/plans.ts:11-30`).
2. Plan/task/note/project operations are consumed CROSS-PACKAGE from `packages/openthrottle-agentic-ralph/src/graphql/ralph/{queries,mutations,fragments}.graphql` (deliberate 'Phase 1 codegen dedupe' - see codegen.ts comment). The MCP's own documents live in `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/graphql/*.graphql` (33 ops; 45 more in the shared ralph set).
3. ROOT CAUSE of the drift: the shared `fragment Plan on PlanObject` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-ralph/src/graphql/ralph/fragments.graphql:9`) omits `runConfigJson` (while including its sibling `jobRunHooksJson` - an omission, not policy). Every plan-shaped op spreads `...Plan`, so `getPlan`, `listPlansByStatus`, `createPlan`, `updatePlan`, `createPlans` ALL under-select. `PlanObject.runConfigJson` is non-nullable (`String!`), so adding it needs no null handling. Proof it's fetchable: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx.graphql` selects it (lines ~63, ~142).
4. Tool output = fragment selection set passed through verbatim (`runTool<{ plan: GetPlanQuery['plan'] }>` in plans.ts:199-207; serialization in `src/utils/tool-result.ts`) - which is why the omission propagated silently to tool results.
5. WHY NO TRIPWIRE FIRED: `verify-graphql-codegen` in `packages/openthrottle-mcp/package.json` runs `git diff --exit-code -- packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/__generated__`, but `.gitignore:36` (`**/__generated__/**/*`) means only `.gitkeep` is tracked - git diff over ignored untracked files ALWAYS exits 0. The guard can never fail. Its description and `packages/openthrottle-mcp/AGENTS.md:15-16` both wrongly assume the output is committed.
6. `update_plan`'s tool description (`plans.ts:90`) omits `runConfigJson` even though the generated `UpdatePlanInput` accepts it, while `create_plan`'s description documents it - discovered the hard way during the bulk-link pass.

## Goal
Fix the field omission, make drift detectable again, and add a schema-vs-fragment coverage check so the NEXT server-side field addition can't silently vanish from MCP tool output.

## Constraints
No TS enums, no `as`/`any`, alphabetized keys where order doesn't matter. Never hand-edit `__generated__`. MCP tool changes must respect the four-place registration parity (`tools/plans.ts` -> `nest-tool-handlers.ts` -> `tool-registry.ts` -> `nest/openthrottle-mcp-mcp-surface.ts`; parity test enforces). Both openthrottle-mcp AND openthrottle-agentic-ralph consume the shared fragments - regenerate and validate both. openthrottle-mcp is server-consumed/built-to-dist (exports -> dist).
title: MCP GraphQL drift: add runConfigJson to the shared Plan fragment, revive the dead codegen guard, add a fragment-coverage tripwire

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

At the moment we kick off a plan/task run we know four things: WHAT we're running (plan/task), WHICH agent/CLI + model, WHERE on disk it runs (worktree folder), and WHICH git branch. Today that provenance is scattered and two inputs aren't durably stored at all, which blocks downstream use-cases: mapping a branch to its PR, finding the worktree folder on disk, and building "open in editor" deep-links.

## Current state (research, 2026-08-01)

The spine already exists — `plan_runs` IS the "we're kicking things off" record, and `work_sessions.plan_run_id` already bridges a run to its commits and PRs. But:

- **Agent** = `plan_runs.execution_backend` — real column ✅ (`packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/plan-runs/plan-run.entity.ts`).
- **Model** = only inside `run_config_snapshot.ralph.model` (JSONB) + `work_sessions.model` after a session opens — not a first-class run column.
- **Worktree path** = only inside `run_config_snapshot.workspace.workingDirectory` (JSONB); the canonical home is `repository_checkouts.filesystem_path`, and `repository_checkouts.kind='worktree'` is already reserved but never written (`databases/migrations/078_create_repositories_and_checkouts.sql`).
- **Branch** = ❌ nowhere per-run. Only `repositories.default_branch` (repo-level). This is the clearest gap.
- **PR** = a `work_artifacts` row (`type='pull_request'`, payload `{repo, number}`) hung off the run's `work_session` via `work_sessions.plan_run_id` — exists, but there's no direct run→PR join/resolver.

## Decision

Promote provenance to first-class, queryable columns on `plan_runs` (rejected alternatives: a separate `plan_run_provenance` companion table — extra join for no gain; JSONB-only + resolvers — branch is genuinely absent and JSONB stays hard to query/index). Use `repository_checkouts` (kind='worktree') as the durable on-disk home that editor deep-links resolve against. Keep PR linkage on the existing work-ledger `pull_request` artifact and expose a run→PR resolver over the `work_sessions.plan_run_id` bridge.

**Branch:** since branch is a mix of enqueue-time and worker-start-time knowledge, don't infer it late — FLIP it and force it as an explicit REQUIRED kickoff input, passed as an arg from our skills and from the UI launch surfaces, and fail fast and loud if missing (preferred path). The `plan_runs.branch` column stays nullable for legacy/backfilled rows; enforcement is at the input boundary, not a DB constraint. Optional UI/skill default pre-fill (worktree name / HEAD) is allowed, but the value is always passed explicitly, never silently inferred server-side.

**Shared-code homes:** editor deep-link scheme logic → the editor package (`@openthrottle/react-router-ide` client, `@openthrottle/openthrottle-ide` engine); generic path/URL helpers → a util package (`@openthrottle/react-router-utils` client, `@openthrottle/nestjs-utils` server). Not app-local. (There is likely no existing editor-link helper yet — search first, then add to these packages.)

## Scope (v1)

Storage/capture foundation + read surface + the Developer-app payoff (open-in-editor deep-links and branch↔PR surfacing).

## Key files
- Entity/service: `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/plan-runs/{plan-run.entity.ts,plan-runs.service.ts}` (`recordQueuedRun`, heartbeat writers)
- Enqueue/snapshot: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/{plan-enqueue.service.ts,enqueue-plan-run-config-snapshot.ts}`, `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-snapshot.*`
- Checkouts: `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/repositories/{repository-checkout.entity.ts,repository-checkouts.service.ts}`, migration `078_*`
- Work ledger (PR/commit artifacts): `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/work-ledger/*`, `artifact-type-registry.ts`
- GraphQL: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plans.resolver.ts` (`PlanRunObject`)
- Shared homes: `packages/{react-router-ide,openthrottle-ide,react-router-utils,nestjs-utils}`
- Migrations live in `databases/migrations/` (next sequential number after the current max)

## Conventions
- Code-first GraphQL → regen `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` + `__generated__` (see CLAUDE.md codegen flow). No breaking field changes without `@deprecated`.
- SQL: follow `ot-postgres` — idempotent DDL, `COMMENT ON COLUMN`, backfill-safe.
- Commit each task with `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers; record the merged squash on the work ledger after merge.
summary: Promote the facts we know at run kickoff — branch, worktree path (via repository_checkouts), model, and PR linkage — to first-class, queryable data hanging off plan_runs, then surface editor deep-links and branch↔PR in the Developer app.
title: Persist run provenance on plan_runs (branch, worktree, model, PR linkage)

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

Adding `claude` to `WorkspaceEditorId` (plan ec3dcee9) was supposed to be safe: the design leaned on **exhaustive `Record<WorkspaceEditorId, …>` maps as tripwires**, so typecheck would fail at every consumer until each was updated. Three maps did exactly that. A fourth consumer did not, and it shipped a real bug:

```ts
// app/routing/settings/utils/workspace-settings-action.ts — BEFORE
const WORKSPACE_EDITOR_VALUES = new Set<string>([
  WorkspaceEditorIdEnum.Cursor,
  WorkspaceEditorIdEnum.Vscode,
]);
const isWorkspaceEditorId = (value: string): value is WorkspaceEditorId =>
  WORKSPACE_EDITOR_VALUES.has(value);
```

`parseEnabledEditorsFromFormData` silently `continue`s past unknown ids, so Claude Code was selectable in the picker, appeared checked, and was **dropped on save**. The apply table then listed two targets instead of three. Fixed in PR #443, but the fix is the symptom, not the cause.

**Root cause:** `Set<string>` (and `string[]`, and `.includes()`) erase the union. Only an exhaustive `Record<Union, …>` produces a compile error when a member is added. The codebase has both patterns side by side with nothing distinguishing them, and there were two divergent `isWorkspaceEditorId` functions — the multi-select used the derived one, the form parser used the hardcoded copy.

The goal is not "audit harder." It is to make the hand-rolled form **not compile** and **not lint**.

## The subset problem (do not get this wrong)

Not every enumeration should be complete. These are legitimate and must keep working:

- `conversation-stream.resolver.ts` — `PROMPT_ROLES` deliberately excludes the `tool` role.
- `rule-applications.service.ts` — `TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES = ['CANCELED', 'COMPLETED', 'SKIPPED']` is a real subset of the task-status union.
