Both are hand-listed arrays today, so both have the same defect: add a member and it is silently *excluded*, with no prompt to decide. The rule is therefore **not** "subsets are banned" — it is:

> Every enumeration of a vocabulary must be exhaustive **at the type level**, including subsets. A subset is `Record<Union, boolean>`, so a new member forces an explicit yes/no rather than defaulting to no.

## Shape to build

A new **raw, dependency-free** package — `packages/nodejs-parts-department` (`@openthrottle/nodejs-parts-department`), source-first (no `build` target, `main`/`types` → `./src/index.ts`, per `packages/AGENTS.md`). It must import nothing, so server packages, React Router apps, CLIs, and generators can all use it.

Scaffold it with the generator, not by hand — it is a plain-Node package, so `--type=node`:

```bash
NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:package --organization=@openthrottle --type=node --name=nodejs-parts-department
```

```ts
// The vocabulary itself: values + type + guard, from one declaration.
export const WORKSPACE_EDITORS = vocabulary(['claude', 'cursor', 'vscode']);
//    .values  readonly ['claude','cursor','vscode']
//    .is(v)   type guard
//    .has(v)

// Exhaustive derivation — omit a member and it does not compile.
export const EDITOR_LABELS = WORKSPACE_EDITORS.labelled({
  claude: 'Claude Code', cursor: 'Cursor', vscode: 'Visual Studio Code',
});

// Exhaustive SUBSET — a new member must be classified, not silently dropped.
export const TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES = TASK_STATUSES.subsetOf({
  BACKLOG: false, BLOCKED: false, CANCELED: true, COMPLETED: true,
  IN_PROGRESS: false, PENDING: false, QUEUED: false, SKIPPED: true,
});
```

`subsetOf` is the load-bearing piece — it is what turns today's silent-exclusion arrays into a forced decision.

## Interaction with GraphQL codegen (settle this in task 1)

The client's editor union is the **generated** `WorkspaceEditorId` enum in `app/__generated__/graphql.ts`, derived from `schema.gql`, which is derived from the server enum, which is derived from `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_IDS`. A second hand-written vocabulary in the new package would be a *fifth* copy — the exact thing this plan exists to kill.

So: for GraphQL-backed unions the generated enum stays the source, and the package supplies helpers that **wrap** it (`vocabularyFromEnum(WorkspaceEditorId)`). For non-GraphQL unions (`DRIVER_IDS`, checkout kinds) the package's `vocabulary()` is the source. Decide and document the boundary before writing consumers.

## Enforcement

1. **ESLint rule** `openthrottle/no-adhoc-vocabulary` in `tools/dotfiles/src/rules/` (alongside `route-primitive-shape.ts` and `pre-hooks-unpack.ts`, which are the working precedent, each with a co-located test). Flags array/Set literals containing ≥2 members of a registered vocabulary outside that vocabulary's own SSOT file, and points at `subsetOf`. Ship as `warn` first — `route-primitive-shape` is `warn` today.
2. **Audit script** `scripts/audit-vocabularies.ts` mirroring `audit-component-shape.ts` (which the pre-commit hook already runs and which prints a per-project violation table). Catches what lint cannot see: duplicate exported guard names across files, e.g. the two `isWorkspaceEditorId`s.

## Scope

Pilot on three vocabularies, chosen because they churn:

- **workspace editors** — the one that just broke; 5 consumers.
- **driver ids** — `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/registry/index.ts`. `DriverRegistry = Partial<Record<DriverId, AgentDriver>>`; `Partial` means adding an id never forces registering the driver. Gemini and Antigravity were both added recently, so this churns.
- **task statuses** — the `TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES` subset above.

Explicitly **not** in scope: a repo-wide sweep of every union. Prove the pattern on three, then fan out with the audit script listing the backlog.

## Done means

Re-running the ec3dcee9 exercise — adding a fourth editor — produces a **compile error at every consumer**, not a silent drop. Add a regression fixture that asserts this.
summary: Add a raw @openthrottle/nodejs-parts-department package (exhaustive/subsetOf/labelled helpers), an openthrottle/no-adhoc-vocabulary ESLint rule, and an audit script — then migrate the editor, driver, and task-status vocabularies onto them so adding a member fails typecheck at every consumer instead of silently dropping it.
title: Exhaustive vocabularies: make choke-point unions impossible to re-list by hand

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Update the posture and copy of the OpenThrottle Developer legal pages so they match the recent Apache-2.0 open-core relicense and read as a serious, invested product — while keeping the personal, solo-maker connection the owner values.

Scope is the three legal routes in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/` that are now stale:
- `legal.terms-of-use.tsx`
- `legal.privacy-policy.tsx`
- `legal._index.tsx`

`legal.license.tsx` was ALREADY updated to the Apache-2.0 open-core posture (open-core, Apache-2.0 core, reserved trademark, DCO sign-off) and is the reference voice to align the other three against. Do NOT rewrite the license page's substance; only touch it if a cross-link or a shared phrase needs to match.

## Why now

Two problems on the live pages:
1. **Direct contradiction** — `legal.terms-of-use.tsx` still says the source code is *"source-available and licensed under a proprietary End User License Agreement (EULA)"*, which conflicts with `legal.license.tsx` now declaring the core Apache-2.0. This must be fixed.
2. **Stale, self-deprecating posture** — terms-of-use, privacy-policy, and the legal index all open with *"a personal portfolio and developer playground … not a commercial product."* The owner wants these to read as a real, invested product without losing the personal connection.

## Locked decisions (owner-confirmed 2026-07-30)

- **Entity voice: "Steward + open project."** Frame OpenThrottle as an open-source product **stewarded by Matthew Scholta** — keep the solo-maker / personal-portfolio connection front-and-center and signal genuine investment, but drop the "just a playground / toy" framing. Not a company/"team" voice.
- **Keep ALL protective legal disclaimers.** Retain as-is / no-warranty / no-SLA / no-uptime-guarantee / limitation-of-liability language on terms-of-use (and the as-is note on privacy/index). Elevate the *tone*, not the legal protection. Do NOT soften disclaimers to "reasonable/best effort."

## Voice & terminology guardrails (apply to all three pages)

- Lead with OpenThrottle as an **open-source product** (open-core, Apache-2.0), **stewarded/built by Matthew Scholta**, rather than "a personal portfolio and developer playground."
- Keep the personal connection: Matthew Scholta is the named steward/author and the contact.
- Replace the EULA/"proprietary" framing in terms-of-use with the Apache-2.0 open-core framing, cross-linking to `/legal/license` (which already carries the full license explanation). Do not re-explain the whole license — defer to that page.
- Preserve the substance of every protective clause (acceptable use, disclaimer of warranties, limitation of liability, governing law, changes, contact). Only the framing/tone changes, plus the license correction.
- Keep using the shared constants (`SITE_TITLE`, `OPENTHROTTLE_CONTACT_PORTFOLIO`/`_REF`) and the existing `GlobalScreen`/`GlobalHeading` structure and section-comment scaffold — this is copy/posture work, not a component rewrite.

## Constraints

- Copy/JSX only; no new components, no schema/GraphQL changes, no new deps. Keep the generated section-comment scaffold (Hooks/Setup/Handlers/Markup/Life Cycle/🔌 Short Circuit).
- Validate with `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`; live-smoke the three routes in the dev server (`/legal`, `/legal/terms-of-use`, `/legal/privacy-policy`).
- Conventional commits; `Plan-Id:`/`Task-Id:` footers per task. Record the merged squash on the work ledger after merge.

## Out of scope

- The already-updated `legal.license.tsx` substance.
- Any legal pages in other apps (only `openthrottle-developer` has legal routes).
- Legal/attorney review — this is copy alignment, not legal sign-off.
title: Reframe developer legal pages to Apache-2.0 open-core "steward" posture

author: visormatt
description:
# Rules hierarchy: scope ladder, precedence, and prompt-backed actions

Continues the `/rules` route (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/rules.*`) and the `tag_action_rules` engine behind it. Three threads: (1) make the scope hierarchy that already exists in the schema actually reachable and meaningful, (2) layer `custom_prompts` onto rules via a new `attach-prompt` action type, (3) fix a shipped bug and give rules an inspectable detail/dry-run surface.

## Where things stand

**Data model** — `tag_action_rules` (migration 065, +072 title) is user-owned and carries a full scope ladder: `project_id` (NULL = all projects), `environment` (NULL = all; `ci|interactive|ralph`), `status` (NULL = any plan status), `tag_all` (AND semantics over the plan's effective tag set). Actions: `inject-task`, `availability-exception`, `promote-task-to-plan`. Applications are ledgered in `rule_applications` (migration 066) with `UNIQUE (rule_id, plan_id)` as the apply-once fingerprint; states `applied | pre-satisfied | flagged | orphaned`.

**Evaluation** — `evaluateTagActionRules` in `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/evaluate-tag-action-rules.ts` is pure and AND-composed. The `plan-rules:evaluate` BullMQ worker (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/plan-rules/`) does the fingerprint check, dispatches through `ActionExecutorRegistry`, reconciles `applied` rows, and flips un-matched rows to `orphaned`.

**UI** — `/rules` (index + `new` + `$ruleId/edit`), components under `app/routing/rules/`, onboarding via `GlobalFeatureOnboarding`.

## Gaps this plan closes

1. **The project layer is unreachable from the UI.** `projectId` exists in the entity, the GraphQL input/object, the resolver, and the MCP tool — but *both* UI routes call `.omit({ projectId: true })` on the parsed input, and `RuleFormMatchSection` has no project control. Per-project rules (an explicit promise in the onboarding copy: "Give each project its own defaults with per-project rules") cannot be created from the app at all.

2. **`promote-task-to-plan` cannot be persisted.** `TAG_ACTION_TYPES` in `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/tag-action-payloads.ts` includes it and `promote-task-to-plan.executor.ts` ships, but migration 065's `chk_tag_action_rules_action_type` still only allows `('inject-task','availability-exception')` and was never widened. Any rule created with that action type dies on INSERT with a constraint violation.

3. **No precedence.** By design "all matched actions dispatch (no global priority)". That is fine for `inject-task` but wrong for a hierarchy: a project-scoped `availability-exception` cannot override a broader global one, and two rules injecting the same skill both fire.

4. **The environment layer is inert in the worker.** `plan-rules.processor.ts` builds its evaluation context with `environment: null`, so environment-qualified rules never match on the worker path — they only apply on qualified plan-context reads. The UI offers the control with no indication of that.

5. **Custom prompts are disconnected.** `custom_prompts` (migration 036, +048) already models `prompt_type ∈ (agents, skills, commands, prompts, rules, personas)` with `user_id` / `project_id` scoping, `labels`, `file_path` natural key, soft delete, and embeddings — but no rule action can reference one. Rules can only inject a `skillSlug`.

6. **No way to see why a rule did or didn't fire.** The ledger is only surfaced per-plan (`PlanRuleApplications` on the plan detail tab). There is no `/rules/:id`, no matched-plan count, no dry-run.

7. **The design doc is missing.** `docs/monorepo/plan-task-tags-rules-design.md` is cited in roughly a dozen source comments and every migration comment, and does not exist in the repo.

## Approach

Scope ladder first (project control + specificity ranking), then the `attach-prompt` action type reusing the existing executor/ledger seam, then the detail + dry-run surface. Precedence is added as a *pure* ranking function alongside `evaluateTagActionRules` so it stays testable with zero I/O, matching the `resolveSkillAvailability` precedent.

Specificity order, narrowest wins: `project_id` set (2) > `environment` set (1) > `status` set (1) > `|tag_all|`, ties broken by `created_at ASC` (stable, oldest first). Ranking never suppresses `inject-task` (additive by nature); it arbitrates `availability-exception` and dedupes identical injections.

## Non-goals

- No change to the apply-once ledger semantics or the `UNIQUE (rule_id, plan_id)` fingerprint.
- No undo of applied actions — `orphaned` stays "left in place".
- No glob/`alwaysApply` path-scoped prompt resolution (the Cursor `.mdc` layering); that is a separate plan if wanted.
- No tag-matching changes (`tagAny` / `tagNone` / dimension-aware matching) — `tag_all` AND semantics stay as-is.
title: Rules hierarchy: scope ladder, precedence, and prompt-backed actions

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

One new markdown file — `docs/marketing/scripts/SEASON-1-NARRATION.md` — containing **three narration iterations for every Season 1 episode**: `01` through `22`, plus `L1` and `L2`. Twenty-four episodes, seventy-two takes, one file.

## The shape of the file

One `##` per script. Under it, the beat times once as a reference row, then three iterations. An iteration is a thesis id, one line of thesis prose, and a flat cue list:

```
[
  ['0:00', 'the words'],
  ['0:07', 'the words'],
]
```

Nothing else — no per-iteration front matter, no repeated action column, no tables. That list is already the `NarrationCue[]` shape the typed episodes take, so everything about one script sits in one place and migrating it later is a copy rather than a translation.

## Founding constraints

**1. Beats are frozen. Only the words change.**

The single most important finding in `docs/marketing/episode-format.md`: all five files of episode 05 (`05-connect-ot-mcp.md` and `-v0`…`-v3`) have a **byte-identical action column and identical beat times**, verified by hashing. They differ only in narration. That is the whole economic case for iterating — a beat carries the picture, a variant carries the words, and **one recording serves all three takes**. This file never restates an action column; it lists each episode's beat times once and writes three narration tracks against them.

**2. Fill the runtime. Context beats empty space.**

This reverses the standing guidance in `docs/marketing/scripts/README.md`, which says "the budget is a ceiling, not a target" and that most shorts should land 25–35 seconds of speech across 55 seconds of picture. That produced scripts like `01` at 101 spoken words and `05-v3` at 102 — roughly 42 seconds of speech in a 55-second video, with the rest silent.

The decision for this rewrite is the opposite: **use the runtime to say more.** Shorts target **115–132 spoken words** (132 is the hard ceiling: 145 wpm × 55s, derived from `format.json`). Under 110 words a short is under-narrated and the take goes back. Silence is still allowed where the action is doing the explaining — it is no longer the default.

Long-form is the far bigger gap. `L1` currently carries **299 spoken words across ten minutes of picture** and `L2` is the same shape — both are beat outlines, not scripts, and the validator warns about it on purpose. Filling them properly means roughly **1,200–1,400 words each, per iteration**. That is where most of the writing effort in this plan actually lives.

**3. Tone: the keys to your first car.**

Positive, forward-leaning, high tempo. The feeling is a sixteen-year-old handed the keys — the road is open, the potential is limitless, and nothing about it is hedged or defensive. No fear-based framing, no "agents are broken today", no enterprise-speak. Momentum in the sentence rhythm, not just the adjectives. This tone gets written down as a charter at the top of the file in task 1, because seventy-two takes written to a vibe will not agree with each other; seventy-two takes written to a charter will.

**4. Nothing on screen that does not exist.**

`01-what-is-openthrottle.md` carries a standing note about a first draft that narrated a linked-commit UI which the app does not have. `15-kill-runaway-run.md` and `16-worktrees.md` are `blockedOn` unshipped surfaces. A denser narration track is more exposed to this failure, not less — more words means more claims. Every iteration is audited against the actual beats before the file is done.

## Relationship to the typed-episode migration (OT 2cef373a)

That plan replaces `docs/marketing/scripts/*.md` with typed TypeScript episodes carrying a `variants[]` array, and explicitly states the markdown scripts disappear with nothing regenerating them. This file is therefore a **drafting surface, not a permanent home**. The cue-list shape above is exactly what a `Variant` holds, and variant ids name a thesis (`payoff-first`), never an ordinal (`v3`), per that plan's decision.

Writing the words in markdown first is deliberate. Prose is faster to iterate on and to read in a diff than a TypeScript literal, and the words are the thing being iterated — the format is not.

## Out of scope

- Any change to an action column, a beat time, a flow, or a recording.
- Recording, narrating or assembling any video.
- The typed-episode migration itself.
- Deleting `05-connect-ot-mcp-v0…v3.md`. Their thesis prose is the record of why four openings existed and is carried into the new file first; retiring the files is a follow-up once the migration lands.
summary: Write a single markdown file holding three narration iterations for each of the 24 Season 1 scripts (01–22, L1, L2), against frozen beats, in a denser and more optimistic voice.
title: Season 1 narration rewrite: three iterations per episode in one file

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem
Human developers using `openthrottle-developer` treat Plans and Tasks as project-management work, but the UI still reads as an internal admin console: nested-only task URLs, metadata buried in card grids, weak hierarchy/breadcrumbs, and list rows that don't scan like GitHub Issues or JIRA.

## Primary user
**Human developer** triaging and executing work in the developer app. Agent operators benefit secondarily via clearer status/assignee surfaces, but v1 optimizes for humans.

## North-star outcomes
1. A developer can scan `/plans` like a GitHub Issues list (title + status + assignee + tags + recency).
2. Plan and task detail pages feel like an issue: breadcrumb hierarchy, title-first hero, right-rail metadata, primary actions always visible.
3. In-plan task table/board matches the same visual language (no redundant columns; inline metadata).

## Architecture constraints
- **App boundary:** UI lives in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/` (+ thin `app/routes/` modules). Do not invent a new Nx package for presentation.
- **Data:** Prefer fields already on Plan/Task GraphQL fragments. Add fields only when missing; never remove/rename schema fields — deprecate if needed.
- **Patterns:** Generator-first (`@tools/generators` react-router component), `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`, component/data boundaries (`data.copy.ts` for copy), URL-driven filters (existing toolbar pattern).
- **Reuse:** Extend `PlansToolbar`, `PlanDetailRouteHeader`, `TaskDetails`, `PlanTabTasks` / board — do not fork parallel list UIs.
- **Related prior art (do not duplicate blindly):** PlanTasksTable more-info plan; PlanTabTasks layout tighten; existing board view (`PlanTasksBoard`).

## v1 scope (shippable)
- Plans index: denser issue-list rows / table cells; sticky filter bar polish; clearer empty states.
- Plan detail: breadcrumb (Projects → Plan); issue-style header (status/assignee/tags/dates); keep existing tabs.
- Task detail: issue-layout (description main + metadata side rail); status/assignee/category always visible; breadcrumbs Plan → Task.
- Plan tasks tab: finish compact title-cell metadata; consistent status chips with list/detail.
- Copy + empty/error paths aligned with precise OT tone.

## Explicitly deferred (follow-up OT plans/tasks)
- Global cross-plan Tasks inbox route (needs list query + nav entry).
- Inline drag-reorder / kanban drag-to-status mutations if not already solid.
- Full activity timeline (comments) beyond plan output / work-ledger surfaces.
- Human-readable short IDs (OT-123) — needs schema + migration.
- Keyboard shortcuts / command-palette issue jumps.
- Real-time collaborative presence.

## Acceptance (plan-level)
- Reviewer can verify each task's checklist without reading the diff.
- No GraphQL breaking changes; codegen only if documents gain fields.
- Validate: `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`, `:test` (affected specs), visual check via `:dev`.

## Validation targets
`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint` · `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test` · optional standalone `tsc` on touched files · `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:dev` smoke of `/plans`, plan detail, task detail.
summary:
SHIPPED (branch openthrottle/loop-plan-tasks-issue-ux, off main b80e3c63) — Plans & Tasks now read like a GitHub Issues / JIRA tracker.

What shipped, per task:
1. Audit (e41807ac) — gap matrix mapping every issue-tracker gap to a target component (in that task's summary).
2. Index rows (f0f400be) — /plans table reshaped to Status | Plan | Actions; task count folded into the meta line; plan tags surfaced inline. PlanCard fragment gained `tags` (only additive GraphQL change) + codegen.
3. Plan header (5b49eefb) — PlanDetailRouteHeader: breadcrumb (Plans → Project → Plan), title-first, status + author→assignee + tags + created/updated. PlanToolbar untouched.
4. Task detail (73166af9) — issue layout: description main column + metadata side rail (stacks on mobile); extracted TaskDetailRouteHeader (breadcrumb Plans → Plan → Task, title-first, always-visible status chip). Status unified on PlanStatusBadge (task statuses ⊆ planStatusValues). Empty body → data.copy.ts.
5. In-plan table (0769003b) — dropped wasteful Category + Requirements columns (and dead commented columns); folded them into the title cell. Board (PlanTaskCard) already consistent — untouched, shared PlanTaskInlineActions intact.
6. Empty/error copy (643f409c) — PlanTasksEmpty gained variant ('plans'|'tasks') + filtered boolean. Task-less plans show 'No tasks yet' (not 'No plans yet'); /plans filtered-empty now detects status/assignee filters, not just q. All copy single-sourced in data.copy.ts.
7. Smoke + deferred (this task) — lint/typecheck/test(1673)/build all green; interactive browser walkthrough deferred to the branch handoff (auth-gated in fresh worktree).

Acceptance: no GraphQL breaking changes (single additive PlanCard.tags field). Each task's checklist verifiable from its summary + the diff. Every touched surface has render-level spec coverage.

NEXT ACTIONS / deferred follow-ups (created as separate BACKLOG OT plans, NOT implemented here):
- 8ec7de61 Global cross-plan Tasks inbox route — BLOCKED on a new GraphQL query: server exposes only tasksByPlanId + task(id); needs listTasks(input:{ assignees?, statuses?, planIds?, titleSubstring?, limit, offset }) → { tasks, totalCount }.
- 67bb901d Human-readable short IDs (OT-123) — schema + migration.
- e140323e Plan/Task activity timeline (comments).
- 203bee35 Keyboard shortcuts + command-palette jumps.
- 617db22a Kanban drag-to-status + inline reorder mutations.
- e23d3e84 Real-time collaborative presence.
title: Plans & Tasks routes: issue-tracker UX (JIRA / GitHub Issues parity)

author: visormatt
description:
Lift the duplicated `?page=` / `?limit=` search-param parsing that loaders (and a few client pagers) reimplement by hand into `@openthrottle/react-router-utils`, then switch every developer-app copy onto that helper.

## Why

`settings.repositories._index` is one of many near-identical copies of:

```ts
const page = Math.max(1, Number(url.searchParams.get('page')) || 1);
const limit = Math.max(1, Math.min(100, Number(url.searchParams.get('limit')) || DEFAULT));
```

The package already exports `DEFAULT_PAGINATION_PAGE` (1) and `DEFAULT_PAGINATION_LIMIT` (25), and `/skills` already extracted `parsePaginationPage` / `parsePaginationLimit` — but those live in the app (`routing/skills/utils/parse-skills-pagination.ts`) instead of the shared package. Plans, prompts, projects, project-detail tasks, search, and queue jobs each re-roll the same logic with slightly different `Number` vs `parseInt` vs `Number.isFinite` dances and inconsistent flooring/clamping.

`readSearchParam` (`q` / `search`) already lives in `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global` and should stay there — this plan is only the numeric pager params.

## Shared API (target)

Add to `packages/react-router-utils/src/utils/parsers.ts` (already re-exported from `src/index.ts`):

```ts
parsePagination(searchParams: URLSearchParams, options?: {
  readonly defaultLimit?: number; // DEFAULT_PAGINATION_LIMIT
  readonly defaultPage?: number;  // DEFAULT_PAGINATION_PAGE
  readonly maxLimit?: number;     // omit = no upper cap
  readonly minLimit?: number;     // default 1
}): { readonly limit: number; readonly offset: number; readonly page: number }
```

Keep `parsePaginationPage(raw)` / `parsePaginationLimit(raw, options)` as the primitives (skills already uses that shape) so client-side pagers that only have a raw string can call them without wrapping a `URLSearchParams`.

Canonical parse rules (unify the copies; slight behavior change on a few edges is intended):

- missing / empty / non-finite / `< 1` → default
- otherwise `Math.floor`, then clamp into `[minLimit, maxLimit]` when those options are set
- `offset = (page - 1) * limit`
- page is never upper-clamped here (skills already documents that as the caller's job once `totalPages` is known)

## Call sites to switch

Loader / client copies of the Math.max/Number dance:

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.repositories._index.tsx` — `{ defaultLimit: REPOSITORIES_DEFAULT_LIMIT, maxLimit: 100 }`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects._index.tsx` — `{ defaultLimit: PROJECTS_DEFAULT_LIMIT, maxLimit: 100 }`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans._index.tsx` — package defaults (no max)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/prompts._index.tsx` — package defaults (no max)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects.$projectId._index.tsx` — `{ defaultLimit: PROJECT_TASKS_DEFAULT_LIMIT }`

Already-extracted app-local helpers to delete or thin:

- `routing/skills/utils/parse-skills-pagination.ts` (+ its spec) — import the package primitives instead; skills still clamps `page` to `totalPages` itself
- `routing/search/utils/parsers.ts` — `parseSearchParams` should delegate page/limit (`defaultLimit: DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT, maxLimit: 100`) and keep `q` / `details`
- `routing/queues/utils/parse-queue-jobs-pagination.ts` — keep the URL wrapper; parse via `{ minLimit: QUEUE_JOBS_LIMIT_MIN, maxLimit: QUEUE_JOBS_LIMIT_MAX }` so `limit=1` still clamps to 10

Out of scope: `resources.queue-job-logs.tsx` is cursor-paged (`after` + `limit`, no `page`). Do not force it onto `parsePagination`.

## Non-goals

- Do not move `readSearchParam`
- Do not collapse route-specific default constants (`REPOSITORIES_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 10`, etc.) into the package default of 25 — pass them as `defaultLimit`
- Do not add a `maxPage` option; callers that slice client-side already clamp after they know `totalCount`
title: Share URL pagination parsing from @openthrottle/react-router-utils

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The `cursor-agent` chat backend intermittently fails on the **first** chat of a session/conversation. It is a cold-start / first-invocation symptom: switching to another agent (claude/codex/opencode), sending one chat, then switching back to cursor usually makes cursor work.

## Current architecture (as of this plan)

- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/cursor-agent/cursor-agent.ts`
  - `createCursorAgentSession()` spawns `cursor-agent create-chat`, accumulates stdout, and returns **`stdout.trim()` verbatim** as the session id.
  - `streamCursorAgent()` spawns a second process: `--print --output-format stream-json --stream-partial-output --workspace <cwd> --trust --resume <sessionId> [-- prompt]`.
  - Both children run under `buildScrubbedEnv()` - an allowlist of exactly `CURSOR_API_KEY, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TERM, TMPDIR, USER`.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts:260`
  - On the first cursor turn (`sessionId` null/empty) it publishes a keepalive, then awaits `mintCursorSession()`. A throw becomes a terminal `Failed to start a cursor-agent session: ...` chunk. **No retry.**
  - The minted id is persisted to `conversation.metadata[cursorSessionId]`.
- Timeouts (`cursor-agent/teardown.ts`): `resolveSessionCreateTimeoutMs()` default **30_000 ms** (`OPENTHROTTLE_AGENT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS`); per-agent idle 120s, wall-clock 900s.

## Findings — task 1 evidence gate (COMPLETE)

Full raw capture is on the plan output stream. Verdicts, re-ranked:

1. **(NEW, reproduced) Cold startup does unbounded blocking network work and the child does not exit promptly.** With `~/.cursor/statsig-cache.json` moved aside, the turn reported `outcome=success duration_ms=15150` yet the process had still not closed **4+ minutes later**; warm baseline for the same sequence is **result → close = 3021 ms**. Cold startup does MCP OAuth discovery over the network (`needsAuth` / `Unauthorized`) and runs Claude-plugin hooks at 1–4 s each, some firing *after* the turn ends. cursor also leaks a `worker-server` grandchild that inherits our stdout pipe and outlives the run (observed alive 2:44 later) — and `terminateChild()` signals only the direct child, never the process group.
2. **H3 env allowlist — PARTIALLY CONFIRMED.** Not the trigger on this machine (none set), but provably wrong: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (selects the config dir, so our child can use a *different chat store* than the user's terminal), `AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE` (`file`|`memory`|`default`; `default` on darwin = macOS login keychain), `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` (dropped = no network behind a corporate proxy). Also read by cursor: `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`, `SHELL`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, `CI`.
3. **(NEW) Keychain auth from a daemon-spawned child.** Mechanism and exact error strings captured (`Authentication required. Please run 'agent login' first…`, `⚠ Warning: The provided API key is invalid.`, both exit 1 with ANSI on stderr; keychain osStatus 36/44/45 mapped by cursor). Unconfirmed as the trigger.
4. **H1 (banner poisons the id) — DISPROVEN as the failure cause.** `handleCreateChat` is local-only and `console-io` writes the id to stdout and *everything else* to stderr; ~10 runs (cold, fresh workspace, concurrent) gave byte-identical clean output. Decisively, **`--resume` accepts any string** — resuming with a never-minted UUID and with the literal `"Update available!  1.2.3"` both produced full successful turns. Survives re-scoped: a polluted id silently starts a *fresh, disconnected* chat, losing multi-turn continuity while appearing to work.
5. **H4 (poisoned persisted id = dead end) — DISPROVEN.** Resume never rejects an id, so there is no "chat not found" signal. **Task 6's re-mint-on-resume-failure half has no trigger and must be dropped or re-scoped;** the retry-on-mint-failure half stands.
6. **H2 (cold token mint in `create-chat`) — DISPROVEN.** Local-only (`randomUUID()` + SQLite store), no network, no auth, 2.0–2.6 s warm *and* cold, clean under 4-way concurrency — ~12× headroom against the 30 s budget.

**Task 2 (structured logging) is now the critical path**, not merely standalone-valuable: naming which failure the user actually hits needs server-side evidence.

## Scope

In scope: the cursor-agent backend adapter, the mint call site in `ConversationStreamService`, its timeouts/retries, and the composer-facing error copy. Out of scope: other CLI backends (except where a shared helper is the right home), and any change to cursor's own model/flag surface.

## Success criteria

- A cold-start reproduction is captured with raw stdout/stderr bytes (task 1) and the failure mode is named. ✅
- First cursor chat in a fresh session succeeds without the switch-to-another-agent workaround.
- A bad mint is recoverable: bounded retry on the mint. (Re-mint-on-resume-failure is moot — see H4.)
- A minted id is validated so a conversation can never silently fork into a disconnected chat.
- Teardown reaps the whole process group, so `worker-server` grandchildren do not accumulate.
- Failures the user cannot fix (auth expired, cursor-agent not installed) surface as distinct, actionable composer copy — ANSI-stripped, never a raw exit code or a silent hang.

## References

- `docs/openthrottle/agentic-cli-chat-backends.md`
- `docs/openthrottle/agentic-cli-backend-compatibility-guide.md`
- `docs/openthrottle/cursor-agent-stream-json-schema.md`
summary: Diagnose and fix intermittent cursor-agent failures on the first chat of a session — cold `create-chat` session/token minting.
title: Fix cursor-agent first-chat startup failures (cold session mint)

author: visormatt
description:
Port `docs/marketing/scripts/06-prd-to-plan.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

**This plan opens BLOCKED.** Unlike 04, where one beat pointed at UI that did not exist, here the entire feature the short demonstrates is a placeholder. Recording it as written would put a false product claim on camera.

## The gate: upload-decompose is a stub end to end

`app/routes/plans.upload-decompose.tsx` has a `parse` intent that calls `buildStubProposal(file)` from `app/routing/plans/utils/document-decompose.ts`. That function ignores the document's contents entirely. Whatever you upload, it returns:

- `planTitle: "Imported: <filename>"`
- `planDescription: "Stub preview for «<filename>» (<size> bytes). The ingest API will replace this output."`
- exactly two tasks, always the same two: "Review imported tasks" and "Validate requirements"

The `commit` intent validates the payload parses as JSON and then returns the error string: *"Creating a plan from this preview is not available until the document ingest API is implemented."*

Beat by beat against the script:

- 0:21 "It reads the whole thing and pulls out the actual work" — it reads the filename and the byte count. The narration is not true, and the on-screen text says so in the frame: the word "Stub" is rendered in the preview the camera is pointed at.
- 0:29 "You get a draft plan with tasks, in order, before anything is saved" — you get two hardcoded tasks unrelated to the document.
- 0:38 "Edit one task title; delete one task" — `DocumentDecomposePreview.tsx` renders no `Input`, no `Textarea` and no delete control. It is read-only. There is nothing to edit and nothing to delete.
- 0:46 "Click Save; plan detail loads with the accepted tasks" — Save returns an error and no plan is created.

Five of the script's eight beats are unrecordable. This is not a framing problem and it cannot be worked around in the flow.

The script's frontmatter says `blockedOn: []`, which is wrong and is itself a deliverable of this plan.

## Secondary gap: there is no PRD fixture

The script's own note says the PRD on screen must be a fictional one shipped with the demo seed, never a real internal document. `tests/demo/fixtures/demo-content.ts` seeds plans, tasks, notes, projects and one output run. It ships no document. `ACCEPT_EXTENSIONS` in `app/routing/plans/config/upload.ts` accepts `.csv,.htm,.html,.json,.md,.markdown,.xls,.xlsx`, so the fixture PRD is a Markdown file — cheap to write, and needed regardless of how the primary gate resolves.

## What already exists and needs no work

- The route, the drop zone, the progress state and the preview component all render; the shell of the flow is real even though the output is not.
- `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is 25 MiB, far above a two-page PRD.
- The 0:46 destination, plan detail, is already exercised by the 03 and 04 flows.

## Constraints

- 75 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; any rewrite must re-validate against `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` and the `short` budget in `docs/marketing/format.json`.
- A flow may not invent a step the script does not describe, and a script may not describe UI that does not exist.
- Do not record a stub and narrate it as a feature. The channel's whole premise is that the product does what the video says.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.
summary: Port docs/marketing/scripts/06-prd-to-plan.md to a recorded flow. Blocked: /plans/upload-decompose is a stub that returns two fixed tasks, is not editable, and cannot save.
title: Build the 06-prd-to-plan screencast flow

author: visormatt
description:
Install Piper (https://github.com/rhasspy/piper) — local neural TTS — and wire it into the demo narration pipeline as the first on-box candidate for the ship voice.

Source of truth: `applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/NARRATION.md` § “How to settle it”. The current default is macOS `say` (`backends/say.ts`). It is rehearsal-only: a rendered sample measured 0.2 LU of loudness range (effectively no prosody) and is recognisably synthetic inside a sentence. Piper is free, sends nothing off-box, and matches this project's self-hosting stance. Hosted backends (ElevenLabs / OpenAI / Google) and Kokoro are out of scope for this plan.

Constraints already encoded in the pipeline — do not reopen them:
- The TTS backend is three fields (`id`, `render`, `sendsDataOffBox`). Add a sibling of `backends/say.ts`; parsing, lexicon, loudness, timings, and captions stay untouched.
- Loudness is measured once across the whole take and one gain is applied to every clip (target -14 LUFS / -1.0 dBTP from `docs/marketing/format.json`). Do not per-sentence-normalise.
- Lexicon substitution (`narrate/lexicon.ts`) applies to spoken text only; captions keep the written form.
- `sendsDataOffBox` must be `false` for Piper. Narration is text about unreleased work.
- The pilot script is **01** (`docs/marketing/scripts/01-what-is-openthrottle.md`), not 03.
- Do not change the default from `macos-say` until a human has listened to Piper vs `say` back-to-back **on phone speakers**. A voice change mid-season reads as a different channel.

Install shape: a Piper **binary** plus one quality **English** voice model (onnx + json). Do not commit the model into git. Document the install path, the voice id, and how `NARRATION_BACKEND` / `NARRATION_VOICE` (or `--backend` / `--voice`) select it. Fail loudly if the binary or model is missing.
title: Install Piper as a local narration backend

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Applying workspace editor configuration writes `.openthrottle/workspace-editors.json` into a **foreign** repo (any checkout that is not the OT monorepo) and leaves it untracked and un-excluded. The user's `git status` then shows `?? .openthrottle/` — OT residue in someone else's repo.

Confirmed live in `/home/demo/Development/github/atlasworks/services/ssm-data-pipeline` (manifest dated 2026-08-26).

Same *class* of problem as OT plan `b409da6e` (foreign-skill injection), which was just fixed. Different feature, different owner, and — importantly — a **different correct answer**.

## Who writes it

`WorkspaceEditorConfigService.applyForRepositoryEditor` in `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/workspace-settings/workspace-editor-config.service.ts` (path constant: `workspace-editor-config-paths.ts` → `OPENTHROTTLE_MANIFEST_RELATIVE_PATH`).

It is **user-initiated**, not ambient: the user applies editor configuration from `/settings/workspace`. That difference matters for the decision below.

## Not everything it writes is residue

The same method writes several files. They are **not** the same kind of thing, and treating them uniformly would be a bug:

| Written | What it is | Should OT hide it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.mcp.json` / `.cursor/mcp.json` / `.vscode/mcp.json` | The editor config the user **asked for**. Merged into any existing file via `mergeManagedMcpServers`. | **No.** It is the user's file; a team may legitimately commit it. Excluding it would be actively wrong. |
| rules dir (`.claude` / `.cursor/rules` / `.vscode`), skill dirs | Directories created for the user's editor. Git does not track empty dirs. | **No.** |
| `.openthrottle/workspace-editors.json` | **OT's own bookkeeping** — an on-disk identity anchor the user never asked for. | **Yes.** This is the residue. |

So the scope is exactly one file.

## Why (b) "move it out of the repo" is ruled out

The ledger pattern from `b409da6e` does not transfer. `RepositoryInspectionService` reads this manifest **from inside the repo root** (`repository-inspection.service.ts`, `OPENTHROTTLE_MANIFEST_RELATIVE_PATH`) to recover `repositoryId` + `checkoutId` and reconcile a **moved or re-added folder** to its existing DB rows. An out-of-repo store keyed by path would lose the anchor in precisely the case it exists for. Being in-repo is the feature.

Option (c) "clean up on teardown" has no trigger either — unlike the injected skill layer, this config is meant to persist.

## Direction: (a) exclude the manifest, via the managed-exclude-block mechanism

Verified: excluding the single file removes the whole `?? .openthrottle/` entry, because git does not report an untracked directory whose only file is ignored.

```
?? .openthrottle/                                  # before
echo '/.openthrottle/workspace-editors.json' >> .git/info/exclude
                                                   # after: clean
```

## The trap — the shared helper cannot be reused as-is

`writeManagedExcludeBlock` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/foreign-skill-injection/git-exclude.ts`) is `@public` and already reachable — `nestjs-repositories` depends on `openthrottle-agentic-utils` and there is no reverse dependency, so no cycle. **But:**

- its markers are **hardcoded constants** (`GIT_EXCLUDE_BEGIN_MARKER` / `..._END_MARKER` in `types.ts`), and they literally say `foreign-skill-injection`;
- it **replaces the block wholesale** — `stripManagedBlock` then re-emit.

So a naive reuse makes the two features clobber each other. Worse, whichever runs second wins: if applying editor config strips foreign-skill-injection's block, every injected skill becomes visible again and **`b409da6e` silently regresses**.

The marker must be parameterized (one managed block per feature) before this is wired up.

## Non-goals

- Excluding the editor config files themselves. They are the user's.
- Changing the manifest's location, shape, or its role as the identity anchor.
- Touching foreign-skill injection's behavior beyond making its exclude helper multi-tenant.

## Related

- OT `b409da6e` — foreign-skill injection symlinked-target-dir fix; the reference implementation and the thing that must not regress.
- `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md` — non-mutation guarantee and §4a.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/docs/workspace-settings-graphql-design.md` — documents the manifest write.
summary: Applying editor config writes .openthrottle/workspace-editors.json into the user's repo and leaves it untracked, so git status is dirty. Exclude just the manifest — but the shared exclude-block helper has a hardcoded marker and replaces wholesale, so it must be parameterized first or the two features clobber each other.
title: Hide OT's workspace-editors manifest in foreign repos (untracked .openthrottle/ residue)

author: visormatt
description:
The `/skills/:slug` detail loader and action cannot read or write a personal-tier skill, even though the index already lists them.

## Why it fails today

A personal skill lives at `~/.openthrottle/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` (override: `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_DIR`) and is only linked into the repo as a gitignored symlink under `.agents/skills/` (and the other `AGENT_SKILL_DIRS`). See `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md` §7.

Discovery already flags that case: `discoverRepoSkills` sets `isPersonal: true` and `source: 'external'` when the skill folder's realpath escapes the repo (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/agents/data/discover-repo-skills.server.ts`). The index loader uses that list directly, so `/skills` shows the Personal badge and filter. The detail route does not.

`readSkillFileBySlug` (`app/routing/skills/data/read-skill-file.server.ts`) re-discovers, then runs a realpath containment check that requires the SKILL.md to resolve **inside the monorepo root**. After realpath a personal skill is outside, so the helper returns `entry: undefined` and `skills.$slug.tsx` 404s.

`writeSkillFileBySlug` has the same containment check **plus** a provenance gate: `entry.source !== 'openthrottle'` refuses. Personal skills carry `source: 'external'` (they are not authored under `skills/`), so even a relaxed path check would still refuse the save. `useSkillDetail` mirrors that gate (`canEdit = editable && source === 'openthrottle'`), so the editor is unreachable from the UI.

The route module itself stays thin. `skills.$slug.tsx` already delegates to those two server helpers; this plan changes the helpers (and the one UI gate that would otherwise leave the write path dead). Do not grow the route file.

## Required behaviour

- **Read:** a discovered personal skill at `/skills/:slug` returns the same shape as an authored skill: `content`, `rawContent`, `metadata`, `editable: true`, `entry.isPersonal === true`.
- **Write:** saving a personal SKILL.md writes through the discovered `repoRelativePath` (the in-repo symlink) so the file under the personal root is updated. Never replace the symlink with a real directory/file — that would break `ot-skill-sync` and risk staging a personal skill. Frontmatter still re-validates before any write (`validateAgentAssetFrontmatter`, slug must match).
- **Still refused:** lockfile-installed external skills (`source: 'external'` and not personal); any realpath that is in neither the monorepo nor the currently-resolved personal root (rogue/dangling/other-home-dir links); unknown slug; null monorepo root (deployed app).
- **Personal root contract:** use `resolvePersonalSkillsRoot()` from `@openthrottle/openthrottle-agentic-utils` (already a dependency of `openthrottle-developer`). **Never** `resolvePersonalSkillsDir()` — that is the foreign-injection wrapper gated by `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_ENABLED` (default off). In-repo personal is presence-opt-in, same as `sync.sh` (§7.1). Membership in the **currently-resolved** personal root is the test, not "anything outside the repo" (§7.3). Honour `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_DIR`.
- **Tighten `isPersonal` in discovery** while here: today any realpath that escapes the repo is flagged personal. Align with §7.3 so `isPersonal` is true only when the skill folder realpath is under `resolvePersonalSkillsRoot()`. A rogue outside-repo link stays discoverable as ordinary `external` (not Personal) and remains unreadable/unwritable via the allowlist.

## Implementation notes

- Extract the duplicated `isPathInsideRoot` in the read and write helpers into one allowlist: realpath of the target is allowed iff it is under the monorepo root **or** under the realpath of `resolvePersonalSkillsRoot()`. Keep deriving the absolute target strictly from the discovered `repoRelativePath` — never from client input.
- Write provenance gate becomes: allow when `source === 'openthrottle'` **or** `isPersonal === true`. Provenance still comes from freshly discovered disk, never from the client or from a frontmatter `source:` key.
- GraphQL merge (`mergeRepoSkillsWithProjectSkills`) already spreads `isPersonal` through. The write helper talks to `discoverRepoSkills` directly, so it sees the disk flag. Do not invent a third `SkillSource` — personal stays a local overlay.
- CI has no `~/.openthrottle/skills`. Tests must use a temp dir as the personal root (and/or set `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_DIR` for the test process). Absence of the personal root must stay byte-identical to today for authored/external paths.

## Out of scope

- Promote/demote CLI (`skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/personal.sh`).
- Foreign-workspace injection / `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_ENABLED`.
- Custom-prompt `filePath` writes (`resolveCustomPromptWritePath` already refuses `SKILL.md`).
- Ingesting personal skills into `project_skills` / changing GraphQL `SkillSource`.
- Creating new personal skills from the UI (this is read/update of skills already linked in by sync).

## Manual verification

With a personal skill linked in (e.g. `test-personal-skill` under the personal root, synced into `.agents/skills/`):
1. `/skills` lists it with the Personal badge.
2. `/skills/<slug>` renders the SKILL.md body (not 404).
3. Edit + Save persists to `~/.openthrottle/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` (or the override dir); `git status` does not pick up a real file under `.agents/skills/`.
4. An external lockfile-installed skill is still read-only.
5. An authored `skills/<slug>` skill still reads and writes as today.
title: Skill detail: read and write personal-tier SKILL.md

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal Add the shared `GlobalFeatureOnboarding` component (`packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalFeatureOnboarding.tsx`) to the Repositories settings route so a brand-new user (no repositories yet) sees a "teach-me-fast" empty state instead of the current plain paragraph. Mirror the established convention used by Rules, Plans, and Schedule. ## Reference pattern (Rules / Plans / Schedule) Each feature wires onboarding in three cooperating pieces, sharing ONE typed copy object (`GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent`): 1. **Copy** at `app/routing//data/data.copy.ts` — a `_ONBOARDING: GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent` object (fields: `cta`, `icon` (LucideIcon), `internalUsage`, `steps[]`, `tagline`, `title`, `useCases[]`, `whatItIs`, optional `secondary`). 2. **Block** (`renderAs="block"`, the default) — rendered only when the list is genuinely empty AND unfiltered, replacing the toolbar/table. 3. **Modal + trigger** — `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal content={...}` rendered unconditionally (URL-driven via `?modal=onboarding`), and a `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger` placed in the page-heading action slot so the pitch stays reachable once the list is populated. All three exports (`GlobalFeatureOnboarding`, `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal`, `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger`) and the `GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent` type are barrel-exported from `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global`. ## Current state of the Repositories feature - Route: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.repositories._index.tsx` — loader returns `repositories: data.workspaceRepositories` plus `discoveredFolders`, `pickerCapabilities`. Renders `` inside ``. No onboarding wiring yet. - Section: `app/routing/settings/repositories/components/RepositoriesSection.tsx` — renders `GlobalHeading` (icon `FolderGit2Icon`, hardcoded title "Repositories") with `CloneRepoDialog` + `AddFolderDialog` in the action slot, then a section description. Current empty state (lines ~110-125): ```tsx {repositories.length === 0 ? (

{WORKSPACE_FOLDERS_COPY.repositoriesEmpty}

) : (
    {repositories.map(...RepositoryCard...)}
)} ``` - **No `data/` folder exists** under `settings/repositories/` yet — feature copy currently lives one level up at `app/routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts` as `WORKSPACE_FOLDERS_COPY`. ## Key divergences from the reference features (call out during implementation) - **No filters/search on this route** — the empty condition is simply `repositories.length === 0` (no `&& !isFiltered` clause). - **No `*Introduction` component** — Repositories renders its heading + action slot directly inside `RepositoriesSection`, so both the trigger and the block live in the section (Rules puts the trigger in a separate `RulesIntroduction`). Keep everything in `RepositoriesSection`. - Reuse the existing `FolderGit2Icon` for `content.icon` to stay visually consistent with the heading. ## Acceptance - New user (zero repositories) sees the `GlobalFeatureOnboarding` block instead of the plain empty paragraph. - Once repositories exist, the list renders as today and the pitch remains reachable via the "How it works" trigger + `?modal=onboarding`. - Copy is single-sourced from a new `settings/repositories/data/data.copy.ts` and typed `GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent`. - typecheck + lint + test green for `openthrottle-developer`; route render test covers both empty and populated states. ## Out of scope - No GraphQL/schema/loader changes (the `repositories` list is already available). - No changes to Rules/Plans/Schedule.
summary: Wire the shared GlobalFeatureOnboarding teach-me-fast empty-state (and its modal + trigger) into the Repositories settings route, mirroring the Rules/Plans/Schedule pattern.
title: Add GlobalFeatureOnboarding to settings.repositories._index route

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Programmatic (BullMQ) plan runs must default to a **cursor** backend running in a **dedicated git worktree that OpenThrottle creates itself**, with **verbose agent logging**, and with the run's **workspace bound to that worktree** (working directory, `plan_runs.checkout_id`, and `run_config_snapshot.workspace`). Today only the backend default (`cursor`) is right; the rest default to "no worktree, no verbose, run in whatever cwd the server process has".

`cursor` stays the default backend deliberately: Claude requires a different payment model for this kind of unattended programmatic invocation, so the queue must not silently route to it.

## Decision (settled 2026-08-20)

**Option A — OpenThrottle creates the worktree.** The server provisions the worktree via the single sanctioned entrypoint `pnpm run worktree:new <name>` (`scripts/create_worktree.sh`) and passes the resulting absolute path as the run's `workingDirectory`. The agent CLI's `-w` / `--worktree` flag stays **off** for queued runs, so there is exactly one worktree per run and the path is known up front — which is what checkout registration, `.env` provisioning, and per-path agent-CLI MCP approval all require. Option B (let the agent CLI create it and discover the path afterwards) is rejected.

Second decision from the same conversation: **centralize where worktrees live.** `scripts/create_worktree.sh:115` currently hardcodes `BASE_DIR="$(dirname "$REPO_ROOT")/openthrottle-worktrees"`. That root becomes configurable so every agent (Claude, Cursor, Ralph, the BullMQ worker) puts its worktrees in one predictable, user-chosen place. See the dedicated task for the precedence chain and the in-repo-vs-sibling trade-off.

## Decisions settled by task 1 (2026-08-20)

Recorded in full in `docs/openthrottle/plan-run-worktrees.md`.

- **Naming** — `plan-<first 8 chars of the plan UUID>` (e.g. `plan-5e172b67`), so the branch is `openthrottle/plan-5e172b67`. Deterministic (survives a plan retitle), collision-free, already within the `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` set `create_worktree.sh` sanitizes to, and short enough to read in `git branch` and a PR.
- **Lifecycle** — one worktree per **plan**, reused across runs. Ralph runs are iterations of the same work landing as one branch and one PR; reuse preserves branch history and keeps disk flat, where per-run worktrees would multiply ~2 GB `node_modules` trees per iteration.
- **Cleanup** — no automatic removal. Removal stays manual (`git worktree remove`) until a dedicated sweep lands as a follow-up; safe automatic removal requires a clean tree, no unpushed commits, no active run, and an age floor. Ceiling: one worktree per plan that has ever run programmatically.
- **Failure policy** — fail the run fast, with the provisioner's stderr in the plan output stream. A fallback to the process cwd silently drops the agent into the primary checkout, which is the bug this plan fixes.
- **Timing** — at job start in the orchestrator, not at enqueue: a run queued for hours should not hold a worktree, and it keeps `validateWorkingDirectory`'s existence check honest (the enqueue payload carries a worktree *name*; only an explicit caller-supplied `workingDirectory` is existence-checked).
- **Concurrency** — idempotent provisioning (reuse an existing linked worktree at the target path) plus per-path serialization in-process. The plans worker is `concurrency: 1`, so this guards re-runs after a stall and multi-instance deployments.

## Current state (verified in-repo)

- `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.constants.ts` — `DEFAULT_PLAN_RUN_RALPH_RUNNER = 'cursor'`. No worktree/debug defaults exist.
- `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.defaults.ts` — `getDefaultPlanRunConfigRalphV1()` returns `debugCli: 'omit'`, `worktreeCli: 'omit'`, `worktreeName: ''`, `worktreeBase: ''`, `skipWorktreeSetup: false`; `workspace` is all-empty (`checkoutId`, `repositoryId`, `workingDirectory`).
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/enqueue-plan-ralph-tuning.ts` — `parseEnqueueRalphTuning` only forwards what the caller sent; `resolvePlanRunExecutionBackend` falls back to `'cursor'`. Nothing injects worktree or debug when the caller omits them, so **API / scheduled-agent-job / rule-driven enqueues get no worktree and no verbose**, regardless of what the developer UI shows.
- Every queued run is now `runKind: 'orchestrator'` (in-process, no nested `workflow-ralph` spawn) — see `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/plans/plans.types.ts`. The legacy `WORKTREE_TARGETS` pooled-worktree path in `plans.processor.ts` is dead commentary.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/agentic-ralph/agentic-ralph-orchestrator.service.ts` computes `configCwd = getWorkflowConfigCwd(jobData.workingDirectory, process.env)` and calls `maybeRegisterWorktreeCheckout({ filesystemPath: configCwd })`. When the agent CLI creates its own worktree via `-w`, `configCwd` is the **parent repo**, not the worktree — `RepositoryInspectionService.scan()` reports `isLinkedWorktree: false` and registration is skipped, leaving `plan_runs.checkout_id` NULL. This is the core "workspace isn't bound to the worktree" bug.
- Worktree is currently a passthrough agent-CLI flag: `context.worktree` / `worktreeBase` / `skipWorktreeSetup` → `iterationRunner.run()` → `runIterationAsync` → `-w` on `cursor-agent` (`tools/workflows/src/utils/ralph-worktree-cli.ts`). The orchestrator never learns the resulting path, and `agentCwd` is unchanged.
- `scripts/create_worktree.sh` already handles three invocation modes (CLI arg, Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook payload on stdin, provision-in-place), prints ONLY the absolute worktree path on stdout, allocates a deterministic port block via `scripts/worktree_ports.sh`, and provisions through `scripts/setup_worktree.sh`. The server-side provisioner consumes exactly this contract — it does not reimplement it.

## Target behavior

1. **Worktree by default.** A run enqueued with no explicit worktree config gets one, created by OpenThrottle, with a deterministic collision-free name derived from the plan/run.
2. **Verbose by default.** `debugCli: 'verbose'` in stored defaults *and* injected at enqueue when the caller omits it, so `--verbose` reaches the agent CLI and the run output stream.
3. **Workspace = the worktree.** The orchestrator's `agentCwd`, the registered `repository_checkouts` row, `plan_runs.checkout_id`, and `run_config_snapshot.workspace.workingDirectory` all point at the worktree this run created.
4. **Defaults are server-side, not UI-side.** Every enqueue path (GraphQL mutation, scheduled agent jobs, tag-action rules, Ralph CLI handoff) inherits them; the developer UI just reflects the same shared defaults.
5. **One configurable worktree root** shared by every agent and by the BullMQ worker.

## Known traps (from prior work)

- A fresh worktree path needs its own agent-CLI MCP approval and a valid `.env`; a stale `.env` shows up as a password prompt. See the recent `make scheduled agent runs reach their MCP servers` / `warn when a provider cannot reach workspace MCP` commits — the new default multiplies how often this path is hit.
- `pnpm run worktree:new` is the ONE provisioning entrypoint; a bare `git worktree add` only self-heals on first `:dev`.
- Existing plans already have persisted `run_config` JSON. New defaults must apply to new plans and to omitted fields, without silently rewriting a plan the user deliberately configured.
- Worktrees accumulate on disk; unbounded creation per run is a real cost.
- Moving the worktree root does not relocate existing worktrees — `git worktree` stores absolute paths in `.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`. Changing the root affects new worktrees only.

## Out of scope

- Changing the default backend away from `cursor`.
- Interactive chat runs (`react-router-chat`) — this plan is the BullMQ/programmatic path only.
- Any worktree pooling / `WORKTREE_TARGETS` revival.
- Migrating or relocating worktrees that already exist under `../openthrottle-worktrees`.
- An automatic worktree-cleanup sweep (deferred per the task-1 cleanup decision).
title: BullMQ plan-run defaults: always worktree, verbose logging, workspace bound to the worktree

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

On plan detail (`/plans/:id`), `PlanDetailTabsList` renders `PlanCheckoutSelector`, which delegates to `ChatCheckoutSelector` from `@openthrottle/react-router-chat`. That trigger is sized for the chat composer: it renders a folder icon, the (possibly `owner/repo`-promoted) label, an optional `+N`, and a branch chip inside an `h-8 w-auto max-w-56` button. In a tabs row that already holds Overview / Tasks / Output / editor actions / Configuration, that button dominates the row — the copy is far too large for what is a rarely-touched, in-place course-correct control.

## Goal

Give the selector an icon-only presentation, driven from the plan surface:

- `PlanCheckoutSelector` gains `minimal?: boolean` (default `false`) and `minimalHint?: string`.
- When `minimal` is true, the trigger shows ONLY the `FolderGit2` icon (no label, no `+N`, no branch chip) and is hover-explained by a tooltip.
- Default behavior is unchanged for every existing caller, chat composer included.

The plan-detail call site is already written as `minimal={true}` in the working tree (uncommitted edit to `PlanDetailTabsList.tsx`); this plan makes that prop real.

## Approach

The trigger lives in the shared package, so `minimal` has to be threaded:

`PlanCheckoutSelector` (app) → `ChatCheckoutSelector` (package) → `ChatCheckoutSelectorTrigger` (package)

Do NOT try to fake this with app-side CSS that hides the label — the label span, `+N` and branch chip are the trigger's own markup, and hiding them from outside leaves the accessible name and the button's width padding wrong.

### Accessibility

Icon-only means the visible label disappears, so the accessible name must not. The trigger already sets `aria-label="Checkout"`; in minimal mode it should carry the resolved label too (e.g. `Checkout: openthrottle/monorepo`, or the placeholder / empty label when nothing is selected), so a screen reader still hears which checkout is selected.

### Tooltip precedence in PlanCheckoutSelector

`PlanCheckoutSelector` today wraps the selector in a `Tooltip` ONLY in its two failure states (empty registry, stale/de-registered selection), deliberately, so a healthy selector's tooltip never hovers over its own open popover. Minimal mode changes that: with no visible copy, the healthy state needs a tooltip too.

Precedence: `emptyRegistryHint` / `staleCheckoutHint` still win — they explain a broken state and are more important than a name. Otherwise, in minimal mode, show `minimalHint` (prop) falling back to a new `PLAN_CHECKOUT_SELECTOR_COPY.minimalHint` default. In non-minimal mode nothing changes.

Radix tooltips close on pointer-down, so the tooltip-over-open-popover concern is bounded, but verify it live rather than assuming.

## Constraints

- `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` components only; no new primitives.
- Component section comments (`// Hooks`, `// Setup`, …) stay, even when empty.
- Copy strings belong in the nearest `data/data.copy.ts`, not inline in the component.
- `ChatCheckoutSelectorTrigger` must keep forwarding its ref and spreading `...rest` — Radix `PopoverTrigger asChild` injects handlers/ref through it, and swallowing them silently breaks the picker.
- New/changed package exports that are public API need a JSDoc `@public` tag (Knip).
- Watch the component line cap; run the check AFTER prettier, not after lint.

## Out of scope

- The cmdk fuzzy-filter tightening tracked separately (OT `d72565fd`).
- Any change to multi-select / context-directory behavior.
- Changing which surfaces render the selector.
summary: Add a `minimal` (icon-only) mode to the checkout selector trigger and expose it on PlanCheckoutSelector with a configurable `minimalHint` tooltip, so the plan-detail tabs row stops carrying full "owner/repo · branch" button copy.
title: Minimal (icon-only) checkout selector for the plan-detail tabs row

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

Now that worktree placement is settled (one root ladder, `<org>/<repo>` beneath it, shared by `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/root.sh` and `worktree-root.resolver.ts`), `/settings/repositories` should be quiet when everything is fine. It isn't. On a normal machine the page currently renders ~20 bullets under **"Some worktrees may be missing from this list"**, none of which are actionable, and all of which describe states that are perfectly healthy.

Observed on `visormatt/round-eight` at `localhost:6020/settings/repositories` with 9 registered repositories:

```
worktree root /home/demo/.openthrottle/worktrees/atlasworksinc/atlasworks could not be read: ENOENT ...   (x7)
git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir failed in /home/demo/Development/monorepo-worktree-two ...
git status --porcelain failed in /home/demo/Development/monorepo-worktree-two ...
git branch --show-current failed in /home/demo/Development/monorepo-worktree-two ...   (x3 for each of 4 dead paths)
git worktree list --porcelain failed in /home/demo/Desktop/example-folder: fatal: not a git repository
```

## Root causes (all in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/worktree-discovery/worktree-discovery.service.ts`)

1. **`collectFromRootScan` warns on every `readdirSync` failure.** `resolveRoots()` derives `<root>/<org>/<repo>` for *every* registered primary checkout, but that directory is only created when the first worktree is made. A repository with zero worktrees therefore produces a guaranteed `ENOENT` warning, forever. **This is the stated case: a repo with no worktrees is "all good" and must be silent.**

2. **One stale `git worktree list` entry produces four probe failures.** `git worktree list --porcelain` keeps reporting worktrees whose directories were deleted until someone runs `git worktree prune`. `collectFromGitWorktreeList` adds them as candidates with no existence check (unlike `collectFromRootScan`, which gates on `isLinkedWorktreeDirectory`). `describe()` then fires `branch` + `status` + `rev-parse` at a path that does not exist -> 3 warnings each, plus a silent `aheadCount` failure. 4 dead paths = 12 bullets for one actionable fact.

3. **A per-repository condition is reported page-wide.** A registered folder that is not a git repo (`/home/demo/Desktop/example-folder`) fails `git worktree list` on every load. That belongs on that repository's row, not in a page footer list.

4. **`worktreeRoot` is singular but N roots are scanned.** The notice says "Scanning for worktrees in `<first root>`" while the warnings name seven other roots. The copy misrepresents what happened.

5. **Warnings are raw internal command strings.** `WorktreeDiscoveryNotice` renders `readonly string[]` as an always-expanded, unbounded `<ul role="alert">` at the bottom of the page. Even after 1-4, the residual set needs a count-first, collapsible presentation.

## Shape of the fix

Do **not** simply suppress warnings - the surface exists precisely so a half-working scan says so. Replace the free-text `warnings: string[]` with a typed, classified problem list so the server decides *what happened* and the UI decides *how loud it is*:

```ts
WORKTREE_DISCOVERY_PROBLEM = {
  CAP_EXCEEDED, CHECKOUT_LIST_FAILED, NOT_A_GIT_REPO,
  PROBE_FAILED, ROOT_UNREADABLE, STALE_WORKTREE_ENTRY,
} as const
```

with `{ detail, kind, path }` per entry. A root that simply does not exist (`ENOENT` / `ENOTDIR`) is **not a problem at all** and emits nothing; `EACCES` and friends still emit `ROOT_UNREADABLE`. Stale git entries collapse to one `STALE_WORKTREE_ENTRY` per path with a `git worktree prune` remedy. `NOT_A_GIT_REPO` carries a `repositoryId` so the table can badge the row.

## Constraints

- `warnings: [String!]!` is live schema. Add the typed field alongside it and mark the old one `@deprecated(reason: ...)` - never remove a field on an existing type without a migration plan (CLAUDE.md).
- Discovery must stay non-fatal and bounded: no new unbounded fs walk, no new unbounded git probe, every failure still degrades to data rather than an exception.
- Copy lives in `data/data.copy.ts`; no sentence-length literals in components.
- Every component change ships with its `__tests__` sibling updated; `component` not `screen`, `userEvent` not `fireEvent`.

## Gates

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-server:test`, then for `openthrottle-developer`: `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`. GraphQL changes require the boot-the-server -> `codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router` -> commit `schema.gql` + `__generated__` flow.
summary: Reclassify worktree-discovery warnings so the common healthy states (repo with no worktrees, stale git worktree entries, a registered folder that is not a git repo) stop rendering as a wall of raw git errors under /settings/repositories.
title: Repositories settings: stop treating "no worktrees" as a scan failure

author: visormatt
description:
Found while validating CI sharding on a fat affected graph (plan `b19377d1`, task `befc47c3`). **Pre-existing and independent of sharding** — reproduced locally with no matrix involved.

## Symptom

`@openthrottle/agentic-hooks:bundle-hooks-check` fails on a clean checkout:

```
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "@openthrottle/nodejs-utils"
    packages/agentic-hooks/src/adapters/cursor/payload.ts:9:25
  The module "./dist/src/index.js" was not found on the file system:
    packages/agentic-hooks/node_modules/@openthrottle/nodejs-utils/package.json:13:16
```

Observed on CI run `32198879567` (all three shards). Reproduced locally with:

```bash
rm -rf packages/nodejs-utils/dist
pnpm exec nx run @openthrottle/agentic-hooks:bundle-hooks-check --skip-nx-cache
```

Restoring `packages/nodejs-utils/dist` makes it pass again.

## Root cause

Two gaps that only fail together:

1. **`bundle-hooks` and `bundle-hooks-check` declare no `dependsOn`** (see the `nx.targets` block in `packages/agentic-hooks/package.json`). They esbuild-bundle `packages/agentic-hooks/src/**`, which imports `@openthrottle/nodejs-utils`, so they need that dependency materialized — but Nx is never told, and so never schedules it.
2. **`@openthrottle/nodejs-utils` has no target that emits `dist/src/index.js`.** Its `exports` map points at `./dist/src/index.js` / `./dist/src/index.d.ts`, but its `nx.targets` are `__build: {}` / `__build-package: {}` (prefixed, i.e. disabled) plus `lint`/`test`/`typecheck`. `typecheck` runs `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly`, producing the `.d.ts` but **not** the `.js` esbuild needs.

## Why nobody noticed

The failure is masked from both directions:

- **On CI:** `bundle-hooks-check` is `cache: true`, and its `inputs` do not include the dependency's `dist`. Once the target hash was recorded as passing, every later run cache-hits and the command never executes. It only ran for real on the fat-graph run above because an unrelated `nx.json` edit invalidated the hash.
- **Locally:** dev machines carry a stale `packages/nodejs-utils/dist` from some earlier build, so esbuild resolves it and the check passes.

Sharding did not cause this and did not fix it — the shard run simply happened to be the first real execution in a long time. Worth noting that project sharding *would* have surfaced it eventually anyway: with the dependency on a different box, co-scheduling can no longer accidentally satisfy it.

## Work

1. Decide the resolution shape. Either (a) give `@openthrottle/nodejs-utils` a real `build` target so its dist-pointing `exports` are honest, or (b) make `nodejs-utils` source-first (`main`/`exports` → `./src/index.ts`, like `@tools/dotfiles`) so esbuild bundles from source and no dist is needed. Note the constraint from prior work: packages the **server** imports need top-level exports resolving to `dist` for Docker type-stripping, so check whether `nodejs-utils` is server-consumed before choosing (b).
2. Add the missing `dependsOn` (`^build`, or whatever step 1 settles on) to **both** `bundle-hooks` and `bundle-hooks-check`.
3. Fix the cache correctness that hid this: the `inputs` for both targets must cover whatever the bundle actually reads, so a missing or changed dependency invalidates the hash instead of serving a stale pass.
4. Audit for siblings — any other `nx:run-commands` target that bundles or imports workspace packages without a `dependsOn` has the same latent bug.

## Success

`rm -rf packages/nodejs-utils/dist && pnpm exec nx run @openthrottle/agentic-hooks:bundle-hooks-check --skip-nx-cache` passes from a cold cache, because Nx builds what the bundle needs rather than relying on a leftover artifact.
title: Fix agentic-hooks bundle targets: undeclared dependency on nodejs-utils dist

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

In the ChatModelPicker left rail (the vertical column of icon-only agent selections), add a gear/settings icon **below** the agent selections. It links out to the developer app's `/settings/setup` route (the page where users enable/disable agents). The empty space between the gear icon and the existing agent icons should **grow** so the gear is pushed to the bottom of the rail, visually separated from the agent icons.

## Current state (verified)

`react-router-chat` is a purely presentational package — it hardcodes no agents and does NOT import `react-router`'s `Link`; it communicates via callbacks (`onSelect`, `onModelChange`, etc.). Navigation happens in the consuming developer app.

Key files:
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatModelPicker.tsx` — the two-column popover. The rail is the vertical flex column at ~lines 142-155: `<div className="bg-muted/40 flex max-h-80 flex-col gap-1 overflow-y-auto border-r p-1.5">` mapping `resolvedGroups` to `ChatModelPickerRailItem`.
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatModelPickerRailItem.tsx` — per-agent icon button (ghost `Button size="icon"` `size-9`, tooltip on the right). Icons come from `lucide-react` and custom brand SVGs.
- Consumers: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/{hooks/useHomeComposer.tsx,components/HomeComposer.tsx}` and `.../skills/{hooks/useRunSkillDialog.tsx,components/RunSkillDialog.tsx}`.

`/settings/setup` route exists and is live (`app/global/data/data.navigation.ts` uses `WrenchIcon`, `to: '/settings/setup'`). No Gear/Cog/Settings icon is currently imported in `react-router-chat` — use `lucide-react`'s `Settings` (or `Cog`).

## Design decisions

- **Presentational purity**: add an optional `onOpenSettings?: () => void` prop to `ChatModelPicker` (and thread through as needed). The picker renders the gear button and calls the callback; the developer-app consumer supplies the callback that navigates to `/settings/setup` (via `react-router`'s `useNavigate` or a `Link`). Do NOT import `react-router` into the chat package.
- **Spacing / push-apart**: the requirement is that the gap between the gear and the agent icons grows. Implement with a flex spacer inside the rail column: keep the agent items in a group at the top, insert a growing element (`<div className="flex-1" />` or `mt-auto` on the gear wrapper) so the gear pins to the bottom. Note the rail currently has `max-h-80` + `overflow-y-auto`; ensure the rail container establishes enough height for the spacer to actually grow (may need the rail to stretch to the popover content height, e.g. `min-h-full`/matching the right panel height) so the push-apart is visible even with few agents. Verify the scroll behavior still works when there are many agents.
- **Gear affordance styling**: reuse the same visual as `ChatModelPickerRailItem` (ghost `Button size="icon" size-9`, tooltip `side="right"` label e.g. "Agent setup", `aria-label`, `data-testid` e.g. `ChatModelPicker-rail-settings`) for consistency. Render it only when `onOpenSettings` is provided.

## Acceptance criteria

- A gear/settings icon appears at the bottom of the ChatModelPicker rail, below all agent selections, visually separated by growing space.
- Clicking it navigates to `/settings/setup` in the developer app (Home composer + Run Skill dialog consumers wired).
- Tooltip + aria-label present; keyboard focusable; matches existing rail item styling.
- No `react-router` import added to `react-router-chat`; navigation stays in the consumer.
- Existing rail scroll behavior with many agents is preserved.

## Validation

Source-first package (no build target). Run: `pnpm nx run react-router-chat:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`; then `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck` + `:test` as the integration check. Add/extend a render test asserting the gear button renders, has the right aria-label/testid, and invokes `onOpenSettings` on click.
summary: Add a bottom-pinned gear/settings icon to the ChatModelPicker left rail (below the agent selections) that navigates to /settings/setup, with a growing flex spacer pushing it apart from the existing agent icons.
title: ChatModelPicker: gear icon in rail linking to /settings/setup

author: visormatt
description:
# Roadmap proposals — 2026-08 (mid-month delta)

Companion to the first August run [`061025c8-b514-4b6d-b53e-623b7d0d663a`](061025c8-b514-4b6d-b53e-623b7d0d663a) (filed 2026-08-17). **That plan is still PENDING with all three tasks PENDING — still open, still relevant, not re-filed here:**

1. Merge-driven reconciliation (PR merge → work-ledger → plan status)
2. Real browser E2E suite in CI against a production build

This run only adds proposals that became legible from **2026-08-17 → 2026-08-21** activity and that are not already owned by an open plan.

## Where the last 30 days actually went

~200 non-merge commits; path churn dominated by `applications/openthrottle-developer` (~2300 file-touches), then `openthrottle-server`, `react-router-shadcn`, `react-router-chat`, `openthrottle-agentic-utils`. Hot files reinforce the same story: `conversation-stream.{service,resolver}.ts` (~13–14 touches), `schedule._index.tsx` (8), `scheduled-agent-jobs.*` and `plan-runs.*` repeatedly, plus generated GraphQL churn.
