Month's effort still maps to **Self-Host & Operate**, **Open Interfaces**, and increasingly **Orchestration Engine** (schedule + worktree + Ralph cwd). Now/Next/Later sections remain empty (last updated 2026-06-19) — effort-vs-priority gap analysis is still theme-level only.

That constellation *is* proposal 1 below — one large change wearing five disguises.

Also noted: many recent Job_* / sweep plans are PENDING with empty descriptions (process noise, not evidence of a missing abstraction). Chat-surface consolidation [`d246beb9`](d246beb9-be98-4933-95f4-6040d9086438) is COMPLETED — do not reopen.

## Method notes

- `semantic_search` returned **zero chunks** for every query this run (same failure mode as the 2026-08-17 run). `list_sources` and `list_plans_by_status` work; the vector path does not. Dedupe used plan lists + titles, not embeddings. That failure is itself evidence for proposal 2.
- Open PRs (~12) are mostly in-flight features, not a DONE-but-unmerged backlog illusion. The Aug-17 diagnosis that post-merge bookkeeping is the real residue still holds — see prior plan task 1.

## Considered and rejected

- **Re-file the three 061025c8 proposals** — still PENDING and unacted; noted above, not duplicated.

author: visormatt
description:
# ⛔ VERDICT: REJECTED on CI-time grounds — 2026-08-19

Measured by plan `88f747ff` (Phase A probes + baseline task `41133fc7`) at base commit `0e170105`, before anything moved. **Read this before re-proposing any of what follows.**

## The measurement that killed it

Heaviest CI unit (`openthrottle-developer`), deps warm, target forced cold:

| target | wall clock | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lint | 9.6s | 5.5% |
| typecheck | 10.6s | 6.1% |
| **test** | **154.1s** | **88.4%** |

`test` is ~88% of the cost. Splitting into libraries is the only lever that touches `lint`/`typecheck` — but that is just **11.6%** of the problem. Meanwhile **Vitest `--shard` splits the `test` slice within the single project**, config-only, and runs green on this suite today:

| shard | files | wall clock |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1/3 | 227 | **60.9s** |
| 2/3 | 226 | 54.6s |
| 3/3 | 226 | 48.4s |

### Head-to-head on the heaviest unit

| option | heaviest unit | reduction | cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 174.3s | — | — |
| **Vitest `--shard` 3-way** | **81.1s** | **−53%** | config + workflow only, **zero files moved** |
| coarse split (88f747ff Phase B) | ~134s | −23% | 1,255 files moved, 325 imports rewritten |
| this plan's 5-6 library split | worse than coarse per file moved | — | far more churn again |

**A config-only change beats the split by ~2.3x.** This plan's own *Risk / kill criteria* section named that fallback — "the fallback is a Vitest-level `--shard` split of this one project inside a single Nx target, which is strictly worse for lint/typecheck but does not require moving code." The kill criterion was met. The "strictly worse for lint/typecheck" caveat is true and turns out not to matter, because lint+typecheck is 11.6%.

## Second, independent finding: the partitioner would have eaten much of the win anyway

`scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts` deals applications first, then packages, on one global round-robin cursor. A new heavy PACKAGE (`developer-routing`) collides with `openthrottle-developer` on the same shard in **~30% of realistic affected sets** (Monte-Carlo, 20k samples). The obvious fix — an explicit heavy allowlist dealt in the applications pass — **does not work** (30% -> 25% only), because `@…` names sort ahead of application names. The fix that does work is an ORDERED heaviest-first deal (`HEAVY_ORDER = ['@openthrottle/developer-routing', 'openthrottle-developer']`), giving a structural 0%. Recorded in `88f747ff` task `d4d987ab` in case a heavy package ever appears for other reasons.

## What DID survive from this line of work

- The nested-`project.json` shortcut is **disproven and dangerous** — it produces no Nx edge and yields a **false cache hit that reports green** on stale inputs. Evidence in `88f747ff` task `0930f67f`. Never re-propose it.
- The extraction *mechanism* is sound — a source-first package under `packages/` gives a real Nx edge with correct invalidation, standalone targets, correct `affected` propagation, and Tailwind coverage (task `12c1babb`).
- The 21 `app/routing -> ~/routes/*` reverse imports are **fixed and merged** — see `88f747ff` task `8ab97f22`. That was independently valuable and is done regardless.

## If this is ever revived

**Only on architectural grounds** — the ~60 cross-domain `routing/X -> routing/Y` edges becoming intra-library, and a cleaner module boundary. Those are real. **The CI-speed argument below is dead and must not be reused.** Any revival must first beat the `--shard` numbers above.

Successor plan for the actual CI win: **`9fc16731`** — shard the developer Vitest suite across CI boxes with `--shard`.

---

# Original plan (retained for its coupling measurements, which are still accurate)

## Why

CI shards by PROJECT (`scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts` partitions the affected project list across 3 `ubuntu-latest` boxes). `openthrottle-developer` is ONE Nx project, so whichever box draws it runs 100% of it. That single project is the wall-clock floor for the whole matrix: **677 test files**, plus lint/typecheck over the entire app. Suite-level tuning has already been taken about as far as it goes (`vmForks` + `vmMemoryLimit: 512MB`, `maxWorkers: 4` — OT plan e448a51d, 253s -> ~83s). The only remaining lever is making the app more than one project.

> Verified 2026-08-19: 679 test files now (not 677); `app/routing` holds 529, `app/routes` 124, kernel-scope 26.

The existing folder convention already provides the seams. `app/routing/<domain>/` is 26 self-contained domain folders (components/hooks/data/config/utils/actions/testing) and `app/routes/*.tsx` is the thin React Router entry layer.

## Coupling (the actual work)

- **292** imports of `~/__generated__/graphql` from `app/routing` (+ 93 from `app/routes`). This is the linchpin — nothing extracts until generated types are consumable by name.
- **~60** cross-domain `~/routing/X -> ~/routing/Y` edges. Heaviest: `skills -> agents` (27), `skills -> home` (6), `projects -> prompts` (5), `personas -> agents` (4).
- ~~**17** reverse edges `app/routing -> ~/routes/*`~~ — **actually 21, and now FIXED** (88f747ff task 8ab97f22).
- **34** `~/testing/route-fixtures` + **41** `~/testing/root-match-fixture` uses; ~24 `~/global/data`, ~20 `~/services/graphql-ws-client`, plus `~/global/{config,hooks,utils,components}`. 70 files total across `global/ services/ testing/`.
- ~~**10** distinct `@/*` (`.react-router/types`) imports inside `app/routing`~~ — **actually 22**, still present, deliberately deferred.
- **89** of 90 `.tsx.graphql` documents sit next to `app/routes/*.tsx`; only **1** lives under `app/routing`. Documents stay with the route layer.

## Target shape (NOT proceeding — retained for reference)

Route modules CANNOT move — `routes.ts`, fs-routes, and `.react-router/types` typegen are app-scoped. The app keeps `app/routes/**`, `root.tsx`, `entry.*.tsx`, `styles.css`, and the colocated `.graphql` documents. Everything under `app/routing` was fair game.

Proposed source-first libraries under `packages/`: `developer-graphql`, `developer-kernel`, `developer-plans`, `developer-settings`, `developer-workspace`, and one or two for the tail. Per-domain libraries (26 of them) were explicitly NOT the goal.

## Non-negotiable constraints (still true, if ever revived)

- **Nx must SEE the edges.** The `~/*` path alias maps inside the app, so Nx infers no project dependency from it. **Proven empirically** in 88f747ff task 0930f67f: nested `project.json` produces a false cache hit that reports green. Extraction must go through real package names, top-level entry only.
- Tailwind already scans `@source '../../../packages/**/*.{css,ts,tsx}'` — **verified working** in task 12c1babb.
- Both codegen passes must keep working: the app's own (`enumsAsTypes: true`) and the divergent `@openthrottle/openthrottle-developer-codegen` pass (runtime enum objects). Do not "consolidate" them.
- Use `@tools/generators` to scaffold every new library — do not hand-write package skeletons.
- Nx `sync` is disabled (cf8469de); tsconfig `references` are manual. **Note:** `check:tsconfig-refs` does **not** exist on `main` — it ships with unmerged plan `cf8469de`.
- Each new lib needs tags (`pnpm nx:validate-tags`) and must pass knip; public API needs `@public` JSDoc.
- React Router test setup is shared: one `setupReactRouterTest` call. Do not re-add jsdom shims per lib.
summary: REJECTED ON CI-TIME GROUNDS (2026-08-19, plan 88f747ff). Measured: the heaviest unit is 88.4% `test`, so splitting buys ~23% while a config-only Vitest `--shard` buys ~53%. The kill criterion this plan wrote for itself was met — the `--shard` fallback won. Successor: 9fc16731. May only be revived on ARCHITECTURAL grounds, never the CI-speed argument below.
title: Split openthrottle-developer into sub-projects so CI sharding can distribute it

author: visormatt
description:
# Goal

Since this branch (`openthrottle/loop-plan-slash-commands`) was rebased, commit `1e7cb09d` landed the **route-primitive-shape** ESLint rule + repo-wide audit gate (`docs/monorepo/route-primitive-shape.md`). `pnpm audit` (→ `pnpm run "/^audit:.*:strict$/"`) now fails on this branch. Remediate every reported violation so the gate is green.

## What `pnpm audit` reports

`pnpm audit` runs three strict audits. The **failing gate** is `audit:route-shape:strict` (`scripts/audit-route-shape.ts --strict`), which exits non-zero on any **R1/R3** violation. `audit:component-shape:*:strict` currently passes but reports VR6 over-cap files.

- **R1 — disallowed named value exports** (2 files): the route module may export only the RR framework surface (`loader`/`action`/`meta`/`links`/`handle`/`headers`/`shouldRevalidate`/`middleware`/`clientLoader`/`clientAction`/`clientMiddleware`/`Layout`/`ErrorBoundary`/`HydrateFallback`/default Component) plus **type-only** exports. A value `export const` is an R1 violation → move it to `~/routing/<area>/config/` and import it back. `export interface`/`export type` are allowed and stay.
- **R3 — module-scope helpers/config/data** (35 files): any non-exported module-scope `const`/`function` (other than the default Component) must be hoisted into `~/routing/<area>/{utils,config,data,hooks}` and imported back. Values computed *inside* loader/action/Component bodies stay put.
- **R4 — over the 210-line cap** (19 route files): report-only in the audit (does NOT fail the strict gate) and `warn` in ESLint `max-lines`. Included in this plan by decision — split by hoisting per R3 and extracting sub-components into `~/routing/<area>/components/`.
- **VR6 — shadcn component over-cap** (3 files): report-only. Included by decision.

## The fix pattern (per the doc + generators)

For each route file: identify its feature `<area>` (the route's first segment, e.g. `plans`, `settings`, `skills`, `docs`, `faq`). Move each flagged symbol into the matching sibling folder under `app/routing/<area>/`:

- pure functions / mappers → `utils/`
- tunables / thresholds / windows / flags → `config/`
- option lists / column defs / static arrays+maps → `data/` (user-facing copy → `data/data.copy.ts`)
- stateful/behavioral logic that outgrows the Component → a co-located `use<Name>` hook in `hooks/`

Then import the symbol back into the route. If the `<area>/<subfolder>` subtree does not exist, scaffold it with the folders generator (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:folders ...`) rather than hand-creating. New pure `utils/` functions get a unit test (mirrors the `toSkillDetailUsageData` worked example in the doc). Never bypass the hook with `--no-verify` or add a `route-shape: opt-out` pragma unless a route is genuinely irreducible (near-zero expected use, written reason).

**R1 gotcha:** the two R1 consts (`MAX_FILE_MENTION_RESULTS`, `MAX_SLASH_COMMAND_RESULTS`) are imported by tests / hooks. After moving them to `config/`, update every importer (e.g. `app/routes/__tests__/ide.files.loader.test.ts`) and keep the route's exported response `interface`s where they are (type exports are allowed).

## Enforcement reference

- Gate: `scripts/audit-route-shape.ts` (R1/R3 fail `--strict`; R4 report-only). Rule level today is `warn` in `tools/dotfiles/src/index.ts` (`openthrottle/route-primitive-shape` scoped to `**/app/routes/**`), so `nx lint` does not break — the **audit gate** is the thing to satisfy.
- Doc: `docs/monorepo/route-primitive-shape.md` (R1–R5). Destination map: `tools/generators/src/generators/folders/CANONICAL_ROUTING_SUBTREE.md`.

## Acceptance (whole plan)

1. `pnpm audit` exits 0 (route + component strict audits clean of R1/R3; R4/VR6 down to zero given the chosen scope).
2. `pnpm nx affected --target=lint,typecheck,test` green for touched projects; `pnpm run check:local` green.
3. No `--no-verify`, no opt-out pragmas added (or each justified in the diff).
4. Commit per task with `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers.

Task ordering: developer app (largest) → admin → email → website → shadcn → final verification.
summary: Fix all route-shape audit violations (R1/R3 gate + R4 over-cap + shadcn VR6) so `pnpm audit` and check:local pass on this rebased branch.
title: Remediate route primitive-shape audit violations on the /skills slash-command branch

author: visormatt
description:
Split `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/**` into Nx feature packages, following the atlasworksinc/native-apps "feature packages" pattern — but only after the two prerequisites that would otherwise void the win, and only as far as the measurements justify.

## Why (measured 2026-08-29)

Per-project Vitest timings, `--skip-nx-cache`, one project at a time:

| Project | Test files | Duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| openthrottle-developer | 724 | 133.7s |
| openthrottle-server | 171 | 40.6s |
| react-router-shadcn | 226 | 39.1s |
| react-router-chat | 68 | 38.3s |
| (12 projects measured) | 1,505 of 1,963 repo-wide | 366.8s |

`openthrottle-developer` is 36% of test files and 36% of measured suite time — 3.3x the next-heaviest project, and a project is Nx's atomic unit.

**The runner-scaling argument does NOT motivate this work.** Vitest `--shard` already splits within the project at file granularity, which bin-packs better than project sharding; going 3 -> 6 boxes is a one-line `jobCount` change in `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml:212`. Project sharding would reintroduce a floor at the largest package. Measured lint (9s) and typecheck (24s) are not a meaningful un-shardable remainder either.

**The motivating argument is affected-set granularity**, which sharding does nothing for. Over the last 300 commits, 201 touched the developer app:

- 69% touched <= 1 routing feature (108 touched exactly one, 30 touched none)
- only 16% touched 3+

Today each of those reruns all 724 files and invalidates the whole app's Nx cache entry. With feature packages a plans-only change runs plans (~139) + the app's remaining route/global tests (~155) ~ 294 files — roughly 60% less work on the majority of commits, and it cuts local `nx affected` too, not just CI.

**Second argument: boundaries.** `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` `depConstraints` (`tools/dotfiles/src/index.ts:133`) only sees project edges; everything inside the app is unpoliced. There are 19 undeclared cross-feature edges today, including `skills -> agents` (31 imports), `settings -> dashboard`, `queues -> plans`, `dashboard -> navigation`.

## The two blockers

1. **`~/__generated__/graphql`** — 68 imports in `plans` alone, and 107 of the 201 commits touched `__generated__`. If every feature package depends on one generated types package, a schema change invalidates all of them and the granularity win evaporates. The escape hatch already exists: `@openthrottle/openthrottle-developer-codegen` is a real workspace package emitting typed ops from the same documents.
2. **`flatRoutes` file-system routing** (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes.ts`) pins route modules to `app/routes/`, and those are not thin — 12,173 lines, ~200 each with loaders. Routes therefore stay in the app; features become UI/hooks/utils packages with thin route modules calling in. That is why the post-split app suite is ~155 files, not zero.

## Shape of the work

Do NOT create 22 packages. The sizes are lopsided: `plans` (157 src + 139 test) and `settings` (152 + 131) are ~40% of the app between them; `personas` is 4 files. Migrate off `__generated__`, fix the cross-feature edges, extract `plans` as a pilot, measure, then decide.

Origin: analysis session 2026-08-29 (no code written, no branch). Packages are source-first React Router libs — no `build` target (see MONOREPO.md).
title: Extract openthrottle-developer routing features into feature packages

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

During a fresh `./scripts/setup.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts` mints service-account bearer tokens (`OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN`) and prints each **once** to stdout (bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts:136-141). In the wall of setup output these scroll past and are frequently missed. Because the mint path *skips* any account that already has an active credential (bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts:114-124), recovering a missed token is expensive: you must revoke the existing credential via admin GraphQL and re-mint. `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts` similarly echoes the seeded dev login (email/password) that a new machine needs.

## Goal

Write the bootstrap values to a **non-git-tracked file at the repo root** at mint time, so a user who misses the echoed stdout can recover them from disk WITHOUT having to expire/regenerate keys. The stdout echo stays; the file is an additional durable record.

## Approach

- Pick a root-level, git-ignored file (e.g. `.demo-workstation.local`) and add a `.gitignore` entry. Note `.env*` (`.gitignore:26`) already ignores any `.env*`-named file, so if the file is named under that pattern it's auto-ignored — but an explicit, clearly-named entry is preferred for discoverability.
- At mint time in `bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts`, append/write each minted `ENV_VAR=token` line to the file (secrets only exist at mint time — cannot be re-derived later, so persistence MUST happen in the mint branch). Keep the existing one-time stdout echo.
- Persist the default-user login (email/password + login URLs) from `bootstrap-default-user.ts` to the same file for convenience.
- Idempotency: a re-run that mints nothing must not clobber a still-valid file. Decide overwrite-vs-append and de-dup behavior in the design task.
- Update `databases/README.md` and any "shown once" setup docs to point at the file.

## Non-goals

- No change to token minting/verification logic or the env-provided upsert path.
- Not a secrets manager — this is a local convenience file, kept out of git for the same reasons as `databases/seed.sql`.

## Key files

- `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts`
- `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts`
- `scripts/setup.sh`
- `.gitignore`
- `databases/README.md`
title: Persist fresh-setup bootstrap values to a git-ignored local file

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The developer app's chrome has no "what am I looking at / how do I drive this?" affordance. The only help surface today is buried inside the metrics panel (`GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger` -> `?modal=ServerMetricsInfo`), which is route-scoped and hidden on most pages. A first-time operator has no in-app, linkable place that explains the commander (Cmd+K), the sidebar toggle (Cmd/Ctrl+B), plans/tasks, and where docs/FAQ/debug live — they have to leave the app.

## Primary user

**Human developer** using `openthrottle-developer` (secondary: agent operator who wants a shareable URL that opens orientation content).

## Jobs to be done

- As a developer on any authenticated route, I want a persistent info icon in the nav bar so I can get oriented without leaving the page.
- As a developer, I want the help state in the URL (`?modal=help`) so I can deep-link/share it and so back/forward behaves.
- As a maintainer, I want the trigger and the modal decoupled (URL is the source of truth) so the icon can live in the shared header while the dialog renders once at app root.

## Approach (follow the existing pattern, do not invent a new one)

Mirror the `GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger` / `GlobalMetricsInfoModal` pair in `packages/react-router-ui-global`:

- `useUrlSyncedOverlay({ param: 'modal', openValue: 'help' })` for both pieces — no shared React state, no context.
- `GlobalHelpModal` composes `GlobalModal` (`param="modal"`, `value="help"`), which already wraps shadcn `Dialog`/`DialogContent`.
- `GlobalHelpTrigger` is a ghost icon button rendered inside `GlobalLayoutHeader` (`packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalLayoutHeader.tsx`), next to `NotificationBell` / GitHub / sign-out.
- `GlobalHelpModal` renders once in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/root.tsx` in the overlays area alongside `OpenThrottleCommander`.
- Copy lives in `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/data/data.copy.help.ts` (currently-empty `src/data/` folder), per `.agents/rules/coding/component-data-boundaries.mdc`; the component imports it. Do not inline copy in the component and do not spec the pure copy file.

Note on generators: `@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=modal|component` targets `applications/<app>/app/...` via `--application`, so it does not scaffold into a package. Run `--describe` first to confirm; if there is no package-targeting generator, hand-author the two files following the `GlobalMetricsInfo*` pair exactly and say so in the task output.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] An info icon is visible in the nav bar (`data-testid="global-layout-nav"`) on every route that renders the global header, with an accessible label (e.g. `aria-label="Help and shortcuts"`).
- [ ] Clicking the icon sets `modal=help` on the current URL and preserves all other search params.
- [ ] Loading any URL that already has `?modal=help` opens the dialog on first render (no click required).
- [ ] Esc, overlay click, and the dialog close button remove only the `modal` param; other params and scroll position survive (`preventScrollReset: true`).
- [ ] The dialog has a `DialogTitle` + `DialogDescription` and is reachable by keyboard (focus trapped by Radix `Dialog`).
- [ ] Help content covers: what OpenThrottle is in one paragraph, Cmd+K commander, Cmd/Ctrl+B sidebar, plans/tasks basics, and links out to `/docs`, `/faq`, `/settings/debug`, and the GitHub repo.
- [ ] `GlobalHelpModal` + `GlobalHelpTrigger` are exported from `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/index.ts` (alphabetized).
- [ ] Existing `?modal=ServerMetricsInfo` behavior is unchanged (no key collision, no double dialog).
- [ ] `pnpm nx run react-router-ui-global:lint|test|typecheck` and `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint|test|build` all pass.

## UX notes

- Icon: `Info` from `lucide-react` (same icon as `GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger`) or the Phosphor equivalent already used in the header — match the header's existing `Button variant="ghost" size-6 rounded-full` treatment so it does not read as a bolted-on control.
- Placement: right cluster of the nav, before `NotificationBell`; wrap in `Tooltip` (`delayDuration={1_000}`) like `SidebarTrigger` does, with the shortcut hint in the tooltip once/if a shortcut lands.
- Tone: precise, no marketing fluff; `pnpm`/`nx` in any command examples; no Cursor attribution.
- Content structure: short lead paragraph, then a shortcuts list, then a "where to go next" link list. Reuse the muted/`text-sm` type scale from `GlobalMetricsInfoModal` rather than new sizes.
- Empty/error states: none — content is static copy, so there is no loading or failure path.

## Scope

**In v1:** trigger in the shared nav bar, modal at developer-app root, `?modal=help` URL sync, static copy module, tests, validation.

**Deferred (follow-up OT tasks):**
- "Open help with the `?` keyboard shortcut (global hotkey)"
- "Route-aware help: per-area help content keyed off pathname"
- "Add the help trigger to openthrottle-admin and openthrottle-email headers"
- "Add a Help row to OpenThrottleCommander that sets ?modal=help"
- "First-run help auto-open (once per user, persisted in config atom)"
summary: Add a persistent info icon to the shared nav bar (`GlobalLayoutHeader`) that toggles a new URL-synced `?modal=help` dialog rendered once at `openthrottle-developer` root. Mirrors the existing `GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger`/`GlobalMetricsInfoModal` + `useUrlSyncedOverlay` pattern in `packages/react-router-ui-global`; copy lives in `src/data/data.copy.help.ts`. v1 is static orientation content (commander, sidebar, plans/tasks, links to /docs, /faq, /settings/debug, GitHub). Keyboard shortcut, route-aware content, and other apps are deferred.
title: Global help modal: info icon in the nav bar toggling ?modal=help

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

The goal is converting Atlasworks leadership and engineering from "supportive to date" to fully bought in, which buys OSS OpenThrottle runway. Two distinct internal audiences need two distinct artifacts:

- **Engineers** convert by trying a feature that solves a problem they have this week → weekly, invitation-framed digest ("multi-repo chat landed — if you work across A and B, try this").
- **Leadership** converts on trajectory + evidence → monthly one-page brief: adoption/throughput chart, 2–3 "this happened because OT existed" stories, honest cost-per-outcome numbers, direction statement. Weekly cadence at leadership altitude reads as noise — keep it monthly.

Key strategic points from the design discussion:

1. **Two jobs, two layers.** Mechanical release notes (versioning, tags, commit lists) ≠ showcase. `nx release` is the right mechanical layer for this repo — conventional commits are already enforced by commitlint, squash merges + merge queue are in place, and nx release understands the project graph and tags. Do NOT add release-please or changesets on top (second versioning brain that doesn't know the Nx graph; changesets is a per-PR tax duplicating conventional commits).
2. **OT's own telemetry is the unfair advantage.** Plans, tasks, runs, token usage, and the work ledger (Plan-Id/Task-Id commit footers → plans) let the digest/brief make claims with receipts: "N plans executed, X PRs landed through the loop, cost per landed PR." The token-usage surfacing plan (OT a55b76ba) is the evidence engine for this — it's strategic, not a UI nicety.
3. **Cost is a trust tool, not a liability.** Voluntarily showing tokens + CI spend per outcome builds leadership trust; the CI cost-reduction work (OT 6ced8d0e) becomes a story ("cut CI cost by X while shipping more") instead of a discovered bill.
4. **Adoption evidence can't be automated around.** The honest chart currently has one user. Many people already have a local OT database on their machines — a dead-simple ask ("run this skill, shoot me the JSON") turns those installs into countable adoption data points, and the first non-Matt user story becomes the centerpiece of a leadership brief.
5. **The pipeline is itself a demo.** The weekly digest is written by an OpenThrottle scheduled job; say so in the post footer.

## Shape

- Weekly, automated: `nx release` (tags/versions/changelog/GitHub Release) + agent-written "This week in OpenThrottle" digest posted to a Atlasworks engineering Slack channel. Five bullets max, invitation-framed, screenshot/clip when visual.
- Monthly, curated: one-page leadership brief, agent-drafted from the month's digests + OT telemetry, human-edited (this is the one artifact where Matt's judgment is the product).
- Opportunistic: Season 1 demo videos (OT 48770ad9) for marquee features only.

## Related plans

Token usage surfacing a55b76ba (evidence engine), CI cost reduction 6ced8d0e (cost story), scheduled jobs infra 097c23b7 / scheduled-run metadata 2c9bd39e, YouTube Season 1 48770ad9.
summary: Turn OpenThrottle's shipped work into buy-in artifacts for Atlasworks: mechanical weekly releases via nx release, an agent-written weekly engineering digest, a monthly leadership brief with cost-per-outcome evidence, and a lightweight adoption-snapshot skill users can run against their local OT database.
title: Showcase pipeline: weekly release digest, leadership brief, adoption snapshots

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Turn OpenThrottle's real, already-out-of-pocket infrastructure bill into a credible sponsorship ask. Two halves:

1. **Mechanics** — a `.github/FUNDING.yml` so GitHub renders a **Sponsor** button on the repo (docs: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/displaying-a-sponsor-button-in-your-repository).
2. **Substance** — a short funding page that states what the money actually pays for, so the button converts instead of decorating. Today the owner personally pays for **Vercel**, **Blacksmith**, and **GitHub**; the near-term goal is a **fully self-deployed GCP stack**. `$100–$200/mo` of recurring sponsorship should visibly fund "OpenThrottle is a production-deployable toolset," not just a repo.

## The estimate comes first

The plan opens by rebuilding the cost model, because the numbers *are* the pitch. `infra/gcp-estimate.csv` (Cloud Pricing Calculator, us-west1, effective 2026-03-04) totals **$52.61/mo** across four SKUs — one E2, 10 GB SSD PD, Memorystore Redis Basic M1, and a zonal micro Cloud SQL + 7300 GB-mo storage — and it no longer describes the toolset:

- The Cloud SQL line is **MySQL**, but OpenThrottle is **Postgres + pgvector** end to end (`databases/`, `@openthrottle/nestjs-typeorm`, `semantic_search`). `infra/modules/gcp_cloud_sql_postgres` already exists; pgvector's index memory pushes off the smallest tiers.
- The single E2 assumes the server runs as `all`. `applications/openthrottle-server/src/config/process-role.ts` splits `api` / `worker` — production is two compute units.
- Services that exist in `docker-compose.yml` but not in the estimate: the OT MCP server, `whisper` (voice), run-once `migrations`/`bootstrap`, and local-Ollama embeddings. Plus the supporting bill entirely: Artifact Registry, Cloud Storage, Secret Manager, log/monitoring retention, egress, LB + certs.
- All four React Router apps currently deploy to **Vercel** (`applications/*/vercel.json`). Whether GCP takes them over is the single decision that moves both the GCP total and whether the Vercel bill is retired.
- The 7300 GB-mo (7.3 TB) storage row reads like a calculator default, not a projection.

So task 1 produces **two priced tiers, not one number** — **required** (the floor that actually runs: single env, single zone, no HA, honest about what breaks) and **desired** (staging + production, split API/worker, Memorystore Standard, HA or PITR, real retention). Task 2 then adds the real Vercel/Blacksmith/GitHub amounts, flags which a GCP move retires versus which persist, and reconciles everything against the ask. If required lands under $100 and desired over $200, that's a good outcome — it gives the tiers a natural shape ($100 keeps the lights on, $200 buys staging + production) and sponsorship somewhere to grow. Report real figures either way; don't tune them to fit.

## Other constraints

- **GitHub Sponsors requires owner enrollment** (Stripe Connect + tax/identity forms) before the `github:` key resolves; an unenrolled handle renders no button and no error. That is a human-only gate — see task 3. Nothing else is blocked by it: file, docs, and UI links can all ship and go live the moment enrollment completes.
- **Two remotes, unrelated histories**: `origin` = `OpenThrottle/monorepo` (canonical, private) and `openthrottle` = `OpenThrottle/OpenThrottle` (public mirror). **The public mirror is what visitors see, so that's where the Sponsor button matters** — confirm how the mirror is produced so `.github/FUNDING.yml` actually lands there. An org-level `.github` repo also exists (from the org-alignment licensing work) and can supply a default for every org repo.
- Licensing posture is settled and should be echoed, not re-litigated: open core, Apache-2.0 core with a separate EULA for commercial modules, trademarks reserved (`LICENSE.md`, `LICENSING.md`, `TRADEMARK.md`). Sponsorship copy must not imply sponsors get license or trademark rights.

## Non-goals

- **Not** performing the GCP migration or writing Terraform for it. This plan only *prices* it. The migration is separate work.
- Not setting up a legal entity, not changing licensing, not adding paid tiers/billing to the product.
- No fabricated sponsor counts, testimonials, or logos.

## Definition of done

Required and desired footprints are priced from the current stack and committed, `.github/FUNDING.yml` is in place (and present in whatever repo renders the public button), a funding page explains the cost model with numbers traceable to those estimates, README and the website footer link to it, and the only remaining step is the owner finishing platform enrollment.
summary: Add a GitHub sponsor button (.github/FUNDING.yml) plus an honest "where the money goes" cost page so a $100–$200/mo sponsorship tier visibly covers Vercel + Blacksmith + GitHub today and a full GCP production deploy next.
title: 🚀 Pre-launch: Sponsorship funding — FUNDING.yml + cost transparency

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`/skills` renders `SkillsIndexUsage` → `SkillUsageLeaderboard` ("Top skills"), ranked by invocation count over a 30-day window. The rows come from `skillUsage.bySkill` (harness-captured history); the on-disk skill list comes from `discoverRepoSkills(getMonorepoRoot())`. Today the only place those two sets meet is `linkableSlugs`: a row links to `/skills/$slug` when its `skillName` matches a discovered slug, and is rendered as plain text otherwise. Plain text is not a signal — a user cannot tell a renamed/deleted skill from a third-party one.

Early in adoption the ranking churns: skills get renamed, moved, deleted, or vendored away, and their history keeps them at the top of the leaderboard even though nobody can invoke them any more. The stats are worth keeping (they are real history), but they should not compete with live skills for the top of the list.

## Goal

1. **Signal presence.** Every leaderboard row carries an explicit presence state, not an inferred one.
2. **Split the two.** The main "Top skills" table ranks only skills present on disk. Rows with usage but no SKILL.md move to a separate, de-emphasized section below it. When there are none, that section does not render at all.

## Presence is a three-member vocabulary, not a boolean

`discoverRepoSkills` is repo-rooted: it scans `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.grok/skills`, `.opencode/skills` and deliberately excludes per-tool global dirs. A plugin-namespaced third-party row (`vercel:deploy`) therefore never matches a disk slug — but it is **not** missing, it is out of scan scope. Flagging it "missing from disk" would be a false positive on roughly every third-party row.

So the classification keys off `scope` as well as slug match:

| scope | slug on disk | presence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ours` | yes | `installed` |
| `ours` | no | `missing` |
| `third-party` | — | `external` |

Per `.agents/rules/coding/vocabularies.mdc` this is declared **once** with `vocabulary([...] as const)` from `@openthrottle/nodejs-parts-department` (see `routing/settings/data/agent-clis.data.ts` for the in-app precedent) and enumerated nowhere else: `.is()` for the guard, `.labelled()` for badge copy, `.subsetOf()` for "does this row link through". `linkableSlugs` stops being a prop in its own right — linkability is derived from presence (`installed` links, the other two do not), which keeps the two rules from drifting apart.

## Scope

- `applications/openthrottle-developer` only. No server, GraphQL schema, or migration changes — both routes already discover disk slugs (`routes/skills._index.tsx:~78`, `routes/usage._index.tsx:45`), so this is purely a classification + presentation change over data already in the loaders.
- `/usage` gets the same split, because `SkillUsageLeaderboard` is deliberately shared between the two routes and a divergence there is exactly the kind of drift this repo has been burned by.

## Prior art to match

- `SKILL_RECORD_TAGS_COPY.orphanBadge` ("Missing from disk") already names this exact condition for DB-only `projectSkills` orphans in `SkillsTable`. Reuse the wording so the two surfaces agree; do not invent a second phrase.
- Copy lives in `routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts` / `routing/usage/data/skill-usage-copy.ts`, never inline.
- Components follow the generated section-comment shape (`// Hooks` / `// Setup` / … / `// 🔌 Short Circuit`); the leaderboard table stays presentational and the partitioning happens in a `utils/` function.

## Non-goals

- No new "clean up dead usage rows" action — this is read-only signalling. Removing an orphaned `projectSkills` row already has its own affordance on the table.
- No change to the 30-day window, the chart, or the `skillUsage` query.
- Not merging this with the DB-side orphan concept; they are different sources (usage history vs `projectSkills`) that happen to share copy.
summary: Signal on the /skills (and /usage) "Top skills" leaderboard which skills with recorded usage are no longer present on disk, and split them out of the main ranked list so the primary table only ranks skills you can still invoke.
title: Split "Top skills" into installed vs missing-from-disk

author: visormatt
description:
# Centralize human-readable Zod error messages in `parseFormData`

## Problem

Now that route actions parse `FormData` through generated Zod schemas via `parseFormData` (`@openthrottle/react-router-graphql`, `packages/react-router-graphql/src/utils/form-data-schema.ts`), the *messages* that come out of `parsed.error` / `parsed.fieldErrors` are Zod's raw defaults — mostly generic `"Required"` (missing/undefined field) or `"String must contain at least 1 character(s)"` (empty string hitting `.min(1)`).

Root cause: the codegen (`@openthrottle/graphql-codegen`, `defineCodegen`, `typescript-validation-schema` with `notAllowEmptyString: true`) emits bare `z.string().min(1)` with **no message argument**. Nothing humanizes the field.

Consequence — the boilerplate we set out to delete just moved: actions call `parseFormData` and then **ignore `parsed.error`**, hard-coding per-field copy instead.

## Goal

Make `parsed.error` and `parsed.fieldErrors` carry good, human-readable messages **by default and centrally**, so actions can surface them directly without per-field handling — and so direct `safeParse` callers (MCP tools, loaders) can opt into the same messages.

## Approach (recommended)

**Centralized Zod `errorMap` inside `parseFormData`** — no codegen changes, works for every generated schema at once. Pass a custom `errorMap` to `schema.safeParse(raw, { errorMap })`; export a standalone `zodErrorMap` + `formatZodError(error, options)` so direct `safeParse` callers get identical messages.

## Decisions (from Task 1 spike)

- **Precedence needs NO detection.** Zod does not invoke a parse-level `errorMap` for any issue that already carries an explicit author message (`.min(1,'msg')`, `.refine(fn,'msg')` both confirmed to win). The map only ever sees default-message issues, so it fills defaults only.
- **Issue codes handled:** `invalid_type` + `received:'undefined'` → "{Label} is required."; `too_small` string `minimum===1` → "{Label} is required." / `minimum>1` → "{Label} must be at least {n} characters."; `invalid_enum_value` → "{Label} must be one of: …"; else `ctx.defaultError`.
- **Label rule:** last path segment → split camelCase + snake_case → sentence case (first word capitalized). `startIso`→"Start iso", `tag`→"Tag".
- **Override shape:** `ParseFormDataOptions.labels?: Record<path,string>` (swap the humanized label) and `messages?: Record<path,string>` (replace whole message for a path; wins over labels), both keyed by dot-joined path.

## Rejected alternative — codegen-level messages

Configuring `typescript-validation-schema` to emit messages was rejected: message support is coarse/per-scalar, it bakes copy into a ~5000-line generated file no one edits, it can't humanize per field path, and it can't be overridden per call.

## Out of scope

- Migrating generated schemas off the `zod/v3` compat subpath to native v4.
- Field-level i18n / localization.

## Validation

- `pnpm nx run react-router-graphql:test` (new error-map unit tests)
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test` (swept actions + specs)
- `pnpm run check:local`
title: Centralize human-readable Zod error messages in parseFormData

author: visormatt
description:
# Settings › Setup: per-model enable/disable + favorite models

## Context — this is a follow-up
Builds directly on **"Settings › Setup: agent CLIs as an actionable table + per-user enable/disable"** (OT plan `84d4a42b-ead1-4944-9bb0-6a171d39c427`), which introduces the compact `SettingsSetupTable`, per-user **agent-level** on/off persistence, and the downstream gate (hide from chat/model pickers + block new runs). Do not start until that plan's persistence + table land; this plan extends the same seams rather than inventing new ones.

## Goals
1. **Per-model enable/disable.** Extend the per-user enable/disable state from the agent (backend) granularity down to individual **models** within an agent. Row expansion in `SettingsSetupTable` reveals per-model toggles; an agent-level toggle remains a bulk control over its models. Semantics to settle: does disabling every model imply the agent is off, and does an agent-off hard-override individual model state?
2. **Favorite models.** Let a user star/favorite specific models. Favoriting is cheap to add once model-level rows exist (same per-user, per-(backend,model) store). Favorites float to the top of / are highlighted in chat model pickers and run selection.
3. **Surface downstream.** Chat/model pickers and run/scheduled-job selection consume per-model enabled + favorite state (ordering + filtering), reusing the gate wired at agent granularity in the base plan.

## Design questions to resolve first
- Storage shape: extend the base plan's per-user disabled-agents store to a per-(user, backend, model) table, or a superset store keyed by (user, backend, model?) with a null model meaning "whole agent".
- Precedence between agent-level and model-level state (override vs. union).
- Whether favorite implies enabled.
- Model identity stability: models come from `discoverAgentClis` probing and can change between scans — key favorites/toggles by (backend, model-id string) and tolerate models that disappear.

## SHIPPED BY BASE PLAN 84d4a42b (actual seams to extend — verified in code)
- **Persistence**: table `user_disabled_agent_clis (id, user_id, backend, created_at)` — **presence-as-disabled** (a row = disabled; absence = enabled; empty table = default all-enabled). Migration `databases/migrations/091_create_user_disabled_agent_clis.sql`. NOTE: this is a DISABLED-set, not an enabled-set — extending to models likely means adding a nullable `model` column (null = whole agent) with a partial/overloaded unique key, OR a sibling table; decide precedence there.
- **Service**: `AgentCliPreferencesService` in a NEW package module `@openthrottle/nestjs-repositories` → `modules/agent-cli-preferences/` (NOT under `graphql/agent-setup/*`). API: `getDisabledBackends(userId): Set<string>`, `isEnabled(userId, backend)`, `setEnabled(userId, backend, enabled)`.
- **Mutation**: `setAgentEnabled(backend, enabled): SetAgentEnabledResult` on `AgentSetupResolver` (SETTINGS_WRITE, isDriverId-validated). A per-model variant would live alongside it.
- **Query surface**: `enabled: Boolean!` is on `AgentCliOptionObject` (the `discoverAgentClis` agents), resolved per-request by overlaying the caller's disabled set AFTER the shared discovery cache — NOT on `agentCliSetupConfig`. A per-model `enabled`/`favorite` would extend the model shape here (models are currently a `[String!]` list; per-model state needs an object type — a breaking reshape, so add-only/deprecate).
- **Downstream gate (single source of truth = AgentCliPreferencesService)**: pickers filter `agent.enabled` in `toAgentChatOptions` + `toDriverEndpointChatOptions` (app-side); server rejects disabled backends in `startConversationStream` (chat), `registerCliPlanRun` + `enqueuePlanRun`/`enqueuePlanRalphOrchestrator` (plan runs, guard `ralph.backend` when set), and `createScheduledAgentJob`/update (`driverId`). Per-model gating reuses these same insertion points.
- **UI**: `SettingsSetupTable` + `SettingsSetupTableRow` (compact Models cell = "N models" → Popover badge list — the natural expansion point for per-model toggles) + `SettingsSetupAgentToggle` (Switch → `resources.agent-enabled` resource route, optimistic + revalidate) + `SettingsSetupToolbar` (All/Enabled/Installed filter + single install notice) + `SettingsSetupInstallNotice`. `SettingsSetupCliCard` was DELETED. Copy in `data/data.copy.ts` (`SETTINGS_SETUP_COPY`); filter helper `filterAgentCliStatuses` + `AGENT_CLI_FILTERS` in `data/agent-clis.data.ts`.

## Key references (inherited)
- Route + components: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.setup.tsx`, `app/routing/settings/components/SettingsSetup*.tsx`
- Data/merge: `app/routing/settings/data/agent-clis.data.ts`
- Server: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-setup/*`, `.../agent-discovery/*`; persistence in `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/agent-cli-preferences/*`

## Constraints
- Same as the base plan: generators-first components, shadcn Table/primitives, code-first GraphQL codegen flow, idempotent migration with COMMENTs, `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` commit footers.
- This plan is intentionally left at design-then-decompose depth; its first task is the design decision above, after which tasks are added.
summary: Follow-up to the agent-level table/enable-disable plan: take enable/disable down to the agent+model granularity and add the ability to favorite a model, surfacing favorites/enabled state to chat/model pickers and run selection.
title: Settings › Setup: per-model enable/disable + favorite models

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

Measured on 2026-08-18 against `OpenThrottle/monorepo`:

- **Repo visibility: PUBLIC** (`gh repo view` → `"visibility":"PUBLIC"`, 47 MB). Standard GitHub-hosted runners (`ubuntu-latest`, 4 vCPU / 16 GB) are **free with unlimited minutes on public repos**. Larger/managed runners are not.
- **Every job runs on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2204`** — `changes`, `build`, `ci-success`, `nx-dependency-graph` in `continuous-integration.yml`, plus both jobs in `vercel-deploy.yml`. Same 4 vCPU count as the free GitHub box, with *less* RAM (GitHub's standard runner is 16 GB).
- **Live spend is essentially one workflow.** `openthrottle-docker.yml`, `vercel-deploy.yml`, `secret-scan.yml`, `daily-merged-prs-summary.yml`, `dependency-graph-scheduled.yml`, `docs-watch.yml` are all already `if: false` or dispatch-gated. The 💰 markers throughout show this ground has been worked; the remaining wins are structural, not more disabling.
- **Volume is the multiplier.** 100 workflow runs in an 8-hour window (2026-08-17 23:40 → 2026-08-18 07:47), of which 26 were Continuous Integration. Extrapolates to ~78 CI runs/day ≈ ~2,300/month. Per-job timing over the last 12 CI runs: `build` avg **5.3 min** (ran 6 of 12 times; the draft/docs gate correctly skipped the rest), while `changes` and `ci-success` each spin a **separate billed runner** — so even a docs-only or draft PR pays two runner startups, and a real build pays three.
- **GCS Nx cache**: `gs://openthrottle-staging-nx-cache` is 2.19 GB, US multi-region, 90-day lifecycle. Storage is pennies; the cost is **egress**. GitHub-hosted runners are on Azure, so every cache read is billed GCS internet egress (~$0.12/GB) plus Class B ops, on every one of those ~2,300 runs/month. Meanwhile `.github/actions/node-setup` **already** caches `.nx/cache` via `actions/cache` — a free layer duplicating a paid one.

## Strategy

Do not trade away correctness or the CREEP-safe (CVE-2025-36852) cache model. Every change here is either "same guarantee, $0 instead of $" or "delete work that gates nothing".

Ordered by expected saving per unit of effort:

1. Move compute to the free tier the public repo already entitles us to.
2. Stop paying egress for a cache layer we duplicate for free — and note that GitHub Actions cache scoping (a PR branch reads its base branch's caches but cannot write into them) reproduces the current trusted-`main`-writes / PRs-read-only model *by construction*.
3. Cut run volume at the source (agentic per-task pushes).
4. Stop re-running full-tree checks whose result cannot have changed.

## Non-goals

- Re-enabling any currently disabled workflow.
- Removing test coverage or lint/typecheck gates to save minutes.
- Nx Cloud DTE (see `nx-audit-plan` — already decided against).

## Baseline to beat

~2,300 CI runs/month; ~7 billed job-minutes per real build (5.3 build + 2 satellite runners), ~2 per skipped run; ~2,300 GCS cache-read sessions/month of egress.
summary: Cut GitHub Actions / CI spend for a budget-limited OSS monorepo. Headline lever: OpenThrottle/monorepo is a PUBLIC repo, so standard GitHub-hosted runners are free and unlimited — yet every job runs on paid blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2204. Second lever: the paid GCS Nx remote cache duplicates a free actions/cache layer that is already wired. Third lever: run volume (~78 CI runs/day observed) from agentic per-task pushes.
title: 💰 CI cost reduction: free-tier runners, cache egress, and run volume

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Some AGENTS.md files deep-link a specific skill's SKILL.md through the **generated** `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` view. For OT-owned skills those entries are symlinks whose source of truth is `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (skill-sync generates the `.agents/skills/` view). Docs should link to the authored source, not the generated symlink view.

## Scope of the audit (already completed)

Swept all 100 AGENTS.md files (`grep -rn "\.agents/skills/[a-z0-9-]*/SKILL\.md" --include=AGENTS.md`). Only **two** files deep-link a specific SKILL.md through `.agents/skills/`, and **both** target OT-owned skills that are symlinks back into `skills/`:

1. `AGENTS.md:15` → `.agents/skills/openthrottle-generators/SKILL.md` — symlink; source at `skills/openthrottle-generators/SKILL.md`.
2. `databases/AGENTS.md:15` → `.agents/skills/ot-postgres/SKILL.md` — symlink; source at `skills/ot-postgres/SKILL.md`.

Every other `.agents/skills` mention in AGENTS.md files is prose describing the `.agents/skills/` directory as the merged-view concept (correct as-is), not a deep-link to a source-owned skill. No deep-link points at a real external-skill directory, so nothing else needs repointing.

Symlinked (OT-owned) skills confirmed via `find .agents/skills -maxdepth 1 -type l`: agents-code-review, agents-ralph, github-*, openthrottle-folders, openthrottle-generators, openthrottle-stack, ot-*, skill-sync, validate-plan. Real dirs (external, leave alone): brag-sheet, create-cli, frontend-design, git-commit, grill-*, handoff, improve, link-workspace-packages, monitor-ci, nx-*, skill-cleaner, skillopt-sleep, teach, writing-great-skills.

## Fix

Rewrite the two deep-links to point at the `skills/` source, using the correct relative path from each file's location:
- Root `AGENTS.md` → `./skills/openthrottle-generators/SKILL.md`
- `databases/AGENTS.md` → `../skills/ot-postgres/SKILL.md`

## Guard (optional follow-up)

Consider a lint/CI check that flags any `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` deep-link in Markdown where `<name>` is a symlinked (OT-owned) skill, so docs don't drift back to the generated view.
title: Repoint AGENTS.md skill deep-links from generated .agents/skills view to skills/ source

author: visormatt
description:
Agents keep reaching for the wrong component generator and concluding "no generator fits" — most recently on plan b67c8e27 (PR #468), where two package components were hand-written and a false "the generator cannot scaffold into packages/" claim was then recorded in the PR body, the plan output and agent memory. The rule file `.agents/rules/personal-generators.mdc` already carries a "What Went Wrong Previously … This must NEVER happen again" section, so this is at least the second occurrence.

THE NUANCE (for reference, not the thing to fix):
- `@tools/generators:react --subGenerator=component --destination=<nx project>` → components in a **package** (any project tagged `technology:react`; also works for app-local).
- `@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=<app> --folder=<path>` → components **inside an application**, resolved under `applications/<app>/app/routing`.

INVESTIGATION FINDING — DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY WRITING MORE DOCS. The nuance is already documented correctly in FIVE places: `skills/ot-generators/SKILL.md` states it three times (the registered-generators table row for `react` says "packages or apps (`--destination`)"; the "Typical OpenThrottle entrypoints" bullet says "Shared UI / packages: often `react` with `--destination`"; and the batch example scaffolds into a real package, `--destination=@openthrottle/react-router-profiling`), and `docs/tools/templates/AGENT_USAGE.md` states it twice (the generator matrix row at ~line 160, "Package or app components … `--destination=<project>` (not `--folder`)", and the note at ~line 187, "Use react for shared UI packages and react-router for apps under applications/"). Every one of those is accurate. A sixth restatement changes nothing.

ROOT CAUSES (what this plan actually targets):
1. `CLAUDE.md` is always in context and its "## Generators first" section (lines ~81-91) inlines a single concrete example — the `react-router` component command — with no selection rule. It reads as *the* answer, so discovery never happens and the `ot-generators` skill never loads. The agent that made this mistake went straight from that snippet to `--describe` on the generator the snippet named. Per the user: CLAUDE.md must not be the SSOT here — take what is referenced there, remove it, and point at the correct source.
2. The wrong generator fails uninformatively. `--application=<a package>` produces `Unable to read "applications/react-router-chat/app/routing" … ENOENT`, which reads like "packages are unsupported" rather than "wrong generator" — and that is precisely the wrong conclusion that got written down. The failure moment is the highest-signal teaching moment available and it currently teaches the opposite of the truth.
3. Duplication across four surfaces (CLAUDE.md, `.agents/rules/personal-generators.mdc`, `skills/ot-generators/SKILL.md`, `docs/tools/templates/AGENT_USAGE.md`) means each can drift; CLAUDE.md already has.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — an audit/lint that detects a hand-written component. Verified infeasible: the generator emits a scaffold whose shape (single export, `<Name>Props`, arrow component taking `props`, the six section markers in canonical order, `data-testid="<Name>"` on the root) is already enforced by `scripts/audit-component-shape.ts`. Re-running the generator over the two hand-written components on PR #468 and restoring the implementations left the tree BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed state. Provenance is therefore undetectable after the fact, and arguably does not matter once the shape matches — the harm is the wrong *conclusion* and the lost time, both of which are decision-time problems.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Skills: `skills/` is the source; `.agents/skills/` is generated and fans out to `.claude/skills/` + `.gemini/skills/`. Never hand-edit the generated dirs — edit `skills/` and re-sync via `/ot-skill-sync` (`./skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh`).
- Rules: `.agents/rules/` is the source of truth; `.cursor/rules/` are symlinks to the same bodies.
- Docs: CONTRIBUTING.md "## Documentation" contract applies, and `scripts/audit-docs-index.ts` enforces that every doc stays reachable from an index — keep that gate green.
- Generators: every invocation needs `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false`. Generator sources live in `tools/generators/src/generators/{react,react-router}/`, schemas in `schema.json`, dynamic lists via `--list=destinations` / `--list=applications`.
title: Generator selection: make CLAUDE.md defer to one SSOT and make the wrong generator fail informatively

author: visormatt
description:
Biweekly Postgres health sweep (2026-08-21).

**How it ran:** Read `databases/README.md`; ran `pnpm run check:local:migration-comments` (OK — no changed migration files vs `main`); inspected migrations since ~90 days (082–096); compared TypeORM entities under `packages/nestjs-repositories` to live catalogs; scanned GraphQL field resolvers for N+1 (most list relations already use DataLoaders); queried the local Postgres read-only (`\d+`, counts, orphan checks, `EXPLAIN`) for index/FK/growth evidence.

**Live database:** Available. Findings mix static analysis and live inspection. Counts/shapes only — no row contents, credentials, or PII.

**Cap:** 12 findings kept. Dropped lower-severity items: empty/obvious `COMMENT ON COLUMN` gaps on older tables (table-comment gate already green for the diff), `agent_conversations.project_id` index (FK unindexed but 0 non-null rows today), and several redundant single-column indexes already covered by unique composites beyond the two called out below.

**Dedupe:** `list_plans_by_status` for PENDING/IN_PROGRESS found no open `🔁 Database health: …` plan and no open `database`-category retention/FK plans matching these subjects. `semantic_search` returned no overlapping chunks. Nothing skipped as a duplicate.

**Headline:** Live DB is missing several FKs that migrations declare (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` / restore drift). Orphans exist today (`tasks.plan_id` 178/5072, `plan_embeddings.plan_id` 68/639, `plan_output_stream.plan_id` 50/3441, `plans.project_id` 12, `user_roles` 6). Separately: unindexed FKs on hot paths, unbounded agent-growth tables with no retention, and an activity query that loads all `plan_output_stream` rows in a date range before JS pagination.
title: 🔁 Database health: 2026-08-21

author: visormatt
description:
# Queues route redesign — a real live ops console

## Why
The Queues feature lives only in `applications/openthrottle-developer` (4 routes). Today it is functional but boring and leaky:

- **Flat stacked sections** — `QueuesIntroduction` + `QueuesTable` + two recharts blocks with no cohesive dashboard framing.
- **Copy leaks internals** — user-facing hint paragraphs literally name GraphQL operations in `<code>` tags (`retryJob`, `cancelPlanRun`, etc.) on `/queues/:queueId` and the job detail route.
- **Leftover lorem ipsum** in the job-detail header (`queues.$queueId.$jobId.tsx`).
- **Dead `QueuesToolbar`** component (renders a bare `<h2>`, only referenced in a commented-out block).
- **Broken pagination** — detail route sets `total = current page length`, so paging is effectively wrong.
- **Rich backend already exists but is UNUSED by the UI**: `queueJobLogTail` subscription (live per-job log tail, topic `bullmq:<queue>:<jobId>:logs`) + `queueJobLogs` cursor-paged history + `repeatableJobs` query + `duplicateJob`/`removeRepeatableJob` mutations. The single biggest "real love" win is a **live job console**.
- **Dashboard queue health is dead** — `DashboardQueueStats` is `@deprecated` and commented out in `dashboard._index.tsx`.

## Goal
Make Queues feel like a real ops surface: cohesive dashboard framing, a working toolbar, a live streaming job console, correct pagination, honest user-facing copy, and revived queue health on the dashboard — all matching the app's mature patterns (`app/routing/plans/*` list/detail/toolbar/stats triad, `OpenThrottleStatCard`, `DataTable`, `GlobalScreen`/`GlobalHeading`, shadcn `ChartContainer`).

## Design principles
- Reuse the plans/ feature as the reference for list/detail/toolbar/stats structure.
- No GraphQL operation names or internal jargon in user-facing copy.
- Preserve the component section-comment scaffold (`Hooks/Setup/Handlers/Markup/Life Cycle/🔌 Short Circuit`) and `data-testid` roots; keep the co-located test suites meaningful.
- Prefer generators for any net-new components (`@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component`).

## Out of scope
- The generic scheduled-agent-job feature (separate OT plan). This plan may leave a reusable live-console component that the scheduled-jobs UI later consumes.

## Key files
- Routes: `app/routes/queues._index.tsx`, `queues.$queueId._index.tsx`, `queues.$queueId.$jobId.tsx`, `queues.create.tsx` (+ co-located `*.graphql`).
- Components/utils: `app/routing/queues/{components,utils}/*`.
- Server surface: `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` (queue/job types, `queueJobLogTail`, `queueJobLogs`, `repeatableJobs`), `src/graphql/queues/*`, `src/graphql/queue-job-logs/*`.
- Dashboard: `app/routes/dashboard._index.tsx`, `app/routing/dashboard/components/DashboardQueueStats.tsx`.
summary: Redesign the openthrottle-developer Queues routes (list, detail, job detail, create) from flat/boring into a cohesive live ops console: wire the already-shipped queueJobLogTail live-log subscription, fix broken pagination + leaked GraphQL copy + leftover lorem ipsum, revive queue health on the dashboard, and match the mature plans/ + dashboard design patterns.
title: Queues route redesign — turn the ops screens into a real live console

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`packages/openthrottle-mcp` is currently a **stdio child process** of Claude/Cursor, launched on the host via `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` → `node dist/src/bin.js`. It is a **GraphQL-only client** to `openthrottle-server` (`<API_URL>/graphql`, default `http://localhost:6021`) using an `ot_sa_` service-account bearer token (`OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`).

Commit #296 (7a6e5f42) made the whole stack dockerizable — but there is **no `mcp` service**. In a fully-Dockerized install (Docker only, no host Node/pnpm/built `dist/`), the current launcher cannot run.

**Goal:** ship how Claude/Cursor reach openthrottle-mcp when the stack runs in Docker, without a host-Node dependency, while still supporting hybrid (host Nx + Docker infra) and worktree-isolated setups.

---

## ✅ DECISION (2026-08-06, task 5) — Transport = **A, HTTP service**

Spike-first evaluation complete; full rubric rows + live evidence in the plan output stream. Against the ★★★ criteria (no-host-Node / hybrid / worktree / agent_conversation-JWT):
- **A (HTTP)** fails no ★★★ — **chosen.** Only transport that satisfies both C1 (Docker-only) and C4 (agent_conversation human-JWT), the latter **proven live**: one server, per-request identity via `Authorization` header (ot_sa machine tools + human-JWT agent_conversation), because @rekog/mcp-nest guards are HTTP-only.
- **B (docker-exec stdio)** fails C4 (single-identity stdio).
- **C (host-stdio)** fails C1 + C4 → retained as the **hybrid fallback** (it PASSes hybrid + worktree).

**Adopted strategy:** Docker-native default = HTTP `mcp` container registered as `{type:http, url}`; host-stdio launcher stays for hybrid dev. A's PARTIALs map to Phase-3 tasks — C2→task 9, C3→task 8, C7→task 6, C8→tasks 8/10/11/12.

---

## Candidate transports (evaluated)
- **A. HTTP service (CHOSEN):** long-running `mcp` container exposing @rekog/mcp-nest streamable-HTTP (stateless JSON) on a published port; `.mcp.json {type:http, url}`. Per-request auth via Bearer→AsyncLocalStorage.
- **B. docker exec stdio:** `docker compose exec -T mcp node bin.js`. No host Node, but stdio = single identity (C4 fail).
- **C. Host stdio (status quo):** host child hitting the dockerized server's published port. Needs host Node+dist (C1 fail); kept as hybrid fallback.

## Install scenarios all must satisfy
1. Fully-Dockerized (no host Node) — the #296 target.
2. Hybrid — host Nx server/developer + Docker infra.
3. Worktree isolation — per-worktree ports; MCP targets the correct server.

## Known tensions
- **Auth vs `agent_conversation_*`:** those require a human JWT (reject `ot_sa_`). HTTP solves via per-request header→ALS store (proven). 
- **Worktree isolation vs static config:** a static HTTP `url` needs a per-worktree port/URL resolver (task 8).
- **Bootstrap coupling:** the `ot_sa_` credential is upserted by `docker compose run --rm bootstrap`; mcp path depends on migrations+server health + a provisioned token.

## Key references
- Launcher: `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh`; verify: `scripts/verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh`
- Registration: `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json.example`, `docs/openthrottle/mcp-registration.md`
- Auth: `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/auth/get-auth-token.ts` (per-request store → env)
- Compose: root `docker-compose.yml`; MCP nest wiring `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/nest/`
- Env: `.env.default` (`OPENTHROTTLE_SERVER_APP_URL`, `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OT_CONTAINER_PREFIX`)
- Docs: `databases/README.md` §Bootstrapping a fully-Dockerized install; `docs/openthrottle/run-locally-oss.md`
title: Dockerized openthrottle-mcp access — evaluate transports, ship a Docker-native path

author: visormatt
description:
# Refresh the `/usage` route for accuracy

The Developer-portal `/usage` route (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/usage._index.tsx` + `app/routing/usage/**`) carries a lot of hand-written narrative copy that was written when the surface only had coarse OpenThrottle plan/task daily counts. The data and its granularity have since grown substantially, and several claims — concentrated in the **"Analytics gaps (by design today)"** section (`components/UsageAnalyticsGaps.tsx`) — are now stale or directly contradicted by what the page renders.

## What actually ships today (verified against `usage._index.tsx.graphql`)

- **Token usage** (`tokenUsage` query): per-turn rows and totals with `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `reasoningTokens`, `costUsd`, `model`, `provider`, `turnCount`. Provider filter across claude/codex/cursor/grok/opencode/openai. Rendered by `UsageTokenUsage` + `UsageTokenUsageFilters`.
- **Skill usage** (`skillUsage` query): per-skill leaderboard with `count`, `avgDurationMs`, `outcomeCount`, `successCount`, `errorCount`, `abandonedCount`, `scope`; plus `byDay` (ours vs third-party), `byScope`, and `filterOptions` (cwds, gitBranches). `UsageSkillUsage` renders an **Outcomes** column and an **Avg duration** column, with a success/abandoned/error breakdown tooltip.
- **Daily stats** (`dailyStatsRange`): plans/tasks created/updated/completed per UTC day.

## Concrete stale/contradicted claims found

1. `UsageAnalyticsGaps.tsx` bullet: *"No latency or outcome metrics yet (Phase 4 enrichment is optional)."* — **Contradicted.** The Skill usage leaderboard directly above now renders **Avg duration** (latency) and **Outcomes** (success/abandoned/error) columns. This is the marquee inaccuracy.
2. The "Phase 4 enrichment" framing is internal jargon and stale — outcome/duration enrichment is live (opt-in for authored skills), not a future phase.
3. Skill-path references: bullet cites *".agents/skills vs .cursor/skills"* — the source-of-truth is now `skills/` (synced into `.agents/skills`); `.cursor/skills` does not exist at repo root. `skill-usage-copy.ts` already states the correct model ("Authored under skills/ (and synced into .agents/skills)").
4. `UsageOverview.tsx` contains a commented-out "Not in this chart" block referencing `~/.cursor/skills-cursor` — decide keep/delete; ensure no stale commented copy ships.
5. Cross-surface pointers ("Prompt versioning & debug", `/prompts`, `/skills`, "Copy usage snapshot (JSON)") should be re-verified against the current UI so every reference still resolves and reads correctly.

## Goal

Make every narrative claim across the whole `/usage` route and its components current and internally consistent with the data the page now surfaces. The "Analytics gaps" section should describe only genuine remaining gaps (e.g. per-prompt/per-command invocation counts, IDE-only runs, user-local skills the harness never invokes), not things that now exist. Preserve honest caveats (Private-mode turns excluded, opt-in outcome enrichment, approximate historical completion attribution).

## Scope

- `app/routes/usage._index.tsx`
- `app/routing/usage/components/*.tsx` (Introduction, Overview, DailyActivityOverview, AnalyticsGaps, Snapshot, TokenUsage(+Filters), SkillUsage(+Filters/Summary))
- `app/routing/usage/data/*.ts` (token-usage-copy, skill-usage-copy, daily-stats-series-glossary)
- Co-located `__tests__` — update assertions to match corrected copy.

Out of scope: server resolvers / GraphQL schema changes (data contract is fine as-is); only the developer-portal narrative/presentation is being reconciled.

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`, and a live render check of `/usage` (authed user with `settings:read`) confirming the corrected copy and that Outcomes/Avg-duration columns render.
title: Refresh /usage route accuracy: reconcile narrative with current data granularity

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Agent-CLI and local-model discovery feel slow on repeat loads. Investigation of the current caching found that the ONLY real cache is two 60s in-process singleton caches on the server; the client re-fetches on every mount/navigation, and the home loader amplifies each load into 2x calls per query. Every ~60s the next request pays the full cold cost (spawning up to 5 `--version` + 3 `<cli> models` child processes with 3s/5s timeouts, plus ~48 HTTP probes for local models).

## Current caching (as-is)

- **Local models** — `NestjsModelDiscoveryService` (`packages/nestjs-model-discovery/src/nestjs-model-discovery.service.ts`): singleton, 60s TTL (`LLM_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 60_000), has both cache + `inFlight` promise coalescing + `invalidate()`. Good citizen.
- **Agent CLIs** — `AgentDiscoveryService` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/agent-discovery.service.ts`): singleton, `CACHE_TTL_MS = 60_000`, cache-only. **NO in-flight dedup** — concurrent cache-miss callers each launch a full CLI sweep.
- **Client** — none. `executeGraphqlWithAuth` is plain fetch; no React Query/Apollo/localStorage/Jotai memoization. No HTTP cache headers on resolvers.

## Repeat-load amplifiers

- Home route loader `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx` fires all three discovery loaders every load; `loadDriverEndpointModels` (`models.server.ts`) re-issues BOTH GraphQL queries, so one home load triggers `discoverLocalModels` x2 and `discoverAgentClis` x2 (deduped only by the 60s server TTL, not the client).
- Header chat `useHeaderChatController.tsx` calls `optionsFetcher.load('/resources/chat-options')` per mount; a page reload re-fetches. `routes/resources.chat-options.tsx` re-runs both discovery loaders.
- Both loaders swallow errors -> `[]`, so failures silently re-probe next time.
- Multi-instance/serverless server deployments each keep their own in-memory cache -> low hit rate.

## GraphQL surface

- `discoverLocalModels` -> `ModelDiscoveryResolver` -> `NestjsModelDiscoveryService`
- `discoverAgentClis` -> `AgentDiscoveryResolver` -> `AgentDiscoveryService`
- Both guarded by `@Permissions(SETTINGS_READ)`. MCP tools go through the same cached queries.

## Levers to evaluate/apply

1. In-flight coalescing on `AgentDiscoveryService` (parity with model-discovery).
2. Stale-while-revalidate / background refresh: serve last-good snapshot instantly, refresh out of band, so repeat loads never pay cold cost.
3. Dedupe the double-fetch in `_index.tsx` / `loadDriverEndpointModels`.
4. Client-side caching so repeat mounts/navigations don't re-hit the server (persist loader result + `shouldRevalidate`, and/or HTTP cache headers on the resolvers).
5. Optional: shared cache (Redis) for multi-instance deployments — evaluate cost/benefit vs longer TTL.

## Approach

Design-first: task 1 measures current repeat-load cost and locks the chosen levers before code changes. Keep changes behind the existing config knobs where possible. Validate repeat-load latency drops and add regression tests.
summary: Speed up agent-CLI + local-model discovery on repeat loads: add in-flight coalescing + stale-while-revalidate to the server caches, dedupe the home-loader double-fetch, and add client-side caching so repeat mounts/navigations don't re-probe.
title: Model discovery caching: faster repeat loads

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

`/settings/workspace` offers Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code with no signal about which are actually installed. Enabling one you do not have produces a button whose deep link silently does nothing when clicked — the OS has no handler for the scheme. Observed live: VS Code enabled on a machine without it.

There is **no browser-side way** to detect this, and that is deliberate on the browsers' part:
- `navigator.registerProtocolHandler` registers, it cannot query.
- `getInstalledRelatedApps()` is Chrome-only and scoped to PWAs tied to your own origin.
- Navigate-and-detect-blur is unreliable and fires an OS prompt regardless.

Scheme-handler enumeration is a fingerprinting vector, so no engine exposes it. Detection therefore has to happen **server-side**, and OT already has that pattern.

## The hard constraint: this is a HINT, never a gate

The server is not guaranteed to be running on the user's machine. `WorkspaceEditorConfigService` already handles this via `toContainerPath`, which is identity when the bridge env (`OPENTHROTTLE_HOST` / `CONTAINER_WORKSPACES_DIR`) is unset — i.e. every host-run flow — and translates when the server runs in a container. **A containerized server probing its own filesystem would confidently report "VS Code not installed" about a Mac it cannot see.**

So the result is **three-state, not boolean**:

| State | Meaning | UI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `installed` | probe found it | quiet confirmation |
| `not_found` | probe ran on the host and found nothing | advisory "we couldn't find this" |
| `unknown` | probe could not be trusted (containerized, unsupported OS, probe error) | say nothing at all |

**Detection must never auto-disable, auto-enable, or block saving an editor.** Stored `enabledEditors` stays authoritative. A user on a container-backed server, or one whose editor lives somewhere unusual, must still be able to turn an editor on and have it work. Collapsing `unknown` into `not_found` and greying out the checkbox would break exactly those users — do not do it.

## Editors are NOT the agent CLIs (do not conflate)

Tempting shortcut, wrong answer: reuse `discoverAgentClis`. The drivers registry's `cursor` is `cursor-agent` (the CLI) and `claude` is `claude-code` (the CLI) — **not** the Cursor and Claude Code desktop apps that register `cursor://` and `claude://`. Someone can have the CLI without the app, or the reverse. Editor detection needs its own probe table keyed by `WorkspaceEditorId`, even though it borrows discovery's machinery.

## `code` in PATH under-detects (the macOS trap)

Probing for a `code` binary is the obvious approach and it is wrong on macOS: VS Code ships the `code` shell command **opt-in** ("Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH"), so a large fraction of real installs have the app and no CLI. A PATH-only probe reports `not_found` for a working editor — worse than no detection, because it is confidently wrong.

Detection is therefore per-platform:
- **macOS** — look for the `.app` bundle (`/Applications/…`, `~/Applications/…`); consider `mdfind`/Launch Services for non-standard locations. Bundle ids, not binary names.
- **Linux** — `.desktop` entries and/or PATH.
- **Windows** — registry / known install paths.

Ship whichever platforms are actually supported and return `unknown` for the rest. **Never guess.** That is the same rule the plan-toolbar deep links landed on: a confidently wrong answer beats no answer only in the sense that it is worse.

## Reuse, do not rebuild

`AgentDiscoveryService` is the template and is already solved for the expensive-probe problem: `StaleWhileRevalidateCache`, a soft TTL (`AGENT_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 60s) serving fresh, a hard TTL (default 600s) past which a call blocks rather than serve indefinitely-stale data, and a single coalesced background refresh. Filesystem probes are cheaper than the 3–5s CLI spawns, but they still should not run per page load. Mirror the knobs and naming.

Security: probe an **allowlist only**, derived from the editor vocabulary. Never spawn or stat a caller-supplied path.

## Relationship to plan 4d6bdf92

This adds a per-editor detection table — another exhaustive `Record<WorkspaceEditorId, …>`. It must be built on whatever [[exhaustive-vocabularies]] settles, not as a fourth hand-maintained editor list. If 4d6bdf92 has not landed, still express the table as an exhaustive Record so it fails typecheck when an editor is added.

## Out of scope

- Installing editors from the UI (agent CLIs have `installEnabled`; editors are GUI apps, different problem).
- Detecting editor *versions* or capabilities.
- Changing plan-toolbar deep-link behavior — that already degrades correctly with disabled buttons and tooltips.
summary: Probe the host for installed editors server-side (reusing the agent-CLI discovery + StaleWhileRevalidateCache pattern) and surface it as a three-state hint on /settings/workspace — installed / not-found / unknown. The stored enabledEditors stays authoritative; detection never auto-disables an editor, because a containerized server cannot see the user's host.
title: Editor presence detection: hint which editors are installed, never gate on it
