author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Make the developer-app Commander (⌘K palette) recognize a short UUID-ish fragment like `f5e40886` (the leading segment of a full plan id such as `f5e40886-36d3-4886-9781-9722e0b9217b`), resolve it to the real plan, and offer a confident one-keystroke redirect to `/plans/<full-id>`. Where practical, make the resolution logic reusable so it works everywhere the Commander is used (developer app first; admin/other apps as a follow-on).

## Today's behavior (baseline)

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/global/utils/commander-empty-extras.tsx` gates ALL id-based jumps on `REGEX_UUID` = a full 36-char UUID. Short fragments match nothing.
- When a full UUID is typed it offers three *type-guessing* rows (Open plan / Open queue / Open generator) plus a workspace-search escape — it never confirms which entity the id actually is; it just builds three speculative jumps.
- The jump is a POST to the root action (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/root.tsx`, intent `commander-search`), which re-validates `REGEX_UUID` and `redirect('/plans/<id>')`.
- Server side: `plan(id: ID!)` requires a full UUID; `searchPlans` is semantic/vector search, NOT an id-prefix lookup. **There is no way to resolve a short id prefix to a plan today** — this is the core backend gap.

## Proposed approach

1. **Backend prefix resolver** — add a GraphQL query to resolve a short id fragment to plan(s), e.g. `resolvePlanRef(prefix: String!): [PlanRefObject!]!` (or a nullable single result with an `ambiguous` signal). Server does a `WHERE id::text ILIKE $prefix || '%'` (bounded) with a small `LIMIT`, returning minimal fields (`id`, `title`, `status`). Unique match → confident redirect; multiple → show top N; none → fall through to existing behavior. Keep the input a bounded hex string (min length ~6–8) to avoid scanning on tiny fragments.
2. **Recognition util** — replace the all-or-nothing `REGEX_UUID` gate with a shared helper that also recognizes a *short hex fragment* (min length threshold, hyphen-optional) and classifies it as "looks like an id prefix". Lives in a shared location so other apps can reuse.
3. **Commander wiring** — when a short fragment is typed, debounce-call `resolvePlanRef`; on a unique plan, surface a real row `Open plan: <title> (f5e40886…)` that redirects to the resolved full id (no more guessing). On multiple matches, list them. Preserve the existing full-UUID and queue/job/plan-task pair behaviors.
4. **Redirect path** — resolver returns the FULL id, so the root-action redirect stays valid without loosening its UUID guard (short prefix is resolved to full id before the POST).
5. **Everywhere** — factor the resolver hook + recognition util into `@openthrottle/react-router-*` shared UI and apply to the admin app's commander (and any other consumer) as a follow-on task.

## Constraints / notes

- Code-first GraphQL: after resolver changes run the server to regen `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`, and commit generated output (CI fails on drift).
- Follow component-shape + data/component file boundaries; use `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` Command primitives.
- Add render-level Vitest for the empty-extras builder + a root.action test for the resolved-redirect path (see existing `root.action.test.ts`, `commander-empty-extras.test.ts`).
- Debounce + minimum-length gating to avoid a resolver call on every keystroke.
summary: Teach the developer-app Commander (⌘K) to recognize a short UUID fragment like `f5e40886`, resolve it to the real plan via a new server-side prefix resolver, and offer a confident one-keystroke redirect to /plans/<full-id>. Factor the logic to be reusable across apps.
title: Commander: short-UUID plan detection + quick redirect

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

On a fresh clone/DB provisioned from `main`, the `admin` role does NOT have `plans:read` / `plans:write`, even though the RBAC contract says admin is the full permission superset. Reproduced on a fresh clone on another machine.

## Root cause (not migration order — a static-vs-dynamic seed mismatch)

- `databases/migrations/034_create_roles_and_permissions_tables.sql` grants `admin` all permissions via `INSERT INTO role_permissions ... CROSS JOIN permissions p WHERE r.name = 'admin'`. This is a **point-in-time snapshot**: at migration 034 only `settings:*` and `users:*` permissions exist, so admin only ever gets those four.
- `databases/migrations/045_seed_service_accounts_bootstrap.sql` (lines 8-60) inserts `plans:read` / `plans:write` and grants them **only** to the `mcp` and `workflow-ralph` roles. It never re-grants `admin`.
- Contrast with `databases/migrations/085_seed_rollout_flag_permissions.sql`, which added `flags:*` and DID correctly re-grant `admin` (lines 22-31). Migration 045 omitted that step.
- Code contract in `packages/nestjs-rbac/src/roles.ts:49-54`: `ROLE_PERMISSIONS[ADMIN] = Object.values(PERMISSIONS)` — dynamically the full superset, with a comment claiming it "mirrors the DB seed's CROSS JOIN for admin in migration 034." The mirror is broken: the code side auto-includes every new permission; the DB side is frozen at migration-034 time.

Migrations are now run-once via the `schema_migrations` ledger, so admin was never backfilled after 045. Matt's original box masked the bug (older DB state / `seed_v0` backup already had the grants); a truly fresh migrate-from-034 exposes it.

## Fix strategy

1. Add a new idempotent migration that re-grants `admin` **all** permissions currently in the `permissions` table (same CROSS JOIN as 034, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). This backfills `plans:read`/`plans:write` on existing AND fresh DBs, and self-heals any future admin drift for perms added before this migration.
2. Add a regression test asserting the DB `admin` role holds every row in `permissions` (mirroring the nestjs-rbac ADMIN superset contract), so this can't silently regress.
3. Establish + document the convention: any future permission-adding migration MUST also re-grant `admin`. Update `databases/README.md`.
4. Verify against a genuinely fresh DB (reset volume -> migrate) that `admin` has `plans:read`/`plans:write`.

## Notes
- Next migration number is `092` (highest committed is `091`; note historical duplicate 084/085/087 numbers exist).
- Keep all DDL/DML idempotent (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`); the compose runner re-applies files and the ledger guards re-runs.
- No schema/type changes; DB-seed + test only.
title: Fix: admin role missing plans:read/plans:write on fresh DB (migration 045 never granted admin)

author: visormatt
description:
React Router apps repeatedly hand-roll the same fetcher/action-result narrowing: `fetcher.state !== 'idle'`, `'ok' in data && data.ok === false`, `'error' in data`, and in-flight `formData` intent checks. The trigger is `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx` (lines 129–140). The same error extraction also shows up on `useActionData()` (`actionData && 'error' in actionData`) across settings, notes, and schedule routes.

**Home:** `@openthrottle/react-router-utils` (`packages/react-router-utils`). It already owns RR app helpers (`useForm`, metadata, CSP) and is imported by developer/admin consumers. Keep GraphQL transport in `@openthrottle/react-router-graphql` — `executeGraphqlWithAuth` already unwraps to `TData` and throws typed errors. These helpers are for **route action JSON** returned to fetchers / `actionData`, which we conventionally shape with `data`/`error` (and often `{ ok, error }`).

**Do not** pull GraphQL into utils. **Do** declare `react` + `react-router` as peerDependencies (the package currently claims zero runtime deps but already imports them in `useForm`).

**Out of scope:** mutation-field errors (`retryJobError`, `updateTaskError`) and wholesale replacement of every `fetcher.state !== 'idle'` — first wave is the shared envelope + the proving-ground route, then identical `'error' in` call sites.
title: Abstract React Router fetcher and action-result helpers

author: visormatt
description:
Continue building OpenThrottle Rollout (our LaunchDarkly-inspired feature-flag system) beyond the current boolean + role-targeting v1.

## Context (today)
- Package: `@openthrottle/nestjs-rollout` — `RolloutFlag` entity, `RolloutService` CRUD + RBAC-aware `isEnabled` / `evaluateAll`.
- Schema: `databases/migrations/084` (`rollout_flags`: key, description, enabled, target_roles). Migration comment explicitly defers percentage/per-user targeting.
- GraphQL resolver lives in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/rollout/` (not in the package).
- Developer UI: `settings.rollout._index.tsx` + Settings rollout components (create/list/edit/delete boolean flags).

## Goal (this plan)
Ship **typed flags** and **percentage-based split allocations**, inspired by LaunchDarkly CodeControl flag variations — without user stickiness yet.

### Flag value types
Support four flag kinds (discriminated):
1. `boolean` — true / false variations (keeps today’s mental model)
2. `string` — string variations
3. `number` — numeric variations
4. `json` — JSON object/array variations (stored as jsonb; validated as parseable JSON)

Each flag has:
- Master `enabled` switch (unchanged)
- Optional `targetRoles` gate (unchanged semantics: empty ⇒ everyone; else actor must hold ≥1 role)
- A **kind/type**
- Two or more **variations** (typed values + optional names/descriptions)
- A **default / off variation** returned when the flag is disabled or the actor fails targeting
- A **fallthrough / on allocation** that picks among variations via **percentage weights** (0–100, must sum to 100)

### Percentage allocations
When evaluating an eligible actor, choose a variation by percentage buckets (e.g. 90% control / 10% treatment). Model allocations as ordered buckets with `weight` (basis points or integer percent — pick one and document; prefer integer 0–100 that sums to 100 for v1 simplicity).

### Evaluation strategy (explicitly non-sticky)
**Out of scope:** sticky bucketing per user (hashes, local storage, server-side assignment persistence).

**In scope — simple deterministic split:** treat the actor id as a numeric discriminator.
- Derive a stable integer from the principal id (user/service-account UUID).
- Suggested v1: take the last hex nibble / parse a fixed substring as int, OR hash UUID → int and use **even vs odd** for a binary 50/50; for N-way percentage splits, map `bucket = idInt % 100` into cumulative weight ranges `[0, w1)`, `[w1, w1+w2)`, ….
- Document that this is a stand-in for true sticky hashing and will be replaced later.
- Even/odd is fine as an illustrative binary case; the production path for percentages should be `mod 100` buckets so weights other than 50/50 work.

### Evaluation API shape
Extend beyond boolean `isEnabled`:
- Keep `isEnabled(key, principal)` for boolean flags (and as a convenience: "resolved variation is the truthy boolean" or "flag enabled + roles pass" — decide and document; prefer typed `evaluate(key, principal) → { key, kind, value, variationIndex, reason }`).
- Add `evaluate` / `evaluateAll` returning typed values (not just on/off).
- GraphQL: evolve `myFeatureFlags` / admin flag types to expose kind, variations, allocations, and evaluated value (union or JSON-encoded value + kind discriminator).

### Settings UI (developer app)
Surface on `/settings/rollout`:
- Create/edit flag with type selector (boolean | string | number | json)
- Variations editor (add/remove/reorder; typed inputs; JSON textarea with validation)
- Percentage allocation editor (weights must sum to 100; live validation)
- Table columns: key, type, enabled, allocation summary
- Detail/edit: show default variation + fallthrough weights
- Copy in `routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts`

### Explicitly deferred
- Sticky / consistent bucketing per user
- Environments, segments, rules, prerequisites, experiments, metrics
- Client-side SDKs / streaming flag updates
- Percentage targeting *by role/segment* layered on top of splits (role gate stays all-or-nothing before split)

## Architecture notes
- Migrations own schema (`synchronize` off); new migration(s) after 084/085.
- Domain stays in `@openthrottle/nestjs-rollout`; GraphQL objects/inputs/resolver stay in `openthrottle-server`.
- Prefer jsonb columns for variations + allocations (single-row flag config) unless normalized child tables clearly win for querying — document the choice in the migration COMMENT.
- Preserve backwards compatibility for existing boolean flags: migrate rows to `kind=boolean` with variations `[false, true]` (or `[true]` only — pick the LD-like default of false/true indexes) and 100% weight on `true` when enabled.
- Tests: service unit tests for evaluation matrix (disabled, role miss, 0/50/100 weights, even/odd or mod-100 buckets, each kind); resolver + developer component tests; assert against `data.copy.ts` constants where copy is the contract.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Can create and persist flags of all four kinds via GraphQL + Settings UI.
2. Percentage allocations validate (sum 100) on write.
3. `evaluate` returns the correct typed variation for role-eligible actors using the simple id→bucket strategy; disabled/role-miss returns the off/default variation.
4. Existing flags migrate cleanly; `isEnabled` still works for boolean flags.
5. README + AGENTS.md for nestjs-rollout updated for typed evaluation and non-sticky bucketing caveat.
summary: Shipped typed rollout flags with percentage allocations: migration 089 (kind/variations/off_variation/fallthrough), nestjs-rollout typed evaluate + mod-100 bucketing, GraphQL admin + myFeatureFlags shapes, developer Settings UI for create/edit/list/detail. Sticky assignment deferred.
title: Rollout typed flags with percentage allocations

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem
Claude Code sessions keep losing (or failing to establish) the openthrottle-mcp stdio connection.

## Investigation findings (2026-08-27, main checkout)
Claude's MCP logs (~/Library/Caches/claude-cli-nodejs/-Users-matt-Development-openthrottle/mcp-logs-openthrottle-mcp, 110 files Aug 25-28) show 95 clean client shutdowns and 14 startup FAILURES in three clusters — all launcher preflight hard-exits in scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.ts, none mid-session crashes:

1. 9x 'server rejected the token' (Aug 25-26) — token rotated by database:bootstrap-service-accounts, .env still held the old one.
2. 3x 'no reachable OpenThrottle server' (Aug 27) — the stable server was down/restarting at MCP launch; the launcher probes once and exits, no retry.
3. 2x 'OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN is unset' (Aug 27 evening) — scripts/setup.ts ran that day (.demo-workstation.local mtime 19:23), resetEnvironmentFiles() wiped .env, and the outro banner asks the HUMAN to manually copy the tokens back from .demo-workstation.local. The copy never happened; every MCP launch after that failed. Hotfixed 2026-08-27 by upserting both tokens into .env and applications/openthrottle-server/.env; verify:mcp-env green.

## Exonerated hypotheses
- openthrottle-developer:dev does NOT rebuild the MCP: its resolved Nx task graph is 7 tasks, none touching @openthrottle/openthrottle-mcp (the package deliberately has __dev, not dev, so ^dev cascades skip it).
- Running openthrottle-server with :start (built, no watch) is safe.
- dist rewrites cannot kill an already-running node process; the only real dist risk is SPAWNING during a ^build clean-rebuild window when dist/src/bin.js is momentarily absent (test/build targets depend on ^build and @nx/js:tsc cleans dist).

## Direction
Make the launcher self-healing (token fallback to .demo-workstation.local, retry on transient server-down, re-read after rotation), remove the manual token copy step from setup, guard the dist spawn window, and add a launch-outcome ledger + doctor so the next 'MCP lost' takes minutes to diagnose, not an evening.
summary: Claude keeps losing the openthrottle-mcp connection. Investigation (2026-08-27) proved it is NOT the developer app dev mode: every disconnect is a launcher preflight hard-exit. Fix the token pipeline, add retry/fallback, and add diagnostics.
title: openthrottle-mcp connection resilience: stop losing the stdio MCP

` (skills, currently commented out). - Several tables have no actions column at all (PermissionsTable, ProjectTasksTable, PromptsTable, ScheduleTable, ScheduleRunsTable, RolloutFlagsTable) — those are in scope only for an explicit keep/add decision, not a forced migration. ## Goal One promoted primitive — `GlobalPopover` in `packages/react-router-ui-global` — modeled on `RepositoryRowActions`, plus one canonical `Actions` column header, adopted by every `XxxxTable` in `openthrottle-admin`, `openthrottle-developer`, `openthrottle-email`, and `openthrottle-website`. All four apps already depend on `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global`, so no new package wiring is needed. ## Design decisions (assumptions — change here first if wrong) 1. **Primitive: `DropdownMenu`, not `Popover`.** Both existing implementations are built on `DropdownMenu` (`packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/DropdownMenu`), not `Popover`. `DropdownMenu` is also the correct primitive for a menu of actions: it gives `menu`/`menuitem` roles, typeahead, arrow-key navigation, and `onSelect`. So the component keeps the requested **name** `GlobalPopover` (matching the `Global*` naming in that package) while being **implemented on the DropdownMenu primitives**. If the name should instead be `GlobalActionsMenu`, decide that in task 1 before anything migrates onto it. 2. **`RepositoryRowActions` is the shape to generalize.** The API is derived from what that file already does, not invented; the queues menu then has to fit inside it. If a capability exists there and not in `GlobalPopover`, `GlobalPopover` is wrong. 3. **Action shape is a discriminated union** (per `.agents/rules/coding/discriminated-unions.mdc`), because the real call sites need three behaviors: a `Form`-submitted intent with hidden fields (repositories refresh / apply-editor-config / remove), a `react-router` `Link` (queues "View"), and a client `onSelect` callback (queues pause/resume). No `as` casts, no enums (`as const` objects only). 4. **Destructive items get a confirm.** The remove-checkout flow already gates on `AlertDialog`; `GlobalPopover` owns that so no caller re-invents it. 5. **Per-row pending state is first class.** `RepositoryRowActions` swaps an item's label while its own intent+id is submitting. The primitive must support a per-action pending label rather than pushing every caller back to raw `useNavigation` plumbing. 6. **Inline primary buttons collapse into the menu** where the row already links to its detail view elsewhere (queues links from the name column), so rows end at a single trigger. Where a row has exactly one action and no detail link, leave it inline — a one-item menu is worse UX than a button. 7. **Component shape is enforced.** Everything here must satisfy `openthrottle/component-primitive-shape` + `pnpm run audit:component-shape`: one component per file, exported `Foo` + `FooProps` only, the six ordered section markers, 210-line cap, file-scope data/helpers hoisted to sibling `data/`/`utils/`. Copy lives in `data.copy.ts`. Scaffold with `@tools/generators` (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false`), never hand-write the component file. ## Validation Per task: `pnpm nx run :lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`. Integration check for the source-first packages is `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build` (and `openthrottle-admin:build`) — `react-router-ui-global` has no `build` target by design. Do not run Nx targets in parallel. A visual pass on `/settings/repositories`, `/queues`, and two migrated routes closes the plan.
summary: Normalized table row Actions onto GlobalPopover across developer/admin. Visual pass confirmed queues/repositories/plans alignment, keyboard, destructive confirm; admin Roles/Users Actions-less by design. PR: https://github.com/OpenThrottle/monorepo/pull/426
title: Normalize table row Actions on a shared GlobalPopover

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Add a `GlobalFeatureOnboarding` instance to `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills._index.tsx` so the Skills index teaches a new (or new-to-skills) user what Skills are, following the pattern already shipped for Rules / Schedule / Plans (OT f599b238 + onboarding-in-a-modal 0cbfffd3).

The differentiator: the copy must be geared to the **Agent Skills open format** that our AGENTS.md / docs/Skills.md already reference — [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/) and its [specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) — while staying human and helpful rather than reading like a spec dump. Concretely: a skill is a folder + `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description` with USE WHEN triggers), portable across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, etc.; OpenThrottle authors them in `skills/` (SSOT) and fans them out to `.agents/skills/` via skill-sync. Never invent a parallel format.

## Current state

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills._index.tsx` renders `SkillsIntroduction` → toolbar → `SkillsTable` → pagination → deferred `SkillsIndexUsage`. There is **no** onboarding block and **no** `?modal=onboarding` surface.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/components/SkillsIntroduction.tsx` wraps its `GlobalHeading` in a legacy `SkillsOverviewDialog` (click-the-title dialog, `h3` heading) instead of the now-standard `GlobalHeading` + `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger` header row used by `RulesIntroduction` / `ScheduleIntroduction`.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts` has many `*_COPY` objects but no `SKILLS_ONBOARDING: GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent`.
- Zero-result empty state is `SkillsEmpty` (filtered case) — keep it; onboarding is only for genuinely-empty & unfiltered.

## Reference implementation (copy this shape)

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/rules._index.tsx` — `isNewUser = totalCount === 0 && !isFiltered`, then `{isNewUser ? <GlobalFeatureOnboarding content={RULES_ONBOARDING} /> : <toolbar + table>}`, plus `<GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal content={RULES_ONBOARDING} />` as a sibling of `GlobalScreen`.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/rules/data/data.copy.ts` → `RULES_ONBOARDING` for the copy voice and field usage.
- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalFeatureOnboarding.tsx` — the typed contract: `cta`, `icon`, `internalUsage`, `secondary?`, `steps[]`, `tagline`, `title`, `useCases[]`, `whatItIs`.

## Notes / constraints

- Copy lives in `data/data.copy.ts` only — no feature wording inside components (component/data boundary rule).
- Use `secondary` for the spec link (`https://agentskills.io/specification`) — this is the first onboarding block to use an external `secondary`; verify `GlobalFeatureOnboardingBody` renders an absolute URL sanely (react-router `Link to`), and if it only handles internal routes, that gap is the one real implementation risk — resolve it in task 2 rather than dropping the link.
- Skills entries are discovered from disk, so "empty" means no `SKILL.md` found (e.g. no local checkout / `WORKSPACE_ROOT` unset) — the CTA should point somewhere useful in that state (`/skills/vocabulary` or the docs/spec) rather than a non-existent "create skill" route; confirm what exists before wiring `cta`.
- Validate with `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`.
title: Skills index onboarding: GlobalFeatureOnboarding geared to the Agent Skills spec

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Add a GitHub-contributions-style **calendar heatmap** (weekday rows × week columns, color-graded by daily activity) as a **reusable primitive** in the shared `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` package, then consume it on the OpenThrottle Developer dashboard (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/dashboard._index.tsx`) as a new card.

## Approach & key facts (from codebase survey)

- **Package is source-first.** `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` (`packages/react-router-shadcn/`) has `main`/`module`/`types` → `./src/index.ts`; no consumer build step. Add the component file + one barrel line (`export * from './components/ContributionHeatmap';`) to `src/index.ts`. Follow the existing barrel + section-comment conventions.
- **Hand-rolled SVG/CSS grid, not Recharts.** `recharts@^3.6.0` is already a dep and shadcn `Chart/*` wrappers exist, but a contributions heatmap is a fixed grid of day cells — build it as an accessible SVG or CSS-grid component. No new dependency required. Intensity buckets should reference theme CSS vars (e.g. `--chart-1`…`--chart-5` or dedicated `--heatmap-*` vars) so light/dark both work.
- **No existing heatmap/contributions/calendar-heatmap component** anywhere in the repo — greenfield. (`Calendar.tsx` is a react-day-picker date picker, unrelated.)
- **Best data source: `dailyStatsRange.items`** — `DashboardDailyStatsCardFragment[]`, already day-bucketed: `{ date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', plansCompleted, plansCreated, plansUpdated, tasksCompleted, tasksCreated, tasksUpdated }`. Default cell intensity = sum of the six counts (total activity); leave the metric configurable.
- **Window must widen.** The loader (`dashboard._index.tsx:47`) currently requests a **14-day** window. A contributions calendar shows many weeks (target ~26–52 weeks). This is a variable-only change (`start`/`end` on the existing `dailyStatsRange(start, end)` query) — **no GraphQL document change, no codegen**. Confirm the server range query is happy returning ~180–365 day rows.
- **Card conventions** (`DashboardQueueHealthCard.tsx`): named arrow component, props destructured on line 1, explicit `React.ReactElement` return, `<Card className={clsx('gap-3 p-4', className)}>`, `data-testid` matching the component name, import from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` by name, and the fixed section-comment scaffold (`// Hooks / // Setup / // Handlers / // Markup / // Life Cycle / // 🔌 Short Circuit`).
- **Streaming.** The card renders inside a `<React.Suspense>` + `<Await resolve={core}>` boundary; add a matching skeleton (mirroring `DashboardActivityChartSkeleton`'s `min-h`) so streamed content doesn't shift the grid.
- **Click-through.** Reuse the existing `?modal=daily-stats&date=…` deep-link (`handleSelectDate` in the route) so clicking a heatmap day opens the daily-stats modal — parity with `DashboardDailyStatsCard`.

## Open decisions (sensible defaults chosen; revisit during impl)

- **Window length:** default to ~26 weeks (fits the dashboard column without a full 53-week GitHub width); make the component render whatever range it's handed.
- **Metric:** default = total of all six daily counts; expose a `metric`/`getValue` prop for future per-metric views.
- **Intensity scale:** 5 buckets (empty + 4), quantile or fixed thresholds — decide against real data.

## Validation

- `pnpm nx run react-router-shadcn:{lint,typecheck,test}`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:{lint,typecheck,test}` and a `dev`/`build` integration check on the developer app.
- No codegen expected (no schema/document change); if any `.graphql` is touched, run `codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router` and commit `__generated__` + `schema.gql`.
summary: Add a reusable GitHub-contributions-style calendar heatmap to @openthrottle/react-router-shadcn, then surface it as a new card on the Developer dashboard (dashboard._index) sourced from dailyStatsRange.
title: Contributions heatmap in react-router-shadcn + Developer dashboard

author: visormatt
description:
# Hook overlay for child repositories — direction E (plugin + spawn-time injection)

**Status:** DIRECTION SET — option **E** chosen by the owner, 2026-08-18. Implementation tasks below.

**Related plans:** `d3a30314` (foreign-workspace skill injection, DONE), `21f150c6` (`@openthrottle/agentic-hooks` package, DONE), `96bfd217` (agentic lifecycle hooks, PENDING), `d3759118` / `91679bbf` (skill usage tracking, PENDING), `60c8e0b8` (agentic-hooks bundle target dependency fix, PENDING — **blocks distribution work**).

**Docs:** `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md`, `docs/monorepo/agent-editor-folders.md`.

---

## Problem

`@openthrottle/agentic-hooks` authors a tool-neutral core in TS and esbuild-bundles per-tool adapters into committed, self-contained `.cjs` under each tool's hook folder — five under `.claude/hooks/`, one under `.cursor/hooks/`. Those bundles are wired up by **this repo's** `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json`, so they only ever fire inside the OpenThrottle monorepo.

~99% of real work happens in **child repositories** — foreign checkouts OT drives agents against, plus repos humans open directly. None of them get hooks. Skills already solved their half of this (`d3a30314`); hooks are the unsolved half.

Hard constraint from the owner: **never override or clobber a user's own hooks.**

## The key asymmetry — this is NOT the skills problem again

Skill injection was forced to materialize into the target working tree because *no* agent CLI exposes an out-of-repo skills directory (§2 of the injection decision record). Hooks are different — `claude --help` confirms:

| escape hatch | effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--settings <file-or-json>` | loads **additional** settings for the session; merges with project/user settings |
| `--plugin-dir <path>` | loads a plugin (hooks + skills + MCP) from a directory or `.zip`; repeatable |
| `--plugin-url <url>` | fetches a plugin `.zip` for that session only |
| `/plugin install` (marketplace) | durable, per-machine; hooks merge additively — Claude Code never rewrites the user's `settings.json` |

Claude Code merges hooks from user settings, project settings, local settings, and every installed plugin. They are **additive by construction** — which is why the no-clobber requirement is satisfied by *mechanism* rather than by careful merge logic.

Counterweight that killed option C: skills are one directory per skill, so collision handling is trivial. Hooks live in a **single user-owned JSON file** with no fragment-include mechanism, so anything writing into it inherits merge, restore, and corruption risk the skill materializer never had.

---

## Decision — option E

**Ship both legs against one shared artifact:**

- **Leg A — plugin.** An OpenThrottle Claude Code plugin (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `hooks/hooks.json` referencing `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/*.cjs`), published to a marketplace and installed once per machine. This is the durable, human-facing path: it applies in every repo the user opens, writes nothing into their checkout, and can later carry skills and the OT MCP server too.
- **Leg B — spawn-time.** `@openthrottle/openthrottle-drivers` appends `--plugin-dir` to the Claude CLI invocation so OT-orchestrated runs never depend on the user having installed anything. Zero disk mutation in the target repo: no ledger, no teardown, no `.git/info/exclude` block.

**Unifying design:** the plugin directory is built **once**, as a first-class Nx artifact produced by the existing `bundle-hooks` pipeline. Leg A publishes that directory; leg B points `--plugin-dir` at it in place. One payload, two delivery paths, one drift gate — this is what makes E cost barely more than either leg alone.

### Rejected

- **C (extend foreign-skill-injection to hooks)** — rejected. Reuses shipped machinery but requires a managed-block merge into a user-owned `settings.json`, with restore-on-teardown and real corruption risk, to reach somewhere the CLI already offers a first-class out-of-repo flag for. May only be revisited if the capability matrix proves a non-Claude CLI has *no* out-of-repo hook config and parity becomes a v1 requirement.
- **D (server-side transcript derivation)** — not chosen as the mechanism, but retained as the **fallback for non-Claude CLIs** until they grow real hook support, and as the degraded path when no hook can run.

---

## Open questions still owned by this plan

1. **Multi-CLI capability matrix** — what hook/plugin surface codex, cursor, opencode, and grok expose, and whether any accepts out-of-repo config. E covers Claude fully; this decides what the other four get (likely D). Cursor reads `.cursor/hooks.json` in-repo and we already ship one adapter there.
2. **Child-repo scoping and privacy contract** — the hooks phone home to the OT GraphQL API. Which server, how a foreign repo is identified and scoped, behavior when no server is reachable (core is already fail-open), and the privacy default for a repo the OT operator does not own. Overlaps `91679bbf`.
3. **Scope of the overlay** — telemetry-only in v1 (just skill-usage) versus a general hook channel (`96bfd217` would add more). Telemetry-only is far easier to justify installing into someone else's repo; recommend v1 stays telemetry-only.
summary: DIRECTION SET (owner, 2026-08-18): **option E — plugin (A) + spawn-time injection (B)**. Both legs are additive by construction, so "never clobber a user's hooks" is met by mechanism, not merge logic. Option C (extending foreign-skill-injection into the target's settings.json) is explicitly rejected. Unifying design: build the Claude plugin directory as ONE Nx artifact — A publishes it to a marketplace, B points `--plugin-dir` at it. Key precedent: unlike skills, hooks have first-class out-of-repo escape hatches (`--settings`, `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, marketplace) so nothing is ever written into a child repo.
title: 🪝 Overlay agentic hooks into child repositories — options and direction

Not yet triaged in any pass: the ~264-item "Unused exports" bucket (beyond the @public-annotation items already covered), the 11 "Unused exported types" (beyond PaginationConfig), the 6 duplicate-export pairs, and stale TODO/commented-out-block sweep — left for a future weekly run per this job's per-run cap.

author: visormatt
description:
Audit and harden all GitHub Actions workflows and composite actions under `.github/` so CI/CD is least-privilege, supply-chain safe, and free of common footguns.

## Scope
- Workflows: continuous-integration, vercel-deploy, openthrottle-docker, nx-release, secret-scan, terraform-validate, docs-watch, dependency-graph-scheduled, daily-merged-prs-summary
- Composite actions: node-setup, docker-build-push, nx-affected-docker-apps, google-cloud, graphql-url
- Config: dependabot.yml, pull_request_template.md (only where it affects CI expectations)
- Related docs: docs/monorepo/CI-quality-gates.md, docs/monorepo/NX.md (CI/release sections)

## Goals
- No overly broad `permissions` / default write tokens where read suffices
- No unpinned third-party actions (prefer commit SHA; tags only when intentionally accepted)
- No secret leakage via logs, artifacts, or fork-PR triggers
- No dangerous triggers (`pull_request_target` + checkout of untrusted code, etc.) without mitigations
- Dependabot (or equivalent) covers GitHub Actions updates
- Workflow behavior matches documented CI gates; dead/duplicate jobs removed or documented
- Composite actions are minimal, documented inputs/outputs, and don't smuggle privileged credentials unnecessarily

## Out of scope
- Changing product CI gate policy (P0–P4) unless a gate is broken or contradictory
- Non-GitHub CI systems
- Rewriting Nx Cloud / parallelization strategy unless a security or correctness bug is found

## Done when
- Findings documented (severity + file/job)
- High/critical issues fixed or explicitly accepted with rationale
- Checklist of remaining medium/low items (if any) recorded on the plan summary
summary: GHA hardening complete on branch openthrottle/harden-github-actions (commit abe028a4, from main cf70294a); pnpm check:local green. FIXED: [HIGH] continuous-integration.yml top-level GITHUB_TOKEN reduced from 5 write scopes to least-privilege read (actions/contents/packages:read) on the PR-reachable build job; [MED] docs-watch.yml pinned contents:read (was missing→broad default); [MED] dependabot.yml now covers github-actions ecosystem (grouped, limit 5) since all actions are SHA-pinned with no other bump path; [MED] google-cloud composite action stops interpolating ${{inputs}} into bash (script-injection shape)→env+quoted; [LOW] removed dead graphql-url composite action; docs/monorepo/CI-quality-gates.md reconciled to real workflow (Knip NOT in CI, circular-deps is a build step not a job, schema-sync covered by codegen drift guard, +documented 5 live gates). CONFIRMED CLEAN: all third-party actions SHA-pinned; no pull_request_target/workflow_run/untrusted-checkout+write; no secret echoed/written to outputs/artifacts; nx-release workflow_dispatch-only; deploy/docker/release secrets gated to trusted refs. REMAINING BACKLOG (owner decision, not in PR): (1)[HIGH owner-call] re-enable secret-scan gitleaks job (currently if:false → false sense of security); (2)[MED] --build-arg GITHUB_TOKEN bakes token into image layers, needs BuildKit secret mount (Dockerfile scope, jobs if:false); (3)[MED] static GCP SA keys → OIDC/WIF (infra); (4)[LOW] CI build gets GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_STAGING on PRs — gate to non-fork/OIDC if repo goes public; (5)[LOW] secret-scan head.sha/base.sha via ${{}} → env when re-enabled. Branch committed (not pushed/no PR yet); worktree removed for local checkout.
title: Harden GitHub Actions and workflows

author: visormatt
description:
Revisit GraphQL → Zod codegen so the operations we write (queries/mutations) produce usable validation schemas, then add a shared FormData util so route actions stop hand-parsing fields.

## Why

Route actions still invent per-field FormData extraction. The motivating example is `readSlugAndTag` in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/actions/project-skill-tags.ts`: `formData.get`, `typeof === 'string'`, `trim()`, empty-string errors, then a GraphQL `input` object. The same pattern is duplicated for plan/task tags and elsewhere.

We already generate Zod via `graphql-codegen-typescript-validation-schema` in `@openthrottle/graphql-codegen` `defineCodegen` (`app/__generated__/schemas.ts`). That output is **schema-level Input types** (`AddProjectSkillTagInputSchema()`), not **operation-variable** schemas derived from the `.graphql` documents we author. MCP tools already consume those Input schemas; the developer app only uses them sporadically (`planId.ts` `AddHookInputSchema().parse(...)`) **after** still reading FormData by hand. Empty strings currently pass `z.string()` because `notAllowEmptyString` is off.

The goal is: write the mutation → codegen emits the schema → one util turns `FormData` into typed variables (or a structured action error). No parallel hand-rolled parsers.

## Current state (do not rediscover blindly)

- `packages/graphql-codegen/src/index.ts`: `withZodSchemas` default true; plugin config `schema: 'zod'`, `zodImportPath: 'zod/v3'` (FIXME), `importFrom: './graphql.js'`, `strictScalars: true`.
- Generated schemas are **functions** (`FooInputSchema(): z.ZodObject<…>`), covering the full GraphQL input type universe, not only types referenced by this project's documents.
- Plugin can emit operation-adjacent constraints (`notAllowEmptyString`) but does **not** emit per-operation `AddProjectSkillTagVariablesSchema` from documents. Forms also carry extra keys (`intent`) and often flatten `{ slug, tag }` instead of `{ input: { slug, tag } }`.
- `RemoveProjectSkill` uses top-level `$projectId` / `$slug` variables, not an Input type — Input-schema-only codegen leaves that mutation without a matching schema unless we generate operation variables.

## Target design (investigate, then lock)

1. **Schema source of truth:** prefer generated Zod from GraphQL. Decide whether to (a) keep Input-type schemas and compose them in the util, (b) add operation-variable schemas (custom plugin or second generates block keyed off documents), or (c) a thin wrapper that maps a Document's variables type onto existing Input schemas. Operation variables must cover mutations that do not use a single `input:` argument.
2. **FormData adapter:** one util (likely `@openthrottle/react-router-graphql` or a small sibling under react-router-— not inlined in the skills action). Responsibilities: FormData → plain object (string trim, empty → omit/undefined, optional nested `input.*` / bracket keys), `safeParse` against the generated schema, map Zod issues to a concise action-error shape, strip/ignore form-only fields (`intent`). Strict: unknown GraphQL fields fail; form extras are an explicit allowlist.
3. **Codegen knobs:** evaluate `notAllowEmptyString: true` (would make `readSlugAndTag` empty checks redundant) and the `zod/v3` FIXME vs zod v4. Changing plugin config regenerates every consumer `schemas.ts` (developer, admin, email, mcp, ralph) — treat as a compatibility task, not a silent flag flip.
4. **Pilot:** `runSkillRecordTagAction` / `readSlugAndTag` using `AddProjectSkillTagInputSchema` / `RemoveProjectSkillTagInputSchema` and whatever covers `RemoveProjectSkill`. Then apply the same util to the duplicated plan/task tag FormData blocks in `planId.ts` / `taskId.ts` — do not boil the ocean of every action in the first pass.
5. **Convention:** document in graphql-codegen README + developer AGENTS: new mutations get a `.graphql` document; actions parse FormData through the util + generated schema; do not add new `formData.get` + trim helpers.

## Out of scope

- Replacing MCP tool parameter wiring (already on generated Input schemas) except where the same operation-variable work helps both.
- Client-side RHF/shadcn form binding (follow-up once the server-action util is proven).
- Hand-editing `__generated__/`.
title: Generate Zod from GraphQL operations for form actions

author: visormatt
description:
Make the skills index source toggle (All / OpenThrottle / External / Personal, `data-testid="skills-source-filter"`) shareable and refresh-stable via a URL search param, matching how `?search=` already works. The default remains All — omit the param when All is selected.

## Current behavior

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills._index.tsx` keeps `sourceFilter` in `React.useState('all')`. Toggling already resets `?page` via `setSearchParams`, but the filter itself never lands in the URL, so Back/Forward, refresh, and shared links lose it.
- Search is already URL-first: `GlobalToolbarSearch` commits `?search=` and the route reads it with `readSearchParam`.
- Filter values live in `SKILL_SOURCE_FILTERS` (`all` | `openthrottle` | `external` | `personal`) with `isSkillSourceFilter` as the guard (`~/routing/skills/utils/filter-skills-by-source`).
- Filtering stays client-side over the loader's merged list — do not re-query GraphQL or change the loader contract.

## Target behavior

Follow `docs/monorepo/url-first-ui-state.md`:

- Param name: `source` (same unprefixed style as this route's existing `search` / `page` / `limit`). Values are the `SkillSourceFilter` tokens.
- Default All: **delete** `source` when the selection is `all` (bare `/skills`, not `?source=all`). Missing or invalid values (`garbage`, empty) fall back to `all` — do not 404.
- The URL is the source of truth: drop the `useState`. Derive `sourceFilter` from `searchParams` with `isSkillSourceFilter`; write it in `handleSourceFilterChange` in one `URLSearchParams` mutation that also deletes `page` (keep landing a tighter filter on page 1). Use `preventScrollReset: true`. Prefer push (current `setSearchParams` default) so Back undoes a filter change.
- Preserve sibling params (`search`, `limit`, `modal`). `GlobalToolbarSearch`'s `transformCommittedParams` already only deletes `page` — keep `source` across a search submit.
- **Pagination must not drop `source` or `search`.** Today's `OpenThrottlePagination` rebuilds the query from `page`+`limit` only (`buildProjectsSearchParams`), so page links already wipe `?search=` and would wipe `?source=` too. Preserve the current query string on page links (clone `useSearchParams` and set `page`/`limit`, as `OpenThrottlePaginationSimple` does) — do not extend `ProjectsSearchParamsExtras` with a skills-only key, and do not map skills `search` onto extras.search (`q`).
- Empty state: `SkillsEmpty` currently treats only a non-empty `search` as "filtered". A `?source=` that matches nothing should also show the clear-filters CTA (link to `/skills`), not the "create your first skill" path. `isFiltered` on the route already includes `sourceFilter !== 'all'` for the new-user onboarding gate; thread that (or the source filter) into `SkillsEmpty` so the empty-table copy matches.
- `SkillsToolbar` can stay presentational (`sourceFilter` + `onSourceFilterChange`). URL ownership stays on the route.

## Out of scope

- Server-side filtering, GraphQL `SkillSource` changes, or treating Personal as a backend enum.
- Changing the default from All, or adding `?source=all` to the URL.
- Reworking other list toolbars.
title: URL-sync the skills source filter

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Stand up a library of high-impact **recurring** agent jobs that continuously improve this monorepo without a human driving each run. Deliverable is 10 prompt files in `.agents/prompts/`, each runnable standalone via Ralph `--prompt-file` (layer-1 prompt delivery) or an OT scheduled job.

## Decisions (locked)

1. **Output contract = OT plan + tasks.** Every job is *read-only on source code*. It never edits, fixes, or refactors. Its single side effect is creating one OpenThrottle plan (with prioritized, self-contained tasks) via the `openthrottle-mcp` MCP — the same posture as the `improve` skill. Nothing merges without a human starting that plan.
2. **Fully self-contained prompts.** No shared preamble file, no new skill. Each prompt repeats the shared rules so it works alone when passed to any agent CLI via `--prompt-file`. Duplication is accepted deliberately; the cost of a broken cross-file reference in an unattended run is higher than the cost of repetition.

## Conventions

- Location: `.agents/prompts/` (flat, SSOT; ingested into `custom_prompts` by `packages/openthrottle-skills`).
- Naming: `Job_<PascalCaseName>.md`, matching the existing lifecycle-phase prefix convention (`Before_*.md`, `After_*.md`). `Job_` denotes a standalone scheduled run, not a lifecycle hook.
- No frontmatter required — the prompt walker derives title/slug from the filename (`walk-agent-assets-on-disk.ts`).
- Every file uses the same section skeleton, locked by task 1 and copied verbatim into the other nine:
  - `# <Job name>` + one-line mission
  - `## Cadence` — the recommended schedule and why
  - `## Repo context` — commands, paths, and rules the job needs (no external links required to function)
  - `## What to inspect` — the specific, deterministic sweep
  - `## Ranking` — how to prioritize findings by impact
  - `## Hard rules` — read-only; no source edits; no PRs; no Markdown plan fallback; fail loudly if OT MCP is down
  - `## Dedupe` — check existing OT plans via `list_plans_by_status` / `semantic_search` before filing; skip or amend rather than duplicate
  - `## Output` — exactly one `create_plan` (author/assignee `visormatt`) + `create_tasks`; title prefix `🔁 <Job>:`; each task self-contained with file paths and acceptance criteria; if nothing material is found, file nothing and say so
- Budget guard: each prompt states a finding cap (top N by impact) so an unattended run cannot file a 200-task plan.

## The 10 jobs

1. `Job_TestHealth` — coverage gaps weighted by git churn, plus flaky/slow test detection (`audit:test-coverage:json`, repeat runs, timing outliers).
2. `Job_DeadCode` — knip report triage + unused/duplicate/misplaced dependencies. Report-only; never `knip --fix` on app UI.
3. `Job_Security` — secret scanning, `pnpm audit` CVE triage, unsafe patterns (auth guards, RBAC coverage, injection surfaces, exposed env).
4. `Job_DocDrift` — CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (3-tier + per-project) / README / docs commands vs actual code and targets.
5. `Job_RulesConformance` — `.agents/rules/coding/**` adherence beyond ESLint (enums, `as` casts, `any`, return types) + `audit:component-shape` / `audit:route-shape`.
6. `Job_DatabaseHealth` — migration hygiene, `COMMENT ON` coverage, index/FK gaps, entity↔schema drift, N+1 risk in resolvers.
7. `Job_ArchitectureDrift` — Nx tags, cross-project boundary violations, deep package imports, source-first packages that grew a `build` target, oversized files.
8. `Job_Performance` — RR app bundle growth per route, server hot paths, GraphQL resolver cost, build/test wall-clock regressions.
9. `Job_WorkInFlight` — unmerged PRs for DONE plans, stale branches/worktrees, stranded IN_PROGRESS plans with all tasks complete, missing work-ledger artifacts.
10. `Job_Roadmap` — monthly strategic sweep: propose 2–3 large structural changes / product bets from recent commit history, OT backlog, and open PRs.

## Validation

- `pnpm run check:local:agent-assets` (agent-asset frontmatter/ingest validation) must pass.
- Smoke-run at least two prompts end-to-end and confirm each files exactly one OT plan and no source edits.
- Update `AGENTS.md` and `docs/monorepo/agent-editor-folders.md` to document the `Job_` convention.
summary: Author 10 self-contained `.agents/prompts/Job_*.md` prompts for recurring scheduled agent runs. Each job is read-only on source and files findings as an OpenThrottle plan with prioritized tasks.
title: Recurring quality-job prompts: 10 scheduled audits that file OT plans

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The `/docs` and `/faq` routes in `applications/openthrottle-developer` are thin:
- `/faq` renders a 3-entry accordion (`FaqView`) topped with a literal **"Lorem ipsum" placeholder** paragraph (`app/routes/faq._index.tsx`).
- `/docs` has only 4 Markdown pages (`index`, `getting-started`, `docker-builds`, `docker-compose`); only docker-builds has real depth. Presentation is a bare sidebar + article — no search, no on-page TOC, no prev/next, no code-copy, weak landing.

Content and rendering are driven by the source-first package `@openthrottle/react-router-docs` (`FaqView`, `DocPageView`, `DocsNav`, `buildDocsManifest`, `buildDocsNav`) reading Markdown from `app/docs-content/{docs,faq}/`. Convention: `docs/openthrottle/docs-faq-convention.md`.

## Goals

1. **Content depth** — substantially expand docs pages and FAQ entries; kill placeholder copy.
2. **Four presentation upgrades**, each **independently toggleable on/off** so the owner can test with/without:
   - Client-side search across the manifest (title/description/body + FAQ), with a keyboard shortcut.
   - On-page TOC (right rail, scroll-spy) + copy-anchor links on headings.
   - Better landing/index for `/docs` (card overview) and a real `/faq` intro/category hero.
   - Prev/next sequential nav in docs + copy-to-clipboard on code blocks.

## Toggle design (key constraint)

Reuse the app's existing per-user persistence (`app/global/config/persistent-setting-storage.ts` + `useSyncExternalStore` hook pattern). Add a typed `DocsFeatureFlags` config (each upgrade its own flag, sensible defaults), overridable per-user via localStorage, and surface toggles in the Settings area (e.g. `settings.debug` / a "Docs (experimental)" panel). New package components must accept explicit props (enabled/data) so they render identically in tests both on and off; routes translate flags → props. SSR-safe: flags resolve to defaults on the server.

## Architecture constraints

- New presentation components live in `@openthrottle/react-router-docs` (source-first — no `build` target; validate via lint/typecheck/test, then `dev`/`build` on openthrottle-developer as the integration check).
- Feature-flag config, the settings toggle UI, and route wiring live in the app.
- Follow `.cursor/rules` code style; use `@tools/generators` (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component ...`) for new components/routes rather than hand-writing; keep the section-comment scaffold and one-component-per-file rule.
- Content is authored Markdown under `app/docs-content/` — no code changes needed for content tasks; frontmatter per the convention doc.
- No GraphQL/schema changes expected (docs/FAQ are static Markdown).

## Model guidance

- Taste-heavy UI tasks (search, TOC, landing, prev/next) → opus-4.8 or fable-5 (taste ≥ 7).
- Content-heavy Markdown tasks → sonnet-5 (bulk authoring).
- Reviews/validation → fable-5 or opus-4.8.

## Validation

Per-feature route + component tests covering flag ON and OFF; `pnpm nx run <project>:lint|typecheck|test`; consumer `dev`/`build` on openthrottle-developer; browser-preview screenshot verification of each toggle state.
summary: Refresh the thin /docs and /faq routes in openthrottle-developer: expand the Markdown content and add four presentation upgrades (client-side search, on-page TOC + anchors, better landing/index, prev-next nav + code-copy), each independently toggleable on/off for A/B testing via a persistent feature-flag layer.
title: Docs & FAQ refresh (openthrottle-developer) — content depth + toggleable UX upgrades

author: visormatt
description:
Wire @openthrottle/nestjs-rollout to React Router client apps via a new source-first package @openthrottle/react-router-rollout.

## Goal
Give each client app a typed, root-level rollout provider plus hooks so nested UI can read flags safely. Clients declare their full flag catalog (key, kind/type, default) alongside an application key (APP_NAME today; swappable for a UUID later). On mount the provider hydrates evaluations from the API, validates client catalog vs server payload (with caching), and exposes strongly typed hooks.

## Decisions (confirmed)
- Package: new @openthrottle/react-router-rollout; first consumer is openthrottle-developer.
- Application identity: use process.env.APP_NAME / window.env.APP_NAME as the per-app configuration key until a proper application UUID exists. Design the provider API around applicationKey (string) so swapping to UUID later is non-breaking.
- Audience: flag evaluation must work for authenticated AND unauthenticated users. Returning/authenticated identity is enrichment for targeting/bucketing, not a hard gate. Admin CRUD stays behind flags:read / flags:write.
- Depth: detailed implementation tasks with acceptance criteria.

## Existing building blocks
- Domain: packages/nestjs-rollout (RolloutService.evaluate / evaluateAll / isEnabled; kinds boolean|string|number|json).
- GraphQL (app-owned): applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/rollout/ — myFeatureFlags returns FeatureFlagObject[] (key, kind, reason, valueJson, variationIndex, enabled) but today requires FLAGS_READ and an auth principal.
- Client patterns to mirror: packages/react-router-notifications (provider + context hooks); other source-first react-router-* packages.

## Target client API (direction)
```ts
const flags = defineRolloutFlags({
  'billing.invoices': { kind: 'boolean', defaultValue: false },
  'theme.mode': { kind: 'string', defaultValue: 'system' },
} as const);

<RolloutProvider applicationKey={APP_NAME} flags={flags} client={graphqlClient}>
  {children}
</RolloutProvider>

const enabled = useRolloutFlag('billing.invoices'); // boolean
const theme = useRolloutFlag('theme.mode'); // string
```

## Out of scope (unless discovered blocking)
- Sticky hashing / assignment persistence (nestjs-rollout still uses non-sticky bucket).
- Full admin UI redesign beyond what hydration needs.
- Wiring every React Router app in this plan (developer first; package API must be reusable).

## Success criteria
1. New package scaffolds, links, lint/typecheck/test green.
2. Typed catalog + hooks compile-fail on unknown keys / wrong value usage.
3. Provider hydrates (anon + auth), caches validations, falls back to defaults on miss/error.
4. Server exposes a public evaluation query usable without flags:read.
5. openthrottle-developer mounts provider and demonstrates at least one real flag usage.
summary: Shipped @openthrottle/react-router-rollout: public evaluateFeatureFlags (anon+auth, no flags:read), typed defineRolloutFlags + RolloutProvider + hooks, wired in openthrottle-developer with catalog/data boundaries and demo usage. Lint/typecheck/tests green for package, server rollout, developer. Docs + nestjs-rollout cross-link in place.
title: Client rollout SDK: typed react-router-rollout package
