author: visormatt
description:
# Settings › Setup: agent CLIs as an actionable table + per-user enable/disable

## Context
`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.setup.tsx` renders a responsive **card grid** (`SettingsSetupCliCard` + `SettingsSetupCliControls`) — one card per agent-CLI backend, each listing every model as a wrapping `Badge` cloud. With more backends and long model lists this grows tall fast and wastes horizontal space. Today the only per-agent action is Install/Update (gated by the server env `OT_AGENT_CLI_INSTALL_ENABLED` and the `settings:write` permission), and the env disclaimer is repeated inside **every** card's controls.

Loader data comes from two queries: `SettingsSetupAgentClisDocument` (`discoverAgentClis` → `{ agents, scannedAt }`) and `AgentCliSetupConfigDocument` (`agentCliSetupConfig → { canManage, installEnabled }`). The display catalog + merge lives in `app/routing/settings/data/agent-clis.data.ts` (`mergeAgentCliStatuses`); the server owns the real allowlist via `@openthrottle/openthrottle-drivers` (`ALL_DRIVERS`). Server modules: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-setup/*` and `.../agent-discovery/*`.

## Goals
1. **Table, not cards.** Replace the card grid with a dense, scannable `SettingsSetupTable` — one row per agent — so status, models, enable/disable, and install/update read at a glance without vertical sprawl. Long model lists render compactly (count + truncation/expand), not an unbounded badge cloud.
2. **Per-user enable/disable at the agent level.** Each user can toggle an agent CLI on/off. Decisions (locked with owner):
   - **Persistence: per-user preference** — a user-scoped store of disabled agent backends (default: all enabled).
   - **Disable effect:** a disabled agent is (a) **hidden from chat/model pickers** and CLI selection surfaces, and (b) **blocked from new runs** (plan/task runs + scheduled jobs), enforced server-side — not merely dimmed on this page.
3. **One disclaimer, once.** The `OT_AGENT_CLI_INSTALL_ENABLED` explanation moves out of per-row controls to a single route-level notice (toolbar/introduction). Per-row permission reasons (e.g. missing `settings:write`) may still surface contextually, but the env-flag explanation appears exactly once.
4. **Standard component shape.** Scaffold the conventional gaps via `@tools/generators` (`react-router` component sub-generator): `SettingsSetupToolbar`, `SettingsSetupTable`, `SettingsSetupTableRow` (+ a small `SettingsSetupAgentToggle` and install-disclaimer piece as needed). `SettingsSetupIntroduction` already exists.

## Scope / non-goals
- **In scope:** agent-**level** on/off only. Per-user persistence + mutation, `enabled` surfaced on the setup query, downstream gating (pickers + run creation), the table/toolbar UI, disclaimer consolidation, codegen, co-located specs.
- **Out of scope → follow-up plan:** enable/disable at the **agent + model** granularity and **favoriting** a model. Tracked in the follow-up plan created by the final task of this plan.

## Key references
- Route: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.setup.tsx`
- Components: `app/routing/settings/components/SettingsSetupCli*.tsx`, `SettingsSetupIntroduction.tsx`
- Data/merge: `app/routing/settings/data/agent-clis.data.ts`
- Server: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-setup/*`, `.../agent-discovery/*`, config `agent-setup.config.ts`
- Registry (server truth): `packages/openthrottle-drivers` (`ALL_DRIVERS`)

## Constraints
- Generators before hand-writing components (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component ...`). Keep section comments + one component per file; copy/lists in nearest `data/`.
- UI from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` (Table primitives). Tests use `component` + `userEvent`.
- GraphQL is code-first; after schema/resolver/document changes run the codegen flow and commit `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` + `__generated__`.
- New user-scoped persistence needs a migration under `databases/migrations/` (idempotent DDL + table/column COMMENTs).
- Commit per task with `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers; no attribution lines.
summary: Refactor /settings/setup from a long card grid into a compact, actionable table; add per-user agent enable/disable that hides disabled agents from chat/model pickers and blocks their use in new runs; consolidate the OT_AGENT_CLI_INSTALL_ENABLED disclaimer to a single route-level notice.
title: Settings › Setup: agent CLIs as an actionable table + per-user enable/disable

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`/skills/:slug` lets any discovered skill's SKILL.md be edited in place. For **external** skills (installed from an upstream source, e.g. `/skills/create-cli`) an in-app edit silently forks the file from upstream: the next `skill-sync` / lockfile install either clobbers the edit or leaves the repo permanently diverged from the source. OpenThrottle-authored skills (e.g. `/skills/agents-ralph`, real directories under the repo's `skills/` tree) are the only ones we own and the only ones that should be editable here.

Provenance is already derived and surfaced — `discoverRepoSkills` sets `RepoSkillEntry.source` to `'openthrottle'` when the skill folder's realpath resolves under the authored `skills/` tree and `'external'` otherwise (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/agents/data/discover-repo-skills.server.ts`), the index has a Source column + filter, and `useSkillDetail` already computes `isOpenThrottle`. Nothing consumes it for write gating.

## Current write path (the only one)

There is **no GraphQL mutation** that writes SKILL.md. The single write surface is the developer app's route action:

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx` → `action` → `writeSkillFileBySlug(slug, content)`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/write-skill-file.server.ts` — resolves the monorepo root, re-discovers by slug, realpath-containment-checks the path, re-validates frontmatter, then `writeFileSync`.

So "API level" for this plan means that route action + `writeSkillFileBySlug`. That server helper is the authoritative gate: the UI gate is a courtesy, the helper must refuse regardless of what the client posts.

## Goal

1. **API:** `writeSkillFileBySlug` refuses with a structured error when the discovered entry's `source !== 'openthrottle'` — checked after slug discovery (so provenance comes from disk, never from client input) and before frontmatter validation / any write.
2. **UI:** on `/skills/:slug` for an external skill, the Edit button is disabled with a tooltip explaining the upstream-sync reason (distinct from today's "needs a local checkout" tooltip), and edit mode is unreachable.

## Explicit non-goals

- **Record-level tags stay editable** for external skills. `project_skills.tags`, add/remove tag, orphan removal, and skill-availability rules are database rows, not SKILL.md content — none of them drift from upstream. Do not gate them.
- **Running** an external skill stays allowed.
- The in-app IDE / any generic file editor is out of scope; this plan gates the skills surface only.
- No schema/migration work — provenance is already available on the entry.

## Key files

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/write-skill-file.server.ts` (+ `__tests__/write-skill-file.server.test.ts`)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/hooks/useSkillDetail.tsx`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/components/SkillDetailEditControls.tsx`, `SkillIntroduction.tsx`, `SkillDetailTabs.tsx`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts` (`SKILL_DETAIL_COPY`, `SKILL_WRITE_COPY`, `SKILLS_SOURCE_COPY`)

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`. Live browser verification of authed pages is blocked without a permissioned seeded user — cover the gate with render-level Vitest instead.
title: Make external skills read-only (UI + write API)

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

The skill catalog has grown to **44 skills** (26 authored under `skills/`, 18 vendored per `skills-lock.json`). Every skill's frontmatter description is always-on context: **~16.9 KB / ~4.2k tokens burned in every session** before any work starts. Meanwhile the real usage data says almost none of it earns its place.

## The evidence (skill_usage_events + skill_usage_outcomes, 2026-07-31 → 2026-08-17)

226 invocations, 185 recorded outcomes.

**Only 13 of 44 skills fired at all. 31 (70%) never fired once.**

Traffic is brutally concentrated — 5 skills are 92% of all invocations:

| skill | invocations | sessions | last used | outcomes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| github-squash | 55 | 53 | 08-16 | 46 ok / 3 abandoned, avg 147s |
| ot-claude-loop | 48 | 47 | 08-17 | 43 ok / 4 abandoned, avg 2190s |
| github-pull-request | 41 | 40 | 08-16 | 34 ok, avg 141s |
| ot-plan-loop | 27 | 26 | **08-14 (stale)** | 18 ok, avg 1849s |
| loop (built-in) | 24 | 12 | 08-13 | 18 ok / 1 abandoned |
| github-commit | 12 | 12 | 08-16 | 8 ok / 1 abandoned |
| ot-plans | 10 | 10 | 08-15 | 3 ok |
| skill-sync | 3 | 3 | 08-14 | 1 ok / 1 abandoned |
| ot-onboarding, agents-ralph, monitor-ci, git-commit, claude-api | 1 each | | | |

**Zero recorded invocations:** every `github-branch`/`create-issue`/`my-pull-requests`/`summarize`/`untracked`/`worktree`, every `ot-ask`/`ot-create-plan`/`ot-edit-task`/`ot-list-by-status`, all five `nx-*`, `openthrottle-folders`/`generators`/`stack`, `ot-postgres`, `ot-workflow-orchestration`, `improve`, `validate-plan`, `create-cli`, `create-readme`, `frontend-design`, `teach`, `handoff`, `grill-me`, `grill-with-docs`, `grilling`, `skill-cleaner`, `skillopt-sleep`, `writing-great-skills`, `link-workspace-packages`.

## Caveat that gates the deletions

The capture hooks record **Skill-tool and slash invocations only**. Skills injected into subagents (`Workflow`/`Agent` prompts) and skills read as reference material by a model that never calls the Skill tool are invisible. `improve` is the proof: memory records a 51-plan `ot-improve` remediation fleet, yet it shows 0 events. **Task 1 closes this blind spot before anything is deleted on 0-use grounds.**

## Confirmed structural fat (independent of telemetry)

- **`ot-plan-loop` vs `ot-claude-loop` are near-identical** — a 16-line diff, and the only real divergence is that claude-loop adds squash + rebase + draft PR. Two 1200-word skills, one job. claude-loop is the live one (48 uses, current); plan-loop went stale 08-14.
- **`grill-me` is a 147-byte file whose entire body is "Run a `/grilling` session."** Plus `grill-with-docs` (34 words). Three skills, one behavior.
- **Four `ot-*` CRUD wrappers** (`ot-ask`, `ot-create-plan`, `ot-edit-task`, `ot-list-by-status`, 126–271 words each) are thin restatements of MCP calls that `ot-plans` already documents.
- **Five vendored `nx-*` skills** (~4.4k words) overlap the `nx-mcp` server's own tools, CLAUDE.md's command table, and `openthrottle-generators` — which actively *contradicts* `nx-generate` (this repo mandates `@tools/generators` with `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false`).

## Target

44 skills → roughly 25. Always-on description budget ~4.2k tokens → under 2k. Every survivor either has telemetry behind it or a written justification for why it has none.

## How to work this plan

Each task is self-contained and promotable to its own plan (`promote_task`). Do **task 1 first** — it validates the data every other cut relies on. Tasks 2–4 are the confirmed-duplicate consolidations and are safe to run in parallel after task 1. Run `/skill-sync` after every skill add/remove/rename so the fan-out and `skills-lock.json` stay reconciled.
summary: Umbrella plan. 44 skills, 13 ever invoked in 17 days of telemetry. Each task below is scoped to be promoted to its own plan and executed independently.
title: Skill catalog trim: cut the fat, consolidate duplicates (metrics-driven)

author: visormatt
description:
> Promoted from task 33dedfa0 in plan 653d1be5-4818-4a6b-ad07-645ff64e16c0, then re-scoped to carry the whole low-risk first pass.

## Intent

653d1be5 proposes 5-6 libraries. That is too much churn to commit to on a hypothesis. This plan does the smallest thing that produces a real CI number:

- **Phase A — probe (tasks 1-3).** Prove the mechanism with a throwaway library. Nothing real moves. Fully reversible.
- **Phase B — the coarse split (tasks 4-6).** Two new libraries, not six. All 26 `app/routing` domains go out as ONE library.
- **Phase C — measure and decide (task 7).** Real before/after CI numbers, then a documented go/no-go on 653d1be5.

## What "start with routes and routing" actually means here

`app/routes/**` **cannot become its own project.** `routes.ts`, `@react-router/fs-routes`, and the `.react-router/types` typegen are all app-scoped — route modules must stay where React Router expects them. So the split is not routes-vs-routing; it is **routing (plus its shared substrate) moves out, routes stays behind as the app**.

Target after Phase B — three Nx projects instead of one:

| project | what it holds | ~test files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openthrottle-developer` (app) | `app/routes/**`, `root.tsx`, `entry.*.tsx`, `styles.css`, the 89 colocated `.tsx.graphql` documents | ~124 |
| `@openthrottle/developer-kernel` | `app/__generated__`, `app/global/**`, `app/services/**`, `app/testing/**` | ~12 |
| `@openthrottle/developer-routing` | all 26 `app/routing/<domain>` folders, as one library | ~553 |

## The honest math on what this buys

Heaviest unit goes from **677 test files to ~553** — roughly an 18% cut to the floor, not a 3x win. Lint and typecheck parallelize better than that since they split cleanly across three projects.

The bigger payoff is structural: once `routing` is out as one library, **all ~60 cross-domain `routing/X -> routing/Y` edges become intra-library and cost nothing to resolve**. Every subsequent split in 653d1be5 then happens inside a library that already has clean external boundaries, which is a far easier problem than the one 653d1be5 describes today. This plan is the cheap way to buy that.

If the measured improvement in Phase C is not worth it, the fallback stands: a Vitest `--shard` split inside the single project (worse for lint/typecheck, no code movement).

## Carried-over constraints from 653d1be5

- **Nx must SEE the edge.** `~/*` maps inside the app, so nested `project.json` files under `app/routing/*` produce NO Nx dependency and therefore **false cache hits**. Task 2 proves this rather than assuming it. Real `@openthrottle/*` package names only; top-level entry imports, no deep package imports.
- Source-first libraries: no `build` target, `main`/`types` -> `./src/index.ts`, Vite transpiles. Same contract as the 16 existing `react-router-*` libs.
- Scaffold with `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:package` — do not hand-write skeletons.
- Nx `sync` is disabled (cf8469de); tsconfig `references` are manual and validated by `check:tsconfig-refs`.
- Tags via `pnpm nx:validate-tags`; knip clean, public API tagged `@public`.
- Both codegen passes must keep working — the app's `enumsAsTypes: true` pass and the deliberately divergent `@openthrottle/openthrottle-developer-codegen` runtime-enum pass. Do not consolidate them.
- One shared `setupReactRouterTest` call; do not re-add jsdom shims per library.

## Definition of done

`pnpm run check:local` green, CI green, and Phase C's before/after heaviest-shard wall-clock recorded in plan output alongside a written go/no-go on 653d1be5.
summary: DONE — draft PR #400. Phase A proved the Nx mechanism works and disproved the nested-project.json shortcut; the baseline measurement (moved ahead of Phase B at the grilling gate) then killed the split: heaviest unit is 88.4% `test`, so splitting buys ~23% where a config-only Vitest `--shard` buys ~53%. Phase B CANCELED, 653d1be5 CANCELED, successor plan 9fc16731 created. Shipped the 21-edge reverse-import refactor, which stood on its own merits.
title: Prove the Nx boundary, then split openthrottle-developer the coarse way and measure CI

author: visormatt
description:
Promote the repeated list-toolbar search pattern (search input + Search button) into a shared GlobalToolbarSearch in @openthrottle/react-router-ui-global.

## Why
SkillsToolbar currently inlines an unconnected search Input + Search button. The same markup and submit-to-URL logic is duplicated across list toolbars (Notes, Calendar, Projects, Plans, Prompts, Rules, QueueOps, Mail, Editor). Most of those write `?q=`. We want one primitive, URL as source of truth, default param name `search`.

## Existing pieces (do not reinvent)
- `@openthrottle/react-router-ui` already has `useDebouncedSearchParam` (default key `q`, live debounce + `commitNow`). Keep it. v1 of GlobalToolbarSearch is **submit-only**, not live search. A later optional live mode can wrap that hook.
- `GlobalSearch` in react-router-ui-global is an unused heading stub, not this control. Do **not** reuse or replace it. New name: `GlobalToolbarSearch`.
- URL conventions: docs/monorepo/url-first-ui-state.md §7 (local input, committed value in URL, `replace: true`).

## Target API (v1)
- Scaffold with `@tools/generators` `react` → destination `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global`, folder `components`, name `GlobalToolbarSearch`. Copy in nearest `data.copy.ts` (default button label). Export from package `src/index.ts` with `@public`.
- Own `<form role="search">` wrapping Input (`type="search"`) + outline Search Button. **Do not nest forms.** Toolbars that wrap the whole row in one form must split: search form is a sibling of other controls (filters/CTAs stay outside).
- Default URL param: `search`. Optional `paramKey` override for gradual `q` migrations.
- Local controlled input; hydrate from URL; sync when the committed param changes (back/forward).
- On submit: trim; set param or delete when empty; `setSearchParams(..., { replace: true, preventScrollReset: true })`; preserve other params.
- Optional `transformCommittedParams` (or equivalent) so paginated lists can reset `page` to 1.
- Props: `placeholder`, `aria-label`, `className`, `paramKey`, `transformCommittedParams`. Consumer-specific copy stays in the area `data.copy.ts`.
- Not in scope for v1: debounce/live typing, semantic search, commander/global overlay search, IDE `/search` and `/agent-search` (those stay dedicated SearchForms on `q`).

## First consumer
SkillsToolbar + `/skills` index: wire the control, filter entries client-side by slug/path/summary from `searchParams.get('search')`, reset page when the query changes. Skills has no existing `q` bookmarks.

## Follow-on migrations
For each list toolbar, swap the duplicated form for GlobalToolbarSearch and update the loader/table parser in the **same** task. Prefer `search`; during a surface’s cutover, reading `search` then falling back to `q` is OK so old URLs still work. Do not change `useDebouncedSearchParam`’s default key until those call sites migrate.
Surfaces: Notes, Calendar, Projects, QueueOps, Rules, Prompts, Plans (usePlansToolbar), plus email MailToolbar / editor EditorToolbar if they share the same submit pattern.

## Tests
Package spec: hydrate from `?search=`, submit writes/replaces URL, empty submit deletes param, other params preserved, transform resets page. SkillsToolbar/index specs: filter + URL. Assert roles/labels/`data-testid` and imported copy constants, not duplicated literals.
summary: Extract a shared GlobalToolbarSearch (submit-to-URL, default param search=) into @openthrottle/react-router-ui-global, prove it on SkillsToolbar, then migrate duplicated list toolbars. Not live/debounced in v1.
title: Promote GlobalToolbarSearch for URL-driven list toolbars

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

A plan is created from inside the checkout it is eventually meant to run in — the OT MCP server is launched by the agent/editor in that workspace. Yet the workspace fact is thrown away at creation, and the user is asked to re-supply it later in the plan-detail Configuration tab under `02. Workspace` (`PlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector`), which writes `checkoutId` → `repositoryId` → `workingDirectory` into the plan's `runConfigJson`.

Today the only automatic fill is a one-shot in `usePlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector`: when nothing is selected AND the plan has a `projectId` that maps to exactly one repository with exactly one checkout, it defaults to that `repositoryId`. Every other plan opens on "Monorepo root (default)" and needs a manual selection before a run is enqueued.

## Approach (decided)

Source of truth for "the workspace we're already in" is **the MCP caller's cwd**, resolved **server-side** into a registered checkout owned by the authenticated caller.

Flow:

1. The stdio MCP bin captures the caller's workspace once at startup (`OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` override, else `process.cwd()`).
2. `create_plan` / `create_plans` send it as a new optional `workspacePath` on `CreatePlanInput`.
3. `PlanCreationService` resolves that path → the caller's checkout (realpath-normalized, deepest containing checkout wins so worktrees and subdirectories land correctly) and seeds `runConfig.checkoutId` (+ `repositoryId`).
4. The plan-detail route already hydrates `runConfigJson` into the run-config atoms, so `02. Workspace` opens pre-selected and the branch pre-fills from the checkout's current branch via `PlanRunConfigRepositoriesHydrator`.

## Hard constraints

- **Never a gate.** An unresolvable, unregistered, or absent path must fall through to today's behaviour (root default + the `projectId` prefill). Plan creation must never fail because of this field.
- **Never trust a client path blindly.** Resolution is server-side and user-scoped, mirroring `code-search.resolver.ts` (`repositoryId → filesystemPath`, user-scoped, never a client-supplied path). `createPlan` / `createPlans` currently take no user context — `@CurrentUser('sub')` must be threaded in (the decorator is already used elsewhere in `plans.resolver.ts`).
- **`process.cwd()` is only meaningful on the stdio transport.** The Nest/HTTP MCP surface (`bin-http.ts`, `src/nest/`) runs inside the server, where `process.cwd()` is the *server's* directory. That surface must omit `workspacePath`, never infer it.
- **Explicit input wins.** A `runConfigJson` that already names a workspace, or an explicitly-passed `workspacePath`, is never overridden by the captured cwd.
- `create_plan`'s tool schema already accepts `runConfigJson`; only its description omits it. Descriptions need updating alongside the new field.

## Key files

- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/plan-creation/plan-creation.service.ts`
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plan.input.ts`, `plans.resolver.ts`
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/worktree-discovery/worktree-discovery.service.ts` (prior art: realpath-keyed checkout index)
- `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/{bin.ts,run-server.ts,tools/plans.ts}`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/{components/PlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector.tsx,hooks/usePlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector.ts,components/PlanRunConfigStoreProvider.tsx}`
summary: Plans are created from inside the checkout they will run in, so the OT MCP should capture the caller's cwd, resolve it server-side to one of the caller's registered checkouts, and seed the plan's runConfig workspace — turning "02. Workspace" from a required selection into a pre-filled, editable default.
title: Record the creating workspace on a plan instead of asking for it in 02. Workspace

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

**Applying workspace editor configuration to a foreign repo causes foreign-skill injection to silently skip 10 of OpenThrottle's own curated skills.** The user is left with empty directories where those skills should be — functionality that looks present on disk but is not there.

Found 2026-08-28 while writing the cross-feature test for OT plan `5a1ac8d1` (task 4). Entirely **pre-existing**: neither `5a1ac8d1` nor `b409da6e` introduced it.

## Mechanism — two correct behaviors colliding

1. `WorkspaceEditorConfigService.applyForRepositoryEditor` (`packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/workspace-settings/workspace-editor-config.service.ts`) does `mkdir(dirname(skillPath))` for every entry in `OPENTHROTTLE_REPO_SKILL_PATHS`. That creates **empty** `.agents/skills/<slug>/` directories for:

   `brag-sheet`, `git-commit`, `link-workspace-packages`, `monitor-ci`, `nx-workspace`, `ot-claude-loop`, `ot-generators`, `ot-plans`, `ot-stack`, `workflow-ralph`

2. `scanTargetOwnedSkillNames` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/foreign-skill-injection/materialize.ts`) lists those directories and treats each basename as a skill **the target repo owns**.

3. `resolveForeignSkillManifest` then drops every target-owned name from the manifest *before* materialization — the target-wins rule in design doc §1, working exactly as designed.

The result is that OT's target-wins protection fires against directories **OT itself created**.

## Reproduction

```
editor-config applied first = false
  injected: [ 'nx-workspace', 'ot-plans', 'some-other-skill' ]
  ot-plans really present? true

editor-config applied first = true
  injected: [ 'some-other-skill' ]
  ot-plans really present? false        <- empty directory, no SKILL.md
```

Both orders are reachable in the real product: applying editor config and injecting skills are independent user actions with no ordering guarantee.

## Why this matters more than the residue bug

`5a1ac8d1` fixed untracked residue — cosmetic. This one removes working functionality, and does so **invisibly**: the directories exist, so nothing looks wrong until an agent cannot find `ot-plans`. The affected set is precisely OT's most important curated skills.

## Direction — needs a decision, options not yet weighed

- **Stop pre-creating the dirs.** Does anything actually depend on empty `.agents/skills/<slug>/` existing? If the intent was "advertise which skills OT offers", the manifest's `enabledSkillPaths` already records that. Simplest fix if nothing reads them.
- **Make target-owned detection require a real skill.** A directory with no `SKILL.md` is not a skill; `scanTargetOwnedSkillNames` could require one. Arguably correct regardless of this bug — an empty dir should never mask a real skill.
- **Record OT-created dirs** so injection can distinguish its own scaffolding from the repo's content. The ledger already records `createdDirs` for a related purpose.

The second option looks strongest on its own merits and fixes the class rather than the instance, but the first should be checked first — if nothing needs those dirs, not creating them is less machinery.

## Non-goals

- Changing the target-wins precedence rule itself (design doc §1). It is correct; it is being fed bad input.

## Related

- OT `5a1ac8d1` — where this was found; its task 4 test uses a deliberately out-of-list skill name to avoid tripping on this.
- OT `b409da6e` — foreign-skill injection non-mutation fix.
- `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md` §1 (precedence / target-wins).
summary: The editor apply pre-creates empty .agents/skills/<slug>/ dirs for 10 OT slugs; foreign-skill injection reads those as skills the target repo owns and refuses to inject them. Result: empty directories where OT's skills should be, in whichever order the user happens to hit.
title: Applying editor config silently drops 10 of OT's curated skills in foreign repos

author: visormatt
description:
## Origin

Spun out of the **Skill usage tracking** plan (OT d3759118). That plan ships skill-usage capture with a FIXED default privacy level (truncated args) but deliberately funnels args through a single `applyPrivacy(level, args)` seam. This plan turns that seam into a real, user-configurable control — a natural productizable / paid-tier feature (fine-grained telemetry governance is something orgs pay for).

**Depends on** OT d3759118 shipping the `applyPrivacy` seam + persistence first. Do not start until at least Phases 1–2 of that plan exist.

## Levels to support (draft)

- `off` — capture nothing (skill not recorded at all).
- `name-only` — skill name + metadata (session, cwd, branch, scope, timestamp); NO args.
- `truncated` — name-only + args truncated/redacted (the fixed default from the base plan).
- `full` — full args verbatim (heaviest privacy/retention burden; likely gated behind explicit opt-in).

## Dimensions to think through (design task should settle these)

1. **Config scope & precedence** — global default vs per-project vs per-skill override. Where does the setting live (settings.json? OT rollout flags — see OT 184a4971? server-side org policy)? Likely a hybrid with a clear precedence order.
2. **Enforcement point** — client-side (hook redacts before it ever leaves the machine — strongest privacy guarantee) vs server-side policy. Client-side redaction should be the floor so raw args never transit when a lower level is set.
3. **Retention** — different retention windows per level (e.g. `full` args auto-expire faster). Ties into a retention/TTL job.
4. **Paid-feature gating** — which levels / which granularity (per-skill overrides, org policy enforcement, audit log) sit behind a paid tier. Reuse the rollout/feature-flag package (OT 184a4971) rather than bespoke gating.
5. **Auditability** — an org admin should be able to see/prove what level is in effect and that lower levels actually redact.

## Not now

This is a design-first, future track. No implementation until the base capture plan is live and there's real demand signal. Keep it on the roadmap, not in the current build queue.
summary: Make the privacy level of skill-usage capture a configurable knob (name-only → truncated → full args), building on the applyPrivacy seam from the skill-usage-tracking plan. Candidate paid/enterprise feature.
title: Configurable privacy levels for skill-usage capture (future / paid-feature track)

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Relocate the existing **Repositories** feature from `/settings/workspace` into its own first-class **`/settings/repositories`** section in `applications/openthrottle-developer`. This is **phase 1: housekeeping only** — move, rename, and reorganize. No new capabilities, no behavior changes. A clean home for repositories so later phases can build on it.

## Current state (as-is)

Repositories currently live inside the Workspace settings page. Everything below is under `applications/openthrottle-developer/`.

**Routes (file-based flat-routes via `app/routes.ts`):**
- `app/routes/settings.workspace._index.tsx` (+ `.graphql`) — Workspace index; renders profile form, editor-config, AND the repositories section. Loader returns `workspaceRepositories`, `discoveredFolders`, `pickerCapabilities` (repo) alongside `profile` (non-repo). Action dispatches repo intents `cloneRepo`, `deleteRepo`, `refreshCheckout`, `addFolder`, `browseDirectory`, `pickFolderNative` plus non-repo `updateProfile`, `applyEditorConfig`.
- `app/routes/settings.workspace.repositories.$repositoryId._index.tsx` (+ `.graphql`) — repo detail (`getWorkspaceRepository`).
- `app/routes/settings.workspace.repositories.$repositoryId.edit.tsx` (+ `.graphql`) — repo edit (`getWorkspaceRepositoryForEdit` + `updateRepository`).

**Repo components** (`app/routing/settings/components/`): `SettingsWorkspaceRepositoriesSection`, `WorkspaceRepositoryCard`, `WorkspaceRepositoryDetail`, `WorkspaceRepositoryEditForm`, `WorkspaceRepositoriesProjectSelect`, `WorkspaceCloneRepoDialog`, `WorkspaceAddFolderDialog`, `WorkspaceAddFolderCandidate`, `WorkspaceAddFolderResult`, `WorkspaceDirectoryPicker`, `WorkspaceBrowseEntryRow`, `WorkspaceNativeBrowse`. Hook: `useWorkspaceAddFolderDialog`. Action impls: `app/routing/settings/actions/workspace.ts`. Path helper: `workspaceRepositoryDetailPath` in `app/routing/settings/utils/workspace-settings-action.ts`.

**Stays on Workspace:** `SettingsWorkspaceIntro`, `SettingsWorkspaceProfileForm`, `SettingsWorkspaceApplyEditors`, editor multi-select/affiliate-link components, `workspace-editors.ts` config, `is-workspace-editor-id`, `format-editor-config-result`, `drift-labels`, and the `updateProfile`/`applyEditorConfig` actions.

**Nav:** `app/global/data/data.navigation.ts` — the `Settings:` array is where the `/settings/repositories` entry gets added.

**GraphQL:** all ops in the three colocated `.graphql` files; generated into `app/__generated__/graphql.ts` + `gql.ts` via codegen (must be regenerated + committed).

**Tests:** component tests under `app/routing/settings/components/__tests__/`; route tests under `app/routes/__tests__/` (`settings.workspace.repositories.$repositoryId.*`); util/hook tests for `workspace-settings-action` and `useWorkspaceAddFolderDialog`.

## Target state

- New `/settings/repositories` index route owning the repository list, add-folder, clone, refresh, and delete flows.
- `/settings/repositories/:repositoryId` detail + `/settings/repositories/:repositoryId/edit` sub-routes (moved from under workspace).
- Repository components/hooks/actions/utils renamed off the `Workspace*` prefix and organized under a `repositories/` grouping within `app/routing/settings/` (naming TBD in the reorg task — favor `Repository*` / `repositories.ts`).
- `/settings/workspace` retains only profile + editor configuration.
- A `Repositories` entry in the Settings nav; breadcrumbs and path helpers point at `/settings/repositories`.
- All tests moved/renamed and passing; GraphQL codegen regenerated; typecheck/lint/build green.

## Constraints & notes

- **No behavior change** — pure move/rename/reorg. Prefer `git mv` to preserve history.
- Flat-routes derive URLs from filenames — renaming `settings.workspace.repositories.*` → `settings.repositories.*` is the mechanism.
- Update the hardcoded `/settings/workspace/repositories/...` path in `workspace-settings-action.ts` and the `Workspace → /settings/workspace` breadcrumb crumbs in the two sub-routes.
- After any `.graphql` change: `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel`, then commit `__generated__`.
- Use `@tools/generators` (`react-router` generator) where new files are scaffolded rather than hand-writing; then move logic in.
- Validate with `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck` + `:lint` + `:test`; integration check via `:build` or `:dev`.

## Out of scope (future phases)

New repository capabilities, backend/schema changes, and any UX redesign. This plan only relocates what exists.
summary: Move the existing Repositories feature out of /settings/workspace into a dedicated /settings/repositories route — rename, relocate, and reorganize with no behavior change. Phase 1 housekeeping ahead of future repository work.
title: Extract Repositories into a first-class /settings/repositories route

author: visormatt
description:
Prevent a recurrence of the poisoned Nx remote-cache failure hit on PR #254 (branch ot/license-compliance-automation, 2026-07-29). CI restored a truncated `@openthrottle/openthrottle-agentic-utils:build` artifact from the GCS Nx cache (gs://openthrottle-staging-nx-cache/nx-cache/<hash>): the cached dist had a correct `import { getOpenThrottleRoot } from "./workflow.js"` in `foreign-workspace-context.js` but was MISSING `workflow.js` itself, so `monorepo:test` (which imports the package via scripts/openthrottle-database-migrations.test.ts) failed with "Cannot find module .../dist/src/utils/workflow.js". Two GCS objects (hashes 12318852324888656449, 14094666500388666538) were confirmed incomplete and purged 2026-07-29; a fresh build is healthy. Root cause is the same class as the agentic-ralph incident fixed 2026-07-24 (commit 4c8062b7): a `tsc --build` incremental no-op "succeeds" against stale on-disk state and caches an incomplete/stale dist under a fresh hash, permanently poisoning that key. See the poisoned-gcs-nx-remote-cache runbook. This plan hardens agentic-utils (and audits the remaining latent siblings) so a truncated dist can never be produced or cached again.

Reference commit that fixed agentic-ralph: 4c8062b7 (per-package .gitignore `!src/__generated__/**/*` + narrow codegen-graphql outputs to app/__generated__ and src/__generated__). Still-latent siblings called out in the runbook: openthrottle-mcp, vscode-openthrottle, openthrottle-developer-codegen, admin/email/website apps — plus openthrottle-agentic-utils (this plan).
title: Harden openthrottle-agentic-utils build against poisoned Nx cache (truncated tsc dist)

author: visormatt
description:
Capture and enforce a Component body convention that agents currently miss: unpack `props` (and anything taken from those bindings) at the top of the function, before `// Hooks`. Derived/narrowed values stay under `// Setup`. This is **one abstract contract** that both authored components (`FooProps`) and route default Components (`Route.ComponentProps`) must persist — not two one-off rules.

## Why this exists

Exemplar (already applied locally, not yet the house rule):

`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.repositories.$repositoryId._index.tsx` and `settings.repositories._index.tsx`.

Before: `const { loaderData } = props` and `const { repository } = loaderData` sat after `// 🔌 Short Circuit`, immediately above `return`. After: those identity unpacks sit between the signature and `// Hooks`. On the list route, `'error' in actionData` narrowing stayed in `// Setup` — that split is the rule.

The same split applies to authored components: `const { className, repository } = props` (and `const { id, name } = repository` when `repository` came from props) belongs in the pre-Hooks block; a formatted label or `'x' in y` narrowing belongs in `// Setup`. Route.ComponentProps is just a specific props shape (`loaderData` / `actionData` / `params` / `matches`), not a different convention.

The written contract already hints at the first line only:

- Component R3 (`docs/monorepo/component-primitive-shape.md`): optional `const { … } = props` between the signature and `// Hooks`.
- Route R2 (`docs/monorepo/route-primitive-shape.md`): same sentence for the default Component — currently a fork of that sentence, not a pointer.
- Route generator already emits `const { actionData: _a, loaderData: _l, matches: _m, params: _p } = props;` in that slot.
- Component generator currently comments out `// const {  } = props` and binds `_props`.

Gaps:

1. Nested unpack (`const { repository } = loaderData` or `const { id } = item` from a prop) is unspecified, so agents treat it as Setup or dump it with the return.
2. Unpack vs derive is unspecified — identity destructure vs `'x' in y` / mapping / formatting.
3. ESLint `openthrottle/component-primitive-shape` and `openthrottle/route-primitive-shape` only check marker presence, order, and blank lines. They do not look at statement placement. The after-Short-Circuit dump is the common anti-pattern (still in `settings.workspace._index.tsx`, `settings.repositories.$repositoryId.edit.tsx`, `settings.rollout.$flagId.edit.tsx`, and many others).
4. Agent rules (`.agents/rules/coding/frontend-design-openthrottle.mdc` and siblings) mention the six markers but not the pre-Hooks unpack block, so agents will keep writing the anti-pattern even after docs change unless the rule files say it.
5. The two ESLint files already duplicate `MARKERS` / `checkMarkers`. A third copy of unpack logic would drift; the checker must be shared.

## The convention (normative, one idea)

Inside **any** render function that follows the six-marker shape (authored component or route default `Component`):

1. **Pre-Hooks unpack block** (between `{` and `// Hooks`, one blank line before the marker):
   - `const { … } = props;` (unused keys prefixed `_`).
   - Immediate nested identity destructure of those bindings: `const { repository } = loaderData;`, `const { slug } = params;`, `const { id, name } = item;` when `item` came from props.
   - No derived/narrowed values here.
2. **`// Setup`**: derived values from those bindings (discriminated-union narrowing like `actionData && 'error' in actionData ? actionData.error : null`, maps, formatters).
3. **Never** place `const { … } = props` (or nested unpack from a props-derived binding) after `// Hooks`, and especially not after `// 🔌 Short Circuit`.

Hooks stay first after the unpack so Rules-of-Hooks order remains stable; Setup can then use both unpacked props and hook results.

## Architecture — pull the idea out, wire it into both

Do **not** implement a route-only check and a component-only check. The abstract rule is “identity ObjectPattern unpack of `props` and of bindings taken from `props`, before `// Hooks`." Route keys (`loaderData`, …) fall out of that walk; they are not a special case.

- **Docs:** Component R3 owns the unpack-block contract (SSOT). Route R2 says the default Component follows component R3 including that block, then shows a route-shaped example (`loaderData` → `repository`). Do not fork the rule text.
- **Agent rules:** One bullet covering both surfaces.
- **ESLint:** Extract a shared helper (e.g. `tools/dotfiles/src/rules/pre-hooks-unpack.ts`) that, given a function body + source, reports identity unpacks after the first `// Hooks` marker. Both `component-primitive-shape` and `route-primitive-shape` call it. Unit-test the helper; each RuleTester still has a valid/invalid fixture for its surface.
- **Warn-first on both rules.** Inventory routes *and* authored components. Graduate to error later, independently if the tails differ, same rollout as route-shape R4.

## Enforcement details

- Flag a `VariableDeclarator` whose init is Identifier `props`, or an ObjectPattern destructure of a binding previously taken from `props`, if it appears after the first `// Hooks` marker in the same function body.
- Do **not** flag ordinary `const` in Setup (narrowing, mapping) — only identity ObjectPattern unpack from props-derived names.
- Message should point at the pre-Hooks slot and component R3 (route reports can still link route R2, which points at R3).
- Autofix is optional and not required.
- Keep the generator as SSOT: route template already correct; component template currently comments out `const { } = props` — uncomment/normalize so template, docs, and rule cannot drift.

## Out of scope

- Mass-migrating every violating route or component in this plan (inventory + a few exemplars; bulk fix is a follow-up once warn-first is live).
- Requiring unused `_a` / `_l` / `_m` / `_p` keys — generator style, not this rule.
- Changing marker order or the Short Circuit early-return contract.
- Deduplicating the existing `MARKERS` / `checkMarkers` copies (nice-to-have, not this plan) — only the new unpack checker must be shared.
title: Pre-Hooks props unpack: agent rule + ESLint

author: visormatt
description:
Plans created through the OT MCP never get their workspace seeded (plan 8c1396b8 / PR #450 feature), because the MCP authenticates as a service account and workspace resolution is user-scoped: createPlan passes the service-account UUID as userId, repository_checkouts rows all belong to human users, so seedWorkspaceFromPath silently no-ops and the plan-detail editor buttons (Claude/Cursor) stay dead.

Fix (option 1, chosen 2026-08-27): let a service account act as a user. Add nullable service_accounts.acting_user_id (FK users, ON DELETE SET NULL). When the auth principal is a service account with a linked user, user-scoped conveniences — starting with plan workspace seeding — resolve against that user's registered checkouts. The link is provisioned by bootstrap-default-user.ts (both bootstrap SAs → the seeded developer user, only when unset) and editable via the updateServiceAccount GraphQL mutation. Resolution stays a hint, never a gate: an SA without a link seeds nothing, exactly as today.
summary: All 6 tasks done on branch openthrottle/service-account-acting-user (stacked on openthrottle/loop-plan-workspace-cwd). Migration 107 adds service_accounts.acting_user_id; EffectiveUserResolutionService maps SA subs to their acting user in plan workspace seeding; bootstrap-default-user links openthrottle-mcp + workflow-ralph to the default user; actingUserId on the GraphQL surface. Live-verified: a fresh stdio MCP create_plan from /home/demo/Development/openthrottle seeded checkoutId/repositoryId to the developer-e1e878@atlasworks.example checkout.
title: Service accounts act as a user — fix MCP plan workspace seeding

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Rename the `/settings/setup` route in `applications/openthrottle-developer` to `/settings/agents`. The page is really the agent-CLI configuration surface, so "agents" reads better than "setup". Carry the rename through every name, helper, constant, label and doc comment so nothing is left calling this "setup" at the URL/UI layer.

## Scope decisions

- **URL + UI naming** change to "agents". Nav label and breadcrumb become **"Agents"** (were "Setup").
- **Backend "agent-setup" concept stays as-is.** The `agent-setup` GraphQL resolver/object, the `resources.agent-setup.tsx` action route, and the `useAgentSetupStream` hook model the real "agent setup" (detection/install) domain concept — do NOT rename these. Only fix their doc comments that point at `/settings/setup`.
- The page H1/`<title>` "Agent CLI setup" is descriptive and may stay; only the route-path-derived label ("Setup" → "Agents") is required to change. (Confirm with owner if they'd rather the heading change too.)

## Inventory (from recon)

App uses `@react-router/fs-routes` flatRoutes — the URL is derived from the route filename, so there is NO central route table or path-builder; the string `/settings/setup` is hardcoded at each call site.

Functional (MUST change for the URL to move):
- `app/routes/settings.setup.tsx` → `settings.agents.tsx` (+ `+types/settings.setup` regenerated, `import type { Route }` path at L22, breadcrumb L28, meta title L51)
- `app/routes/settings.setup.tsx.graphql` → `settings.agents.tsx.graphql` (+ regenerate `__generated__`)
- `app/routes/__tests__/settings.setup.test.tsx` → `settings.agents.test.tsx` (import + `/settings/setup` path strings L32,L37)
- Path string call sites: `app/global/data/data.navigation.ts:222`, `app/routing/dashboard/data/get-started-steps.ts:22`, `app/routing/home/demo/HomeComposer.tsx:106`, `app/routing/skills/components/RunSkillDialog.tsx:111`

Consistency (rename for cleanliness):
- Components in `app/routing/settings/components/`: `SettingsSetup*` (Introduction, Table, TableRow, Toolbar, InstallNotice, CliControls, AgentToggle, ModelToggle, ModelFavorite, ModelBulkToggle, ModelRow) + their `__tests__` → `SettingsAgents*`
- Copy in `app/routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts`: `SETTINGS_SETUP_COPY`, `settingsSetupModelsSummary()`, `settingsSetupModelsEnabledSummary()`, `SETTINGS_SETUP_FILTER_LABELS` → `SETTINGS_AGENTS_*`
- Nav label `data.navigation.ts:219` "Setup" → "Agents"; breadcrumb `settings.setup.tsx:28` "Setup" → "Agents"

Doc comments only (no routing impact) mentioning `/settings/setup`:
- Developer app resource routes: `resources.agent-setup.tsx:18`, `resources.agent-enabled.tsx:13`, `resources.agent-model-enabled.tsx:14`, `resources.agent-models-enabled.tsx:13`, `resources.agent-model-favorite.tsx:14`, `app/routing/settings/data/agent-clis.data.ts`
- Server: `agent-discovery.object.ts:41`, `agent-setup.resolver.ts:65`, `plans.resolver.ts:274`, `conversation-stream.resolver.ts:270,280`, `scheduled-agent-jobs.resolver.ts:189` + `.resolver.test.ts:4`
- Drivers: `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/__tests__/install-metadata.test.ts:2`

No Maestro/E2E flows reference this route. `ONBOARDING_STEP_ID.agentCli` is a join key, not a path — leave unchanged.

## Validation

`pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel`, then `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck lint test build`. Grep for any residual `settings/setup` / `SettingsSetup` / `SETTINGS_SETUP`.
summary: Move the developer app's agent-CLI settings page from /settings/setup to /settings/agents, renaming the route module, path references, components, copy constants, labels and doc comments for consistency, then regenerate GraphQL codegen and validate.
title: Rename /settings/setup route to /settings/agents

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

`@openthrottle/agentic-hooks` today is a **skill-usage** capturer, not a lifecycle layer. Concretely:

- Its types are skill-shaped (`UsageEvent`, `OutcomeEvent`); there is no neutral event envelope, so every new signal (token usage, task boundaries, session lifecycle) would need its own parallel pipeline.
- `.claude/settings.json` wires only **three** hook events (`PreToolUse:Skill`, `Stop`, `UserPromptExpansion`). Three of the six committed bundles — `skill-usage-drain.cjs`, `skill-usage-outcome.cjs`, `skill-usage-scope.cjs` — are **not referenced by any hook**; they exist as manual CLIs only. `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `PreCompact`, `PostToolUse`, `SubagentStop` are unused.
- Nothing binds a harness session to an OT plan/task, so no hook can reason about plan state.
- Token usage has a durable home (`agent_token_usage`, migration 083 — explicitly built for "future non-chat sources") and a read query (`tokenUsage`), but **no ingest mutation**, so nothing outside the chat resolver can write a row. A `/ot-claude-loop` run burns tokens that OT never sees.
- The `/ot-claude-loop` contract is **prose only**. Its own SKILL.md calls the missed `COMPLETED` flip "the single most common failure of this loop", and `append_plan_output` narration is entirely on the model's good behavior. Prose the model can skip is not a contract.

The goal: when a loop runs **inside Claude directly** (not via the workflow CLI), the OT side-effects — output stream narration, task status hygiene, token accounting — happen because the harness fires hooks, not because the model remembered.

## Two layers, kept distinct

This plan is the **harness layer** (in-process hooks fired by Claude Code / Cursor around prompts, tools, sessions). It must not be conflated with the **plan-run layer** already designed as `job-run-lifecycle-hooks` in `tools/workflows/src/types/job-run-lifecycle-hooks.ts` (Jest-style `beforeAll`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach`/`afterAll` phases attached to a plan and executed by the BullMQ runner — OT plan `1bee2916`). Task 1 must state where the seam sits and which layer owns which event; ideally the harness layer emits into the same event envelope the plan-run layer consumes.

## Non-goals (and their owners)

- New developer-UI surfaces for lifecycle/token data — token-usage surfacing is OT `a55b76ba`.
- Privacy-level expansion of skill capture — OT `91679bbf`.
- Foreign-workspace skill delivery mechanics — OT `d3a30314` (the vendor-plugin spike in task 9 must reconcile with it, not redo it).
- Cursor/Codex/OpenCode adapters beyond the one existing Cursor capture hook: enumerate them in task 1, implement Claude first.

## Invariants

- **Fail-open, always.** A hook must never throw into the harness, never block on a dead server, and never stall tool use. Enforcement hooks (task 8) are the one exception and must be opt-in and default to `warn`, escalating to `block` only after a soak.
- **Zero runtime `node_modules`.** Bundles stay self-contained esbuild `.cjs` under each tool's hook folder, committed, with the existing `bundle-hooks-check` drift gate green.
- **No breaking public API.** `UsageEvent` / `OutcomeEvent` and the existing exports stay working; generalization is additive with deprecations, not renames.
summary: Expand @openthrottle/agentic-hooks from a skill-usage capturer into the tool-neutral agentic lifecycle layer: a generic event envelope, session→plan binding, full Claude/Cursor hook-event coverage, token-usage capture from the harness transcript, and hook-enforced /ot-claude-loop invariants (forced append_plan_output, no stranded IN_PROGRESS). Ends with a GO/NO-GO spike on shipping it all as a vendor plugin.
title: Agentic lifecycle hooks: make harness-driven loops honor the OT contract

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

While counting OT plans, an agent queried `listPlansByStatus` with `["cancelled","draft","archived"]` and got a generic "The request was rejected as invalid" error, then wrongly concluded those statuses don't exist. Investigation revealed the real cause is status-vocabulary drift across four layers of the stack, none of which agree, and none of which is introspectable by a caller.

## Ground truth (DB)

Postgres enum type `plan_task_status`, defined in `databases/migrations/028_plan_task_status_enum.sql` and extended by `029_add_queued_status.sql`:

- `BACKLOG`, `BLOCKED`, `CANCELED`, `COMPLETED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PENDING`, `QUEUED` (plans-only), `SKIPPED`
- Note: `CANCELED` is **single-L**. `FAILED`, `DRAFT`, `ARCHIVED` are **not** members.
- `plans.status` and `tasks.status` are columns of this enum type.

## The drift

1. **Entity vs DB** — `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/plans/plan.entity.ts:59` declares `@Column({ default: 'pending', name: 'status', type: 'text' })`. The ORM believes the column is free `text`, not the `plan_task_status` enum, and the default `'pending'` is lowercase while the enum labels are uppercase. Same likely applies to the task entity.
2. **GraphQL** — `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` exposes `status: String!` on every plan/task type and `statuses: [String]` on `ListPlansByStatusInput`. No enum, so consumers cannot introspect the valid set. Input descriptions in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plan.input.ts` are inconsistent and partly wrong: line ~452 says "COMPLETED, CANCELLED, or FAILED" (double-L + `FAILED` doesn't exist in the enum); line ~486 says "COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING, QUEUED".
3. **MCP** — `ListPlansByStatusInputSchema()` in `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/__generated__/schemas.ts` generates `statuses: z.array(z.string().nullable()).nullish()` (no enum), and the tool description in `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/tools/plans.ts:75` only lists `pending`/`in_progress`/`completed`.
4. **Resolver** — `PlansResolver.listPlansByStatus` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plans.resolver.ts:548`) uppercases and filters `status IN (...)` with **no validation**. An unknown value reaches Postgres → `invalid input value for enum plan_task_status: "CANCELLED"`. The MCP error mapper (`packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/utils/errors.ts:58`) then flattens this to the generic `validation` message "The request was rejected as invalid. Check the provided arguments and retry." — losing the actual reason. (`BLOCKED` "worked" only because it's a valid enum value returning 0 rows.)

## Goal / desired contract

- One canonical, code-level source of truth for the status vocabulary (shared const, ideally derived from or asserted against the DB enum).
- GraphQL exposes it as a **real enum** (or a query returning the valid set) so it is introspectable; deprecate `String` gradually per the repo's no-break-schema rule (`@deprecated`, migration plan) rather than hard-swapping.
- MCP types + tool descriptions regenerate from the GraphQL enum automatically (no hand-maintained status lists).
- Entity column type corrected to the enum with an uppercase default.
- Resolver validates status input up front and returns a **clear, actionable** error listing valid values, instead of leaking a raw Postgres enum error through the generic MCP sanitizer.

## Constraints / gotchas

- Code-first GraphQL (`autoSchemaFile`); after any schema change follow the codegen flow in CLAUDE.md (boot server to regen `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`, commit `__generated__`). CI fails on codegen drift.
- No new TS `enum`s — use an `as const` object per `.cursor/rules/`. A GraphQL enum can be registered from an `as const` map via `registerEnumType`.
- Never break existing fields without a migration/deprecation plan.
- `QUEUED` is plans-only; task status set is the 7 non-QUEUED values. The canonical model must capture that distinction.
- The UI already has status vocab in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/config/status-options.ts` and related components — reconcile so the UI consumes the same source.

Plan authored 2026-08-11.
summary: The valid plan/task status set has drifted across four layers, so callers can't know the real values and unknown statuses fail with an opaque error. Ground truth is the Postgres enum plan_task_status = {BACKLOG, BLOCKED, CANCELED, COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING, QUEUED (plans-only), SKIPPED} (databases/migrations/028,029; CANCELED is single-L). But: (1) plan.entity.ts declares the column as `type: 'text'` with a lowercase default 'pending' — TypeORM thinks it's free text, not the enum, and the lowercase default doesn't match the uppercase enum labels; (2) schema.gql exposes `status: String!` with no enum, so consumers can't introspect valid values, and input descriptions cite inconsistent/nonexistent sets ("COMPLETED, CANCELLED, FAILED" — double-L + FAILED doesn't exist; elsewhere "COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING, QUEUED"); (3) the openthrottle-mcp tool schema is auto-generated to z.array(z.string()) with no enum and its description only lists pending/in_progress/completed; (4) listPlansByStatus does `status IN (...)` with no validation, so an unknown value reaches Postgres and throws "invalid input value for enum plan_task_status", which the MCP maps to the generic "The request was rejected as invalid" — which is exactly what bit an agent that guessed `cancelled`/`draft`/`archived`. Goal: define one canonical status source of truth, expose it as a real GraphQL enum (or introspectable const), regenerate MCP types/docs from it, fix the entity, and validate input at the resolver with a clear error instead of leaking a raw Postgres enum error.
title: Fix plan/task status contract drift (DB enum ↔ GraphQL ↔ MCP) and establish a single source of truth

author: visormatt
description:
## LIVE SECRETS
None confirmed. gitleaks reported 1 hit; triaged as a test fixture (false positive).

## How this sweep was run
- `gitleaks detect --config .gitleaks.toml --no-banner` (774 commits / ~228 MB)
- `pnpm audit` (81 advisories: 13 critical / 21 high / 41 moderate / 6 low)
- `pnpm run check:rbac-admin-coverage` — pass
- `pnpm run check:bootstrap-secrets` — pass
- Targeted review: GraphQL `@Public()` / Path A resolvers, route actions vs `parseFormData`, `window.env` / `getPublicEnv`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, raw SQL, CSP nonce configs, CORS

## Gitleaks triage
- **1 finding, 100% false-positive rate.** `generic-api-key` in historical path `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/SettingsKeysFormSuccess.test.tsx:23` (now under `__tests__/`). Value is a fixture-shaped API credential string in a Vitest payload, not a live credential. Confidence: high (fixture).
- No committed private keys / real `.env` files with production credentials found. Committed `.env.default` values look like local/placeholder defaults (JWT marker words, empty Stripe keys).

## Dedup / skipped
- No open `🔁 Security sweep: …` PENDING/IN_PROGRESS plans.
- ADR `18e16dfc-4f22-43f9-9b77-6fc90309b60a` (Path A authenticated-only) and companion BACKLOG plan `ff184aa8-af3f-48c9-a1ae-56a825bf3f51` (Path B/C) already document that many mutations intentionally lack `@Permissions`. This sweep does **not** re-file Path A as an oversight; it files the **revisit trigger** where open registration breaks Path A's single-trusted-principal assumption.
- Dropped by the 10-finding cap / reachability: RSC-only React Router CSRF (GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2; apps do not use unstable RSC APIs), turbo-stream DoS via `@vercel/analytics`→Remix (not the RR8 framework path), Nx/tmp/form-data/brace-expansion toolchain CVEs, low DOMPurify/Monaco issues, per-resolver Path A duplicates.

## Ranking note
Findings ordered by exploitability. No confirmed live cloud credentials.
title: 🔁 Security sweep: 2026-08-21

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

`OpenThrottle/monorepo` is a public repo with **no `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` directory at all**. Today https://github.com/OpenThrottle/monorepo/issues/new/choose falls through to a single blank issue box — no chooser, no structure. `.agents/prompts/Job_Issue_Reporting.md:34` calls this out explicitly as a known triage handicap ("There are no issue templates in the org... Expect unstructured reports with no reproduction steps, no version, and no environment").

## Goal

Two **lightweight** GitHub Issue Forms (YAML `.yml`, not legacy Markdown templates) — Bug Report and Feature Request — plus a `config.yml` for the chooser page. Lightweight is the constraint, not a nice-to-have: a form long enough to feel like paperwork suppresses reports from an OSS project this early. Target ~5 fields for the bug form and ~4 for the feature form, with only the genuinely triage-blocking ones marked `required`.

## Grounding facts

- No `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` dir exists; `.github/` currently holds `actions/`, `workflows/`, `dependabot.yml`, `pull_request_template.md`.
- Existing repo labels usable for auto-labeling: `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `question`, `good first issue`, `help wanted`, `hold`. Do **not** invent new labels in the template `labels:` field — GitHub silently drops labels that do not exist, and a dropped label looks like a template bug.
- **GitHub Discussions is disabled** on the repo (`has_discussions: false`), so `contact_links` must NOT point at a Discussions URL — it would 404. Point at `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `MONOREPO.md` instead.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:14` and `MONOREPO.md:524` both tell people to "open an issue" for questions — worth a pass so the guidance matches the new chooser.
- The repo has two remotes: `origin` = `OpenThrottle/monorepo` (canonical), `openthrottle` = `OpenThrottle/OpenThrottle` (mirror, unrelated history). All work targets `origin`.

## Out of scope

- Pull request template changes (`.github/pull_request_template.md` stays as-is).
- New labels, label automation, issue-triage workflows/Actions, or projects auto-add.
- A security-report template (`SECURITY.md` / private vulnerability reporting is its own decision).

## Verification

Issue forms cannot be previewed locally. Verification is: (1) `.yml` parses and matches GitHub's issue-forms schema; (2) after the branch merges to `main`, load `/issues/new/choose` and confirm both cards render, then open each form and confirm fields, required markers, and auto-applied labels. Note that GitHub reads issue templates from the **default branch only**, so the chooser will not change until the PR lands.
summary: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE with two short GitHub Issue Forms (Bug Report, Feature Request) plus a config.yml chooser, so github.com/OpenThrottle/monorepo/issues/new/choose stops showing a bare blank issue.
title: Lightweight GitHub issue templates: Bug Report + Feature Request

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Let a chat conversation carry more than one repository of context. Today the composer selects exactly one checkout; that id becomes a single `cwd: string` on the server and drives the process spawn, the managed MCP config, and CLI session resume.

## The constraint that shapes the design

`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/types.ts:221` is `cwd?: string` — one process, one working directory. A second repository is NOT a second cwd; it is an **additional granted directory**, and only some CLIs have that concept:

- **antigravity** — already emits `--add-dir <cwd>` (`antigravity/argv.ts:67`); the flag is repeatable.
- **claude** — supports `--add-dir`.
- **cursor**, **opencode** — no equivalent modeled in this repo.

So the shipped model is **one primary checkout + N additional context dirs**, capability-gated per driver. It is not N peer repositories.

## Current chain (single-select), for reference

1. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/models.server.ts:121` — `WorkspaceLocalRepositories` → `RepositoryOption[]` (`{ id, displayName, filesystemPath }`).
2. `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/data/atom.chat-toolbar.ts` — `repositoryId: string | undefined` persisted in `chatToolbarStateAtom` (schema **v3**, key `${APP_NAME}:chat:toolbar`).
3. `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/utils/chat-toolbar-reconcile.ts:159` — re-validates each render; drops a vanished id, clears when `requiresRepository === false`, else falls back to `repositories[0]?.id`.
4. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useHomeComposer.tsx` + `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/hooks/useHeaderChatController.tsx:198` — map to `checkouts`, render `ChatCheckoutSelector` (single-select `DropdownMenu`).
5. `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/utils/chat-turn-fields.ts` — `repositoryId: string` on the `intent=start` form; omitted for the `openai` backend.
6. `packages/react-router-chat/src/conversation-stream-action.ts:85` — form field → `StartConversationStreamInput.repositoryId`.
7. `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.resolver.ts:479` — `findByIdForUser` (ownership check) → `toContainerPath(filesystemPath)` → `cwd`, which then feeds the spawn, `buildManagedMcpServers({ repositoryRoot: cwd })`, and `repositoryMetadataKey(backend)` in conversation metadata.

## Decisions (confirm before task 1)

- **MCP scope: primary-only.** `buildManagedMcpServers` keeps taking the primary checkout as `repositoryRoot`. Registering an OT MCP server per secondary repo is a larger change with unclear value in v1.
- **Conversation identity: primary-as-session-key.** `repositoryMetadataKey(backend)` continues to store the primary id alone, so swapping secondaries mid-conversation does not fork the CLI session. Matches how the CLIs actually resume.
- **`@`-mentions: out of scope for v1.** `useFileMentionProvider` / `/ide/files` stay keyed on the primary repository. Multi-repo mentions need repo-qualified paths (`repo-name/src/foo.ts`) or the agent cannot disambiguate — a UX design task in its own right. Track as a follow-up plan.

## Known risk to surface, not solve here

`findLiveRunsByCheckoutIds` (`packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/plan-runs/plan-runs.service.ts:424`) already exists because two conversations with write access to the same checkout stomp each other. Multi-select makes that collision meaningfully more likely. v1 should not add a lock, but the secondary-dir affordance should not silently imply write safety either.

## Out of scope

Multi-repo `@`-mentions; per-repo MCP servers; any checkout locking or run-concurrency guard; admin app parity beyond what the shared `useHeaderChatController` gives for free.
summary: Turn the chat composer's single-select checkout picker into a capability-gated multi-select: one primary checkout (the spawn cwd) plus N additional granted directories threaded as repeated --add-dir for the CLIs that support it.
title: Multi-select repositories in the chat composer (primary checkout + additional context dirs)

author: visormatt
description:
# Add Gemini CLI as an agent-CLI provider

Add Google Gemini CLI (https://geminicli.com — binary `gemini`, installed via `npm i -g @google/gemini-cli`) as a first-class driver in `packages/openthrottle-drivers`, wired through every consumer seam (plan runs, scheduled jobs, agent discovery, Developer UI, chat streaming, token usage).

## Known Gemini CLI facts (verify against `gemini --help` before implementing — repo rule: never from memory)
- Headless: `-p/--prompt` (non-TTY also triggers headless).
- Output: `--output-format text|json|stream-json`; stream-json is NDJSON with `init`, `message`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `error`, `result` events — a natural fit for the chat `events.ts` mapper.
- Model: `-m/--model`; follow the convention of omitting the flag for empty/`auto`.
- Permissions: `--approval-mode` and `--yolo`.
- Auth: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, OAuth login, or Vertex AI.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 general, 42 bad args, 53 turn limit.

## Architecture notes (from the driver map)
- Driver contract: `AgentDriver` in `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts`; `buildShellCommand` must stay PURE. Registry tuple `DRIVER_IDS` in `src/registry/index.ts` imports no driver modules.
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/README.md` already contains a worked `geminiDriver` example in "Adding a new agent CLI".
- Much is auto-derived from `ALL_DRIVERS` (AGENT_CLI_ALLOWLIST, discovery, CLI_BACKENDS, workflow runner ids, install/update executor) — but there are ~20 hardcoded mirrors that must be hand-edited (see tasks).
- The drivers `buildShellCommand` path (shell string for Ralph/scheduled runs) and the chat adapter argv path (`openthrottle-agentic-utils` conversation-backend) are TWO separate implementations; a drift guard asserts registry keys ≡ drivers with `capabilities.chatStreaming === true`, so the capability flag and the chat adapter must flip together.
- Playbook: `docs/openthrottle/agentic-cli-backend-compatibility-guide.md` — its §12 output belongs at `docs/openthrottle/gemini-stream-json-schema.md`.
- Cross-driver guard tests that hardcode the five-driver set and WILL fail until updated: `discovery-metadata.test.ts`, `install-metadata.test.ts` (requires a curl-shell install descriptor + update descriptor for every driver), `mcp-capabilities.test.ts`, `registry.test.ts` (including the `parseDriverId('gemini')` throws assertion at lines 81–82, which must be inverted).
- Known stale spot to fix in passing: `packages/openthrottle-agentic-ralph/src/utils/context.ts:22-27` local `WORKFLOW_RUNNER_IDS` literal is already missing codex/grok.

## Validation gates
Per touched project: lint + typecheck + test. GraphQL description changes require the schema regen flow (boot server → commit `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` → `nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`). Live smoke: `discover_agent_clis` shows gemini; a scheduled/plan run executes via the gemini driver; chat streams if the adapter task is done.
summary: Add Google Gemini CLI (https://geminicli.com, `gemini`, npm @google/gemini-cli) as a new agent-CLI provider: drivers-package driver, DB/entity widening, server guards, Developer UI mirrors, chat-streaming adapter, and docs.
title: Gemini CLI agent driver: add Google Gemini to providers
