author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Give the skill **Tag vocabulary** manager its own home at `/skills/vocabulary` instead of living at the bottom of `/skills/availability`. Link to it from the `/skills` toolbar (next to **Manage availability**), and remove the non-functional **Create new skill** button.

## Why

`/skills/availability` currently mixes two concerns: (1) per-project model auto-invocation posture + rules, and (2) the workspace **tag vocabulary** (add/rename/remove tags). The vocabulary is a distinct, reusable concept — the availability *rules editor* only needs to *read* the vocabulary to constrain its tag pickers; it doesn't need the management UI. Splitting it clarifies both pages.

## Key facts (verified in code)

- Routing is `flatRoutes` (fs-routes) — a new `app/routes/skills.vocabulary.tsx` auto-maps to `/skills/vocabulary`. No `routes.ts` edit needed.
- The vocabulary UI is `SkillTagVocabularyManager` (+ `SkillTagVocabularyRow`), rendered near the bottom of `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.availability.tsx` (line ~161). Both components are reused as-is; only their host route changes.
- Vocabulary mutations live in `app/routing/skills/actions/availability.ts` under intents `addTag` / `renameTag` / `removeTag`, plus GraphQL docs `AddSkillTag` / `RenameSkillTag` / `RemoveSkillTag` and query `SkillAvailabilityAuthoringVocabulary` in `skills.availability.tsx.graphql`.
- **IMPORTANT:** `/skills/availability` still needs to *read* the vocabulary — `SkillAvailabilityRulesEditor` takes a `vocabulary: string[]` prop to constrain rule tag pickers. So the availability loader keeps the `SkillAvailabilityAuthoringVocabulary` query; only the add/rename/remove management moves.
- Toolbar buttons live in `app/routing/skills/components/SkillsToolbar.tsx`: the `Manage availability` link (SlidersHorizontalIcon → `/skills/availability`) and the dead `Create new skill` button (FilePlusIcon, `type="submit"`, no handler) to remove.
- User-facing copy is centralized in `app/routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts` under `SKILL_AVAILABILITY_COPY.vocabulary` — factor the vocabulary strings into their own copy block for the new route.

## Out of scope
- No GraphQL schema/resolver changes (mutations already exist).
- No changes to the tag-vocabulary components' internal behavior.

## Validation
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:codegen-graphql` after moving GraphQL docs.
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test` (availability, vocabulary, toolbar suites), `:typecheck`, `:lint`.
- Live-verify both routes render (needs a permissioned user per repo memory).
summary: Move tag-vocabulary management off /skills/availability onto its own /skills/vocabulary route, link it from the /skills toolbar, and drop the dead Create-skill button.
title: Extract Tag vocabulary to a dedicated /skills/vocabulary route

author: visormatt
description:
Bring `/skills/:slug` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx`) in line with other developer-app routes by using the standard Introduction header pattern, moving tags off the title row, and dropping the skill summary that is already rendered in full in the Skill tab.

## Current vs target

The skills **index** already has `SkillsIntroduction`: `GlobalHeading` (`heading="h1"`, `BrainCircuitIcon`, title from `SKILLS_COPY.pageTitle`) plus a `text-muted-foreground` description from `SKILLS_COPY.pageDescription`.

The **detail** `SkillIntroduction` is a custom one-row chrome: `GlobalHeading` title is `/${slug}` with no icon; source/invocation badges, tag chips, orphan badge, Run, and Edit all sit in the same flex row; then `entry.summary`; then the repo-relative path + clipboard.

Plan/task detail (`PlanDetailRouteHeader`, `TaskDetailRouteHeader`) is the closer sibling: `GlobalHeading` + icon + entity title, then a metadata row below — not a packed title row.

Target layout for skill detail:
1. Standard header: `GlobalHeading` with `heading="h1"`, `BrainCircuitIcon`, title = skill slug (drop the leading `/` so it matches breadcrumbs and other detail routes). Put Run / Edit / orphan-remove in `GlobalHeading` children (same slot `SkillsIntroduction` uses for `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger`).
2. Standard copy: any standing chrome text lives in `SKILL_DETAIL_COPY` (`data.copy.ts`), not inline in the component. Do **not** render `entry.summary` — the Skill tab already shows the full SKILL.md via `MarkdownRenderer`.
3. Tags (and source/invocation/orphan badges) move **below** the heading, as a metadata row — same idea as plan detail's status/author row. Keep `SkillTagChips` / read-only tag badges and `SkillIntroductionBadges`.
4. Keep the path + clipboard row; it is not duplicated in the body.

Do not invent a second `SkillsIntroduction` (that name is the index component). Reshape the existing `SkillIntroduction`.

## Files

- `app/routing/skills/components/SkillIntroduction.tsx` — layout
- `app/routing/skills/components/SkillIntroductionBadges.tsx` — still display-only; may only need class/wrapping changes
- `app/routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts` — any new standing copy
- `app/routing/skills/components/__tests__/SkillIntroduction.test.tsx` (+ `SkillDetailTabs` / `SkillIntroductionBadges` specs if they assert the old title/summary layout)
- Route `skills.$slug.tsx` should stay thin; wiring stays in `SkillDetailTabs`.

## Constraints

- Generators first only if a **new** component is required; this is a reshape of an existing generated-shaped component.
- Component-primitive-shape: unpack before Hooks, section comments, copy in `data.copy.ts`, one component per file.
- Specs: `component` not `screen`, assert against imported copy constants, keep the edit-blocked-but-tags-and-run-live contract.
- Verify with `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test` on the touched specs and a browser pass on `/skills/:slug` (tagged, untagged, orphan, external vs OpenThrottle, edit blocked).
title: Align skill detail introduction with other routes

author: visormatt
description:
> Spawned from plan `88f747ff` after its Phase B (splitting `openthrottle-developer` into libraries) was **measured and rejected**. This plan is the alternative that won on the numbers.

## Why

Measured on the base commit (`0e170105`), heaviest CI unit is `openthrottle-developer`:

| target | wall clock | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lint | 9.6s | 5.5% |
| typecheck | 10.6s | 6.1% |
| **test** | **154.1s** | **88.4%** |

`test` is ~88% of the cost, so that is the only slice worth attacking. Vitest `--shard` splits it **within** the single Nx project, needs no code movement, and works on this suite today — verified by running it:

| shard | files | wall clock |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1/3 | 227 | **60.9s** |
| 2/3 | 226 | 54.6s |
| 3/3 | 226 | 48.4s |

**154.1s -> 60.9s on the heaviest box (-60%).** For comparison, the rejected 1,255-file project split bought ~23%.

## The stale assumption this corrects

`applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts` currently reasons:

> "project sharding splits the affected PROJECT list, and this suite is a single Nx project, so whichever box draws it runs all of it. The matrix cannot lower this suite's wall-clock — a faster pool can."

Correct about **project** sharding — and it is why the vmForks work (plan `e448a51d`, forks 253s -> vmForks 86s) was the right call at the time. But it frames the options as "faster pool" or "move the code". Vitest `--shard` is a third lever. `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (~line 225) has the same stale framing, calling the heaviest project a floor "which suite sharding cannot split".

## The actual work

The hard part is **not** `--shard` itself; it is that the CI matrix currently assigns each project to exactly ONE shard via `scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts`. To shard a suite *within* a project, the app's `test` must run on all 3 boxes with different `--shard` arguments, which cuts across the existing partitioning contract. Design that interaction carefully:

- The partitioner's job ("which projects are mine?") and per-suite sharding are different axes. Decide whether the app's `test` is special-cased out of the partition, or whether the partitioner grows a notion of per-project shard assignment.
- `getShardSelectionErrors()`'s round-trip guarantee must keep holding — its whole point is that a project cannot silently fall off every box.
- Keep `lint`/`typecheck` on the existing project-partition path; they are 11.6% and do not need this.
- Preserve the `vmForks` + `vmMemoryLimit: '512MB'` + `maxWorkers: 4` tuning. It is orthogonal to `--shard` and still load-bearing against the silent-OOM `(0 test)` failure mode.

## Reconcile first

Plan `e448a51d` (Developer Vitest sharding) is DONE with **PR #267 unmerged** and occupies the same territory. Read it before starting — this plan may be a superset, a duplicate, or a correction of it. Do not open a competing PR without resolving that.

## Definition of done

Heaviest CI box's `openthrottle-developer` `test` wall-clock materially below the current single-box figure, `getShardSelectionErrors()` round-trip still green, no project silently unvalidated, and the stale comments in `vitest.config.ts` / `continuous-integration.yml` corrected.
summary: Config + workflow change to split the 679-file developer suite across the 3 existing CI shards using Vitest --shard. Measured 154.1s -> 60.9s on the heaviest box, zero files moved. Replaces the rejected project-split approach from 88f747ff.
title: Shard the openthrottle-developer Vitest suite across CI boxes with --shard

author: visormatt
description:
## Symptom

Scheduled run `479b58d1-f07e-4fb3-ad4a-d532c46ec122` of the "Weekly - Doc drift" job (`db1e51c8-e009-4a12-b9fd-d785e591c47e`) reports **succeeded, exit 0, 49s** — but the agent did no work at all. Its log says:

> **Stopped.** `openthrottle-mcp` is not available in this session, so this job cannot file findings.

The agent enumerated its MCP catalog (`maestro`, `shadcn`, `plugin-vercel-vercel`) and found neither `openthrottle-mcp` nor `openthrottle-mcp-docker`, so it correctly refused to sweep docs or file a plan. The UI still shows a green run.

## Root cause (confirmed in source)

**1 — No driver emits MCP-enabling flags.**
`packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/cursor.ts` builds exactly:

```
cursor-agent --force -p "<prompt>" --model <model>
```

`cursor-agent --help` exposes `--approve-mcps` (auto-approve all MCP servers) and `--trust` (trust the workspace without prompting). Neither is emitted. In headless `-p` mode the project's `.cursor/mcp.json` servers require approval/trust, so `openthrottle-mcp` never attaches — the schedule fires an agent structurally incapable of the job it was given.

A grep for `approve-mcps|--trust|mcp-config` across `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src` and `tools/workflows/src` returns **zero hits**. This is a gap in **all five registered drivers** (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `grok`, `opencode` — see `drivers/index.ts` `ALL_DRIVERS`), not just cursor. `claude.ts` likewise emits only `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits`.

The engine (`packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/engine/index.ts`) spawns with `shell: true` and the inherited server env — no MCP config or auth token is injected either, and a BullMQ worker's env is not a login shell's env.

**2 — Process exit code is treated as task outcome.**
`ScheduledAgentJobsProcessor.runStatusForAgentStatus` maps `RUN_AGENT_STATUS.ok` -> `succeeded`. Agent CLIs exit 0 when the model declines to act, so an aborted run is indistinguishable from a completed one. Every scheduled job depending on MCP has been silently green.

**3 — No token usage for cursor runs.**
`foldRunUsage` folds JSONL usage lines, but the cursor driver runs the default `--output-format text`, so there is nothing to parse — hence "No token usage was reported for this run." `cursor-agent` supports `--output-format stream-json`. Overlaps plan `2c9bd39e` (scheduled-run metadata); coordinate rather than duplicate.

## Blast radius — three surfaces, not one

`buildShellCommand` is shared by every agent invocation path:

- **scheduled jobs** — `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-runner.service.ts`
- **chat** — `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/agent-setup-executor.ts:220`
- **Ralph** — `tools/workflows/src/bin/run-iteration.ts:109` (and `:125`)

A driver-level fix reaches all three for free, which is the point — but it also means the MCP flags change chat and Ralph behavior, and `--trust`/`--approve-mcps` auto-approve every configured MCP server. That is the intent for an unattended scheduled run in a known repo; it may be a permissions widening for an interactive chat session. The chat/Ralph regression task owns that decision.

## Scope

- **In:** root causes 1 and 2, across all five drivers, with the chat and Ralph surfaces explicitly regression-checked.
- **Out:** token-usage persistence (root cause 3) — owned by `2c9bd39e`. Touch `--output-format stream-json` here only where the run-outcome signal needs a structured result event.

## Key files

- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/{cursor,claude,codex,grok,opencode}.ts`
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts` (`DriverCapabilities`)
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/engine/index.ts`
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.processor.ts`
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/agent-setup-executor.ts`
- `tools/workflows/src/bin/run-iteration.ts`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/schedule/components/RunDetail.tsx`
summary: Agent CLIs are spawned with no MCP servers attached (no --approve-mcps/--trust), so MCP-dependent jobs abort doing nothing — and still record status=succeeded, exit 0, because the processor maps process exit code to task outcome. Affects all five drivers and all three invocation surfaces.
title: 🐛 Scheduled runs: MCP-less agents that silently "succeed"

author: visormatt
description:
Weekly sweep across root docs (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `MONOREPO.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`), the three-tier `AGENTS.md` hierarchy, `docs/**`, agent assets under `.agents/**` plus mirrors under `.cursor/**` / `.claude/**`, package READMEs, and `databases/README.md`.

Verification: documented commands checked against live root scripts (`node -e` over `package.json` scripts) and live Nx inventory (`pnpm nx show projects`, `pnpm nx show projects --with-target=build`, targeted `pnpm nx show project`); did not execute long/stateful docs commands. Also ran `pnpm run check:target-descriptions` (passes) and `pnpm run check:local:agent-assets` (passes with existing rule-description warnings only). Path existence checked directly. `.agents/` vs `.cursor/` / `.claude/` mirrors: no content drift (skill-sync `--check` OK); remaining issues are stale prose pointing at dropped paths, not a re-sync.

Evening pass re-swept, skipped those 6 as duplicates (dead `workflow-ralph`/`git-commit` skill links; `.cursor/skills` fan-out in workflow/persona docs; `docs/Skills.md` inventory; generator README missing `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false`; dead naming-doc links; missing `react-router-chat-state` AGENTS.md), and added 8 new findings that those tasks do not cover. author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Turn per-turn token/cost usage — already parsed AND already normalized in the codebase, but only ephemerally on the client — into a **server-persisted, queryable, per-provider feed**, and surface it on the developer app's Usage route (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/usage._index.tsx`). v1: usage across all providers or narrowed to a single provider, with totals. Rich aggregations (rollups/trends/cost-over-time, budgets, non-chat sources) are an explicit longer-term follow-up carved into its own plan.

## Current state (what already exists — do NOT rebuild)

The heavy lifting is already done in three layers; the gap is a durable, aggregatable store + query + UI.

1. **Per-provider parsing already exists.** Each `ConversationBackend` in `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/<driver>/events.ts` maps its CLI's native structured output onto a terminal `usage`-kind `ConversationStreamChunk`. Shapes vary a lot (the "vary more than the APIs" the request calls out):
   - claude → `{ usage:{input_tokens,output_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens}, modelUsage, totalCostUsd, result }` (single terminal chunk)
   - grok → `{ usage, modelUsage, numTurns, stopReason }` (single terminal)
   - codex → `{ usage }` (single terminal `turn.completed`)
   - cursor → `{ usage }` (single terminal)
   - opencode → `{ cost, tokens:{total,input,output,reasoning,cache:{read,write}} }` emitted **mid-stream per `step_finish`** (`done:false`, MULTIPLE per turn → must be summed)
   - openai (HTTP backend) → its own usage shape
   Verified schema docs: `docs/openthrottle/{claude,grok,codex,cursor-agent}-stream-json-schema.md`.
2. **A canonical normalizer already exists — but only client-side.** `packages/react-router-chat/src/usage.ts` has `normalizeUsage()` (folds every heterogeneous backend shape into one `ChatTokenUsage`), `sumUsage()` (accumulates opencode's per-step counts), `hasUsageCounts`, `formatTokenCount`, `formatUsageCost`; `turn-events.ts#applyTurnUsage` folds a turn's usage into one event. `ChatTokenUsage` = `{ inputTokens?, outputTokens?, cacheReadTokens?, cacheWriteTokens?, totalTokens?, costUsd?, model? }` (`react-router-chat/src/types.ts`). **Reuse this as the canonical shape — do not invent a new one.** Caveat: `react-router-chat` is a browser package, so the normalizer must be lifted to a server-safe shared home (candidate: `openthrottle-agentic-utils` conversation-backend, co-located with the raw parsing and Node+browser-safe) and re-exported to `react-router-chat`, so the SAME normalization runs on the server persistence path. Reconciling these two parallel worlds is a design deliverable.
3. **Usage is already persisted — but unusably.** `ConversationStreamService.persistAssistant` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts`) collects usage chunks into `tool_metadata.events[]` JSONB on `agent_conversation_messages`. Per-message, heterogeneous, un-indexed, not aggregated, not queryable as totals.
4. **The Usage route has no token data.** `dailyStatsRange` / `DailyStatsObject` count only plans/tasks. Only `DashboardDailyStatsCard` (Recharts) and `UsageSnapshot` (JSON export) are data-bound; the rest is static copy. `UsageOverview`, `UsageDailyActivityOverview`, `UsageAnalyticsGaps` explicitly disclaim "No model token, cost, or latency metrics" — those become inaccurate once this ships and must be revised.

## The actual gap this plan fills

Server-side: (a) run the SAME normalizer on the persistence path, (b) write normalized usage to a durable, indexed, aggregatable store, (c) expose a user-scoped GraphQL query filterable by provider + date range returning per-turn/day rows + totals. Frontend: wire the Usage route to it and replace the disclaimers with a real per-provider usage surface.

## Related / overlapping work

- **Pending plan OT 32f38166** ("react-router-chat token usage plan — per-backend token/usage display; event model INERT"). That plan owns the *live in-chat display* of usage; THIS plan owns *durable server persistence + aggregation + the Usage analytics route*. Task 1 must draw the boundary and decide whether 32f38166's INERT event model should be activated as the client-side sibling, and whether the lifted normalizer supersedes part of it. Do not duplicate.

## Placement note

The variance lives in `openthrottle-agentic-utils` conversation-backend adapters (the streaming/parsing counterpart to `openthrottle-drivers`, which only builds CLI commands and today discards usage entirely). The canonical type + normalizers belong there / in a shared server-safe home — NOT in `openthrottle-drivers`. (Bringing usage into the plan-run/Ralph driver path, which uses plain-text output, is out of scope here.)

## Design decisions to lock in task 1

- Confirm `ChatTokenUsage` (+ any added fields e.g. `provider`, reasoningTokens) as the canonical persisted shape; where the shared server-safe normalizer lives; how `react-router-chat` re-consumes it.
- **Persistence model fork** (recommended: dedicated `agent_token_usage` fact table with nullable conversation/message/user FKs + indexes on (user_id, created_at), provider, model — decouples from chat so future sources (plan runs, Ralph) can write to it — over denormalized columns on `agent_conversation_messages`).
- Provider + model identity derivation per backend; usage cardinality (sum mid-stream opencode vs single terminal).
- GraphQL query shape (per-turn/day rows + totals object; filters provider?, start, end; user-scoped, authenticated).
- Boundary vs plan 32f38166; v1 scope vs deferred aggregations.

## Constraints / conventions

- Private mode (`persist=false`) must NOT write usage rows — turn is ephemeral.
- Code-first GraphQL (`autoSchemaFile` → `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`): after schema changes boot server, then `nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`; commit `schema.gql` + all `__generated__`. Deprecate, never break.
- SQL migration under `databases/migrations/` with COMMENT ON standards, idempotent DDL (ot-postgres skill).
- Follow Result/ListResult/PaginatedResult conventions.
- Frontend: `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` + `@tools/generators`; keep Recharts consistent with `DashboardDailyStatsCard`; components export only component+props, copy/data in nearest `data/` folder.

## Deferred (its own future plan)

Cross-provider rollups, trends, cost-over-time charts, budgets/alerts, and usage from non-chat sources (plan runs, Ralph iterations). Carve out once v1 capture+surfacing lands.
title: Token usage capture, persistence & Usage-route surfacing across agent-CLI drivers

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

`/skills` today classifies every skill into three tiers:

- **External** — installed via `skills-lock.json` (`deriveSkillProvenance` → `source: 'external'`, origin URL from the lockfile).
- **OpenThrottle** — real path resolves under `<repo root>/skills/` (`source: 'openthrottle'`).
- **Personal** — real path resolves under `resolvePersonalSkillsRoot()` (`isPersonal: true`, a local overlay, deliberately NOT a `SkillSource` enum value).

There is a fourth thing already on disk with nowhere to go: a skill an **OpenThrottle end user authors in their own repository**. `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md` already names it — the injection resolver's `scanTargetOwnedSkillNames` drops any name **the target repo owns** — but the developer app has no word for it. Such a skill lands in `deriveSkillProvenance`'s final fallback and reports as **External**, i.e. as somebody else's third-party dependency, with a `sourceUrl` lookup that can never hit. That is the exact failure the personal tier was added to fix, one tier over.

It is also read-only: `useSkillDetail`'s `isEditableProvenance` is `source === 'openthrottle' || isPersonal === true`, so a person cannot edit a skill they wrote and own, in a repo they own.

Separately, the create route offers two destinations — `personal` and `repo`, the latter labelled "OpenThrottle repo" and writing to `<root>/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`. That destination is meaningful only to someone working **on** OpenThrottle. For an end user it is an invitation to write into a catalog they do not maintain. It should be visible only when `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW` is on.

## The discriminator — no new directory, no side-ledger

`.agents/skills/<slug>/` is already the ownership boundary, and §7.3 of the injection design reads ownership straight off the on-disk type:

| On-disk | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| real directory | vendored (`skills-lock.json`) |
| symlink → `$REPO_ROOT/skills/<name>` | committed authored |
| symlink → `<personal root>/<name>` | personal tier |
| symlink → anywhere else, or dangling | stale / rogue |

Row 1 is doing two jobs. A real directory is a vendored install **only if its slug is in `skills-lock.json`** — a real directory whose slug is *absent* from the lockfile is repo-authored and target-owned. That absence is the whole discriminator, and `deriveSkillProvenance` already reads the lockfile (for the origin URL) without ever consulting membership.

So Custom needs **no new directory, no new frontmatter key and no side-ledger** — §7.6's "nothing may need a side-ledger; ownership stays answerable from the filesystem alone" is preserved. It also makes Custom committable for free: the managed `.gitignore` block is `.agents/skills/*` with `!.agents/skills/*/`, which ignores the generated symlinks (git classes a symlink as a file) while rescuing real directories.

## Assumption stated up front

**`custom` is a local overlay flag (`isCustom`), not a fourth `SkillSource` enum value** — following the `isPersonal` precedent exactly. `SKILL_SOURCES` is ingested and served over GraphQL, so widening it means a schema change, a migration, an ingest change and codegen across consumers. A repo-authored skill still carries `source: 'external'` on the wire; the tier is derived locally, the way personal already is. If server-side Custom is wanted later (it is the honest fix for the ingested `projectSkills` rows in `merge-project-skills.ts`), that is a follow-on plan with a migration, not this one. Task 1 records the decision in a doc comment where the next reader will hit it.

## Scope

- Discovery, filter, badge and copy grow from three tiers to four.
- Custom becomes **editable** (it is your own committed file) — detail-page `canEdit`, the `write-skill-file.server.ts` guard, and the path allowlist.
- The create route's destination becomes three-way (`personal` / `custom` / `openthrottle`), with `openthrottle` — today's `repo` — gated behind `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW` in the UI **and refused server-side in the action**. A hidden toggle button is not a guard.
- `sync.sh` ownership messaging and the §7.3 table stop calling every real directory "vendored".

## Out of scope

- Widening the GraphQL `SkillSource` enum, and any migration or ingest change (see the assumption above).
- Per-tool global skill dirs (`~/.claude/skills` and friends) — still out of the repo-rooted scan.
- Changing what `sync.sh` *does* with a real directory: never touched, before and after. Only its wording changes.

## Verification

Live-verify against a seeded developer user (see the live-verify recipe) — a fixture real directory under `.agents/skills/` absent from `skills-lock.json` must render as **Custom**, filter under Custom, and be editable; the create page must show the OpenThrottle destination with `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW=true` and hide it (and refuse a hand-crafted POST) with it off. Then run the developer app's four gates: `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`.
summary: Add a fourth skill provenance tier — Custom, a skill an OpenThrottle end user authors in their own repo — alongside External, OpenThrottle and Personal, and stop offering the OpenThrottle (committed catalog) create destination unless FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW is on.
title: Skills: add the Custom tier, and gate the OpenThrottle create destination behind FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Adding `expandHome` (which imports `node:os`) to `@openthrottle/nodejs-utils` broke the developer app at runtime:

```
Uncaught Error: Module "node:os" has been externalized for browser compatibility.
Cannot access "node:os.homedir" in client code.
    at expand-home.ts:1
```

That package is barrel-exported and ~5 client modules import `isRecord` from it, so one `node:os` import at the top of the barrel reached every one of them.

**Nothing caught it.** `typecheck` passed, `lint` passed, and the production build passed — Vite externalizes node builtins for the browser and stubs them, so the failure is deferred to the moment a page actually loads. The first signal was a user opening a plan detail page.

## The convention already exists — it just is not enforced

The codebase already knows this rule and follows it, three different ways:

- **`*.server.ts`** — `openthrottle-agentic-utils` and `openthrottle-skills` are reached only from server-only modules (`ide-engine.server.ts`, `disk-fallback.server.ts`, …).
- **`import type`** — `routing/ide/utils/repositories.ts` does `import type { WorkspaceConfig } from '@openthrottle/openthrottle-ide'`, erased at compile time.
- **A comment** — `routing/settings/data/agent-clis.data.ts` literally says `@openthrottle/openthrottle-drivers` "cannot be imported into the browser bundle (node-only …)".

That third one is the tell: the rule was understood well enough to write down, and enforced by nothing.

## A blanket ban would be wrong

The naive rule — "no node builtins in `packages/*`" — fails immediately. Current node-builtin usage in packages the client apps reference:

| Package | Files using node builtins | How client code reaches it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openthrottle-agentic-utils` | 38 | `*.server.ts` only — legitimate |
| `openthrottle-ide` | 20 | `import type` only — legitimate |
| `openthrottle-skills` | 8 | `*.server.ts` only — legitimate |
| `openthrottle-drivers` | 5 | not imported; comment explains why |
| `nodejs-utils` | 0 (after the fix) | genuinely client-side |

These packages are *supposed* to use node. The invariant is not about the package — it is about **what a client module can transitively reach**.

## What to build — needs a decision (task 1)

Sketches, not a prescription:

- **Lint the consumer side.** `no-restricted-imports` in the React Router apps' client directories, banning node builtins and the known node-only packages, with `*.server.ts` exempt. Cheap and precise about intent; catches a direct import but not a transitive one (which is exactly what bit us — `isRecord` → barrel → `node:os`).
- **Lint the producer side, selectively.** Ban node builtins in packages designated client-safe (`nodejs-utils`, `nodejs-graphql`, `agentic-token-usage`, `react-router-*`), leaving server-side packages alone. Catches the actual failure, needs a maintained list of which packages are client-safe — though `package.json` or Nx tags may already imply it.
- **Catch it at build.** Something that fails when a client bundle externalizes a node builtin. Strongest signal, since it is transitive by construction and needs no list; may be as simple as failing on Vite's externalization warning.

The producer-side option looks closest to the real invariant, but check whether the existing Nx tags (`type:`, `technology:`) already encode client-vs-server well enough to drive it, rather than adding a parallel list to maintain.

## Non-goals

- Banning node builtins in packages that are legitimately server-side.
- Reworking the `*.server.ts` convention — it works; this is about catching violations of it.

## Related

- The break and its fix are in PR #437 (`fix(openthrottle-server): keep node:os out of the browser bundle`) — `expandHome` moved to `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/paths/`.
- `docs/monorepo/agent-editor-folders.md` and the IDE engine's server/client split document the existing convention.
summary: A node builtin reaching a client bundle passes typecheck AND build, then throws in the browser. The convention is already understood and written in comments — it just has no mechanical guard. Add one, without banning node in packages that are legitimately server-side.
title: Enforce the client/node boundary so a node: import in a shared package fails at lint, not at runtime

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal
Make plan→repository auto-linking reliable for **both** directories of work:

- **OpenThrottle (nitrous)** — plans authored inside the OT monorepo checkout
- **Foreign / non-OT repos (cars)** — plans authored inside registered checkouts like `atlasworksinc/native-apps`

Folder you created from → match against the caller's registered checkouts → seed `runConfigJson.workspace.repositoryId` (+ `checkoutId` when resolvable). Linking is **not** the free-text `project` label.

## Problem (current)
1. Cursor's global OT MCP launcher (`scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.ts`) `chdir`s into the OpenThrottle checkout before stdio capture, so "created from native-apps" is reported as the OT path (or seeds nothing).
2. Misses are silent — plan creates with empty `workspace.repositoryId`.
3. Agents often set `project: "native-apps"` and think that is the link; it is not.
4. Cursor-exposed `create_plan` schema omits `workspacePath` (`additionalProperties: false`), so agents cannot easily override.

## Approach
- Preserve the **client workspace path** (Cursor/Claude workspace / true caller cwd) separately from the launcher's need to run inside the OT checkout for `tsx`/deps.
- Prefer: capture path **before** `chdir`, or honor `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` when the editor injects the open workspace; never let launcher `cwd` pretend to be the author's workspace when they differ.
- Keep server-side resolution as today: hint only, deepest registered checkout wins, SA `acting_user_id` for user-scoped checkouts — works for OT **and** foreign repos once the path is correct.
- Verify both paths with live creates; document the contract for agents (`repositoryId` vs `project`).

## Success criteria
- `create_plan` from `/home/demo/Development/openthrottle` → `workspace.repositoryId` = OT monorepo (`08619f7c-…`).
- `create_plan` from `/home/demo/Development/github/atlasworks/services/native-apps` → `workspace.repositoryId` = native-apps (`fc184fa5-…`).
- Neither path requires the agent to hand-write `runConfigJson` for the common case.
- Explicit `runConfigJson` / `workspacePath` still win when provided.

## Non-goals
- Replacing `project`/`projectId` NX association with repo linking.
- Making unregistered folders fail plan creation (hint stays non-gating).
summary: Auto-link plans from folder→registered checkout for both OpenThrottle and foreign repos; fix MCP launcher cwd capture so Cursor/foreign workspaces are not erased.
title: Dual-path plan workspace linking: OT (nitrous) + foreign repos (cars)

author: visormatt
description:
# Project Edit page (openthrottle-developer)

## Goal
Add an Edit page for projects so project fields (name, description, nxProjectName) can be updated from the UI instead of editing the DB directly.

## Context (verified against current code)
- Detail route today: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects.$projectId.tsx` (loader + `ProjectDetailTabs`, action = `runProjectDetailAction`). Sidecar doc: `projects.$projectId.tsx.graphql`. Co-located test: `app/routes/__tests__/projects.$projectId.test.tsx`.
- Backend is DONE — no server changes needed:
  - `updateProject(input: UpdateProjectInput!): ProjectObject` already exists in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/projects/projects.resolver.ts`.
  - `UpdateProjectInput { id: ID!, name, description, nxProjectName (all nullable) }` in `project.input.ts`.
  - Editable fields: `name`, `description`, `nxProjectName`.
- Shared form: `app/routing/projects/components/ProjectForm.tsx` — currently create-only (no default values, hardcoded "Create project" button, cancel → `/projects`).
- Create route `projects.create.tsx` is the pattern to mirror for the action (formData → validate → `executeGraphqlWithAuth` → redirect).

## Approach
1. Rename detail route `projects.$projectId.tsx` → `projects.$projectId._index.tsx` (move `.graphql` sidecar and co-located test alongside; update `+types` import path and any `handle`/breadcrumb wiring). This frees the `/projects/:projectId` prefix for sibling leaf routes. Note: these are independent leaf routes (no shared `projects.$projectId.tsx` layout with `<Outlet/>`), so each renders in its own `GlobalScreen`.
2. Extend `ProjectForm` to support edit mode: accept optional `defaultValues` ({ name, description, nxProjectName }), a submit label, and a cancel target; keep create call sites working.
3. New route `projects.$projectId.edit.tsx`: loader fetches the project's current values, renders `ProjectForm` in edit mode; action reads formData, calls `updateProject`, redirects back to `/projects/:projectId` on success. Breadcrumb handle "Edit" under the project.
4. Add GraphQL docs: `updateProject` mutation + an edit-loader query (reuse existing project fields; a lightweight `getProjectForEdit` query or reuse the `ProjectPageDetails` fields). Run codegen and commit `__generated__`.
5. Add an "Edit" affordance on the detail page linking to `./edit`.
6. Tests: rename existing detail test, add render/action tests for the edit route (render-level per authed-page permission constraints).

## Validation
- `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel` (no server schema change, but new consumer docs must generate types)
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build`

## Notes / gotchas
- No new TS enums; `as const`; explicit return types; `import type`.
- Keep component section-comment scaffold (Hooks/Setup/Handlers/Markup/Life Cycle/🔌 Short Circuit).
- Data/copy belongs in nearest `data/`.
- Authed pages need `settings:read`; fresh seed users have zero perms — prefer render-level Vitest over full E2E for the loader/action.
- No repo-root schema change; do NOT run server dev to regen schema.gql unless a resolver/type changes (it doesn't here).
summary: Add an Edit page for projects (openthrottle-developer): rename the detail route to ._index, extend ProjectForm for edit mode, add projects.$projectId.edit.tsx wired to the existing updateProject mutation.
title: Project Edit page (developer app)

author: visormatt
description:
Re-enable the already-wired GitHub Actions matrix so `lint` / `typecheck` / `test` can run across a few free `ubuntu-latest` boxes instead of one.

## Why now

The shard loop in `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (the commented `parallelize-tasks.ts` step around the SCALING RISK note) and `scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts` were **disabled by design as a cost tradeoff**, not because the wiring was unfinished. That tradeoff died when CI moved to GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` on this **public** repo (plan `6ced8d0e`): standard-runner minutes are unlimited and free. The remaining constraints are wall-clock (30-minute job ceiling), queue contention, and not wasting N× checkout/install on shards that do not pay for themselves.

Today the `build` job is still a 1×1 matrix (`jobCount: 1`, `jobIndex: [1]`, single `target: ['lint,typecheck,test']`). `ci-success` already exists as the stable required check so branch protection does **not** pin a matrix-suffixed job name — keep it that way.

## Do not blindly uncomment

Uncommenting the shard loop as-is would be wrong:

- The live `NX ${{ matrix.target }} affected` step would still run the **full** affected set on every box, then the shard loop would run it again. Replace, do not stack.
- Codegen drift, circular-deps, licenses, prettier, agent-asset SSOT, and `audit:strict` are **once-per-run** gates. Running them on every shard multiplies checkout+install for no coverage gain. Keep them on `jobIndex == 1` or extract a sibling `gates` job.
- The Nx Actions cache key is `…-${{ github.sha }}` with no shard suffix. N matrix legs of the same SHA race the save; only the first write wins and the others' task hashes are discarded. Include `matrix.jobIndex` (and `matrix.target` if targets split) in the key; keep the existing restore-key prefixes so shards still warm from prior runs.
- `parallelize-tasks.ts` takes `github.ref` as argv[5] and never uses it. The unquoted `${{ matrix.target }}` form breaks if a target ever contains spaces (`test --coverage`). Empty shards print nothing and the `while read` loop succeeds without running Nx — that is correct, but must stay explicit in comments/tests.
- Round-robin by project name (apps first, then packages) does **not** split `openthrottle-developer`'s Vitest suite. That suite is one Nx project; project sharding will not make it smaller. The vmForks + `vmMemoryLimit` work (plan `e448a51d` / PR #267) stays the lever for that suite. Per-box `nx affected --target=test --parallel` is a **separate** evidence-gated follow-up (see the serialized-test comment in the workflow); do not flip it in the same change as sharding.

## Recommended shape (v1)

Start with **project sharding**, not a target × jobIndex cross product:

- `jobCount: 2` or `3` (same integer as `jobIndex: [1, 2]` / `[1, 2, 3]` — they MUST stay in sync).
- Keep a single `target: ['lint,typecheck,test']` so v1 is 2–3 boxes, not 9.
- `strategy.fail-fast: false` so one red shard does not cancel the others (better signal).
- Each shard runs lint + typecheck + test **only for its project chunk** via `parallelize-tasks.ts` → `nx affected --exclude="*,$tags"`.
- Once-per-run gates stay on one box.

Measure current step timings on a fat affected graph **before** picking 2 vs 3. Typical `build` is ~6 min (ci-cost.md, 2026-08-18); checkout + `pnpm install` is a large fraction of that. If setup is ~2 min/box, a 3-box split of a 6-minute job can lose the wall-clock win. Shard count should be the smallest N where worst-case (full affected, approaching the 30 m ceiling) clearly improves, not a decorative matrix.

Target-split (`target: [lint, typecheck, test]`, still `jobCount: 1`) is a simpler alternative if measurement shows project shards are setup-bound: it parallelizes lint/typecheck against test but leaves the heavy test graph on one box. Record the choice in the workflow comment and in `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md`.

## Docs / comments to retarget

The "deferred by design / cost tradeoff" language is now stale in:

- `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (SCALING RISK block, shard-loop comment, serialized-test note)
- `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` (open item on `--parallel=1`; note that minutes are free so the shard decision is wall-clock vs queue, not spend)
- `docs/monorepo/CI-quality-gates.md` (P4 row: sharded test is Off, tracked by the old coverage plan)
- `docs/monorepo/NX.md` ("pinned to a single runner as a deliberate cost tradeoff")
- `docs/reliability/developer-vitest-pool.md` and the matching comment in `applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts` ("runners we intentionally don't pay for")

Related completed work: CI cost / free runners `6ced8d0e`; developer Vitest pool `e448a51d`. P4 in CI-quality-gates currently points at "Improve test coverage and CI test execution" — retarget that row at **this** plan once created.

## Success

A ready PR (or a few consecutive runs on a scratch branch) shows: shards partition affected projects with no overlap and no silent empty success when work existed; once-per-run gates still run exactly once; `ci-success` is green iff every shard + the changes gate succeeded; draft/docs skips still skip; no `(0 test)` OOM files; docs match the live matrix.
summary:
Shipped as PR #397 (merged, 97a3210a). CI now runs `lint,typecheck,test` across a 3-box `ubuntu-latest` project-shard matrix with fail-fast: false; `ci-success` remains the single required check.

Delivered: measured baseline chose N=3 over 2 and over a target-split (setup is ~1.6 min/box, 6-9% of the job, so shards are not setup-bound); `parallelize-tasks.ts` rewritten with types, 25 unit tests, and a round-trip self-check that exits non-zero if a shard's selector does not resolve back to exactly its chunk — which caught a silent-drop bug where the root `monorepo` project would have fallen off every shard while CI stayed green; eight whole-tree gates pinned to `matrix.jobIndex == 1`; the Nx Actions cache key gained an optional per-shard suffix (also applied to nx-dependency-graph and the vercel-deploy per-app matrix, where the same race was latent); six stale "deferred as a cost tradeoff" locations retargeted, including correcting a false claim that the affected test step ran `--parallel=1`.

Validated across four consecutive green non-docs PR runs plus one fat-affected main run: disjoint partition, explicit empty-shard no-op, no cache-save race, no OOM/(0 test) markers, longest fat shard 17m01s against a 28m24s single-box worst case.

Known limits, deliberately out of scope: `openthrottle-developer` is one Nx project and cannot be split by project sharding (vmForks / plan e448a51d stays the lever), and `nx affected --target=test --parallel` remains evidence-gated. Going private re-prices every box.
title: CI: shard affected lint/typecheck/test across free runners

author: visormatt
description:
# Scripts fresh coat of paint

## Why

`scripts/` is a mix of eras. ~30 scripts are already directly-executed TypeScript (`tsx ./scripts/*.ts` from package.json), many with Vitest coverage in `scripts/__tests__/`. But ~20 remain POSIX/bash shell (`create_worktree.sh`, the `setup_*.sh` family, `docker-smoke-test.sh`, `sync-subtree.sh`, `verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh`, `check-agent-assets-ssot.sh`, …) where logic is untyped, untested, and duplicated (env parsing, port lookups, logging). Meanwhile the .ts scripts themselves have no shared output conventions — exactly one (`setup_mcp-instructions.ts`) uses chalk; the rest are bare `console.log` with ad-hoc emoji.

Direction: keep leaning into executing `.ts` files directly (tsx / `node --experimental-strip-types`) so scripts get types, imports, shared utils, and tests — and use chalk (already in the pnpm catalog) for a consistent, pleasant CLI UX.

## Shape

1. **Shared toolkit first** — a `scripts/lib/` module (chalk logger with heading/step/success/warn/fail + verbose, env-file reader, exec/run helper, arg helper) with tests, piloted on 1–2 existing .ts scripts.
2. **Convert shell → .ts by family** — worktree scripts, setup scripts, standalone checks/utilities, MCP launchers — each family one task, preserving external contracts.
3. **Consistency pass** — adopt the shared toolkit across the existing .ts scripts so all output looks like one tool.

## Hard constraints (do not break)

- **Bootstrap ordering**: anything that runs before `pnpm install` has completed (parts of `setup_environment.sh` / `setup_software.sh`) cannot depend on node_modules (tsx, chalk). Keep a thin POSIX shim for the pre-install bootstrap; everything after install can be .ts.
- **`create_worktree.sh` is a Claude Code WorktreeCreate hook**: stdout must carry ONLY the worktree absolute path; all narration to stderr. It also has 3 invocation modes (CLI arg, hook JSON on stdin, provision-in-place). Any conversion must preserve this contract exactly and be verified against all 3 modes.
- **`worktree_ports.sh` is *sourced*, not exec'd** (exports OT_PORT_* into the caller). A .ts replacement needs an explicit design: print eval-able exports, or fold it into the .ts worktree provisioner as an import (preferred — imports are the whole point of the .ts move).
- **nx.json references**: `check-agent-assets-ssot.sh` is wired as a monorepo target with explicit `{workspaceRoot}` input globs (the root project owns 0 files — default inputs would hash nothing and cache-hit forever). Update the command AND the input globs on conversion.
- **MCP launcher scripts** (`run-openthrottle-mcp.sh`, `run-github-mcp.sh`, `mcp-git.sh`) are referenced from user-global MCP client configs written by `setup_mcp-instructions.ts`. Converting them means updating the emitted config and communicating a re-run of `pnpm run setup:mcp-instructions`.
- Scripts run via `tsx --env-file .env` in package.json — preserve the env-file behavior per script.
- No new TS enums; `as const`; explicit return types; `import type` (repo rules apply to scripts too).

## Conventions to establish (task 1 makes these concrete)

- One shared logger: chalk-based, honors NO_COLOR / non-TTY (chalk does this natively), stderr for narration in stdout-contract scripts.
- Exit-code discipline: non-zero on failure, `--strict` pattern where audits warn vs fail (matches existing audit-*.ts).
- Every converted script gets a Vitest file in `scripts/__tests__/` for its extractable logic (pure functions exported; thin main() shell).
- Testing recipe follows existing patterns (e.g. `openthrottle-database-migrations.test.ts`, `bootstrap-service-account-credentials.test.ts`).

## Out of scope

- `_worktree.sh` legacy shim if it's dead — delete rather than convert (verify with git grep + check-ignore first).
- Behavior changes to what scripts DO (migrations, seeding, GCS upload logic). This is a re-platform + UX pass, not a redesign.
- `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh` (owned by the skills architecture, runs pre-install).
summary: Modernize the highly useful scripts/ toolbox: continue the shift to directly-executed .ts (tsx) so scripts get types, imports, shared utils and Vitest coverage, and introduce a shared chalk-based CLI toolkit for a consistent, pleasant UX across every script.
title: Scripts fresh coat of paint: shell → tsx, shared chalk UX, tests

author: visormatt
description:
# Per-repository keyed concurrency for scheduled agent jobs

Follow-up from OT plan ef4b5c75 (repository targeting for /schedule), which landed the prerequisite but deliberately left concurrency alone.

## Problem

`SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY = 1` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.constants.ts`) exists because two agent CLIs sharing one cwd fight over the git index. Every scheduled job in the system therefore runs strictly serially, even when the jobs target completely unrelated checkouts.

ef4b5c75 made per-repository targeting real: a schedule now names a `repository_checkout_id`, and every run records the exact `resolved_cwd` it executed in. That makes >1 *conceivable* — but NOT safe on its own, which is why it was left at 1 with a comment saying so. Two schedules can still target the SAME checkout, so simply raising the number reintroduces the original git-index race.

## Goal

Allow genuinely-independent scheduled runs to overlap, while still serialising any two runs that would land in the same directory.

## Design sketch

- The concurrency key is the run's **resolved cwd**, not the checkout id: a schedule with a legacy explicit `cwd` and a schedule targeting a checkout can resolve to the same directory, and the id-based key would miss that. `resolveScheduledAgentJobRunCwd` already centralises this resolution.
- Investigate BullMQ's grouping / rate-limit-by-key facilities against the version pinned here; a group key per resolved cwd with a per-group concurrency of 1 is the shape. If groups are unavailable in the OSS version, the fallback is an application-level advisory lock (a Redis key per resolved cwd) taken in the processor before `runner.run`, releasing in the `finally` block — with a TTL so a crashed worker cannot deadlock a directory forever.
- The processor resolves the cwd BEFORE claiming its run row today, so the key is available early enough to gate on.
- `settings.worktree` runs are already isolated per run; consider whether they should bypass the lock entirely (their effective cwd differs from the checkout path).

## Acceptance

- Two schedules targeting different checkouts demonstrably run concurrently (verified by overlapping run timestamps).
- Two schedules targeting the same checkout — including one via a checkout and one via a legacy `cwd` resolving to the same path — still serialise.
- A worker killed mid-run does not permanently block that directory.
- The concurrency constant and the comment left by ef4b5c75 are updated to describe the new mechanism.
summary: Give the scheduled-agent-jobs worker a per-repository concurrency key derived from each run's resolved cwd, so SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY can exceed 1 without two CLIs fighting over one git index.
title: Per-repository keyed concurrency for scheduled agent jobs

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Foreign-workspace skill injection guarantees (design doc §4, `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md`):

> At no observable point does OT's skill injection modify a tracked file in the target repo or leave `git status` dirty.

**That guarantee is false for any repo whose skill target dir is a symlink into tracked space.**

Found 2026-08-28 while verifying the new foreign-skill boot reconcile against real opted-in checkouts.

## Reproduction (live, on visormatt's machine)

`/home/demo/Development/github/atlasworks/services/ssm-data-pipeline` has a legacy layout:

```
.claude/skills -> ../skills
```

After injection, `git status` in that repo shows:

```
?? .openthrottle/
?? skills/agents-ralph
?? skills/github-commit
...
```

## Mechanism

In `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/foreign-skill-injection/materialize.ts`:

1. `ensureDirRecordingCreated` tests the target dir with `existsSync(abs)`. **`existsSync` follows symlinks**, so `.claude/skills` "exists" — it is neither created nor recorded in `createdDirs`.
2. `symlinkSync(sourcePath, injectedAbs)` then writes to `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name>`, which the symlink **redirects into the repo's tracked `skills/<name>`**.
3. The ledger and `.git/info/exclude` both record the **un-followed** path `/.claude/skills/<name>` (see `git-exclude.ts` `writeManagedExcludeBlock`, which anchors each repo-relative path with a leading `/`).
4. Git is asked to ignore `/.claude/skills/agents-ralph` while the file actually on disk is `skills/agents-ralph`. The patterns do not match, nothing is excluded, and `git status` is dirty.

This is exactly the legacy layout `ot-skill-sync` already guards against in its own fan-out — `ensure_agent_skill_dir` in `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/common.sh` detects a symlinked agent dir and replaces it with a real directory, precisely to avoid writing into `SKILLS_SRC_DIR`. The foreign injector has no equivalent guard.

## Blast radius

Of the 6 ledgered foreign repos on this machine, 1 is affected (`ssm-data-pipeline`). Small today, but it is silent: the injector reports success, and the damage shows up as unexplained untracked files in someone else's repo — the exact failure mode the non-mutation guarantee exists to prevent. Any repo that ran an older `ot-skill-sync` layout, or that hand-rolled `.claude/skills -> ../skills`, is a candidate.

## Direction (needs a decision in task 1)

Two viable options, both acceptable:

- **A — resolve then exclude the real path.** `realpath` the target dir before materializing; record and exclude the resolved, repo-relative path. Keeps injection working in symlinked layouts. Must handle a target dir resolving *outside* the repo (exclude cannot help there — that case must be refused).
- **B — refuse to inject through a symlinked target dir.** Skip that dir, emit a warning naming the repo and suggesting `ot-skill-sync`. Simplest and safest; loses coverage in affected repos (for `.claude/skills -> ../skills`, `.agents/skills` still gets injected, so Claude Code coverage would be lost).

Recommendation: **A with a B fallback** — resolve when the resolved path is still inside the repo, refuse with a warning when it escapes.

## Non-goals

- Changing `ot-skill-sync`'s in-repo fan-out (it already handles this correctly).
- Changing the layering/precedence rules in design doc §1.

## Related

- Design doc: `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md` (§4 is the guarantee this violates; update it with whatever task 1 decides).
- Original injection plan: OT `d3a30314-5f91-4213-9ef1-25d21d2f8680`.
summary: Injection follows a symlinked .claude/skills into the repo's tracked skills/, but excludes the un-followed path — so git status goes dirty in the target repo. Resolve the target dir before materializing, exclude the real path, and heal already-affected repos.
title: Fix foreign-skill injection writing through symlinked target dirs (breaks the non-mutation guarantee)

author: visormatt
description:
# Skills route: pagination, usage-chart reuse, and detail tabs

Three related UX improvements to the OpenThrottle Developer app skills routes.

## Goals
1. **Pagination** on the `/skills` index route, wired to the skills Table.
2. **Reuse** the `/usage` route's **"Usage over time"** chart and **"Top skills"** leaderboard on the `/skills` index route.
3. **Tabs** on the `/skills/$slug` detail route (`Skill` default + `Usage`), mirroring the plan detail route.

## Current state (from codebase exploration)

### `/skills` index — `app/routes/skills._index.tsx`
- Loader returns only `{ entries: RepoSkillEntry[] }` — the full skill list discovered from disk (`discoverRepoSkills`), merged with project-skill flags + availability. No pagination fields.
- Component filters client-side via `filterSkillsBySource(entries, sourceFilter)` (local `useState`) and renders `SkillsTable` (`app/routing/skills/components/SkillsTable.tsx`).
- `SkillsTable` wraps the shared `DataTable` from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`, which registers **only `getCoreRowModel()`** — **no built-in pagination**, no `pageIndex`/`pageSize` props. It renders every row.
- **No usage data is loaded on the index route today.**

### Pagination primitives available
- App-level `OpenThrottlePagination` / `OpenThrottlePaginationSimple` (`@openthrottle/react-router-ui`) — URL-driven prev/next pager, computes page count from `total/limit`, preserves query string.
- Low-level shadcn `Pagination/*` primitives.
- Canonical server-side pattern: `app/routes/plans._index.tsx` (parses `page`/`limit` from searchParams → `offset` → GraphQL → renders `OpenThrottlePagination`).

### Usage charts (`/usage` — `app/routes/usage._index.tsx`)
- **Usage over time**: shared `SkillUsageDailyChart` (`app/global/components/SkillUsageDailyChart.tsx`) — Recharts stacked bar (ours vs third-party), props `{ className?, data: readonly SkillUsageChartDatum[] }`. Datum type + config in `app/global/data/skill-usage-chart.ts`. Already reused by `/usage` and `/skills/$slug`.
- **Top skills**: a shadcn `Table` **inlined** in `app/routing/usage/components/UsageSkillUsage.tsx` (~lines 132-196) — NOT its own component. Rows from `bySkill`; skill cell links to `/skills/$slug` when the slug is in `linkableSlugs`. Formatters/copy in `app/routing/usage/data/skill-usage-copy.ts`.
- Query `getUsageSkillUsage` (`usage._index.tsx.graphql`) returns `{ byDay, byScope, bySkill, filterOptions, totalCount }`, 30-day `YYYY-MM-DD` window.
- Established loader pattern: naked deferred promise → `Suspense`/`Await` → `.catch(() => ({ available: false }))`, mapper util hoisted out of the route (see `to-skill-detail-usage-data.ts`).

### Tabs (plan route — `app/routing/plans/components/PlanDetailRoute.tsx`)
- Uses `OpenThrottleTabs` from `@openthrottle/react-router-ui` with a declarative `urlSync={{ defaultValue, param, parse }}` prop; `TabsList`/`TabsTrigger`/`TabsContent` from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`.
- Tab state syncs to a `tab` URL search param; **scroll-reset is already handled** inside `useUrlSyncedTabValue` (`preventScrollReset: true`). Param name + validating parser in `app/routing/plans/utils/parsers.ts`.
- `SkillDetail.tsx` currently renders a single markdown/editor pane with `SkillDetailUsage` stacked below it in the route (`skills.$slug.tsx`) — no tabs.

## Design decisions
- **Pagination is client-side, URL-driven.** Because the index list is disk-backed and fully in memory, parse `page`/`limit` from searchParams, slice the already-filtered `entries` array, and render `OpenThrottlePagination`. Keep `DataTable` unchanged (do not add `getPaginationRowModel`). Reset to page 1 when the source filter changes.
- **Extract "Top skills" into a shared component** (`SkillUsageLeaderboard`) before reusing it — refactor `/usage` to consume it (zero behavior change) so `/skills` can render the same component.
- **Reuse `SkillUsageDailyChart` as-is** for "Usage over time".
- Follow the deferred + graceful-degradation loader pattern for the new index usage fetch so the skills list paints immediately and a usage failure never breaks the route.

## GraphQL / codegen
Adding a usage document to the skills index requires the code-first codegen flow: boot `openthrottle-server:dev` to regen `schema.gql`, then `nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`, and commit `__generated__` output.

## Validation
`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:{lint,typecheck,test,build}`; add/adjust Vitest coverage for pagination, the extracted leaderboard, and the detail tabs.
summary: Add pagination to the /skills index Table, surface the /usage "Usage over time" + "Top skills" charts on /skills by reusing shared components, and add Skill/Usage tabs to the /skills/$slug detail route.
title: Skills route: pagination, usage-chart reuse, and detail tabs

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

Our committed skill pipeline works: `skills/<name>` (hand-authored SSOT, git-tracked) → `.agents/skills/<name>` (symlink) → `<agent>/skills/<name>` fan-out (`.claude/skills`, `.gemini/skills`), all driven by `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh` with `--check` as the CI drift gate, and one managed `.gitignore` block.

What we cannot do today is let a person iterate on a skill of their own. There is no supported place to put a half-finished, personal, experimental skill that (a) gets the exact same fan-out into every agent CLI, and (b) is structurally impossible to commit. People either hand-edit generated dirs (drift), or drop a real dir under `.agents/skills/` (which `!.agents/skills/*/` rescues from the ignore block — i.e. it becomes committable, and the lockfile/ownership rule then treats it as a vendored install).

Goal: make personal skills a first-class, private tier with a one-command path to promote a good one into the committed catalog.

## The mechanism (why this is cheap)

Personal skills live **outside the repo** at `~/.openthrottle/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and are **symlinked in**. That gives uncommittability for free twice over: the content is not in the worktree at all, and the only artifact inside the repo is a symlink under `.agents/skills/*` / `.claude/skills/` / `.gemini/skills/`, every one of which the existing managed `.gitignore` block already ignores (`!.agents/skills/*/` rescues only real directories, not symlinks). We add an explicit assertion rather than relying on that by accident.

## Prior art to reuse, not rebuild

A **personal tier already exists** for foreign-repo skill injection: `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/foreign-skill-injection/personal-skills-config.ts` (`OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_ENABLED`, `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_DIR`, default `~/.openthrottle/skills`, OFF by default) feeding `resolveForeignSkillManifest` in `packages/openthrottle-skills/src` with locked precedence `ot-curated < personal < target repo`. This plan brings the same tier to the **in-repo** sync pipeline and makes the two share one definition of the root — it must not become a second, divergent notion of "personal".

## Non-goals

- No server/API/database surface. This is local developer tooling.
- No sharing or syncing of personal skills between users or machines.
- No change to how vendored (`skills-lock.json`) installs work.

## Definition of done

- `bash skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh` picks up `~/.openthrottle/skills/*` and fans them out everywhere a committed skill goes.
- `git status` is clean afterwards, and `sync.sh --check` proves each generated personal link is git-ignored.
- Staging or committing a personal skill fails loudly.
- With no personal root present (CI, a fresh clone) behaviour is byte-identical to today.
- `promote` moves a personal skill into `skills/` and re-syncs in one command.
title: Personal (user) skills tier — iterate privately, promote when it's great

author: visormatt
description:
Two UX problems in @openthrottle/react-router-chat (consumed by openthrottle-developer home chat + ChatDialog surfaces, and openthrottle-admin ChatDialog):

1) During long agentic turns the timeline floods the user with tool-call groups. Today `buildTurnTimeline` (packages/react-router-chat/src/turn-tool-groups.ts) folds only consecutive `tool` events into a group; every `thinking` event breaks the run, so a turn that alternates tools -> thinking -> tools -> thinking renders as an endless stack of 'shell / 3 actions' groups and 'Thinking' rows that pushes the user down the page without value. Additionally, `ChatToolCallGroup` mounts with `defaultOpen = running` on an UNCONTROLLED Radix Collapsible, so groups that mount mid-run stay expanded forever.

Goal: (a) all tool-call groups start COLLAPSED by default (including while running - the group header's status pill + active tool name already communicate progress); (b) introduce a second-level fold: any consecutive run of tool-group/thinking timeline slots (i.e. everything between text/usage events) collapses into ONE 'activity' super-group, collapsed by default, expandable to reveal the interleaved tools/thinking sequence. Text events (visible prose) and usage summaries break the super-group.

2) Scrolling: the current auto-scroll in ChatThread.tsx is ref-based, event-driven, and its 'user scrolled up' guard is dead on the developer home route because ChatThread is NOT the scroll container there - GlobalLayout (packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalLayout.tsx line ~84) owns page scroll (see also HomeComposerDock docblock). Goal: an explicit 'pin to bottom' mode - enabled automatically when the user sends a message; while pinned, the view tracks the bottom on every streamed update; any user scroll-away unpins; a visible affordance (pin/jump-to-bottom control near the composer) re-enables it. Must work in BOTH scroll-ownership modes: ChatThread-as-scroller (ChatDialog) and external-scroller (home route via GlobalLayout).

Key files (mapped 2026-08-27): src/turn-tool-groups.ts (buildTurnTimeline, aggregateToolStatus, activeToolOf), src/components/ChatTurnTimeline.tsx, ChatToolCallGroup.tsx, ChatToolCall.tsx, ChatThinkingBlock.tsx, ChatThread.tsx (all scroll logic, lines ~28-141), src/types.ts (ChatTurnEvent union), src/index.ts (public API - new props/components must be re-exported deliberately). Consumers: applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx (~line 167), app/routing/home/demo/HomeComposerDock.tsx, ChatDialog.tsx. Tests are colocated: src/__tests__/turn-tool-groups.test.ts, src/components/__tests__/ChatThread.test.tsx (scrollIntoView spy pattern), ChatTurnTimeline.test.tsx, ChatToolCallGroup.test.tsx; app-side app/routes/__tests__/_index.test.tsx + _index.dock.test.tsx.

Constraints: no TS enums (as-const objects), no `as`/`any`, alphabetized keys, shadcn Collapsible from @openthrottle/react-router-shadcn, use @tools/generators for any NEW component (NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component), keep generated section comments. Validation gates: pnpm nx run react-router-chat:lint|typecheck|test, then openthrottle-developer typecheck+test+build as the integration check (source-first package - no build target).
title: Chat timeline: collapse tool/thinking activity runs by default + pin-to-bottom scrolling

author: visormatt
description:
# Problem

The skill detail route `/skills/:slug` (e.g. `/skills/create-cli`) reads the raw `SKILL.md` off disk in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/read-skill-file.server.ts` and passes the **entire file — YAML frontmatter block included — as `content`** to `SkillDetailTabs`. Every skill file begins with a `---` … `---` frontmatter block (name, description, metadata), so that raw YAML is rendered verbatim to the client instead of being parsed out.

We want a **SSR-friendly** helper that, given the raw file string, returns:

```ts
interface SplitFrontmatterResult {
  content: string;                    // the file body, frontmatter stripped
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;  // the parsed frontmatter as an object
}
```

# Existing building blocks (reuse — do NOT add gray-matter)

`@openthrottle/openthrottle-skills` (already a `workspace:^` dependency of `openthrottle-developer`) already ships the two halves, both pure-JS / SSR-safe (backed by the `yaml` package, no `fs`/Buffer/DOM):

- `extractContentAfterFrontmatter(fileContent)` — tri-state body: original string when there is no frontmatter, the substring after the closing `---` when well-formed, and `null` when a block opens but never closes (malformed). Source: `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/frontmatter/extract-frontmatter-body.ts`.
- `parseYamlFrontmatter(fileContent)` — `{ fields }` where fields is `Record<string, FrontmatterScalar>` (a constrained `string | boolean | readonly string[] | undefined` union, not `Record<string, unknown>`). Source: `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/frontmatter/parse-yaml-frontmatter.ts`.

No combined `{ content, metadata }` function exists. `gray-matter` is NOT a dependency and should not be added — it drags in Buffer/`fs` shims and bundles poorly for SSR; the `yaml`-based path already covers us.

# Design decision to lock during task 1

The requested `metadata: Record<string, unknown>` is looser than the package's existing `FrontmatterScalar`-typed `fields`. Two viable approaches — pick one in task 1:

- **(Recommended) Widen from the existing parser.** Call `parseYamlFrontmatter` + `extractContentAfterFrontmatter`, return `{ content: body, metadata: fields }`. `Record<string, FrontmatterScalar>` is assignable to `Record<string, unknown>`, so the public return type is exactly `ResponseType` while behavior stays consistent with the rest of the codebase (same coercions, same unsupported-construct handling, same last-value-wins). Lowest risk, zero new YAML semantics.
- **Raw `yaml` parse for richer metadata.** Re-parse the frontmatter body with the `yaml` package directly to preserve nested maps/numbers/etc. as real values. Only choose this if a consumer actually needs nested/typed metadata; it diverges from the established scalar contract and needs its own corpus coverage.

# Malformed / edge-case contract to define

`extractContentAfterFrontmatter` returns `null` for a block that opens but never closes. The new helper must NOT return `null` content (the type is `string`). Decide and document: malformed → `{ content: <original file>, metadata: {} }` (treat as no usable frontmatter) is the recommended, non-throwing behavior. No frontmatter at all → `{ content: <original file>, metadata: {} }`.

# Scope

- Add ONE combined, SSR-safe splitter to `@openthrottle/openthrottle-skills` and export it from the package index with a `@public` JSDoc tag (Knip).
- Wire it into the skill detail read path so the rendered `content` no longer contains the frontmatter block, and the parsed `metadata` is available to the route.
- Not in scope: redesigning `SkillDetailTabs` UI or how metadata is displayed beyond making it available; changing the on-disk skill format.

# Reference paths

- Route: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx`
- Server read: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/read-skill-file.server.ts`
- Package: `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/frontmatter/`
- Package index: `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/index.ts`
title: SSR-friendly frontmatter splitter for skill rendering ({ content, metadata })

author: visormatt
description:
# Worktree root: delete dangling references, document only the landed ladder

## What we landed on (the ONLY thing docs should say)

Root resolution, highest rung wins — implemented in `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/root.sh` and
mirrored in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/worktree-root/worktree-root.resolver.ts`:

1. `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the environment
2. `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the target repo's `.env`
3. Default `$HOME/.openthrottle/worktrees`

OT then appends `<org>/<repo>` beneath the root, where org comes from the **git remote**, giving
`~/.openthrottle/worktrees/acme/monorepo/feature-x`. There is no settings file, no database column,
and no third channel.

## Verified drift (confirmed by reading code 2026-08-28, re-verified 2026-08-29)

**1. `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT_FILE` does not exist.** Documented as live config in
`docs/monorepo/environment-variables.md:174` and `skills/ot-worktree/references/contract.md:86`
(as `~/.openthrottle/worktree-root`). Implemented in neither `root.sh` (its only rungs are lines
107/114/119) nor anywhere under `applications/openthrottle-server/src`. A documented knob that
does nothing is the worst dangling reference here — someone will set it and be silently ignored.
It also directly contradicts SKILL.md, which states "There is deliberately no settings file and no
third channel."

**2. `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` is a dead name.** `docs/monorepo/environment-variables.md:173` carries it as
a table row: "Legacy/alias name still referenced by migrations 097/108/109 and forwarded to
create.sh". Nothing forwards it — the live name is `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT` everywhere. The row
is pure archaeology sitting in a current-configuration table.

**3. The old default survives in TypeScript, not just in migrations.** The actual default is
`$HOME/.openthrottle/worktrees` + `<org>/<repo>`. The 2026-08-29 sweep found the superseded
directory-name form on three live surfaces outside `databases/migrations/`:

- `discovered-worktrees.object.ts:52` — the `DEFAULT` rung description of `WorktreeRootSourceEnum`,
  which states `~/.openthrottle/worktrees/<repo-name>` and, worse, says it is "namespaced by the
  base checkout's directory name" — the exact thing `root.sh:31-34` exists to *not* do.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql:3327` — the generated copy of the same sentence.
- `scheduled-agent-jobs.constants.ts:232` — JSDoc calling `~/worktrees/<repo>` "the skill's default".

An earlier revision of this plan wrongly listed the first two as *known-good reference wording*.
They are drift. The trustworthy sources are `skills/ot-worktree/SKILL.md`, `root.sh`'s header,
`.env.default:29`, `worktree-root.resolver.ts`, and `docs/openthrottle/plan-run-worktrees.md`
§ "Where worktrees live".

**4. `plan-run-worktrees.md` is otherwise clean** — one paragraph (§ "One variable, no second
channel") narrates the rise and fall of `user_workspace_settings.worktree_root`, and goes.

## Scope note: this is no longer docs-only

Because item 3 lands in `.object.ts` and regenerates `schema.gql`, the change touches
`openthrottle-server` source and the codegen flow (boot the server to rewrite `schema.gql`, then
`nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`). Task 5 adds a Vitest guard. Plan
category stays `documentation` because the intent is documentation accuracy, but expect a
typecheck/test/codegen cycle, not a pure Markdown diff.

## Explicitly NOT in scope: rewriting migrations

`databases/migrations/097`, `108` and `109` are an applied ledger. 097 added
`user_workspace_settings.worktree_root`, 108 re-commented it, 109 **dropped** it. They replay in
order on a fresh database and are internally consistent as history, so they stay untouched — their
stale prose is a record of what was true when written, which is what a migration is for.

The consequence to note: because 109 dropped the column, **the live database has no stale comment**.
There is nothing to fix in Postgres and no new migration to write. Every remaining problem is in
checked-in files. Any task that finds itself editing a migration has gone off-plan.

## Definition of done

`OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT` is the only worktree-root knob named by any live surface; the default is
stated one way everywhere; a reader never learns what the mechanism used to be outside of
`databases/migrations/`; and a guard makes the next drift fail loudly.
summary: Live surfaces describe two worktree-root config knobs that do not exist (OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT_FILE, OT_WORKTREE_ROOT) and an outdated `<repo-name>` default that survives in TypeScript as well as docs. Scrub every live surface to state only the landed 3-rung ladder, regenerate schema.gql, and add a guard; leave applied migrations as history.
title: Worktree root: delete dangling references, document only the landed ladder

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

On `/plans`, the pagination summary reads **"Showing 1–25 of 29 projects"** — it should say **plans**.

## Root cause

`OpenThrottlePagination` (`packages/react-router-ui/src/components/OpenThrottlePagination.tsx:40`) already supports a `resultLabel` prop, but it silently defaults to `'projects'`:

```ts
resultLabel = 'projects',
```

Any call site that forgets the prop inherits the wrong noun with no type error and no visual signal. The label IS already customizable — the defect is the entity-specific default plus two call sites that never opted in.

## Audit of every `OpenThrottlePagination` call site

| Call site | Entity | Passes `resultLabel`? | Renders |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans._index.tsx:203` | plans | no | "… of N **projects**" 🐞 |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/projects/components/ProjectDetailTabs.tsx:161` | project **tasks** | no | "… of N **projects**" 🐞 |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects._index.tsx:171` | projects | no (relies on default) | correct by accident |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills._index.tsx:218` | skills | yes — `"skills"` | correct |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/prompts._index.tsx:164` | prompts | yes — `"prompts"` | correct |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/search._index.tsx:166` | results | yes — `"results"` | correct |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/queues.$queueId._index.tsx:151` (`OpenThrottlePaginationSimple`) | jobs | yes — `"jobs"` | correct |

`OpenThrottlePaginationSimple` (`packages/react-router-ui/src/components/OpenThrottlePaginationSimple.tsx:29`) has the same prop but a safe neutral default (`'results'`) — that is the shape to converge on.

Note the same entity-specific bleed exists in the pagination internals: the shared `basePath` default is `/projects` and the query-string builder is `buildProjectsSearchParams` / `ProjectsSearchParamsExtras`. Renaming those is out of scope here, but worth flagging.

## Approach

1. Fix the two wrong call sites (`resultLabel="plans"`, `resultLabel="tasks"`).
2. Make the default entity-neutral (`'results'`), and pass `resultLabel="projects"` explicitly on `projects._index.tsx` — currently correct only because of the bad default.
3. Prefer making `resultLabel` **required** on `OpenThrottlePagination` so the compiler, not a screenshot, catches the next omission. There are only 4 call sites, so the cost is trivial. Decide in task 2; if required wins, the neutral default in step 2 becomes moot for this component (keep it on `Simple`).

## Out of scope

Pluralization (`1 plan` vs `2 plans`) and i18n. Renaming `buildProjectsSearchParams` / `ProjectsSearchParamsExtras` / the `/projects` `basePath` default.

## Validation

- `pnpm nx run react-router-ui:test`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck` — catches any missed call site once the prop is required
- Visual: `/plans?page=1&limit=25` reads "Showing 1-25 of 29 plans"; the project-detail Tasks tab reads "tasks"
summary: The /plans pagination summary reads "Showing 1-25 of 29 projects".
