OpenThrottlePagination already supports resultLabel but defaults to the entity-specific 'projects'; two call sites (plans index, project-detail Tasks tab) never opt in. Fix both, make the default entity-neutral, and audit every call site.
title: Pagination result label: /plans says "projects"

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Build a living competitive landscape for OpenThrottle (OT) — the agentic-development / plan-and-task orchestration platform this monorepo ships. For each competitor and adjacent tool, capture:

1. **What it is / what it offers** — core product, primary jobs-to-be-done, notable features.
2. **How they frame it** — positioning, target user, category language, pricing model, GTM narrative.
3. **How it ties back to OT** — which OT features/tooling it overlaps, competes with, or complements; where OT is differentiated; gaps OT should consider.

This is intentionally a **growing** list — start with the seed set below and keep adding relevant entrants as they surface.

## Seed set (from request)

- Polygraph — https://trypolygraph.com/
- HumanLayer — https://www.humanlayer.dev/
- T3 (t3.codes) — https://t3.codes/
- Zed "Delta" — https://zed.dev/blog/introducing-delta
- Linear (agentic + Coinbase case study) — https://linear.app/customers/coinbase

## Deliverable

A synthesized competitive landscape write-up + a feature/positioning matrix, plus an explicit OT tie-back (overlap, differentiation, gaps). Findings recorded as plan output / a doc in the knowledge base — not as loose Markdown under docs/.

## Method notes

- Each competitor gets its own task so profiles can be researched in parallel and expanded over time.
- Keep dimensions consistent across profiles (see the framework task) so the matrix is apples-to-apples.
- Cite source URLs for every claim; distinguish marketing copy from verifiable capability.
summary: Map the competitive/adjacent landscape for OpenThrottle: who's out there, what they offer, how they frame it, and how each ties back to OT features/tooling.
title: Competitive landscape & market research for OpenThrottle

author: visormatt
description:
# Goal

Today worktree creation is OpenThrottle-monorepo-shaped: `scripts/create_worktree.sh`, `scripts/ensure_worktree.sh`, `scripts/setup_worktree.sh` and `scripts/worktree_ports.sh` live in this repo, are wired via `pnpm worktree:new` / `pnpm worktree:heal`, the nx `monorepo:ensure-worktree` target, the Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook (`.claude/settings.json`) and `.cursor/worktrees.json`. None of it travels — another GitHub repo gets nothing. And there is no removal path at all: a repo-wide grep finds no `git worktree remove` / prune / teardown anywhere, which is why orphan worktrees accumulate.

Because OpenThrottle skills are already mapped into any repo (`skills/` → `.agents/skills/` → `.claude/skills/` via `ot-skill-sync`), the worktree machinery belongs in a skill. Any repo that has the skill should then create, heal and destroy worktrees the same way.

## Three composable actions

The skill exposes exactly three verbs, each usable standalone and callable from the others:

| Action | Script | Entrypoint | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **create** | `create.sh` | `pnpm worktree:new`, Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook, Cursor | Create the worktree, then provision it |
| **heal** | `heal.sh` | `pnpm worktree:heal`, nx `monorepo:ensure-worktree` | Lazily provision a worktree that was made outside the skill |
| **destroy** | `destroy.sh` | `pnpm worktree:remove` | Tear down and remove a worktree (net-new) |

They share `common.sh` (linked-worktree detection, name sanitization, target validation), `root.sh` (the root ladder), `provision.sh` and the teardown hook.

Two decisions were made up front and are NOT open for re-litigation during implementation:

1. **Single global worktree root, namespaced by repo:** `~/worktrees/<repo-name>/<worktree-name>`. This replaces the current per-repo default (a sibling `openthrottle-worktrees` directory). `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` still overrides it, and a repo-level override is explicitly deferred (a later plan) — leave a seam, do not build it.
2. **Repo-specific provisioning stays in the repo.** The skill owns the generic mechanics (linked-worktree detection, hook-payload parsing, name sanitization, root resolution, `git worktree add`/`remove`, self-heal guard). It delegates to repo-provided provision/teardown hooks if they exist, and no-ops otherwise. OpenThrottle keeps `scripts/setup_worktree.sh` (pnpm install/build, `.env` reset, 6020–6026 port remap, docker compose override, service-account token sync) as ITS provisioner — none of that moves into the skill.

# Shape of the target

```
skills/ot-worktree/
  SKILL.md
  scripts/
    common.sh        # linked-worktree detection, logging, repo/name/target resolution
    root.sh          # resolve_worktree_root — the single global root ladder
    create.sh        # modes: CLI arg / hook stdin payload / provision-in-place
    heal.sh          # lazy self-heal guard (was ensure_worktree.sh)
    destroy.sh       # teardown + git worktree remove + prune (net-new)
    provision.sh     # find + exec the repo provisioner, or no-op
  references/
    contract.md      # the repo provision/teardown contract + env vars
```

Repo provisioner discovery order (first hit wins, all optional):
1. `$OT_WORKTREE_PROVISION` (absolute or repo-relative path)
2. `.worktree/provision.sh`
3. `scripts/setup_worktree.sh`  ← what OpenThrottle uses today, so this repo needs no new file

Teardown mirrors it: `$OT_WORKTREE_TEARDOWN`, then `.worktree/teardown.sh` (no `scripts/` fallback — no incumbent to preserve). Nothing found → log and no-op; a plain `git worktree add`/`remove` is a valid outcome in a repo with no setup needs.

Both hooks get: cwd = the worktree, `OT_SOURCE_REPO` = primary checkout, `OT_WORKTREE_NAME`, `OT_WORKTREE_PATH`, stdin closed. Port allocation (`scripts/worktree_ports.sh`) stays in this repo and stays owned by `setup_worktree.sh` — it is OpenThrottle's canonical-port concern, not a generic one.

# Root-resolution ladder (new)

Highest rung wins:
1. `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the environment (one-off overrides; also how the BullMQ provisioner forwards the workspace setting).
2. `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the primary checkout's `.env`.
3. **Default: `~/worktrees/<repo-name>`** where `<repo-name>` is the basename of the primary checkout.

Rungs 1 and 2 are absolute paths that already include their own namespacing — do NOT append `<repo-name>` to an explicitly configured root; that would silently relocate every existing configured setup. Only the default rung namespaces.

# Back-compat / callers to keep working

- `pnpm worktree:new <name>` and `pnpm worktree:heal` stay as the human entrypoints — thin wrappers onto the skill scripts. `pnpm worktree:remove` joins them.
- nx `monorepo:ensure-worktree` target (`package.json` nx block, wired via `targetDefaults.dev.dependsOn`).
- `.claude/settings.json` `WorktreeCreate` hook — MUST still print only the absolute worktree path on stdout.
- `.cursor/worktrees.json` provision-in-place mode (`cwd=$WORKTREE_PATH`, no args, no stdin).
- Server-side: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/worktree-root/worktree-root.resolver.ts` is the TS mirror of the shell ladder and is consumed by the settings page, `worktree-discovery.service.ts`, `plan-run-worktree-provision.service.ts` and `discovered-worktrees.resolver.ts`. Its `DEFAULT_WORKTREE_ROOT_DIRECTORY_NAME = 'openthrottle-worktrees'` default must change in lockstep or discovery will look in the wrong directory.
- Existing worktrees under the old sibling `openthrottle-worktrees` directory must keep working. They are already registered in `git worktree list`, so nothing needs moving; discovery just needs to not lose them.

# Non-goals

- Repository-level root override (deferred; leave the seam only).
- Moving port allocation, `.env` handling, or docker compose isolation into the skill.
- Auto-migrating existing worktrees to the new root.
- Server-side / UI wiring of the destroy action (a follow-up once the script exists).
summary: Extract worktree create/heal into a portable `ot-worktree` skill, add a net-new destroy action (three composable actions), and move every repo to a single global worktree root (`~/worktrees/<repo>/<name>`), with repo-specific provisioning and teardown delegated to hooks.
title: ot-worktree skill: portable worktree create/heal + single global worktree root

author: visormatt
description:
Ensure GraphQL selection-set fields (and fragment field lists) are alphabetized as much as we can automate, matching the monorepo's "alphabetize when order doesn't matter" convention.

## Motivation

Consumer GraphQL documents (e.g. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx.graphql`) often list fields in ad-hoc order. Alphabetical field order makes diffs quieter, reviews faster, and keeps documents consistent with our TS/object-key alphabetization rule.

Example target shape — fragment fields ABC'd:

```graphql
fragment SkillDetailUsageBySkill on SkillUsageBySkillObject {
  abandonedCount
  avgDurationMs
  count
  errorCount
  lastUsedAt
  outcomeCount
  scope
  skillName
  successCount
}
```

Today that file is *not* fully alphabetized (`skillName`, `scope`, `count`, …).

## Scope (in)

- GraphQL **documents**: `*.graphql` co-located with routes, package operation docs (developer, admin, website, email, mcp, agentic-ralph, vscode-openthrottle, etc.).
- Selection sets inside queries, mutations, subscriptions, and fragments (including nested selections).
- Lint/CI enforcement so new documents cannot regress.
- Optional autofix (ESLint `--fix`, Prettier plugin, or a dedicated sort script) preferred over manual-only cleanup.

## Scope (out / explicit non-goals unless a later task says otherwise)

- NestJS code-first **schema** field declaration order on `@ObjectType` / `@InputType` (decorator order can be domain-intentional; `schema.gql` is generated).
- Reordering operation **arguments** or variable definitions only if the chosen tool supports it safely; prefer fields first.
- Changing runtime behavior or codegen output shapes beyond field order in source documents.

## Approach (investigate → choose → enforce → sweep)

1. Inventory all `*.graphql` document roots and current lint/format pipeline (no `@graphql-eslint` today).
2. Pick automation: prefer existing ecosystem (`@graphql-eslint` custom/community alphabetize rule, Prettier GraphQL plugin + sort, or a small Nx/workspace script using `graphql` AST) that can **lint + autofix**.
3. Wire into monorepo lint (shared ESLint flat config and/or an Nx target) so `pnpm nx affected --target=lint` / CI catches violations.
4. Autofix + commit sweeps per app/package (start with `openthrottle-developer` route docs as the exemplar).
5. Document the convention in coding rules (point at GraphQL documents) so agents/humans know the expectation.

## Acceptance

- A lint/format check fails when selection-set fields are out of alphabetical order.
- Autofix (or a documented one-command sort) brings documents into compliance.
- `openthrottle-developer` route `.graphql` files (including `skills.$slug.tsx.graphql`) pass.
- Other document-owning projects either pass or are listed with a tracked follow-up if intentionally deferred.
- Short rule/docs note: GraphQL selection sets are alphabetized when order does not matter.
title: Alphabetize GraphQL document fields (automated)

author: visormatt
description:
Mirror the component-primitive-shape system for React Router route modules under `app/routes/*.tsx`.

## Problem

Route files are meant to stay thin and aligned with the route generator template (`tools/generators/src/generators/react-router/files/route/__name__.tsx`). In practice they accumulate module-scope helpers, constants, mappers, and config that belong in the feature folder under `app/routing/<area>/` (same layout the `folders` generator scaffolds: `components/`, `config/`, `data/`, `hooks/`, `utils/`).

Example violation: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx` lines 29–60 define `SKILL_USAGE_RANGE_DAYS` and `toSkillDetailUsageData` at module scope inside the route file. Those should live under `app/routing/skills/` (e.g. `config/` / `utils/` / `data/`) and be imported back into the route.

## Goal

Add a second custom ESLint check in `@tools/dotfiles` (alongside `openthrottle/component-primitive-shape`) — tentatively `openthrottle/route-primitive-shape` — plus docs + optional audit script, so route modules stay template-shaped and non-route logic is hoisted into `app/routing/*`.

## Scope

- React Router apps with `app/routes/` + `app/routing/` (at least `openthrottle-developer`; extend to admin/email/website if they share the same layout).
- Generator template remains SSOT for the allowed route skeleton; the new doc/rule implement that contract.
- Canonical routing subtree already documented in `tools/generators/src/generators/folders/CANONICAL_ROUTING_SUBTREE.md` — reuse that destination map (utils/config/data/hooks).

## Out of scope

- Rewriting every existing route in one PR (inventory + phased remediation / opt-outs first).
- Changing React Router framework conventions (`loader`/`action`/`meta`/`handle`/`ErrorBoundary`/`default` export stay in the route file).
- Component-primitive-shape itself (already shipped).

## Success criteria

1. Written contract doc (e.g. `docs/monorepo/route-primitive-shape.md`) with stable rule ids (R1…).
2. ESLint rule in `tools/dotfiles` with unit tests + generator-template contract test (same pattern as `component-primitive-shape`).
3. Rule enabled on RR app route files; clear messages pointing at `app/routing/<area>/{utils,config,data,hooks}`.
4. Baseline inventory of current violations; at least the skills.$slug example (and similar easy wins) remediated as the reference fix.
5. Optional `audit:route-shape` script / `check:local` wiring when ready for a gate.

## Reference implementations to clone

- Rule: `tools/dotfiles/src/rules/component-primitive-shape.ts`
- Tests: `tools/dotfiles/src/__tests__/component-primitive-shape.test.ts`, `generator-template-contract.test.ts`
- Doc: `docs/monorepo/component-primitive-shape.md`
- Audit: `scripts/audit-component-shape.ts` + `pnpm run audit:component-shape*`
- Route template: `tools/generators/.../files/route/__name__.tsx`
- Routing folders: `CANONICAL_ROUTING_SUBTREE.md`
title: Enforce thin React Router route modules (route-primitive-shape)

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal The scheduled-job detail route (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/schedule.$jobId._index.tsx`) currently stacks two sections vertically: the `Prompt` `
` block and the `Run history` table. Move both into tabs — `Prompt` (default) and `History` — matching the tabbed detail pattern already used on skill/plan/project detail routes.

## Existing pattern to copy (do not invent a new one)

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/components/SkillDetailTabs.tsx` — `OpenThrottleTabs` from `@openthrottle/react-router-ui` with `urlSync={{ defaultValue, param, parse }}`, `TabsList variant="line"`, `TabsTrigger` with a lucide icon + `id`, one `TabsContent` per tab.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/utils/parse-skill-detail-tab.ts` — the validating `tab` search-param parser (`null` for missing/unknown so the shared `useUrlSyncedTabValue` canonicalizes the default out of the URL).
- Sibling references: `PlanDetailRoute.tsx`, `ProjectDetailTabs.tsx`.

## Shape

- Keep the `GlobalHeading` action buttons (Edit / Run now / Disable / Delete), the driver/model `Badge`, the cron/timezone line, and the `actionError` alert **above** the tabs — they are page-level, not per-tab.
- New component `app/routing/schedule/components/ScheduleDetailTabs.tsx` owns the tab shell and both tab bodies. Props: `jobId`, `prompt`, `runs` (the loader's `scheduledAgentJobRuns` type).
- `Prompt` tab: the existing `
{job.prompt}
`. Drop the now-redundant inner `
Prompt
` since the tab label names it.
- `History` tab: the existing `ScheduleRunsTable` plus the empty state ("No runs yet. Use “Run now” to trigger one.") and the "Logs stream to the queue console keyed by each run." hint.
- New util `app/routing/schedule/utils/parse-schedule-detail-tab.ts` exporting `ScheduleDetailTab = 'history' | 'prompt'`, `SCHEDULE_DETAIL_TAB_SEARCH_PARAM = 'tab'`, and `parseScheduleDetailTab`.
- Route keeps `data-testid="ScheduleDetail"` on its wrapper so existing route tests keep resolving.

## Constraints

- Scaffold the component with the generator, do not hand-write the file: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=app/routing/schedule/components --name=ScheduleDetailTabs`. Keep the generated section comments (Hooks / Setup / Handlers / Markup / Life Cycle / 🔌 Short Circuit) even when empty.
- Components export only the component + its props interface; no data/copy literals leaking into the route.
- UI primitives come from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; tabs shell from `@openthrottle/react-router-ui`.
- Tests use `component` (not `screen`) and `userEvent` (not `fireEvent`).
- No new TS enums (`as const`), no `as` casts, `import type` for type-only imports, explicit return types, alphabetized props/keys.

## Validation

- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test`
- Live check `/schedule/:jobId`: default lands on `Prompt` with no `?tab=`, clicking `History` sets `?tab=history`, deep-linking `?tab=history` opens History, an unknown `?tab=bogus` falls back to Prompt. Note the known scroll-reset caveat for URL-synced tabs (`GlobalLayout` resets on pathname only).

## Out of scope

- Editing the prompt inline, run filtering/pagination, and any change to the run-detail route (`schedule.$jobId.runs.$runId`).
summary: Split applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/schedule.$jobId._index.tsx body into URL-synced tabs: a `Prompt` tab holding the current prompt content and a `History` tab holding the run-history table.
title: Tab the scheduled-job detail route (Prompt + History)

author: visormatt
description:
docs/ holds 80 markdown files on main. A third of them document HOW WE GOT somewhere rather than WHERE WE ARE: they lead with `Status: accepted`, a `Plan-Id:`, a `Supersedes:` line, a "Problem recap", or a literal "Task breakdown (for this plan)" section. Another set are pure planning artifacts — three of them say "Planning only—no implementation" outright. And docs/README.md indexes only about 40 of the 80 files, so the other half is unreachable and unowned.

## Categorization (all 80 files on main)

- **A. Keep as-is — genuine usage/reference (43 files):** Folders.md, Skills.md, Docker_Compose.md, monorepo/{NX,NX/tags,Knip,Forms,Tooling,Ollama,agent-editor-folders,child-repo-hook-telemetry-contract,component-primitive-shape,route-primitive-shape,test-coverage-audit,worktree-port-allocation,openthrottle-developer-vite-devtools,recurring-agent-jobs}.md, testing/snapshot-replacement-patterns.md, nestjs/wiring-auth-rbac.md, openthrottle/{openthrottle-server-auth,features,styles,scheduled-agent-jobs-usage,plan-run-worktrees,authoring-plans-via-mcp,mcp-registration,agentic-cli-chat-backends,local-quickstart,run-openthrottle-server-developer}.md, workflows/ralph-design.md, tools/templates/{AGENT_USAGE,EXAMPLES,TROUBLESHOOTING,NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS,folders,nestjs,package,react,react-router}.md
- **B. Decision tree → flatten to state (16 files):** tasks 3–8 below.
- **C. Plan/audit artifact, no usage guidance → delete (9 files):** tasks 9–11 below.
- **D. Merge/dedupe (7 files):** tasks 2, 8, 12 below.
- **E. Marketing subtree (8 files) → HOLD:** task 13, blocked.
- **F. Root cause → index gate:** task 1.

## Verified findings behind the deletes

- AUDIT_SCOPE.md / AUDIT_CHECKLIST.md / RULES_TO_GENERATORS_MAP.md all state "Planning only—no implementation" for plan `d8ec2e70`.
- tools/templates/react-native.md documents a generator that is not registered in tools/generators/generators.json (the doc admits it).
- monorepo/PWA.md is a link dump; there is no `vite-plugin-pwa` or webmanifest wiring anywhere in the repo.
- docs/Post_Install.md is 12 lines with ZERO inbound references and duplicates setup.sh output.
- monorepo/local-services-and-ports.md is framed entirely around Caddy; there is no Caddyfile in the repo. The port table is still worth keeping.
- packages/openthrottle-showroom contains only `output/` — no `src/`, no PIPELINE.md — so docs/marketing/{pipeline,episode-format,writing}.md link to files that do not exist. Showroom plan `2cef373a` is still PENDING.

## Sequencing

Task 1 first (it sets the convention the flatten tasks apply). After that every task is independent except: task 6 must land before task 11 (it folds the learnings doc before deletion), and task 10 folds AGENT_INPUTS content into AGENT_USAGE before deleting it. Task 13 is blocked on showroom plan `2cef373a`. Delete tasks are capped at 3 files each so they can be trickled into separate branches.
summary: Audit of all 80 markdown files under docs/ on main. Convert implemented decision records into plain present-tense state, delete plan/audit artifacts that carry no usage guidance, merge duplicates, and add an index gate so the drift does not recur.
title: Docs de-drift: flatten decision trees to state, delete plan artifacts

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`pnpm audit:component-shape:strict` (the R4/R5 component primitive-shape gate) runs today only at **pre-push** (`.husky/pre-push`) and in **CI** (`.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml`, step "🧱 Component primitive-shape audit"). Agents working through Ralph/loop iterations **commit after every task** (`/github/commit`) but only push occasionally — so a shape violation isn't surfaced until much later, after many commits have piled on top of it. We want this audit to behave like the linter: it must pass to successfully **commit**, not just to push.

## Goal

Add the strict component-shape audit to the **pre-commit** lifecycle so every commit (human or agent) is gated, keeping pre-commit / pre-push / CI in lockstep on the exact same command.

## Key facts (already verified)

- Command is fast enough for a commit hook: `pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict` runs repo-wide in ~1.35s.
- CI (line 201) and pre-push both run the SAME single command: `pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict` (the authored variant). Neither runs the `:shadcn:strict` variant — only `check:local:component-shape` runs both. **Decision: pre-commit mirrors CI/pre-push = authored strict only.** Do NOT add the shadcn variant to the commit gate (keep the three surfaces on one identical command).
- `.husky/pre-commit` currently runs only `lint-staged`. `.husky/pre-push` already runs the audit with a clear failure message; the new pre-commit block should reuse that exact wording/command.
- The script (`scripts/audit-component-shape.ts`) is **repo-wide** (`globSync`), not staged-file-scoped — same as pre-push/CI. It reads the working tree, so it can flag a violation in a file not part of the current commit. This matches existing pre-push behavior and is acceptable; do not attempt to scope to staged files (would diverge from CI and add fragility).
- Bypass is prohibited by CLAUDE.md: never `--no-verify` / never bypass Husky. Fix the violation instead.

## Non-goals

- Do not change what the audit checks or the R4/R5/R6/R7 rules.
- Do not scope the audit to staged files.
- Do not add the shadcn strict variant to the commit/push gate.

## Rollout note

This will start blocking commits that previously only blocked on push. Confirm the repo is currently green (`pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict` exits 0 on `main`) before enabling, so we don't hand agents/humans an immediately-broken commit gate.
title: Gate commits with the component-shape strict audit (pre-commit lifecycle)

author: visormatt
description:
Port `docs/marketing/scripts/08-promote-task.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

The feature is real and shipped — `PromoteTaskButton.tsx`, `PlanTaskToolbar.tsx`, the `promoteTask` intent on `plans.$planId.tasks.$taskId._index.tsx`, and the `promoteTaskToPlan` mutation in the server schema. But the script describes a synchronous, navigational flow, and the implementation is an asynchronous, queued one. Half the beats need settling before a line of flow code is written.

## Gate 1: promotion is a queued job, not a navigation (beat 0:21)

The script says "The new plan opens; the task's title and description carried over." `PromoteTaskButton` submits the intent, receives a `jobId`, and toasts *"Promotion queued. Job <id>. The new plan appears on the plans list once the job completes."* It calls `revalidator.revalidate()` and closes its dialog. Nothing navigates. The new plan is created by a BullMQ worker some time later.

So the payoff beat has to be either: hold on the toast and then cut to `/plans` where the new plan has arrived (honest, and it teaches that promotion is a job); or navigate to the new plan explicitly once the job lands (needs the flow to poll, and `waitFor` on app state is the only sanctioned way — there is no `sleep` verb and none should be added).

Whichever is chosen, the narration "The task becomes a plan. Title, description, everything comes with it" is still true — `promoteDialogBody` confirms it carries title, description and tags.

## Gate 2: the confirm dialog is missing from the script

Between 0:16 ("Click **Promote to plan**") and 0:21 ("The new plan opens") sits an `AlertDialog` — title "Promote task to a plan?", body explaining that the task is marked SKIPPED and tagged `promoted`, and that this cannot be undone, then a **Promote** confirm button. The script skips it entirely.

It should not be hidden. The dialog is the most honest beat in the short: it states the cost of the operation on screen. Add it to the script as its own beat and re-budget the words.

## Gate 3: there is no link from the promoted task to the new plan (beats 0:31 and 0:41)

The script's second half rests on "the task now shows a link to the new plan" and "Click through the link, back to the new plan", narrated as "Nothing is lost and nothing is duplicated."

Grepping `app/routing/plans` for `promoted` finds only: `TaskDetailRoute.tsx` checking `task.tags.some((tag) => tag.tag === 'promoted')` to disable the button, and the copy strings. The task's only trace of promotion is a status of SKIPPED and a `promoted` tag. There is no stored reference to the created plan and nothing renders a link.

This is the same defect class the pilot caught (a script claiming a commit-link view the app does not have) and the same class as 04's project badge. Decide before task 2 starts:

- Option A — make the link real. The promotion executor knows both ids; persisting the new plan id on the task and rendering a chip on task detail makes the relationship visible in the product, not just in the video, and keeps the script's strongest beats. Largest scope, and it reaches into `queues/plan-rules/promote-task-to-plan.executor.ts` and the schema.
- Option B — rewrite 0:31 and 0:41 around what does exist: the task now reads SKIPPED and carries a `promoted` tag, and the new plan is on the plans list. Cheap, honest, and weaker — "nothing is lost" becomes a claim about a tag.

## Gate 4: the fixture must not disable the button

`PromoteTaskButton` is disabled, with an explanatory tooltip and no dialog, when the task is already promoted, when the parent plan run is QUEUED or IN_PROGRESS (`planIsRunning`), or when the parent plan is COMPLETED / CANCELED / SKIPPED (`planIsTerminal`). The seeded task the flow opens must sit on a plan that is in none of those states, and the fixture ships one pre-baked run — check that it does not put the target plan in a running state at record time.

## What already exists and needs no work

- The task detail route, the toolbar and the promote control all render and are covered by tests (`PromoteTaskButton.test.tsx`, `PlanTaskToolbar.test.tsx`, `TaskDetailRoute.test.tsx`).
- Runner verbs `click`, `highlight`, `scrollTo`, `waitFor`, `waitForUrl`, `dwell` cover every physical action the short needs.
- Beat 0:08 ("Scroll the long description") needs a seeded task whose description genuinely overflows — the fixture already carries long-form task descriptions.

## Constraints

- 61 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; adding the confirm-dialog beat and rewriting 0:21 will move it. Re-validate against `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` and the `short` budget in `docs/marketing/format.json`.
- Selectors must be the same hooks the Maestro E2E flows use. The app must not grow a second parallel set of test hooks.
- The toast is a 9:16 hazard: Sonner renders in a corner and a portrait crop can cut it. Expect `regionOfInterest` work on the payoff beat.
- Promotion is irreversible and mutates the demo database. Re-seed between takes rather than hunting for a fresh task.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.
summary: Port docs/marketing/scripts/08-promote-task.md to a recorded flow, and settle three beats: the confirm dialog the script omits, the async job that never opens the new plan, and the link-back that does not exist.
title: Build the 08-promote-task screencast flow

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`/schedule` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/schedule._index.tsx`) lists scheduled jobs and nothing else. Its loader runs exactly one query — `scheduledAgentJobs` — whose fragment (`ScheduledJobCard`) carries `cronPattern`, `enabled`, `lastRunAt`, `nextRunAt`, `model`, `driverId`, `repository`. There is no notion of *current activity*: a job that is mid-run looks identical to one sitting idle, and the only way to see a run is to open `/schedule/:jobId` and read its run history.

Meanwhile the run data already exists and is rich — `ScheduledAgentJobRunObject` carries `status` (`queued | running | succeeded | no_op | failed | cancelled`), `trigger` (`schedule | manual`), `startedAt`/`finishedAt`, `exitCode`, `errorMessage`, token counts and `costUsd`. The gap is purely query shape: `scheduledAgentJobRuns(scheduledAgentJobId: ID!, limit: Int)` is **per job**, so the index cannot ask "what is in flight right now" without N queries.

## Goal

On `/schedule`, above the table:

1. A **stats row** — at-a-glance counts (in flight, ran today, failures today, schedules enabled) following the house `OpenThrottleStatCard` pattern already used by `PlansStats`, `ProjectsStats` and `PersonasStats`.
2. An **in-flight activity panel** — the runs currently `running` or `queued` across *all* jobs, each with job name, driver/model, trigger, elapsed time, and a cancel affordance (the `cancelScheduledAgentJobRun` mutation already exists).
3. A **per-row running indicator** in `ScheduleTable`, so the list itself shows which schedules are busy.
4. **Live refresh** while anything is in flight, so the panel is actually live rather than a stale snapshot.

## Design constraints

- **New server query required.** Add a cross-job in-flight query plus a small aggregate object. Do not fan out per-job queries from the loader.
- **Run rows need their job's name.** `ScheduledAgentJobRunObject` has `scheduledAgentJobId` but no name. Add a `job` field resolver backed by a new jobs-by-id DataLoader in the existing `ScheduledAgentJobsLoaders` (request-scoped) — do not N+1.
- **No lifecycle subscription exists.** `type Subscription` has per-stream subscriptions only (`queueJobLogTail`, `planOutputChunkAdded`, …); nothing publishes scheduled-run status transitions. v1 uses interval `useRevalidator()` polling (the established pattern in this app — see `SettingsDebugPanel`, `PlanTasksBoard`). A `scheduledAgentJobRunStatusChanged` subscription is a deliberate follow-up, not in scope.
- **Reuse, don't re-derive.** Status colour/label/variant maps live in `app/routing/schedule/data/data.run-status.ts`; duration and relative-time formatting in `app/routing/schedule/utils/format-duration.ts` and `format-when.ts`. `no_op` is amber and is **not** a failure — do not count it as one.
- **Don't break the onboarding path.** `schedule._index.tsx` shows `GlobalFeatureOnboarding` when `jobs.length === 0 && search.length === 0`. Stats and the activity panel must not render for that genuinely-new user, and must not render for a zero-result search either.
- **House rules.** New UI comes from `@tools/generators` (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component …`), keeps the generated section comments, one component per file, copy in `data/data.copy.ts`, no new enums (`as const`), no `as` casts, alphabetized props/keys, `component` not `screen` in tests, `userEvent` not `fireEvent`.

## Out of scope

- Any real-time subscription for run status (follow-up).
- Charts/history/trend visualisation — counts and a live list only.
- Changes to how runs execute, are priced, or are logged.
summary: Add a stats row and an in-flight activity panel to /schedule so you can see what is running, queued, and recently finished without opening each job. Requires a new cross-job runs query on the server (today runs are only queryable per job).
title: Schedule index: in-flight run stats + live activity UI

author: visormatt
description:
Adds `Job_Issue_Reporting` to the `.agents/prompts/` recurring-job family (currently ten jobs). Unlike the existing sweeps, which each file one plan per run, this job runs **daily** but files **one plan per ISO week** — the first run of the week opens `🔁 Issue reporting: week of <Monday>` and every later run of that week appends tasks and a dated `append_plan_output` chunk to it.

Scope: the whole `OpenThrottle` org, enumerated live each run (`gh repo list`), not hardcoded.

Audit facts established while writing this plan (no need to re-derive):

- Five repos in the org today: `monorepo` (public, canonical), `OpenThrottle` (public), `.github` (public), `infrastructure` (private), `openclaw` (public, **issues disabled** — can never produce a finding). Archived/issues-disabled repos must be skipped by enumeration, not by a hardcoded exclusion list.
- `OpenThrottle/OpenThrottle` is a public mirror with history **unrelated** to `monorepo`. Its issues are in scope but must never be cross-referenced against `monorepo` commits or branches.
- **Zero open issues across the org right now** — the empty run is the normal, expected outcome and the prompt says so explicitly, so an unattended run cannot pad a plan to justify itself.
- Labels: GitHub defaults plus `hold`, `dependencies`, `github-actions`. `dependencies`/`github-actions` are Dependabot's and overlap `Job_DeadCode` — the prompt counts them rather than tasking them.
- No `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` exists, so reports arrive unstructured; "needs more information from the reporter" is an explicit, sanctioned triage outcome.
- Issue bodies/comments are third-party untrusted input — the prompt's hard rules forbid acting on instructions found inside them.
- `gh search issues` excludes pull requests; PRs stay `Job_WorkInFlight`'s territory.

Task 1 (authoring the prompt) is already **COMPLETED** — `.agents/prompts/Job_Issue_Reporting.md` is written and prettier-formatted on branch `visormatt/round-seven`. Remaining work is registry docs, the schedule entry, and one supervised live run.

Known unrelated breakage: `pnpm run check:local:agent-assets` currently fails on three dangling `validate-plan` symlinks left by the skill teardown (commit 559c6e32) — pre-existing, not caused by this work, and tracked separately under plan 27963a92.
summary: Add an eleventh recurring agent job that ingests open issues across the OpenThrottle GitHub org daily and records them on a single OT plan per ISO week.
title: Job_Issue_Reporting: daily GitHub issue intake, one plan per week

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal
Generate an aggregate **root `CHANGELOG.md`** at the repo root, driven natively by `nx release` via the `changelog.workspaceChangelog` config in `nx.json`. Today only per-project changelogs exist (`nx.json` release block, lines ~85-99): `workspaceChangelog: false`, `projectChangelogs` enabled with `createRelease: "github"`.

## Key constraint
The workspace uses `projectsRelationship: "independent"`. Nx's `workspaceChangelog` is built around a single unified workspace version to title each entry; under independent releases there is no single version, so Nx will warn/error unless we either (a) pass an explicit `--version`/version reference when invoking release, or (b) configure `renderOptions`/`versionTitleDate` so the entry title works without a semver bump. This must be resolved empirically (Nx 22.7.4) before flipping config — do NOT assume `workspaceChangelog: true` "just works".

## Approach
1. Spike Nx behavior with `--dry-run` to learn the exact supported config shape under independent projects.
2. Configure `changelog.workspaceChangelog` as an object (file: `CHANGELOG.md`, renderOptions, and a deliberate `createRelease` decision to avoid duplicate GitHub releases now that project changelogs already create them).
3. Seed the baseline root file and verify generation.
4. Wire into the release/CI flow so the root CHANGELOG is committed as part of the release commit.
5. Document + validate (`check:local`, no codegen/lint drift).

## Out of scope
- Switching projectsRelationship to fixed/unified.
- Replacing per-project changelogs.
- Custom conventional-changelog/git-cliff tooling (explicitly rejected in favor of Nx-native).
summary: Enable and configure Nx release workspaceChangelog to generate an aggregate root CHANGELOG.md, working around the independent-projects caveat, without breaking existing per-project changelogs or GitHub releases.
title: Hook up a root-level CHANGELOG via Nx workspaceChangelog

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

`@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` has grown to ~60 exported component groups across 453 `.tsx` files and is consumed by every React Router app in the monorepo. There is currently no way to browse it, exercise a component's variants, or see the theme registry applied across the library. Every visual check today requires booting a consuming application.

## Decisions already made

- **Engine: Storybook 10 + `@storybook/react-vite`.** Verified against the registry on 2026-08-16: `storybook@10.5.8`, released ~weekly. `@storybook/react-vite` peer-declares `vite: ^5 || ^6 || ^7 || ^8` and React `^19`, matching the workspace (Vite `^8.0.5`, React `19.2.4`, TS `~6.0.3`). Post-SB9 consolidation the footprint is small: core ~17 deps, `react-vite` ~9.
- **Rejected — Ladle:** `@ladle/react@5.1.1`, last published 2025-11-04 (~9 months stale). Bundles its own Vite, a real conflict risk against Vite 8 + `@tailwindcss/vite`. Thin on autodocs/controls.
- **Rejected — home-grown catalog** on `@openthrottle/react-router-docs` + `react-router-markdown`: zero new deps and a perfect convention fit, but would rebuild props tables (still needs `react-docgen`), controls, and a11y, and become permanently owned surface area.
- **Scope: docs-only for v1.** No Vitest/browser story-test runner, no visual regression, no a11y addon. Deliberately deferred to a follow-up plan once stories exist to test against.
- **Hosting: local dev only for v1.** Build the nx targets so a later static deploy is a small follow-up, but ship no deploy wiring.
- **Coverage: generator + tiered backfill.** Story sub-generator first, curated tier-1 hand-authored as the quality bar, tail backfilled in later batches.

## Key findings that shape the implementation

1. **The shadcn package is router-free.** `react-router` appears in `packages/react-router-shadcn/src` only inside `__tests__` (Sidebar's `createRoutesStub`) and is not a package dependency. The host therefore needs no React Router framework — plain React + Vite via `@storybook/react-vite`.
2. **Stories were already anticipated.** `packages/react-router-shadcn/eslint.config.ts` already excludes `**/*.stories.tsx` from the `openthrottle/component-primitive-shape` rule. This settles placement: **stories are co-located next to components inside the package**; the workbench app is a thin Storybook host only. Consequence: the package gains a `storybook` devDependency.
3. **Themes are already a data registry.** `src/themes/registry.ts`, `theme-contract.ts`, and `build-theme-stylesheet.ts` (plus `CURSOR_THEMES`) mean a theme toolbar is data-driven and cheap. This is the single highest-value feature of the workbench — there is no way to view the library across themes today.
4. **Docs come nearly free.** Components export real prop interfaces (`ButtonProps extends BaseProps, ButtonVariants`) and use `cva` variant maps with `data-slot`/`data-variant`, so `react-docgen` yields genuine API tables and variants convert directly into controls with no annotation work.
5. **`@nx/storybook` is probably unnecessary.** `@nx/storybook@22.7.4` exists and matches workspace Nx exactly, but targets in this repo are hand-declared in `package.json` `nx.targets` against `nx.json` `targetDefaults`. Prefer two hand-declared targets over the plugin dependency; only adopt the plugin if hand-wiring proves painful.

## Workspace frictions to respect

- **`catalogMode: strict`** — every new Storybook dependency must be added to the `catalog:` block in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; enforced by `pnpm run check:catalog`.
- **`minimumReleaseAge: 10080` (7 days)** — resolution lands ~one week behind latest (today that is `10.5.7`, not `10.5.8`). Expected, not a problem, but do not fight it.
- **Knip** — `*.stories.tsx` are not reachable from `src/index.ts` and will be reported as unused files unless added to `entry` or `ignore` in `knip.jsonc`.
- **Tailwind v4** is CSS-first: the preview must `@import 'tailwindcss'` before the package's `index.css`, matching the contract documented in that file.

## Out of scope (candidate follow-up plans)

- Story-based browser/interaction testing via the Storybook Vitest addon — would directly attack known jsdom gaps (Recharts geometry, Sidebar).
- Visual regression / snapshot diffing.
- `@storybook/addon-a11y`.
- Static build deployment (internal or public).
- Extending the workbench beyond `react-router-shadcn` to other `react-router-*` packages.
summary: Stand up a standalone Nx application (applications/openthrottle-workbench) running Storybook 10 + @storybook/react-vite as the browse-and-interact surface for @openthrottle/react-router-shadcn. Docs-only scope for v1; stories co-located in the package; a story sub-generator plus a curated tier-1 backfill.
title: Component workbench: Storybook 10 host for @openthrottle/react-router-shadcn

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Upgrade the Run-skill modal (from the "Run a skill from the /skills/:slug detail route" plan, id `0cd89ddc-158d-4ce1-8140-551ee7b2eeb7`) from a single free-text **Arguments** box to **typed, per-argument form fields** derived from the skill's own declaration. When a skill declares arguments, render one labeled field per argument (respecting type / required / description / default); when it declares none, fall back to the v1 free-text field.

## Important framing (spec reality)

The user's expectation was that arguments "would already be present" because OT skills follow the Agent Skills spec (https://agentskills.io/specification). **That spec does NOT define a first-class `arguments`/`inputs` field.** Its frontmatter is only: `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (an arbitrary string→string map), and experimental `allowed-tools`. So there is nothing typed to parse today.

This plan therefore has a **design decision as task 1**: pick the source of truth for argument declarations. Options (pick one, spec-compatible first):

1. **`metadata` convention (spec-compatible).** Store an args schema under a namespaced `metadata` key, e.g. `metadata.openthrottle-arguments` = a JSON/YAML string of `[{ name, type, required, description, default, enum }]`. Stays 100% within the spec (metadata is free-form string→string). Slightly awkward (stringified schema).
2. **OT frontmatter extension.** Add a top-level `arguments:` block to SKILL.md frontmatter and teach the OT parser to read it. Cleaner authoring, but a superset of the spec (non-portable; other tools ignore it).
3. **Parse from the body.** Heuristically extract an "Arguments"/"Inputs" section from the markdown body. Rejected as fragile unless a strict convention is enforced — note but don't build.

Recommendation to evaluate: option 1 (metadata convention) for spec-fidelity, with a small typed helper so authoring is still ergonomic. Confirm with the owner before building parser + UI.

## Scope

- Extend the skill frontmatter parser (`packages/openthrottle-skills/src/parse-skill-frontmatter.ts` — add a typed `arguments` field; no new enums, use `as const` for the arg-type union) and thread it onto `RepoSkillEntry` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/agents/data/repo-skills-registry.ts`) and any GraphQL surface if the parsed args need to reach the client that way (the skill route loader is filesystem-based, so it can likely pass parsed args directly).
- Render dynamic fields in `RunSkillDialog` / `useRunSkillDialog`: one control per declared argument (text / number / boolean / enum-select), with required-validation feeding `submitDisabled`.
- Compose the invocation string from the structured values (define the encoding: positional vs `--flag value`; match how skills actually consume args at invocation — verify against the harness/skill-invocation path, not assumed).
- Keep the free-text fallback for skills with no declared arguments (v1 behavior).
- Add a couple of OT skills' declarations as reference/dogfood examples once the convention is chosen.

## Constraints / conventions

- Do not break the v1 modal contract — this is additive.
- Follow the same conventions as the base plan: generators-first for any new components, section comments, one-component-per-file, `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` controls, avoid `as`/`any`, `import type`, explicit return types.
- If a GraphQL type gains an `arguments` field, deprecate rather than break, run codegen, commit `__generated__`.
- Tests: parser unit tests (valid/invalid/absent declarations) + render-level Vitest for dynamic field rendering + required-validation + invocation-string composition.

## Dependencies

Blocked on the base plan `0cd89ddc-158d-4ce1-8140-551ee7b2eeb7` landing (needs the modal + `useRunSkillDialog` to exist).
title: Follow-up: Parse & render structured skill arguments in the Run-skill modal

author: visormatt
description:
Worktree setup (env reset, port remap, compose isolation, secret sync, install, build) currently only runs when a worktree is created through a tool-specific hook: Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` WorktreeCreate hook (→ scripts/create_worktree.sh → scripts/setup_worktree.sh) or Cursor's `.cursor/worktrees.json` (→ scripts/setup_worktree.sh). A plain `git worktree add` (human at terminal, CI, another agent, a future editor) runs NOTHING — git has no native post-worktree-add hook. That gap produces stale/placeholder .env and login-type symptoms (e.g. the "default password too short" report).

Key finding: setup_worktree.sh does NOT seed the DB user/password, and neither does setup.sh. The default login user password (FullThrottle2026!) is set only by the separate, manual `pnpm database:bootstrap-default-user` (package.json:454). Worktrees deliberately SHARE the main checkout's Postgres/Redis, so the seeded user normally already exists — meaning the observed symptom is most likely an unconfigured worktree (.env never set up) or an unseeded shared DB, not something setup_worktree.sh would fix on its own.

Goal: make worktree provisioning "when we create a worktree we…" instead of "when Claude creates a worktree we…". Approach: (1) promote scripts/create_worktree.sh to a single tool-agnostic entrypoint that every consumer calls; (2) add an idempotent lazy self-heal guard on the dev entrypoint so any creation path is caught on first use; (3) resolve default-user seeding (guarded seed vs documented shared-DB dependency); (4) update docs. setup_worktree.sh is already idempotent, which makes the self-heal safe.
title: Tool-agnostic git worktree setup (single entrypoint + self-heal)

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

Google is deprecating the Gemini CLI on **2026-06-18** for consumer tiers (AI Pro/Ultra + free Code Assist); enterprise licenses and API-key usage continue. The replacement is the **Antigravity CLI**: binary `agy`, a ground-up Go rewrite, installed via `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash` to `~/.local/bin/agy` (~50 MB tar.gz, self-updates in the background — no npm/brew distribution). Google states there will NOT be 1:1 feature parity with the Gemini CLI at launch; extensions carry over as "plugins", Agent Skills/Hooks/Subagents are said to remain compatible.

## Approach

Add `agy` as a **new, independent driver** (`antigravity`) next to the six existing drivers — do NOT modify or remove the `gemini` driver; it keeps working (enterprise indefinitely, consumer until June 2026) and can be cut away later. All behavioral differences are absorbed at our existing choke points:

1. Driver definition: `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/` (registry pattern — one file, ~80-100 lines, mirrors `gemini.ts` / `codex.ts`).
2. Conversation backend: `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/` (argv builder + stream event mapper, mirrors the `gemini/` dir).

## Hard gate

None of the Gemini driver's verified assumptions survive the Go rewrite (flags, stdin EOF behavior, exit codes, auth env vars, MCP config location, stream-json schema). Task 1 is a verification dossier with an explicit **GO/NO-GO**: if `agy` has no headless one-shot mode with structured/parsable output yet, the plan blocks there — there is nothing to build against until Google ships one.

## References

- Prior art: Gemini CLI driver plan 99541038 (PR #438) — same effort shape.
- Existing dossier pattern: `docs/openthrottle/gemini-stream-json-schema.md`.
- Deprecation announcement: https://developers.googleblog.com/an-important-update-transitioning-gemini-cli-to-antigravity-cli/
- Download/installer: https://antigravity.google/download
summary: DONE — draft PR #440. Antigravity CLI (agy) added as a seventh driver with a wired streaming chat backend, alongside an untouched gemini driver. Verified live against agy 1.1.21 (plan-run shell, chat streaming, id-based resume, discovery). Live runs caught 3 bugs unit tests could not: `-p` takes the prompt as its value, `--add-dir` is required or agy writes to a scratch project instead of cwd, and `agy models` is tab-separated. Work-ledger artifact owed on merge.
title: Antigravity CLI (agy) agent driver

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The chat message list scrolls to the bottom on *every* new message, which is jarring during streaming.

Root cause (confirmed in code): the auto-scroll effect in [`packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatThread.tsx:65`](packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatThread.tsx) has dependency array `[messages]` (line 82) and calls `endRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' })` on every change of the `messages` array identity. In the true-streaming path (developer + admin apps) `messagesView` returns a **new array on every stream chunk** (see `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useAgenticChatTurn.tsx` `messagesView` memo, ~lines 132-148), so the smooth scroll re-fires on every streamed token — continuous, jarring motion.

## Desired behavior

Scroll to bottom only at two moments:
1. **User sends a message** — a new `role: 'user'` message is appended.
2. **First response token of a turn** — the in-flight assistant message transitions from empty/`pending` to its first non-empty content (streaming start). Fire once per assistant turn, not on subsequent tokens.

Bonus (already partially present, keep it): if the user has scrolled up (more than `NEAR_BOTTOM_THRESHOLD_PX` = 64px from the bottom), do not yank them back — respect their scroll position for the response scroll.

## Why this is a one-file change

Every chat surface renders the single shared `ChatThread` and passes `messages` (streaming `messagesView` or non-streaming appended array): developer home (`HomeComposer`), developer header (`useHeaderChatController`), admin app parity copies, and the packaged `ChatDialog` (non-streaming `useChatTurnFetcher`, which appends the whole assistant message once on completion). The scroll decision is entirely internal to `ChatThread` via refs (`isNearBottomRef`, `hasRenderedRef`) — no props. Changing the effect logic fixes all surfaces at once.

## Design (self-contained in ChatThread — start simple)

Replace the `[messages]`-identity trigger with event detection derived from `messages`, using refs to compare against the previous render:

- **New user message:** track the last message / user-message identity; when a newly appended message has `role: 'user'`, scroll to bottom **always** and set `isNearBottomRef.current = true` (we just jumped to the bottom).
- **First assistant content:** keep a `firstResponseScrolledIdRef`. Find the latest assistant message; when it first has non-empty `body`/`events` (i.e. `pending` cleared / streaming started) **and** its `id !== firstResponseScrolledIdRef.current`, scroll (respecting `isNearBottomRef`) and record its id. Subsequent tokens grow the body but the id already matches → no re-scroll.
- **Keep** the first-paint jump (`behavior: 'auto'` on `!hasRenderedRef.current`) for bulk history hydration, the empty-thread early return, and the existing `handleScroll` near-bottom detection.

This satisfies both required scroll points and gives the "respect user scroll" bonus for free via the existing `isNearBottomRef`. It also covers the non-streaming `ChatDialog` path: user append → scroll; whole assistant message appears with content → first-response scroll fires once.

## Rejected / deferred alternative

Threading explicit `onUserSubmit` / `streamingStarted` signals down from `useAgenticChatTurn` into `ChatThread` as props. More precise but touches both apps' hooks and both surface controllers — deferred; the ref-derived approach keeps the blast radius to one component and its test.

## Key files

- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatThread.tsx` — the effect (lines 65-82) + refs (44-47) + `handleScroll` (52-60). Primary change.
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/__tests__/ChatThread.test.tsx` — asserts current scroll-on-change behavior (lines ~151-176); must be updated.
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/types.ts` — `ChatMessage` (`role`, `body`, `events`, `pending`) is the signal source.
- Integration check surfaces: `applications/openthrottle-developer` home + header, `applications/openthrottle-admin` parity, packaged `ChatDialog`.
summary: Stop the chat thread from smooth-scrolling on every streamed token/array change. Scroll to bottom only when the user sends a message and when the first assistant token of a turn arrives; keep the existing near-bottom guard so a user who has scrolled up is not yanked back. Change is centralized in packages/react-router-chat ChatThread — all surfaces inherit it.
title: Chat auto-scroll: only on user send and first response

author: visormatt
description:
Large cleanup of markdown documentation before the repo goes public.

Goal: strip historical "how we got here" material from the repo so public readers see accurate usage and onboarding docs — not investigation notes, design spikes, mid-flight ADRs, or migration archaeology.

Approach:
1. Inventory everything under `docs/` (~157 files) plus root markdown (README, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, MONOREPO, VISION, etc.).
2. Classify each doc as KEEP (usage/onboarding/contributor essentials), ARCHIVE (historical journey — design spikes, investigation notes, brainstorms, obsolete runbooks), or DELETE (true dead weight with no personal archival value).
3. Move ARCHIVE docs out of the repo into a folder on the author's desktop (e.g. `~/Desktop/openthrottle-docs-archive/`) — not another git-tracked `docs/archive/` folder. Commit the removals from the repo.
4. While classifying and editing KEEP docs, verify correctness against current code/commands (Nx targets, MCP registration, local run paths, env vars).
5. Improve the KEEP set: clear entry points for first-time users, honest prerequisites, working copy-paste commands, and a short navigation map from README → onboarding → usage.

Out of scope for this plan: rewriting agent skills/rules (unless a removed doc is the only source they link to — then fix the link or inline the needed bit). Legal/license markdown stays.

Success criteria:
- Repo docs are oriented to usage + onboarding + contributor essentials.
- Historical material lives on the desktop archive, not in git.
- Remaining docs have been correctness-checked; broken links from removals are fixed.
- README (and related entry points) make the public path obvious.
title: Pre-public markdown docs cleanup

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`/settings/repositories` renders a two-level tree (`buildRepositoryRows`, `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/repositories/utils/rows.ts`): a repository's `kind='primary'` checkout is a parent row and its `kind='worktree'` checkouts hang off it as children. Those child rows only exist when a `repository_checkouts` row exists, and today that happens in exactly two places:

- `PlanRunWorktreeCheckoutService` -> `RepositoryCheckoutsService.upsertWorktreeCheckout` (server-provisioned plan runs), and
- `workspace-folders.service.ts:557`, when a user explicitly adds a folder whose inspection says `git.isLinkedWorktree`.

So every worktree created outside the server — `pnpm run worktree:new <name>` run by hand, by a Claude/Cursor session, or by the ot-claude-loop — is invisible on the page even though it is the worktree the user is actively working in.

Migration 097 added `user_workspace_settings.worktree_root`: "the one directory every agent creates git worktrees under", already surfaced on `/settings/workspace` (`SettingsWorkspaceWorktreeRootForm`) and already forwarded to `scripts/create_worktree.sh` as `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` by `PlanRunWorktreeProvisionService`. That gives us a reliable place to look, so the page can show what is actually on disk.

## Goal

`/settings/repositories` shows every worktree that exists on disk for the user's repositories, whether or not OpenThrottle created it, with an honest activity signal, and lets the user register one with a single action. Read-only with respect to git: v1 never creates, prunes, or deletes a worktree.

## Design decisions (settled — implement these, don't re-litigate)

**1. Two discovery sources, unioned and deduped by resolved real path.**

- *Per-repository, authoritative:* `git worktree list --porcelain` from each registered primary checkout. The parser already exists (`RepositoryInspectionService.parseLinkedWorktrees`, surfaced as `inspection.git.linkedWorktrees`) but that snapshot is a cache keyed on `scannedAt` and goes stale; discovery must run live rather than read the cached snapshot.
- *Root scan, catches the rest:* shallow (depth 1) scan of the resolved worktree root for immediate child directories whose `.git` is a **file** pointer (the `isLinkedWorktree` test the inspection service already uses). For each hit, `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` resolves the owning repository so it can be attached to the right parent row — this is what catches worktrees whose base checkout is not registered, or whose primary lives outside the workspace roots.

Dedupe on `realpathSync` so a symlinked root and a direct path are one row, matching how `browseDirectory` already resolves roots.

**2. Root resolution is a single shared ladder.** `scripts/create_worktree.sh` resolves the root as: `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` env -> `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the primary checkout's `.env` -> sibling `openthrottle-worktrees` directory. The settings value feeds rung 1 via the provisioning service. Extract that ladder (settings value included) into ONE resolver consumed by both `PlanRunWorktreeProvisionService` and the new discovery service, so the page can never disagree with where the script actually writes. Any divergence here is the bug this plan is most likely to introduce.

**3. "In progress" is defined, never inferred from a directory existing.** Each discovered worktree gets one activity state:

- `RUNNING` — an `IN_PROGRESS` `plan_runs` row whose `checkout_id` resolves to this path *and* whose `heartbeat_at` is inside the staleness cutoff (the liveness contract from the heartbeat/staleness work — a stale IN_PROGRESS row is dead, not running).
- `DIRTY` — no live run, but `git status --porcelain` is non-empty or the branch is ahead of its upstream/base.
- `IDLE` — clean, no live run.

A worktree with no `repository_checkouts` row is additionally flagged `unregistered`; that flag is orthogonal to activity (an unregistered worktree can be DIRTY).

**4. Bounded and non-fatal.** Depth-1 scan only; per-path `git` calls get an explicit timeout and `maxBuffer`; a hard cap on discovered worktrees with the overflow reported rather than silently truncated; every failure becomes a warning on the payload (the pattern `RepositoryInspectionService` already uses), never a thrown resolver error. Discovery must not be able to make the page hang or 500 — if the root is missing or unreadable, the table renders exactly as it does today plus a warning.

**5. Path containment.** `browseDirectory` refuses paths outside the configured workspace roots. The worktree root is frequently a sibling *outside* those roots, so discovery is allowed to read the resolved root — but only the resolved root, never a client-supplied path. No new user-controlled path parameter is introduced.

**6. Scope.** In: discovery, activity classification, GraphQL surface, table rows/badges, "register this worktree" via the existing `addWorkspaceFolder` mutation, refresh, docs. Out: creating a worktree from the UI, `git worktree prune`, deleting a worktree directory (destructive — separate plan), and any change to how runs pick their worktree.

## Verification

Unit tests at every layer (mocked `execFile`/`fs` for discovery, fixture rows for the UI). Live browser verification of authed settings pages is blocked in this workspace (fresh users have zero permissions and login needs a password), so the UI gate is render-level Vitest on the table plus a `check:local`-parity run, not a Playwright pass.
summary: Discover git worktrees from the workspace worktree_root (migration 097) plus `git worktree list`, classify each as running/dirty/idle, and show them as children in the /settings/repositories table — including ones OpenThrottle never provisioned.
title: Surface in-progress worktrees on /settings/repositories from the configured worktree root

author: visormatt
description:
# Goal

Permanently stop the recurring `NX  The workspace is out of sync … [@nx/js:typescript-sync] … Run 'nx sync'` hard-fail that blocks `pnpm nx run <proj>:{typecheck,test,lint}` in non-interactive shells (fresh worktrees especially), so a worktree is usable immediately without a manual `nx sync` dance. This is a sibling to OT c9545bb0 (tool-agnostic worktree *provisioning*); that plan fixes stale `.env`, this one fixes the Nx sync gate.

# Root cause (verified 2026-08-07)

1. The custom Nx plugin `tools/nx-plugins/package-typecheck.ts:126` re-attaches `syncGenerators: ['@nx/js:typescript-sync']` to the `typecheck` target (it owns the target because `@nx/js`'s built-in typecheck is disabled). So the sync gate fires on `typecheck` for every `{applications,packages,tools}/*` project.
2. `nx.json` has only `sync: { applyChanges: true }` — no `disabledTaskSyncGenerators`. `applyChanges` auto-applies **only in an interactive TTY** (and silently in CI); a plain Bash/worktree shell has no TTY, so Nx errors out *before running the target*.
3. The generator's output cannot be trusted: on Nx 22.7.4 it injects phantom cross-references BETWEEN the 4 React Router apps (developer/website/admin → email, admin → developer) — `type: static` graph edges backed by NO import / tsconfig ref / paths entry, unstable across runs. Upstream defect: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/issues/36297. Applying them writes bogus refs into the apps' `tsconfig.json` and BREAKS their `typecheck`. So `nx sync` is never a safe remedy for this workspace.

Net: the sync generator provides negative value here (it can only produce noise or breakage), yet it gates every typecheck. The durable fix is to stop letting it gate targets, reconcile the small set of REAL tsconfig-reference drifts by hand one time, and replace auto-sync with a non-blocking check + manual discipline.

# Recommended approach

**Disable the `@nx/js:typescript-sync` task-sync generator globally** via committed `nx.json`:

```json
"sync": {
  "applyChanges": true,
  "disabledTaskSyncGenerators": ["@nx/js:typescript-sync"]
}
```

Critical distinction: `disabledTaskSyncGenerators` disables ONLY the tsconfig-reference sync gate. It does **NOT** touch `@nx/js.analyzeSourceFiles`, so the project-graph edges that drive `nx affected` and build ordering remain intact. This is fundamentally different from the previously ruled-out `analyzeSourceFiles: false` (which drops ~85 real edges). This exact edit has been used repeatedly as an *uncommitted temporary* workaround with no side effects — this plan makes it permanent and cleans up the fallout it papered over.

Trade-off accepted: tsconfig `references` are now maintained manually (they already are, de-facto — policy is already "NEVER run nx sync"). We compensate with a one-time reconcile of real drift + an optional non-gating check so genuine drift is still visible without blocking work.

# Out of scope
- Worktree `.env` / DB seeding (OT c9545bb0).
- Upgrading Nx past the bug (large, uncertain; revisit only if the bug is fixed upstream).
title: Squash "workspace is out of sync" (@nx/js:typescript-sync gate) for frictionless worktrees

author: visormatt
description:
# Page title audit + cleanup across openthrottle-developer routes

## Problem

`document.title` across `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes` was never curated. Titles were emitted by the `@tools/generators:react-router` route template and mostly left as generated, so several routes ship raw PascalCase scaffold identifiers straight to the browser tab. The reported example:

- `app/routes/settings.appearance.tsx` → `SettingsAppearance | OpenThrottle`

That is not a one-off. A sweep of all 191 route files (79 with a `meta` export) found four distinct defect classes plus a root cause.

## Root cause

`tools/generators/src/generators/react-router/files/route/__name__.tsx:24`:

```ts
export const meta = (_args: Route.MetaArgs) => {
  return [{ title: `<%= namePascal %> | ${SITE_TITLE}` }];
};
```

The template interpolates `namePascal` — the flat-route filename converted to Pascal case — as the human-facing title. Every route scaffolded and not hand-edited inherits a machine identifier as its tab title. Fixing the routes without fixing the template guarantees the defect returns with the next generated route.

## Inventory of defects

Baseline: `SITE_TITLE = 'OpenThrottle'` (`app/global/config/settings.ts:4`); root fallback is `Welcome | OpenThrottle` (`app/root.tsx:290`). Most routes wrap meta in `mergeRouteModuleMeta` from `@openthrottle/react-router-utils`.

### Class A — raw scaffold identifiers (4 routes)

| Route | Current title |
| --- | --- |
| `settings.appearance.tsx` | `SettingsAppearance` |
| `notifications._index.tsx` | `NotificationsIndex` |
| `personas.create.tsx` | `PersonasCreate` |
| `plans.temp.tsx` | `TEMP` |

### Class B — missing title, silently falls back to `Welcome | OpenThrottle` (5 UI routes)

`ide.files.tsx`, `ide.semantic.tsx`, `ide.symbol.tsx`, `ide.symbols.tsx`, and `docs.tsx` (pathless layout — verify children always override before treating it as a defect).

Correctly excluded as non-UI resource routes: `resources.*` (11 files), `robots[.]txt.tsx`, `auth.logout.tsx`, `auth.ws-token.tsx`, `skills.autocomplete.tsx`.

### Class C — inconsistent hierarchy, worst inside `/settings`

Three competing conventions coexist:

- parent-first: `Settings | Debug`, `Settings | Logs`
- leaf-first: `Repositories | Settings`
- no section segment: `Agents`, `Keys`, `Rollout`, `MCP connectors`, `Workspace settings`

`settings.application.tsx` also emits bare `Settings`, colliding with `settings._index.tsx`. Same collision on `calendar._index.tsx` and `calendar.list.tsx` (both `Calendar`).

### Class D — inconsistent capitalization and detail-page phrasing

- Title Case vs sentence case: `Create Prompt` and `Pull Requests` against `Create plan`, `Create note`, `Create event`, `Agent search`.
- `Event Details`, `Note Details`, `Plan Details`, `Project Details` use Title Case plus a `Details` suffix, while `Scheduled job` / `MCP connector` do not.
- `skills.$slug.tsx` renders the raw URL slug rather than the loaded skill name, unlike sibling detail routes (`plans.$planId._index.tsx`, `projects.$projectId._index.tsx`, `pull-requests.$prId.tsx`) which prefer loader data and fall back to a generic label.

### Class E — no `description` meta anywhere

Every `meta` in the app returns a title only. Out of scope for this plan; noted so a follow-up can decide whether descriptions are worth adding.

## Approach

1. Write down the convention first, in one place, so the fix is checkable rather than taste-by-route.
2. Fix the generator template, so new routes are born correct.
3. Apply the convention to the routes, in defect-class batches.
4. Add a lightweight guard so a PascalCase or missing title cannot land again silently.

## Proposed convention (task 1 ratifies or replaces this)

- Format: `<Leaf> | <Section> | OpenThrottle`, section segment only where a section exists (`/settings/*`, `/skills/*`, `/queues/*`). Leaf-first, matching the existing majority and the `handle.breadcrumb` order already used in these route modules.
- Sentence case for actions and generic labels (`Create prompt`, not `Create Prompt`); preserve proper nouns and established product capitalization (`MCP`, `IDE`, `FAQ`, `OpenThrottle`).
- Detail routes prefer the loaded entity name, falling back to a generic singular label with no `Details` suffix — `Plan | Plans | OpenThrottle`, not `Plan Details`.
- Every user-visible route sets a title; resource routes deliberately do not.
- Where a route already has a `*_COPY.pageTitle` constant (`rules._index`, `schedule._index`, `skills.availability`, `skills.vocabulary`), keep sourcing the title from copy data per the component/data file boundary rule, and fix the copy constant instead of the route.

## Out of scope

- Adding `description` / OpenGraph meta (Class E).
- Reworking `handle.breadcrumb` strings or in-page `GlobalHeading` copy, except where a title reads directly from a shared copy constant.
- Titles in the other three React Router apps (`openthrottle-admin`, `openthrottle-email`, `openthrottle-website`) — same audit likely applies, but keep this plan to one app.

## Validation

Per task, then once at the end:

```
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test
```

Only two existing tests assert on `meta(...)`, so route titles are effectively uncovered — task 6 closes that gap. Run Nx targets sequentially, not in parallel (shared Nx cache).
title: Page title audit + cleanup across openthrottle-developer routes

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal
Fill missing co-located specs in **applications/openthrottle-developer** — the largest gap surfaced by the test-coverage audit (plan 2e227f88). Scope: 182 enforced-category files missing a spec (routes 18, components 74, hooks 28, utils 62) plus 83 informational (config/data).

## Source of truth
- Baseline inventory: `docs/monorepo/test-coverage-baseline.json` (filter `project == applications/openthrottle-developer`, `status in {missing, stub}`). Regenerate: `pnpm run audit:test-coverage:json > docs/monorepo/test-coverage-baseline.json`.
- Contract + conventions: `docs/monorepo/test-coverage-audit.md`.

## How to fill a gap
Scaffold from the generator starting point rather than hand-writing:
- components → `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component ...` (or `react` component)
- hooks → `--subGenerator=hook`
- routes → `--subGenerator=route|route-api|table|modal|form`
- utils → `@tools/generators:react --subGenerator=util` (no react-router util template — hand-author following that react util template shape)
- config/data are **informational** (never gated); most are static content — cover case-by-case, don't force conformance where a spec would only restate a `const`.

Verify a filled category with `pnpm run audit:test-coverage -- --categories=<cat>` and `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test`.

## Follow-up (not this plan)
Once a category's gap is fully closed, flip it to strict: drop `test-coverage` from the negative-lookahead in the `audit:strict` script and mirror the gate into the husky three-surface pattern (see the audit doc).
summary: Fill the co-located spec gap in openthrottle-developer (182 enforced + 83 informational missing) surfaced by audit:test-coverage.
title: Test coverage remediation: openthrottle-developer

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Observability into which agent skills actually get used, how often, in what context — across BOTH skills we author (skills/ → .agents/skills, tracked in skills-lock.json) and skills we do NOT control (vercel:*, engineering:*, anthropic-skills:*, etc.).

## Key design decision: instrument the harness, not the skill

Every skill — ours and third-party alike — is invoked through the **`Skill` tool**. So a **`PreToolUse` hook matching `Skill`** captures all of them with zero per-skill code, INCLUDING auto-triggered (description-match) invocations that a manual approach can never see.

**Rejected alternative:** a `/skill-tracking <name>` skill embedded in each of our skills. Rejected because it (a) only ever sees skills we author — the exact gap this plan must close, (b) misses auto-triggered invocations, (c) adds token overhead per skill, (d) is one forgotten edit from a blind spot. It survives only as optional depth-enrichment for our own skills (see final task), layered on top of the hook baseline, never as the primary mechanism.

Hooks are already proven in this repo — see the `WorktreeCreate` hook in `.claude/settings.json`.

## Data captured (decided)

Name + metadata + **truncated** args: `{ timestamp, skill_name, args (truncated/redacted), session_id, cwd, git_branch, scope: ours|third-party }`. Scope is derived by looking the skill name up against `skills-lock.json` / `skills/`.

The privacy level (name-only → truncated → full args) is deliberately abstracted so it can become a configurable knob — tracked as a SEPARATE OT plan (future/paid-feature track). This plan ships with truncated-args as the fixed default.

## Open unknowns the spike MUST settle (do not assume)

1. **Subagent coverage** — do `PreToolUse` hooks fire for `Skill` calls made INSIDE subagents (Ralph / Workflow fan-out)? If not, that's a real coverage gap to name loudly.
2. **Privacy/retention** — confirm truncation/redaction rules and a retention window before args ever hit Postgres.
3. **Sink of record** — local JSONL as fallback; OT server as system of record.

## Phased delivery

- Phase 0: Spike — prove the mechanism + payload, settle unknowns.
- Phase 1: Local JSONL capture hook (MVP, zero infra).
- Phase 2: OT server table + ingest mutation; hook posts fail-open (falls back to JSONL).
- Phase 3: Surface in Developer UI (Skills / Usage route), mirroring the token-usage capture pattern (commit e51ebb8e, Usage route, OT a55b76ba).

## Prior art to mirror

Token usage capture/persistence/surfacing (commit e51ebb8e; OT plan a55b76ba) and the existing Skills detail route (OT 6c785a74) are the closest patterns — same server→codegen→UI shape.
summary: Harness PreToolUse/UserPromptExpansion capture → local JSONL fail-open → OT skill_usage_events + aggregation → Developer Usage UI. Phase 4 adds opt-in outcome enrichment for authored skills only; hook remains primary.
title: Skill usage tracking — harness-hook capture → OT persistence → Developer UI

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

OT's real value downstream is its curated skill set (create-readme, ot-plans, the nx-*/openthrottle-* skills, etc.). But when OT drives an agent in a **foreign workspace** — any checkout outside the OT monorepo, e.g. `ssm-data-pipeline` in the reference screenshot — those skills are unavailable. Today the only foreign-workspace handling is a *prompt layer* (`buildForeignWorkspacePromptLayer`, packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/foreign-workspace-context.ts) that does the OPPOSITE of what we now want: it instructs the agent to NOT reference OT `/skills`, generators, or tooling. Result: "OpenThrottle MCP server and /create-readme skill are unavailable here."

## Goal

Make OT's curated skills a **layered, non-mutating, server-scoped** base that gets projected INTO the foreign repo while the OT server is running, reused across runs, and reconciled on shutdown/boot — extending the existing skill-sync SSOT/fan-out (`skills/<name>` → `.agents/skills/<name>` → per-agent dirs, driven by `skills/skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh`) to a third, external target.

## Locked decisions (visormatt, revised 2026-08-13)

These SUPERSEDE the 2026-08-12 decisions, which assumed run-scoped ephemeral injection and that Cursor/Grok had no skill mechanism. The latter was stale: Cursor 2.4+ and Grok Build CLI both read the SKILL.md standard. The former was reframed after confirming CLIs only discover skills from dirs inside the working tree (no out-of-repo `--skills-dir` pointer exists) and that visibility "while the server runs" is the desired property.

1. **Placement — in-repo, forced by CLI reality.** All five CLIs (claude/codex/opencode/cursor/grok) discover skills only from dirs inside the working tree; none exposes an out-of-repo `--skills-dir` flag or env override. Inject into **`.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`** — the union of those two dirs covers all five (`.agents/skills` → claude/codex/opencode/cursor; `.claude/skills` → claude/cursor/grok). Reuse skill-sync's symlink/ownership semantics rather than reinventing them. (Global user dirs like `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.grok/skills` were considered and REJECTED: non-uniform across CLIs and permanently global — they would leak OT skills into every repo and every interactive session, overshooting "while the server runs.")
2. **Lifecycle — server-scoped, per-repo** (changed from run-scoped ephemeral). Materialize the layer lazily on the first foreign run that touches a given repo; keep it in place while the OT server runs; REUSE across all subsequent runs (no per-run setup cost). Teardown on server shutdown, plus a boot-time reaper for missed teardowns. This matches visormatt's stated preference: OT skills present and visible while the server is running.
