3. **Non-mutation — symlinks + `.git/info/exclude` + ledger.** Injected links are made invisible to `git status` via the repo-local **`.git/info/exclude`** (NOT the tracked `.gitignore`, and NOT a global `core.excludesFile`, which would leak into every repo and risk masking real files). A per-repo LEDGER (JSON of every injected path) records exactly what was created. The target repo's tracked files are never modified; `git status` is clean at all times, not merely after a successful teardown.
4. **Recovery — ledger-driven boot sweep.** On startup, reconcile ledgers against live filesystem state and remove exactly the paths recorded (and only still-OT-owned symlinks/copies), covering missed teardowns after a server/run crash. Piggybacks on the existing STALE-run sweep lifecycle (heartbeat/cutoff, PlanRunsService.settleStaleRun).
5. **Precedence — target repo wins.** OT skills are a BASE layer that fills gaps; any skill name the target repo already defines is excluded from the manifest and never masked. Layering low→high: OT curated (`skills/`) < personal/experimental (per-user dir) < target repo.
6. **Container mode — copy, not symlink.** When workspace path-mapping is active (workspace-paths.ts host↔container bridge), symlink targets won't resolve across mount namespaces; materialize COPIES (or arrange a bind mount) in that mode. Host-run mode stays symlinks.
7. **Personal/experimental tier — per-user dir outside the repo.** A configured, opt-in per-user location (e.g. `~/.openthrottle/skills`), layered ABOVE OT curated but BELOW the target repo. It is a resolver SOURCE only — the materializer projects it into the repo like everything else; it does not depend on any CLI reading an out-of-repo dir. Unreleased skills never touch git and are never force-fed to other users.

## Approach (high level)

1. A layered skill-set RESOLVER that merges OT curated (`skills/`) + personal-user-dir into an ordered manifest, applying name-collision precedence and excluding target-repo-owned names, reusing skill-sync's symlink/ownership semantics.
2. A server/repo-scoped MATERIALIZER that, given a foreign repo, idempotently ensures the resolved layer exists in `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/` (symlinks on host, copies under the container bridge), writes a per-repo ledger, and registers `.git/info/exclude` entries. Idempotent "ensure-materialized(repo)" — a no-op when already present. Teardown removes exactly and only the ledger-recorded paths.
3. WIRING into the foreign-workspace run path so ensure-materialized runs at run start (idempotent, reused across runs) and teardown runs on server shutdown — and RECONCILING `buildForeignWorkspacePromptLayer` so it no longer blanket-forbids the now-available OT skills (while still forbidding OT monorepo paths/generators), surfacing which skills were injected.
4. CRASH-SAFETY reaper: a boot-time (and/or periodic) ledger-driven sweep that removes stranded injected links even after a missed teardown, riding the existing STALE-run sweep lifecycle.
5. Container path-mapping awareness (toContainerPath/toHostPath, workspace-paths.ts) so injection works under the Docker host-execution bridge via copy mode, not just host-run.

Non-goal: changing how OT's in-repo skill-sync fan-out works. This adds an external consumer of the same SSOT.
summary: Extend the skill-sync fan-out to reach into a downstream/foreign repo: layer OT's curated skills (plus an opt-in per-user experimental tier) into the target workspace's .agents/skills + .claude/skills. Materialized server-scoped/per-repo (lazily on first foreign run, reused across runs while the server is up, torn down on shutdown + boot reaper), non-mutating via symlink/copy + .git/info/exclude + a per-repo ledger so git status stays clean. Target repo's own skills win on collision.
title: Layer OT curated skills into foreign workspaces (server-scoped, non-mutating)

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

`/usage` renders every distinct `git_branch` seen in the 30-day window as a pill row. `listFilterOptions` in `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/skill-usage-events/skill-usage-events.service.ts` does `SELECT DISTINCT e.git_branch … ORDER BY e.git_branch ASC` with **no cap**, and `UsageSkillUsageFilters.tsx` maps all of them into `<Link>` chips. With one branch per worktree/feature we already have dozens; the row wraps into a wall that pushes the skill-usage content off screen, `main` is buried mid-alphabet, and the payload grows unbounded with every branch we ever touch.

(The screenshot referenced in the request did not come through, but the wall of chips is reproducible on `/usage` today.)

The same unbounded pattern applies to `filterOptions.cwds` (project paths) — the last task reuses the primitive there.

## What we want

1. A **dropdown + autocomplete** branch filter (shadcn `Combobox`/`Command` + `Popover`) instead of N chips.
2. **Ordering**: `All branches` first, then the default branch (`main`, falling back to `master`) pinned to the top, then the rest alphabetically. Ordering is decided **server-side in SQL** so it survives the result cap and paging.
3. A **lazy `LIKE` search API** — the dropdown queries the server as you type (debounced) instead of filtering a preloaded array client-side, so the initial page payload stays small no matter how many branches exist.

## Approach

**Server** — new `skillUsageGitBranches(start, end, query, limit, skillName)` query next to `skillUsage` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/skill-usage/`), backed by a new `searchGitBranches` repository method:

```sql
SELECT e.git_branch AS value, COUNT(*) AS count
FROM skill_usage_events e
WHERE e.occurred_at >= :start AND e.occurred_at < :endExclusive
  AND e.git_branch IS NOT NULL AND e.git_branch <> ''
  AND (:query IS NULL OR e.git_branch ILIKE :pattern)
GROUP BY e.git_branch
ORDER BY (e.git_branch <> 'main'), e.git_branch ASC
LIMIT :limit
```

- `query` is trimmed; escape `%`/`_`/`\` before building the `%…%` pattern (parameterized — never string-concatenated).
- `limit` defaults to 20, hard-capped at 50; the result envelope reports `hasMore` so the UI can say "keep typing to narrow".
- Reuse the existing half-open `[start, endExclusive)` date helper and the `skillName` narrowing already in `listFilterOptions`.
- Auth mirrors `skillUsage`: `GqlPermissionsGuard` + `PERMISSIONS.SETTINGS_READ`.
- Keep `SkillUsageFilterOptionsObject.gitBranches` for back-compat but mark it `@deprecated(reason: …)` pointing at the new query (per CLAUDE.md: never remove fields on existing types), and cap what it returns so the old path can't blow up either.

**Client** — `/usage` seeds the dropdown from the first page of the new query in its loader (so SSR shows a populated, correctly-ordered list with zero JS), then a **resource route** serves keystroke searches. Follow the exact precedent already in this app: `app/routes/resources.resolve-plan-ref.tsx` + `usePlanRefResolver` — loader-only route, debounced `useFetcher().load`, echo the normalized query back in the payload so stale keystrokes are discarded, degrade to an empty list on error instead of throwing.

The shadcn `Combobox` currently only does client-side `cmdk` filtering, so it needs async props (`onSearchChange`, `searchValue`, `loading`, `shouldFilter={false}`) — a backwards-compatible extension, not a fork.

Selection stays URL-driven: `?skillBranch=` via `buildUsageSearch`, preserving `provider` / `skillScope` / `skillCwd` exactly as the chips do today. Navigation on select (`useNavigate`) — no new client-state store.

## Constraints / gotchas

- **No new TS enums**; `as const` objects. Explicit return types, `import type`, alphabetized keys.
- Scaffold every new component/route/util with `@tools/generators` (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router …`) — keep the generated section comments (Hooks / Setup / Handlers / Markup / Life Cycle / 🔌 Short Circuit) even when empty.
- Component files export only the component + props; option lists / copy live in `app/routing/usage/data/`.
- After schema changes: boot `openthrottle-server:dev` until bootstrap to regenerate `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel`, and commit `schema.gql` + all `__generated__` output. CI fails on codegen drift.
- Tests: `component`, not `screen`; `userEvent`, not `fireEvent`. Radix Popover in jsdom — assert on the open listbox contents, not on geometry.
- Existing tests to keep green: `app/routes/__tests__/usage._index.test.tsx`, `app/routing/usage/components/__tests__/UsageSkillUsageFilters.test.tsx`, `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/skill-usage-events/skill-usage-events.service.test.ts` (asserts `filterOptions` shape), `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/skill-usage/skill-usage.resolver.test.ts`.

## Definition of done

- `/usage` shows one branch control, not a wrapping wall; `main` is the first real option; typing narrows via the server.
- Page payload no longer scales with total branch count.
- `pnpm run check:local` green; branch-filter behavior covered by service, resolver, resource-route, and component tests.
summary: Replace the flat wall of branch chips on /usage with a searchable combobox backed by a new server-side branch-search query (default branch first, then A–Z, ILIKE lazy search, capped result set).
title: /usage branch filter: searchable dropdown + lazy branch-search API

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The chat composer's checkout/repository selector (`ChatCheckoutSelector` in `packages/react-router-chat`) is great overall, but its search is too loose: typing `visormatt` should return only the `visormatt/*` checkouts, yet the whole list — `atlasworksinc/monorepo`, `atlasworksinc/atlasworks`, `atlasworksinc/nativeapps`, `atlasworksinc/native-apps` — stays visible.

## Diagnosis

Two compounding causes, both in `packages/react-router-chat/src`:

1. **cmdk's default filter is fuzzy subsequence scoring** (`command-score`). Each `CommandItem` is matched against `value + ' ' + keywords.join(' ')`, and a query matches if its characters appear *in order anywhere* in that haystack — not as a substring.
2. **The keyword haystack is deliberately wide.** `ChatCheckoutSelectorRow` passes `keywords={checkoutSearchTerms(checkout)}` (`utils/checkout-groups.ts`), which joins label, branch, **filesystem path**, project name, host, repo name and owner. Every local checkout lives under `/home/demo/…`, so the letters of `visormatt` (v-i-s-o-r-m-a-t-t) trivially subsequence-match across e.g. `atlasworksinc … main /home/demo/Development/…` for every row.

Wide keywords are the right call (they were added precisely so owner/path/project are searchable); the fuzzy scoring on top of them is what breaks precision.

## Fix direction

Supply a custom `filter` to the `<Command>` in `ChatCheckoutSelector` (cmdk supports `filter(value, search, keywords) => number`):

- Case-insensitive **substring** matching, not subsequence scoring.
- Tokenize the query on whitespace; every token must substring-match at least one search term (AND across tokens, OR across terms).
- Keep matching against the full `checkoutSearchTerms` set so `owner`, path and project searches keep working — `visormatt` matches only rows whose owner/path/label actually contains it.
- Optionally rank: term-prefix or label matches score higher than path matches, but any non-match returns 0.
- Extract the predicate as a pure util (e.g. `checkoutSearchFilter` next to `checkoutSearchTerms`) so it is unit-testable, and export it `@public` with JSDoc.

Note `CommandItem` `value` is `checkout.id` (a UUID) — the custom filter should ignore the value string and match keywords only, so UUID fragments don't produce ghost matches.

## Acceptance

- Searching `visormatt` in a list containing `visormatt/*` and `atlasworksinc/*` checkouts shows only the `visormatt` rows; group headings for empty groups disappear (cmdk handles this once items report 0).
- Searching `monorepo` still shows every `monorepo` checkout across orgs; searching `atlasworksinc mono` narrows to `atlasworksinc/monorepo`.
- Path (`Development`), branch (`main`) and project-name searches still match, as substrings.
- `No matching checkouts.` empty state still appears for garbage queries.

## Where

- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatCheckoutSelector.tsx` — pass `filter` to `<Command>`.
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/utils/checkout-groups.ts` (or a sibling util file per one-export-per-file conventions) — the pure filter function + tests.
- Source-first package: validate with `lint`/`typecheck`/`test`, then run `openthrottle-developer` as the integration check.
summary: Searching the chat checkout/repository selector for `visormatt` matches every checkout (including all atlasworksinc repos). Replace cmdk's default fuzzy subsequence scoring with a strict, token-based substring filter over the checkout search terms so only genuinely matching checkouts survive.
title: Tighten checkout selector search matching

author: visormatt
description:
Fully remove the `vscode-openthrottle` VS Code / Cursor extension package from the monorepo, along with every workspace reference, catalog entry, doc mention, and knip allowance it leaves behind.

## Why

The extension (~1,400 LOC across `src/`, with zero tests — `tests/` is a bare `.gitkeep`) is unshipped: `private: true`, `publish:false`, never built in CI, and packaged only by hand via the local-only `project:build` / `project:install` Nx targets (`vsce package` → `openthrottle.vsix` → `cursor --install-extension`). It carries real ongoing cost: its own `codegen-graphql` target against `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` (so every server schema change drags it along), a `@types/vscode` + `@vscode/vsce` dependency surface (including the `@vscode/vsce-sign` licensing waiver and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` build-script opt-out), and a stale README whose paths (`packages/openthrottle/vscode-openthrottle`, `pnpm nx build @openthrottle/vscode-openthrottle`) no longer exist.

## Current-state inventory (verified at HEAD c3ac13e3)

**The package itself** — 40 tracked files under `packages/vscode-openthrottle/`:
- `src/` — `index.ts`, `api-client.ts`, `auth.ts`, `config.ts`, `errors.ts`, `sort-plan-tasks-by-list-order.ts`, `queries.graphql`, `graphql/`, `__generated__/`, `commands/` (create-plan-from-text, login, logout), `trees/` (plans, welcome, login, docs), `views/` (plans-view, tabs-view, detail-webview)
- `docs/` — `AUTH_DESIGN.md`, `INTEGRATION.md`, `UI-DESIGN.md`
- config — `package.json`, `codegen.ts`, `apollo.config.mjs`, `eslint.config.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.lib.json`, `tsconfig.test.json`, `.gitignore`, `.vscodeignore`, `LICENSE.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `tests/.gitkeep`
- untracked local cruft that disappears with the directory: `openthrottle.vsix` (gitignored via `*.vsix`), `node_modules/`, `.DS_Store`, and a stray `.git/gk/` GitKraken directory

**External references that must be cleaned up:**
| Location | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json:242` | root dep `"vscode-openthrottle": "workspace:^"` |
| `tsconfig.json:20` | project reference `./packages/vscode-openthrottle` |
| `knip.jsonc:260` | `vscode-openthrottle` in the ignoreDependencies list |
| `knip.jsonc:95-96` | `@vscode/vsce` ignore + comment naming this package's `project:build` |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `packages/vscode-openthrottle` importer + root `link:` entry (regenerated) |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml:161,173` | catalog `@types/vscode`, `@vscode/vsce` |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml:16` | `'@vscode/vsce-sign': false` build-script opt-out |
| `package.json:301` | root devDep `"@types/vscode": "catalog:"` |
| `LICENSING.md:51` | names `vscode-openthrottle` in the packages scope |
| `docs/openthrottle/monorepo-architecture.md:39,111` | mermaid node + table row |
| `docs/openthrottle/packages-naming.md:6,37` | `@openthrottle/vscode` row + naming-doc link (note: the linked `vscode-openthrottle-naming.md` does not exist) |
| `packages/AGENTS.md:10` | lists it among the non-prefixed one-offs |
| `packages/graphql-codegen/AGENTS.md:9` | lists it as a codegen consumer |
| `packages/openthrottle-vscode/README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `package.json` | cross-links to the "canonical extension" |

**Note — `@vscode/ripgrep` (`pnpm-workspace.yaml:172`) stays.** It belongs to `packages/openthrottle-ide`, not this package.

## Open decision: the sibling `packages/openthrottle-vscode`

`@openthrottle/openthrottle-vscode` exists solely as the "editor-agnostic logic library for the OpenThrottle VS Code/Cursor extension." It is an empty stub — `src/index.ts` is literally `export const REMOVE_ME = ...`, all three `__tests__/` dirs are `.gitkeep`s — and it is imported by nothing. Removing the extension leaves it with no reason to exist. It is scoped here as its own explicitly-gated task so the call stays yours; the rest of the plan does not depend on it.

## Scope boundary

This is a deletion, not a migration. No functionality is ported to `openthrottle-developer`, `openthrottle-ide`, or `openthrottle-mcp`. If any of the extension's behavior (plans tree, detail webview, `createPlanFromText`) is wanted elsewhere later, it is recoverable from git history — the removal commit sha should be noted in the final report.

## Validation

`pnpm run check:local` must be green, plus a clean install and an explicit `nx show projects` check that `vscode-openthrottle` is gone from the graph. Remember: `check:local`'s affected-test step is narrowed, so mirror CI with `pnpm nx run-many --target=test --all` on the final task.
title: Tear down packages/vscode-openthrottle

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Loading a protected page with an **expired session** (or any authed GraphQL failure inside a deferred loader) **crashes the React Router SSR dev/prod server**. Observed as `Error: GraphQL errors: Unauthorized` thrown from `callListAgentConversations` (the dashboard "Recent Chats" card) with no React Router frames in the stack — i.e. an **unhandled promise rejection**, which Node crashes on by default (`--unhandled-rejections=throw`).

This is one instance of a **class** of bug: any authenticated GraphQL call returned from a loader as a **naked deferred promise** (RR8 Single Fetch streaming) that rejects, with no synchronous `.catch` attached before the microtask, takes down the whole SSR process. `<Await errorElement>` does **not** prevent it — errorElement runs at render time, too late to stop the unhandled rejection.

## Root causes (two, compounding)

1. **The auth-error contract is dead code.** `@openthrottle/react-router-graphql` already ships typed `GraphqlAuthError` (with `httpStatus`), `isAuthError`, `GraphqlTimeoutError`, `isTimeoutError`, and `classifyError()` (`extractHttpStatus` on the error message). But the NestJS GraphQL guard returns **HTTP 200 with a GraphQL error `"Unauthorized"` / `extensions.code: UNAUTHENTICATED`** — there is no HTTP status in the message, so `classifyError` never recognizes it. Auth-detection never fires (confirmed by the `/improve` audit for this package, plan `6d479fa3`). So even the code meant to make auth failures redirectable is inert.
2. **Deferral relied on `<Await errorElement>`** to handle rejections (the plan that introduced dashboard/home deferral, `f9030c40`, says so explicitly) — which cannot stop a microtask-level unhandled rejection.

## Already shipped (L0 — prevention)

`authMiddleware` now treats a **present-but-expired** JWT like a missing one: `isJwtExpired()` pre-flight → clear cookie + redirect to `/auth`. This prevents the **common** case (stale session) from ever reaching loaders. Landed on branch `openthrottle/loop-plan-mcp-connectors`, commit `4ced2b1f` (`packages/react-router-auth`: `isJwtExpired` + middleware gate + tests). This plan covers the remaining, non-expiry cases and the crash-class itself.

## Decision (locked with the owner)

**Defense-in-depth (L1 + L2 + L3), scoped as shared packages so all four RR apps inherit it once.**

- **L1 — Safety net (never crash):** a shared process-level `unhandledRejection` (and `uncaughtException`) handler that **logs, does not exit**. A backstop, not the fix — a logged error is strictly better than a dead server. One shared helper, wired into every app's `app/entry.server.tsx`.
- **L2 — Fix the auth-error contract (auth failures become clean redirects):** extend `classifyError` (or the underlying `@openthrottle/nodejs-graphql` error contract) so a GraphQL `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `"Unauthorized"` error IS classified as `GraphqlAuthError`; plus a single shared `redirectOnAuthError` loader/action helper (redirect to `/auth` + clear cookie) replacing the ~6 hand-rolled per-route auth redirects. Overlaps the existing improve plans `6d479fa3` (react-router-graphql) and `798d5efc` (react-router-auth — single owner of a typed `isUnauthorizedError`) — fold/reference rather than duplicate.
- **L3 — Resilient deferred helper (root-cause fix):** a shared helper for deferred loader values that attaches its `.catch` **synchronously** so the promise can never go unhandled: auth errors → `throw redirect('/auth')` (RR honors thrown redirects even in streamed data); other errors → a resolved error-state value the card renders (or a synchronously-caught re-throw the `<Await errorElement>` handles). Open design point resolved in task 1: **opt-in helper (adoption discipline) vs. an automatic entry-level wrapper that walks loader return values (can't-forget).**

## Scope

All four React Router apps — `openthrottle-developer`, `openthrottle-admin`, `openthrottle-email`, `openthrottle-website` — each with its own `app/entry.server.tsx` (renderToPipeableStream). Shared code lands in `@openthrottle/react-router-utils` (server-entry safety net + deferred helper) and `@openthrottle/react-router-graphql` / `@openthrottle/react-router-auth` (auth-error contract + redirect helper), so apps inherit the behavior rather than re-implement it.

## Grounding facts (confirmed)

- `react-router-graphql` exports: `GraphqlAuthError`, `isAuthError`, `GraphqlTimeoutError`, `isTimeoutError`, `classifyError`, `extractHttpStatus` (`packages/react-router-graphql/src/index.ts`).
- The failing rejection surfaces as `Error: "GraphQL errors: Unauthorized"` (from `@openthrottle/nodejs-graphql` `index.ts:123`), i.e. HTTP 200 + `errors[0].message = "Unauthorized"`, `extensions.code = UNAUTHENTICATED` — **no HTTP status**, so `extractHttpStatus` returns undefined and it is NOT classified as auth.
- `@openthrottle/nodejs-graphql` already has a non-throwing v2 discriminated-union contract (`executeGraphql_v2`, `GraphqlV2Result`, `httpStatus`) that L2 can adopt instead of string-scraping (see `6d479fa3` roadmap).
- Deferred loaders in play today: `dashboard._index.tsx` (`core` / `githubStats` / `recentChats`) and home `_index.tsx` (composer bundle) — from plan `f9030c40`.

## Verification (per the touched apps)

- Reproduce all three failure modes against a running dev server and assert **no process crash**: (a) expired token, (b) mid-session 401/`UNAUTHENTICATED` on a deferred call, (c) API down / timeout on a deferred call. Expected: auth → 302 `/auth` (+ cleared cookie); non-auth → the card/section shows a degraded error state; the server stays up.
- Gates on every touched project: `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`; no GraphQL schema/codegen drift (no server schema change expected).

## Related plans

- `6d479fa3` — Improve: @openthrottle/react-router-graphql (auth-error contract, `redirectOnAuthError`).
- `798d5efc` — Improve: @openthrottle/react-router-auth (single owner of a typed auth-error helper).
- `f9030c40` — Defer slow loader data on Developer home + dashboard (introduced the naked-promise pattern).

Each task carries its own acceptance criteria in `requirements`. Commit per task with `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers.
summary: A deferred (streamed) loader promise that rejects with no synchronous catch becomes an unhandled rejection and crashes the RR SSR process (Node --unhandled-rejections=throw). Fix it once, globally, via defense-in-depth across all 4 React Router apps: L1 a shared process-level unhandledRejection safety net (log, never exit), L2 fix the broken auth-error contract so GraphQL UNAUTHENTICATED errors are classified + a shared redirectOnAuthError helper, L3 a resilient deferred-value helper so deferred loader promises can never go unhandled (auth → thrown redirect, other → resolved error-state). L0 (expired-token redirect in authMiddleware) already shipped.
title: Harden SSR against deferred-loader rejections (never crash) + fix the auth-error contract — all RR apps

author: visormatt
description:
# Goal

On the OpenThrottle Developer dashboard (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/dashboard._index.tsx`), the GitHub stats section currently renders effectively empty/zeroed data when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is unset — with no explanation. Instead, detect the missing token and show a purposeful **empty state** instructing the user to populate `GITHUB_TOKEN`, mirroring how other cards handle no-data.

# Current behavior (why it looks empty)

- `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read server-side only, in `packages/nestjs-github/src/github/github.service.ts` `buildHeaders()` (~line 156). If unset, requests go out **unauthenticated** — no throw at read time.
- The dashboard loads GitHub stats via `GetDashboardGithubStatsDocument` (`dashboard._index.tsx.graphql`), resolved by `packages/nestjs-github/src/graphql/github.resolver.ts` (`openPrCountByAuthor`, `prTimeInStateSummary`) over `GitHubStatsService`.
- With no token: public data returns zeroed/near-empty aggregates, or GitHub eventually 403/404s (rate limit / private repo) which throws a generic `GitHub API error` caught by the card boundary. Either way the user sees empty stats with no guidance.

# Approach

1. **Expose a boolean, never the token.** Add a server-side signal (e.g. a `githubTokenConfigured` / `githubIntegrationConfigured` boolean field) that reflects whether `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, read via `ConfigService`. Do NOT return the token value or any secret.
2. **Wire it into the dashboard query + loader**, run codegen (`codegen-graphql` on server, then `codegen-react-router`), commit generated output + the app `schema.gql`.
3. **Render an empty state** in the GitHub stats card(s) when the token is not configured, using the shared `OpenThrottleEmptyState` (`@openthrottle/react-router-ui`) or the dashboard's local empty-state precedent (`DashboardRecentChatsCard`). Copy should clearly tell the user to set `GITHUB_TOKEN` (mention where — env/`.env`), not just show zeros.
4. **Tests** for the resolver flag (set vs unset) and the card render branch (configured → stats; unconfigured → empty-state prompt).

# Key files

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/dashboard._index.tsx` (loader ~30-75) + `.graphql`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/dashboard/components/` (GitHub stats card; `DashboardRecentChatsCard.tsx` for the empty-state precedent)
- `packages/nestjs-github/src/graphql/github.resolver.ts`, `github-stats.service.ts`, `github/github.service.ts`
- `packages/react-router-ui/src/components/OpenThrottleEmptyState.tsx`

# Constraints

- Never expose the `GITHUB_TOKEN` value over GraphQL — boolean only.
- Code-first GraphQL: after schema changes, boot `openthrottle-server:dev` to regen `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then run `codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router` and commit all `__generated__` output.
- Follow code style in `.cursor/rules/` (no enums, no `as`/`any`, empty-state copy lives in a `data.copy.ts` per component/data file boundaries).
summary: On the developer dashboard, when GITHUB_TOKEN is unset the GitHub stats render as effectively empty/zeroed with no explanation. Detect the missing token server-side (without leaking it) and surface a dedicated empty-state that tells the user to populate GITHUB_TOKEN.
title: Dashboard: prompt to configure GITHUB_TOKEN when unset instead of showing empty stats

author: visormatt
description:
Follow-up surfaced while retargeting docs in plan `b19377d1` (task `a05878fc`). Not a doc bug — a real, unresolved decision that stale prose was hiding.

## The discrepancy

Every doc and comment describing the CI affected-test step called it **serialized (`--parallel=1`)**:

- `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` (open items)
- `docs/monorepo/CI-quality-gates.md` (P2 row + narrative)
- `docs/reliability/developer-vitest-pool.md`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts` (`maxWorkers` comment)
- the inline comment above the step in `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml`

The live command has **no `--parallel` flag at all**, so it runs at Nx's default concurrency of 3, and has for as long as those comments have existed. The only `--parallel=1` in the workflow is a commented-out line.

Plan `b19377d1` corrected the prose to describe reality and added a ⚠️ warning against "restoring" `--parallel=1` on the strength of the old wording — but deliberately did **not** change behaviour, because that was out of its scope and the safe direction was not obvious.

## Why it is not already settled

The docs describe something *stricter* than what runs. So there are two live possibilities and no evidence for either:

1. **The default-3 concurrency is fine** and the comment's fear is obsolete — in which case the step could be widened to `--parallel` and the prose simplified.
2. **The comment described the intent and the flag was simply never added** — in which case CI has been running 3-way concurrent Vitest suites for a long time against a documented ceiling of 1, and `--parallel=1` (or an explicit `--parallel=2`) is the fix.

The failure mode that motivated the original comment is **silent-passing**: an OOM-killed worker surfaces as files reporting `(0 test)` with a green run, not as an error. So "we have not seen a problem" is not evidence — nobody has checked for `(0 test)` files specifically.

## What changed since the comment was written

- `openthrottle-developer` moved to Vitest `vmForks` + `vmMemoryLimit: '512MB'` (plan `e448a51d`, PR #267), bounding per-worker V8 VM-context accumulation.
- `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (plan `6ced8d0e`) doubled RAM from 8 GB to 16 GB at 4 vCPU.
- Sharding (plan `b19377d1`) puts ~1/3 of the affected projects on each box, so fewer heavy suites are available to co-run — but an unlucky partition can still land two heavy app suites together, so this is **not** the evidence either.

## Work

1. Audit recent CI runs for `(0 test)` files and killed workers at the current default-3 concurrency — establish whether the undocumented status quo has been silently failing.
2. On a scratch branch, run the affected test step several times at `--parallel=1`, default, and `--parallel` (full), on a fat affected graph. Record wall-clock and, for each, whether every suite reported a non-zero test count.
3. Pick a posture, make it **explicit** in the command (never rely on Nx's default again — that is what let the drift hide), and align every doc listed above.

## Success

The flag in the workflow, the comment above it, and all five docs agree — and the number they agree on is backed by CI runs, not by reasoning.
title: CI: settle the affected-test parallelism posture

## Goal
Before flipping this repo public, confirm `infra/` (and its git history) leaks nothing sensitive, and decide on defense-in-depth cleanups. None of the infra is actually deployed except the GCS buckets.

## Audit findings (2026-08-01)

**No credentials leaked — tracked or in history.** No service-account JSON keys, DB passwords, tokens, private IPs, or connection strings appear anywhere in `infra/` tracked files or across full git history. `infra/.gitignore` correctly excludes `.terraform/`, `*.tfstate`, `*.tfstate.*`, `*.tfvars` (via secrets/), `secrets/`, override/crash files; on-disk `.terraform/terraform.tfstate` is confirmed git-ignored. Templates (`startup.sh.tpl`, `docker-compose.yml.tpl`) reference `${postgres_password}`, `${redis_host}` etc. purely as Terraform template variables — real values only ever land in gitignored state.

**Old Terraform state in git history (no secrets, bad hygiene).** `infra/environments/staging/terraform.tfstate` (0 bytes) and `terraform.tfstate.backup` (~5 KB) were committed in the initial port commit `8e4af83e` ("chore: initial port from my visormatt/monorepo") and removed later in `08bf9a34` (ot-improve rollup #88–#97). The backup's only resources are two `google_storage_bucket` definitions (project `openthrottle-staging`, bucket names `openthrottle-staging-nx-cache` / `-terraform-state`) — nothing secret, all already public in the README. Publishing keeps these reachable via history.

**Org identifiers in tracked docs (identifiers, not credentials — judgment call).**
- Project IDs `openthrottle-staging`, `openthrottle-production` (locals.tf, READMEs, console deep-links).
- **Stale** project ID `monorepo-staging-473406` in a console URL at `infra/README.md:26` — leftover from the pre-port `visormatt/monorepo` project; should be scrubbed regardless.
- Project **numbers** `11318907976` (production) / `605061926112` (staging) in `infra/environments/README.md:5-6`.
- Bucket names and SA account IDs (`staging-gcs-workflow`).

## Assessment
No hard blocker to going public — nothing exploitable is exposed. GCP project IDs/numbers are non-secret identifiers (they appear in URLs/error messages) but are org-internal recon surface. Remaining work is: (1) one clear fix (stale `monorepo-staging-473406`), (2) decisions on whether to parameterize IDs/numbers and whether to purge state from history, and (3) a repo-wide secret-scan gate so this stays true beyond `infra/`.

## Scope note
User scoped this to `infra/`, but "going public" is repo-wide — the final secret-scan task deliberately extends beyond `infra/` (e.g. `docs/infra/staging-gcs-workflow-service-account.md`, which describes SA-key handling) before the repo flips public.
title: Pre-public infra/leak audit & hardening

author: visormatt
description:
# Settings → Appearance: regroup, prune, and componentize

## Context

`/settings/appearance` in `openthrottle-developer` is one flat `AppearancePanel` component (~205 lines) with four stacked, visually undifferentiated `<section>`s: Theme mode, Theme palette, Brand color, and a "CSS tokens affected by a custom brand" collapsible.

Files today:

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.appearance.tsx` — thin route adapter. Its `loader` calls `getSettingsDiagnosticsLoaderData()` but nothing on the page consumes it (dead loader).
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/AppearancePanel.tsx` — all markup and all handlers.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/config/appearance.ts` — just `THEME_DEFAULT_OPTION`.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/global/data/atom.config.ts` — `configAtom` (`brand` / `theme` / `themeId`), localStorage-backed via `atomWithStorage`.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/SettingsOnboardingRestore.tsx` — written, tested, and **commented out** of the panel (`AppearancePanel.tsx:32,200`).

## Problems

1. **No grouping.** Three related-but-distinct concerns (color scheme, palette, brand) read as one undifferentiated stack. Nothing signals which controls interact.
2. **The CSS-token collapsible earns nothing.** It lists `--brand`, `--ring`, `--color-accent`, … — implementation trivia on a settings screen. Drop it.
3. **Palette picking is blind.** `THEMES` (OpenThrottle + the ported Cursor themes) renders as a name-only `<Select>`. You pick by reading a label, then eyeball the whole app.
4. **Stale copy.** The intro says "Diagnostics below mirror General settings" — there are no diagnostics on this route.
5. **Dead code shipped.** `SettingsOnboardingRestore` is commented out; the route loader is unused.
6. **Hard to change.** Adding, moving, or deleting a settings group means surgery inside one long JSX tree.

## Approach

Move from one long component to a **registry-driven set of small components**, so adding / reordering / deleting a group is a one-line data edit rather than JSX surgery.

- `AppearanceSection` — a shared card shell (title, description, optional aside, children). Every group renders through it, so spacing and heading treatment stay consistent for free.
- One component per control (`AppearanceThemeModeField`, `AppearancePaletteField`, `AppearanceBrandColorField`, …), each owning its own slice of `configAtom` and nothing else.
- `APPEARANCE_SECTIONS` in `routing/settings/data/data.appearance.ts` — an ordered array of `{ id, title, description, Component }`. `AppearancePanel` becomes a `.map()` over it. **Reorder = move an array entry. Remove = delete an entry. Add = append one.**
- Copy lives in `routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts` per the component/data-file boundary rule, not inline in JSX.

Proposed grouping:

| Group | Contains |
| --- | --- |
| **Color scheme** | Theme mode toggle (System / Light / Dark) |
| **Palette** | Palette swatch grid (replaces the name-only Select) + brand color override + "use theme default" |
| **Motion & effects** | Reduced-motion preference |
| **Guides & resets** | Restore dashboard onboarding + reset all appearance to defaults |

A live preview surface sits above the groups so palette + brand + mode changes are visible without leaving the page.

## What we're adding (and why)

**In scope — high value, low risk:**

- **Palette swatch grid.** Render each `THEMES` entry as a small multi-swatch chip drawn from its own `light`/`dark` token record. Picking a palette becomes a visual choice.
- **Live preview card.** A compact sample (buttons, badge, muted text, chart-color row, sidebar accent strip) rendered under the current selections. Answers "what does this actually do" — the honest job the CSS-token list was failing to do.
- **Reset appearance to defaults.** One control returning `configAtom` to `DEFAULT_APPEARANCE_CONFIG`; today you reset brand and palette separately and there's no way back to `system`.
- **Restore onboarding.** Uncomment `SettingsOnboardingRestore` into the "Guides & resets" group — it already exists and is already tested.
- **Reduced motion.** The app ships `GlobalAnimationMesh` / `GlobalAnimationWaves` / `GradientMesh` with no user control. A `reducedMotion: 'system' | 'always'` field on `configAtom` (default `system`, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`) is a real accessibility win.

**Deliberately out of scope:**

- **UI density / font scale.** Genuinely useful, but it needs shared spacing/size tokens in `react-router-shadcn` before a toggle means anything. Worth its own plan.
- **Server-side persistence of appearance.** Stays localStorage-only here.

## Cleanup this plan owns

- Delete the CSS-token `Collapsible` block and its `APPEARANCE_BRAND_OVERRIDE_KEYS` / `APPEARANCE_THEME_COLOR_TOKEN_KEYS` imports from the panel.
- Keep those constants in `packages/react-router-utils/src/utils/theme.ts` — `buildBrandOverrideCss` (`theme.ts:204`) and `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/__tests__/settings.cusomization.test.tsx` still consume them. Only the UI listing goes away.
- Drop the unused `loader` from `settings.appearance.tsx`.
- Fix the stale "Diagnostics below mirror General settings" intro copy.

## Constraints

- Generators first: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=settings --name=A,B,C` (comma-separated batch). Do not hand-write component files.
- Keep the generated section comments (`// Hooks` / `// Setup` / `// Handlers` / `// Markup` / `// Life Cycle` / `// 🔌 Short Circuit`) even when empty.
- One component per file; components export only the component + its props interface. Lists and copy go in the nearest `data/`.
- UI from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` only. No new enums — `as const` objects. No `as` casts.
- Tests use `component` (not `screen`) and `userEvent`.
- Existing tests to keep green: `app/routing/settings/components/__tests__/AppearancePanel.test.tsx`, `app/routes/__tests__/settings.appearance.test.tsx`, `app/routes/__tests__/settings.cusomization.test.tsx`.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test
```

Then a visual pass on `/settings/appearance` in light, dark, and System, across at least three palettes.
summary: Regroup /settings/appearance into registry-driven sections, drop the CSS-token list, and add a palette swatch grid, live preview, reduced-motion, and reset controls.
title: Settings → Appearance: regroup, prune, and componentize

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/legal.privacy-policy.tsx`

Current copy frames the product as a personal portfolio/playground that is not commercial. Business posture is changing: OpenThrottle is (or is becoming) a commercial product/service — that framing must be removed and replaced.

## Goal

1. Move the full paragraph into `@openthrottle/react-router-utils` as a single exported string constant (recommended name near existing brand constants in `src/config/openthrottle.ts`, e.g. `OPENTHROTTLE_SITE_LEGAL_POSTURE` or similar).

3. Update all three legal routes to import and render the constant (fix JSX whitespace splitting so the string is one source of truth).

5. Sweep nearby legal sections for contradictory non-commercial / portfolio-only claims and align if in scope (esp. terms "About this site" and any SLA/liability framing).

## Non-goals

- Full rewrite of License / Privacy / Terms documents (only the shared posture paragraph + clear contradictions).
- Moving legal UI components into the utils package — string constant only.

## Decisions already made

- Posture: commercial product (not personal portfolio).
- Shape: string constant in `@openthrottle/react-router-utils`, consumed by legal routes.

author: visormatt
description:
Filed from plan 09b88bff-036a-4bae-bae6-0b86b43d2538 (the 04-mental-model short). None of these blocked that video; all three affect every flow, so they are their own work rather than comments in a flow file.

## 1. The portrait pass lays out as desktop, wasting most of the Short frame

`runner/run.ts --portrait` records at 1080x1920. 1080 CSS pixels is ABOVE the app's mobile breakpoint (768), so the app renders its desktop layout — sidebar and all — and on a content-light route roughly 60% of the frame is empty background below the content. Verified on the 04-mental-model 9:16 master.

Options: record the portrait pass at a genuinely mobile viewport (e.g. 540x960 at deviceScaleFactor 2, which still downsamples to 1080x1920) so the app's mobile layout fills the frame; or keep the viewport and have the assembler scale the content region up. The first is closer to what a viewer would actually see on a phone.

Not a publish blocker — the captured text is legible either way — but it is the difference between a Short that looks composed for the format and one that looks like a cropped desktop.

## 2. A missing region-of-interest selector costs 30 seconds per step, silently

`sampleRegion` in `runner/run.ts` calls `page.locator(selector).first().boundingBox()` and `.catch(() => null)`. A selector that does not match burns Playwright's 30s default timeout, the error is swallowed, and because nothing is added to `sampledBeats` it retries on EVERY subsequent step of that beat.

One wrong selector turned a 54-second recording into 264 seconds with no error and no warning — the run "succeeded". Give the call a short explicit timeout (a region either exists now or does not) and log loudly when a declared region never resolves. A silent 5x inflation is worse than a failure.

## 3. Dev-only server metrics are in frame on every beat

Both 04-mental-model masters carry a "Server metrics — RSS 286.2 MB · Heap 205.49 MB · CPU 5,533 ms" footer across the bottom of every shot. It is real UI rather than a leak, so `video-scan` passes it, but it is developer diagnostics on a marketing video and the numbers change every take.

The runner already hides the editor deep-link buttons for recording; this belongs in the same list, or behind whatever flag the footer should have had.
summary: Three pipeline-wide issues surfaced while producing the mental-model short; none blocked it, all affect every future video.
title: Screencast pipeline polish found producing 04-mental-model

author: visormatt
description:
## Context

The `openthrottle-developer` app has a large Vitest suite (~354 files / ~1,580 tests). It previously ran on `pool: 'vmForks'` for speed, but under CI memory pressure the reused vmForks worker accumulates V8 VM contexts and **crashes** — surfacing as in-flight files reporting `(0 test)` with no error stack and no Vitest summary. This is a flaky, non-deterministic CI failure with zero real assertion failures (seen on PR #264 / branch `ot/chat-idle-timeout-retry`, run 30667852303 — 4 unrelated `plans.$planId._index*` + `PlanWorkflowRunTransparency` files reported `(0 test)`).

**Immediate mitigation (applied on `ot/chat-idle-timeout-retry`), 3 parts:**
1. `applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts`: `pool: 'vmForks'` -> `pool: 'forks'` (reclaims memory per file; stable) + top-level `maxWorkers: 4` to cap concurrency and bound peak memory. NOTE: Vitest 4 removed `poolOptions.forks.maxForks`/`minForks` and `minWorkers` — the cap is the top-level `maxWorkers` only, and `defineConfig` must be imported from `vitest/config` (not `vite`) for the `test` block to type-check.
2. `applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/setup.ts`: global `vi.mock('~/services/graphql-ws-client', () => ({ getGraphqlWsClient: () => null }))`. Switching to `forks` surfaced 4 pre-existing unhandled errors — test files that mount plan/task-detail routes open a real graphql-ws WebSocket (undici) that errors asynchronously after the test finishes; `vmForks` swallowed these on VM-context teardown, `forks` does not, so Vitest failed the run. Returning null matches the service's real SSR behavior and every subscription hook already guards for null.
3. Verified: full suite green under the final config — 354 files / 1,579 tests pass, 1 skipped, **0 errors**, exit 0. Wall-clock regressed (~90s under vmForks -> ~340s under forks; the `import`-per-file cost vmForks avoided).

## Goal

Recover the wall-clock regression from the vmForks -> forks switch by **sharding** the developer suite across CI runners/workers, so no single worker/process carries the entire 354-file graph. Keep stability (no return to the vmForks crash mode).

## Approach options to evaluate

- Vitest native `--shard=<i>/<n>` split across a CI matrix (parallel jobs), then merge coverage.
- Nx-level split / atomized test target (e.g. `n/ci` style per-file or per-folder targets) if it fits the Nx pipeline better than a manual matrix.
- Revisit `vmForks` **with** `memoryLimit` (Vitest 4 keeps `test.memoryLimit`) + a `maxWorkers` cap as an alternative to forks, benchmarking crash-resistance vs. speed.
- Tune `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` / `isolate` once sharding bounds per-shard memory.

## Constraints / notes

- Do not regress stability — the `(0 test)` crash must not reappear. Validate by running the full suite (and each shard) repeatedly under `CI=true`.
- `CI=true` is required locally to skip the interactive nx-sync prompt.
- Coverage must still merge correctly across shards (`coverage.provider: 'v8'`, reportsDirectory under `coverage/applications/openthrottle-developer`).
- Keep the config comment's rationale accurate as the pool/shard strategy evolves.
- Keep the shared-setup graphql-ws stub (or a per-shard equivalent) so subscription-mounting specs never open a real socket.
- This is a follow-up to the idle-timeout PR; not a blocker for it.
summary: Split the 354-file developer test suite so no single Vitest worker carries the whole graph, recovering the wall-clock lost by moving vmForks -> forks for stability.
title: Shard the openthrottle-developer Vitest suite to recover CI wall-clock

author: visormatt
description:
Put the chat `ChatCheckoutSelector` on plan detail so a missing repository/checkout association can be fixed in place — without opening the hidden Configuration tab — and the plan becomes runnable.

## Why

`PlanDetailRoute` currently has a TODO at the tabs row (after `PlanEditorActions`, ~line 165): "We need to add the Repository selector here." The full workspace picker already exists as `PlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector` inside `PlanTabConfiguration`, but that tab is gated off (`showConfiguration = false`) and the page-level `PlanToolbar` is also gated off (`showToolbar = false`). Plans that were created without a checkout/repository in `runConfigJson` have no on-page way to course-correct, so Execute/Run and editor deep links stay blocked.

The home composer and Run-skill dialog already use `ChatCheckoutSelector` from `@openthrottle/react-router-chat` (searchable, grouped by org, disambiguates colliding `monorepo` names). Reuse that control — do not invent a third picker.

## Placement

- Mount a compact, single-select `ChatCheckoutSelector` in the `TabsList` row of `PlanDetailRoute`, immediately after `PlanEditorActions` (the existing comment).
- `PlanDetailRoute` is already at the 210-line component cap — extract a wrapper (e.g. `PlanCheckoutSelector`) via `@tools/generators` `react-router` `--subGenerator=component`. Do not grow the route body.
- Keep the Configuration tab and page toolbar hidden; this control is the lightweight course-correct, not a replacement for custom-path / monorepo-root / branch-field workspace config.

## Data + persistence

- Source options from the plan loader's deferred `workspaceRepositories` (`PlanRunConfigRepositoryFields`), not a second `workspaceLocalRepositories` fetch. Flatten nested `repository.checkouts[]` into `ChatCheckoutOption[]` (checkout `id` as the option id; carry `branch` / `filesystemPath` / `remoteUrl` / `projectName` so the picker can group and disambiguate the same way chat does).
- Stream the list behind `PlanDeferredSection` the same way `PlanEditorActions` waits on `enabledEditors` — `workspaceRepositories` is the slow deferred field (~1.3s cold).
- Single-select only. A plan run has one cwd (`checkoutId` → `repositoryId` → `workingDirectory` precedence on enqueue).
- On pick: write `workflowCheckoutIdAtom` to the checkout id, set `workflowRepositoryIdAtom` to the parent repository id, clear custom `workingDirectory`, prefill `workflowBranchAtom` from the checkout's inspection unless the branch is user-dirty (`setWorkflowBranchByUserAtom` / `workflowBranchDirtyAtom`), then call `onSaveRunConfig` so the association is durable in `runConfigJson` (not Jotai-only). That unblocks enqueue (branch is required) and editor deep links (they need a resolved folder).
- Empty registry: disabled trigger + hint to register a checkout in Settings (same idea as the home composer CLI empty copy). Selected checkout missing from the loaded list: still show the selector so the user can re-associate (mirrors `selectedCheckoutMissing` on the Configuration selector).

## Out of scope

- Re-enabling the Configuration tab or page toolbar.
- Multi-select / extra context directories (`ChatCheckoutSelector.multiple`).
- Custom path / monorepo-root escape hatches — those stay on the full workspace selector.
- Changing enqueue resolution order or GraphQL.

## Verify

- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test` on the new mapper, wrapper, and `PlanDetailRoute` specs.
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint` on touched files.
- Browser: open a plan with no checkout, pick one, confirm the trigger shows name+branch, refresh keeps the association, Run/Queue and editor deep links un-block.
title: Add chat checkout selector to plan detail

author: visormatt
description:
## Symptom
Sending the FIRST message with the `cursor-agent` model hangs the chat composer. Workaround the user found: switch to another model, send a message, switch back to cursor-agent — then it works.

## Confirmed root cause
- Client fires the `startConversationStream` mutation and awaits it. The mutation awaits `resolveBackendRun` → `resolveCliSession` BEFORE returning.
- For the cursor backend only, `resolveCliSession` calls `await createCursorAgentSession({ cwd })` at `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.resolver.ts:611`, which spawns `cursor-agent create-chat` and blocks up to `DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/cursor-agent/teardown.ts:29`).
- Claude mints a `randomUUID()` instantly (resolver:633); codex/grok/opencode do not pre-mint (resolver:644-652). Cursor is the ONLY backend that blocks the mutation on a child process, because `buildCursorAgentArgv` hard-requires `--resume <sessionId>` (`.../cursor-agent/argv.ts`).
- The client stall watchdog only arms when `pendingAssistantId !== null` (`packages/react-router-chat/src/hooks/use-agentic-chat-turn.tsx:455-467`), and that id comes from the mutation result. So during the slow `create-chat`, no watchdog runs, no auto-retry fires, and the composer just hangs.
- On success the session id is persisted to `conversation.metadata` (resolver:621-626) and reused (resolver:602-606), so later turns skip the spawn — hence the switch-away/switch-back workaround.

## Not the cause (ruled out)
Model/driver discovery (`discoverAgentClis`/`discoverLocalModels`) runs in a loader with a 60s-TTL cached snapshot and is decoupled from the send path.

## Local debugging
1. Time the raw spawn: `time cursor-agent create-chat` — isolates cold-start/auth warmup latency the server inherits.
2. Add a temporary timing log around resolver:611; run an isolated server + developer app; send the first cursor message and observe mutation duration before the stream begins.
3. Devtools Network: the `startConversationStream` POST hangs for the full `create-chat` duration with no subscription activity, confirming the stall is in the mutation phase.

## Fix direction
Primary: get the cursor session mint OFF the mutation's blocking response path — mint lazily inside the fire-and-forget `runStream` (like other backends resume mid-stream), or return the assistant id immediately and mint before first output. Secondary/defense-in-depth: arm client progress + watchdog/recovery during the mutation-in-flight window so a slow mint can never present as a dead composer. Optional: pre-warm the cursor session on conversation open / model select so first-turn latency is hidden.
summary: Chat composer hangs on the FIRST message when the selected backend is cursor-agent. Root cause: startConversationStream awaits createCursorAgentSession (spawns `cursor-agent create-chat`, up to 30s) synchronously inside the mutation, before returning to the client. Cursor is the only backend that blocks the mutation on a child process; the client stall watchdog does not cover the mutation-in-flight phase, so there is no progress and no recovery. Switch-model → send → switch-back "works" because the session id is then persisted and reused, skipping the spawn.
title: Fix cursor-agent first-message chat hang (blocking create-chat mint)

author: visormatt
description:
There are ~50 local copies of the same type predicate:

```ts
const isRecord = (value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> =>
  typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
```

Call sites span openthrottle-developer, openthrottle-server, nestjs-*, react-router-*, agentic packages, node-client, nodejs-graphql, and tools. One already-exported copy lives in `@openthrottle/nestjs-testing` (`packages/nestjs-testing/src/utils/is-record.ts`) — the wrong home for production code.

## Where it belongs (decision)

**New `@openthrottle/nodejs-utils` package** (generator `--type=node`).

Rejected homes:
- `@openthrottle/nestjs-testing` — already exported, but it is a test helper package; production server/UI must not depend on it. Keep a re-export from nestjs-testing after the move so existing test imports keep working, then migrate callers.
- `@openthrottle/nestjs-utils` — NestJS-tagged, DataLoader/headers only, AGENTS.md says not a grab-bag; browser packages must not import it.
- `@openthrottle/react-router-utils` — React Router / Vite only; NestJS, agentic, and tools cannot take that dependency.
- `@openthrottle/nodejs-graphql` — GraphQL client; would couple unrelated packages to GraphQL.

Folder skill: this is a **nodejs** package (server/client agnostic, zero runtime deps). Give it a real `build` target and `exports` → `dist/` so `openthrottle-server` / NestJS Docker can import it (no `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING`).

Canonical name: `isRecord`. Aliases in the wild (`isPlainRecord`, `isPlainObject`, `isObjectRecord`, `isJsonObject`, `isObjectValue`) should import `isRecord` rather than keep local synonyms.

Leave domain-specific guards that *call* `isRecord` then check extra fields (e.g. `isWallClockMetrics` in parse-task-run-metrics) in place.

Test-only local copies in specs may stay local if importing the package would be awkward (e.g. isolated tools tests); prefer the shared export whenever the project already depends on `@openthrottle/nodejs-utils`.
title: Promote shared isRecord type guard

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

From a plan's detail page, one click should land the user in their editor of choice, in the right checkout, with the prompt to run that plan already typed. Today the only editor deep-links in the app are on `plans.create.tsx` via `PlanCreateEditorLinks` — open-folder only, no prompt, and not reachable from the plan you actually want to run.

Target shape (from the request):

```ts
const searchParams = new URLSearchParams({
  folder: '/home/demo/Development/openthrottle/',
  q: `/ot-claude-loop ${planId}`,
});
const href = `claude://code/new?${searchParams.toString()}`;
```

## Decisions already made

1. **Extend `WorkspaceEditorId` with `CLAUDE`** (rather than a developer-app-only launch catalog). The toolbar renders one button per editor the user enabled in workspace settings, so Claude must be a first-class editor id server-side. This also means OT will provision Claude config (`.mcp.json` + `.claude/`) for linked repos, consistent with Cursor/VS Code.
2. **Folder = the plan's run-config `workingDirectory`, falling back to the selected checkout/repository `filesystemPath`.** `usePlanDetailRoute` already exposes `workingDirectory` (from `workflowWorkingDirectoryAtom`) and the loader already selects `workspaceRepositories`. Render nothing when neither resolves — a missing link beats a dead one (same rule `PlanCreateEditorLinks` documents).

## Deep-link capability reality (researched, not assumed)

The three editors do **not** share a URL shape. The catalog must model capability, not just a scheme string:

| Editor | URL | folder? | prompt? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude | `claude://code/new?q=<prompt>&folder=<abs path>` | ✅ (confirmation dialog always shown; folders from links are untrusted) | ✅ `q` or `prompt`, truncated ~14,000 chars |
| Cursor | `cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/prompt?text=<prompt>` | ❌ not supported — lands in whatever window is focused | ✅ `text`, 8,000 char max |
| VS Code | `vscode://file<abs path>` (today's `editorHref`) | ✅ | ❌ no stable prompt param (microsoft/vscode#279701 still open) |

Consequences to encode in the design, not paper over:
- A single `scheme` string is no longer enough; `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_DEEP_LINKS` becomes a per-editor builder/capability record.
- Cursor's button cannot target a folder. Either omit Cursor from the toolbar, or ship it with a tooltip that says it prompts the active window. Pick one deliberately in task 3.
- VS Code's button is open-folder only — same behavior as `PlanCreateEditorLinks` has today. Do not fabricate a prompt param for it.
- All parameter values must be URL-encoded. `editorHref` already encodes path segments; the query-param builders must use `URLSearchParams`.

## Prompt text per editor

- Claude: `/ot-claude-loop <planId>` — the slash command must be the first thing on line 1 of the composed prompt.
- Cursor: no `/ot-claude-loop` equivalent; use plain text that names the skill file, e.g. `Run OpenThrottle plan <planId> following .agents/skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md`.
- VS Code: none.

## Files in scope (verified)

Server / package:
- `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/workspace-settings/workspace-editor-id.ts` — `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_IDS` is `['cursor','vscode']`.
- `.../workspace-editor-config-paths.ts` — exhaustive `Record<WorkspaceEditorId, …>`; needs a Claude entry.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/workspace-settings/workspace-editor-id.enum.ts` + `user-workspace-profile.mapper.ts` (`EDITOR_ID_TO_ENUM` is exhaustive).

Database: **no migration required.** `user_workspace_settings.enabled_editors` is `JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` (migration 042) with no CHECK constraint. A `COMMENT ON COLUMN` refresh is optional polish only.

Developer app — three exhaustive `Record<WorkspaceEditorId, …>` maps that will fail typecheck until updated (this is the intended tripwire):
- `app/global/config/workspace-editor-deep-links.ts`
- `app/routing/settings/config/workspace-editors.ts` (`WORKSPACE_EDITOR_OPTIONS`)
- `app/routing/settings/config/workspace-editor-affiliate-links.ts` (Claude → `null`)

Toolbar:
- `app/routing/plans/components/PlanToolbar.tsx` — `OpenThrottleToolbar` already has a `utilityContent` slot occupied by the "CLI preview and history" link; the new component goes alongside it (or gets its own slot — decide in task 4, don't silently overload).
- `app/routing/plans/components/PlanDetailRoute.tsx` / `hooks/usePlanDetailRoute.ts` — where `workingDirectory` and `workspaceRepositories` already live.
- `app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx.graphql` — must add `enabledEditors` to the plan-detail loader query (it selects `workspaceRepositories` but not the workspace profile).

## Note on the request

The prompt referenced `plans.$planId.edit.tsx` as the source of the existing editor links; the links actually live on `plans.create.tsx` via `PlanCreateEditorLinks`. The edit route renders only `PlanForm`. Work from `PlanCreateEditorLinks` as the reference implementation.

## Out of scope

- Changing `PlanCreateEditorLinks` behavior (it may later be refactored onto the shared builder, but the create page is slated for removal).
- Any prompt/deep-link support for the remaining agent CLI drivers (codex, gemini, grok, opencode) — those are execution backends, not editors.
summary: Add a PlanEditorActions component to the end of PlanToolbar rendering per-editor deep links (Claude, Cursor, VS Code) that open the plan's working directory with a prefilled /ot-claude-loop <planId> prompt. Adds CLAUDE to WorkspaceEditorId server-side so the buttons are gated on the user's enabled editors.
title: PlanEditorActions: one-click "open this plan in my editor" deep links

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The chat composer's repository control (`ChatCheckoutSelector`) renders a flat `DropdownMenu` of `displayName` strings and nothing else. A user with checkouts named `monorepo`, `native-apps`, `nativeapps`, `openthrottle`, `OpenThrottle-.github`, … across multiple GitHub orgs cannot tell which row is which: there is no owner/org, no path, no branch, no search, and no grouping. Picking the wrong one silently spawns the agent in the wrong working directory.

The data to fix this is already on the server. `WorkspaceLocalRepositoryObject` exposes `filesystemPath`, `gitRemoteUrl`, `gitDefaultBranch`, `projectId`/`project`; the developer app's `WorkspaceLocalRepositories` query already selects `filesystemPath` — and `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/models.server.ts` throws it away, because the shared `RepositoryOption` contract in `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/utils/chat-discovery-options.ts` is only `{ displayName, id }`. So v1 is a client-side widening, not a server change.

## Shape of the fix

1. Widen `RepositoryOption` / `ChatCheckoutOption` to carry identity: `filesystemPath`, `remoteUrl`, derived `{ host, owner, name }`, `projectName`, and the existing optional `branch`.
2. Add a browser-safe pure parser that turns a git remote URL into `{ host, owner, name }` — the client twin of `normalizeRemoteUrl` in `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/repositories/normalize-remote-url.ts`. It must handle `git@`/`ssh://`/`https://`, self-hosted hosts, and nested GitLab groups, and return `null` for provisional local-only repos (which fall back to a shortened `filesystemPath`).
3. Replace the flat `DropdownMenu` with a `Command`-based searchable picker (`packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/Command`), grouped by owner/org, each row showing name + `owner/repo` (or shortened path) + branch, with an unambiguous trigger label.
4. Disambiguation must be *content-aware*: when two visible options share a `displayName`, the qualifier is promoted (trigger shows `owner/name`), and a duplicate group is never collapsed.

## Constraints and gotchas

- **Compose with the unmerged multi-repo work.** `feat/chat-multi-repo-select` (OT `98e6c5a3`, draft PR #445) turns this control into primary-checkout + N additional directories with `repositoryIds: readonly string[]` (toolbar atom schema v4). This plan is written against that shape and should be branched off `feat/chat-multi-repo-select` (or rebased once it lands). Do not re-litigate single vs multi select.
- The package is presentational and **hardcodes no repositories** — everything arrives through props. Keep it that way.
- `react-router-chat` / `react-router-chat-state` are **source-first packages with no `build` target**; validate with lint/typecheck/test and then `openthrottle-developer:build` as the integration check.
- Both `openthrottle-developer` and `openthrottle-admin` consume `chat-discovery-options.ts`; the admin discovery query selects fewer fields, so every new `RepositoryOption` field must be optional and degrade to today's behavior.
- A third consumer reads the toolbar atom beyond the two composers: `useRunSkillDialog` (skills route), deliberately single-select.
- Repo rules: no enums (`as const`), no `as` casts, `import type`, explicit return types, alphabetized keys, `component` (not `screen`) + `userEvent` in tests, `@public` JSDoc on package exports for Knip, and the component line cap is checked **after** prettier reformats.

## Out of scope (follow-ups, not this plan)

- Server-side changes to `WorkspaceLocalRepositoryObject` (e.g. exposing the *current* branch rather than `gitDefaultBranch` — the live branch lives on `RepositoryCheckoutObject.inspection.git` / `discoveredWorktrees`).
- Reusing the picker in `ScheduleRepositoryField`, `PlanWorkflowConfigWorkspaceSelector`, and the IDE workspace body — worth doing, but after this one proves out.
- Repo-qualified `@`-mentions across multiple repositories (already tracked from #445).
summary: Rebuild the composer's checkout picker as a searchable, grouped, self-disambiguating list so look-alike repos (several "monorepo" checkouts across different orgs) are tellable apart at a glance.
title: Disambiguate the repository selector in the chat composer

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Re-org the openthrottle-developer **Schedule** UI feature to **Calendar**: URLs (`/schedule/*` → `/calendar/*`), React Router route modules, `app/routing/schedule` feature folder, and `Schedule*` symbols → `Calendar*`.

This is a **naming / IA rename only** — keep behavior, demo data, and layouts intact unless a rename forces a small import/path fix.

## Out of scope

- **`/scheduled-jobs/*`** and `app/routing/scheduled-jobs/**` — different feature; do not rename or move.
- GraphQL / server / DB schema changes (none expected for this UI rename).
- Product redesign of the calendar UX.

## Current surface (developer app)

### Routes (`app/routes/`)
- `schedule._index.tsx` → `/schedule`
- `schedule.calendar.tsx` → `/schedule/calendar`
- `schedule.create.tsx` → `/schedule/create`
- `schedule.$eventId.tsx` → `/schedule/:eventId`
- Co-located route tests under `app/routes/__tests__/schedule*.test.tsx`

### Feature folder (`app/routing/schedule/`)
- Components: `ScheduleIntroduction`, `ScheduleToolbar`, `ScheduleTable`, `ScheduleCalendar`, `ScheduleForm`, `ScheduleEmpty`, `ScheduleEventCard`, `ScheduleEventDetails` (+ `__tests__`)
- Data: `data.copy.ts`, `data.events.ts`, `data.calendar-demo.ts`
- Utils: `events.ts`, `formatters.ts`; `types.ts`

### App wiring that still says Schedule / `/schedule`
- `app/global/data/data.navigation.ts` (nav label + `to: '/schedule'`)
- `app/routing/navigation/data/workspace-jump-links.ts`
- `app/global/hooks/useCommanderOptions.tsx` (commented nav entry)
- Breadcrumbs / meta titles in route modules (`Schedule | …`)
- Copy under `routing/schedule/data/data.copy.ts`

## Target shape

| From | To |
| --- | --- |
| `/schedule` | `/calendar` |
| `/schedule/calendar` | `/calendar` or `/calendar/month` (decide during rename — avoid awkward `/calendar/calendar`) |
| `/schedule/create` | `/calendar/create` |
| `/schedule/:eventId` | `/calendar/:eventId` |
| `app/routes/schedule.*` | `app/routes/calendar.*` |
| `app/routing/schedule/` | `app/routing/calendar/` |
| `Schedule*` components / helpers / copy keys | `Calendar*` equivalents |

## Constraints

- Generators-first if scaffolding any *new* files; prefer `git mv` / rename for existing ones.
- Preserve section-comment scaffold and component/data boundaries.
- Update tests to import from new paths; assert against `data.copy.ts` constants, not duplicated literals.
- Add **legacy redirects** from `/schedule` and `/schedule/*` → `/calendar` equivalents so bookmarks do not 404.
- Run `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint` and `:test` for affected suites; regenerate React Router types if the app expects codegen for `+types/`.
- Commit per task with `Plan-Id` / `Task-Id` footers when executing.

## Success criteria

- No remaining `/schedule` (non–scheduled-jobs) navigations or imports in the developer app.
- Feature live under `/calendar/*` with renamed Calendar* surface.
- Legacy `/schedule/*` redirects work.
- Tests green for calendar routes/components.
summary: Schedule → Calendar rename shipped in developer app: /calendar month index, /calendar/list table, create/detail routes, full Calendar* rename, legacy /schedule redirects. Left uncommitted for Matt to review/commit.
title: Rename developer Schedule feature to Calendar

author: visormatt
description:
Two small, UI-only improvements to the OpenThrottle Developer workspace settings (`/settings/workspace`), both in `applications/openthrottle-developer`:

## 1. Close the "Add folder" dialog after a successful add
Today `WorkspaceAddFolderDialog` (`app/routing/settings/components/WorkspaceAddFolderDialog.tsx`) drives its open state from `useWorkspaceAddFolderDialog` (`app/routing/settings/hooks/useWorkspaceAddFolderDialog.tsx`). The add flow calls `useSubmit()` with `intent: 'addFolder'`, which re-runs the route loader and renders the `WorkspaceAddFolderResult` card on the page (in `SettingsWorkspaceRepositoriesSection`, outside the dialog). Nothing closes the dialog, so it stays open on top of the result. We want it to close automatically once the add succeeds.

Approach: in the hook, track the falling edge of `isAdding` (was submitting `addFolder`, now idle) and call `setOpen(false)` — but only on success, not on error. The dialog already receives an `actionError` prop; thread that (or an explicit success signal) into the hook so a failed add keeps the dialog open with its error visible. Don't reset the picker's browse state prematurely.

## 2. Surface the stack / agent-config tags on the repository detail route
The `WorkspaceAddFolderResult` card (`app/routing/settings/components/WorkspaceAddFolderResult.tsx`) derives two useful badge groups from `checkout.inspection`:
- **Stack**: Nx, pnpm workspace, Turbo, package manager, languages (`inspection.stack`)
- **Agent config**: `.mcp.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules`, `skills` (`inspection.agentConfig`)

That information disappears once you navigate away. The repository detail route (`/settings/workspace/repositories/:repositoryId`, component `WorkspaceRepositoryDetail`) already loads the full `RepositoryCheckoutFields` fragment — including `inspection.stack` and `inspection.agentConfig` — so no GraphQL/schema/codegen change is needed. We want to render these same Stack + Agent config badges on the detail view (per checkout).

To avoid duplicating the derivation logic, extract the current inline badge-building code from `WorkspaceAddFolderResult` into a shared, presentation-free util (e.g. `app/routing/settings/utils/checkout-inspection-badges.ts`) returning `{ detectedStack, detectedAgentConfig }`, and consume it from both `WorkspaceAddFolderResult` and `WorkspaceRepositoryDetail`.

## Scope / constraints
- UI only — no GraphQL document, schema, or codegen changes; the detail route's fragment already has the fields.
- Follow the component/hook shape conventions (section comments, presentation-free hooks/utils, one component per file, `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` `Badge`).
- Keep copy strings in the nearest `data.copy.ts` (WORKSPACE_REPOSITORY_DETAIL_COPY) rather than inline.
- Validate with `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, and `:test`; fresh worktrees need codegen first.
- Optional parity note (not required): `WorkspaceCloneRepoDialog` has the same "stays open after success" behavior and could reuse the same close-on-success pattern — call out if in-scope.
title: Workspace add-folder: close dialog on success + surface stack/agent-config tags on repository detail

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Creating a note on the Developer app `/notes/create` route asks for a free-text "Author (optional)" input, and `createNote` persists whatever string arrives (or `null`). Result: notes created through the UI are usually authorless, and when an author IS present it is unverified typing rather than the identity of the person who created it.

We already know who the caller is on every authenticated request:
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/auth/global-cls-auth-hook.service.ts` loads the user row and calls `globalCls.setUser({ displayName: row.githubUsername, email, uuid: row.id, ... })`.
- `@openthrottle/nestjs-auth`'s `@CurrentUser()` exposes the `AuthPrincipal` (`sub`, optional `email`, `kind`).
- OT convention (CLAUDE.md): author/assignee fields hold the **GitHub username**, which is exactly `users.github_username` / the CLS `displayName`.

## Goal

When a note is created and no explicit author is supplied, the server stamps `author` from the authenticated principal. The Developer create form stops collecting author and instead shows who the note will be attributed to.

## Design decisions

1. **Server-side derivation is authoritative.** Deriving in the resolver (not the React Router action) means every caller gets it — Developer UI, `openthrottle-mcp` `create_note`, raw GraphQL — and the client can't spoof attribution by omitting the field.
2. **Explicit `author` in `CreateNoteInput` still wins.** `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/tools/notes.ts` documents `create_note` as taking an optional author (e.g. `visormatt`), and its tests assert that pass-through. Keep the field, keep it nullable, and only fall back to the principal when it is absent/blank. This keeps the MCP surface and its tests unchanged.
3. **Source of the derived value:** `GlobalClsService.get('user')?.displayName` — already the `githubUsername` for human principals, and the service-account name for machine principals. Preferred over a fresh `UsersService.findById(principal.sub)` lookup because it is per-request cached and already the canonical display identity. Fall back to `principal.email`, then `principal.sub`, then `null` if there is no user in CLS (public/pre-auth paths — the resolver's `@authz-stance` is authenticated-only, so this should be unreachable, but do not throw).
4. **`updateNote` is untouched.** The detail route's edit form deliberately treats a blank author as "clear to null"; stamping the editor there would silently rewrite authorship. Out of scope.
5. **No schema/DB migration.** `notes.author` stays `text NULL`; `NoteObject.author` stays `String`. No GraphQL breaking change, so no `@deprecated` dance.

## Non-goals

- Turning `author` into a FK to `users` (a real identity relation) — worth doing eventually, but it is a migration + resolver + UI change well beyond "use the current user on create".
- Backfilling `author` on existing authorless notes.
- Changing how the notes index/table or detail header renders authors.

## Files in play

- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/notes/notes.resolver.ts` (+ `notes.resolver.test.ts`)
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/notes/notes-graphql.module.ts` (only if a provider import is needed)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/notes/components/NoteForm.tsx` (+ `__tests__/NoteForm.test.tsx`)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/notes.create.tsx` (+ `app/routes/__tests__/`)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/notes.create.tsx.graphql` only if the document changes (it should not)

## Validation

```
pnpm nx run openthrottle-server:test -- src/graphql/notes/notes.resolver.test.ts
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test -- app/routing/notes
pnpm nx run openthrottle-mcp:test
pnpm nx affected --target=lint,typecheck --parallel
```

Manual: log in to the Developer app, create a note with no author, confirm the row/detail shows the logged-in user's GitHub username.
summary: Stop asking for a free-text author when creating a note: default NoteObject.author from the request principal (githubUsername via GlobalCls) server-side, and drop the author input from the create form.
title: Notes: derive note author from the authenticated user on create

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

A `/skills/create` route where you author a new `SKILL.md` in `@openthrottle/react-router-editor`, seeded with the required frontmatter, and save it to one of two destinations: your **personal tier** (private, uncommittable) or the **repo** (`skills/`, to be committed and PR'd).

## What already exists — do not rebuild it

- **Write path + guards.** `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/write-skill-file.server.ts` is the edit-side precedent: null-monorepo-root refusal, realpath containment guard, `validateAgentAssetFrontmatter({ kind: 'skill', expectedSlug })` before touching disk, structured `{ ok: false, error }` refusals. Create reuses the *shape*, not the function — `writeSkillFileBySlug` requires an already-discovered entry and refuses anything that is not `source: 'openthrottle'`.
- **Frontmatter contract.** `skillFrontmatterSchema` in `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/schemas/agent-asset-frontmatter.schemas.ts` is `.strict()`: `name` (kebab-case, must equal the directory slug), `description` (required, non-empty), optional `tags` (kebab-case array), optional `disable-model-invocation`. No other keys are legal — the seeded scaffold must not invent any.
