- **Editor usage.** `@openthrottle/react-router-editor` is already an `openthrottle-developer` dependency and already mounted for skills in `app/routing/skills/components/SkillDetail.tsx`. `EditorWindow` needs **both** `path` and `value` (README: swapping `value` without `path` bleeds undo/redo across models). Monaco loader/worker config is the app's job and is already done — do not re-add it.
- **Create-form precedent.** `app/routes/prompts.create.tsx` + `app/routing/prompts/hooks/usePromptCreateForm.ts` + `PromptCreateForm.tsx` is the exact route shape to mirror (thin route adapter, draft state in a hook, ⌘S submit). That one posts to GraphQL; this one writes to disk.
- **Personal tier is shipped.** `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/personal.sh new|list|promote|demote`, root `~/.openthrottle/skills` overridable via `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_DIR`, must live outside the repo, links are gitignored and blocked from staging by a Husky gate.

## The finding that shapes the action

**Writing the file is not enough to make the skill exist.** `discover-repo-skills.server.ts` scans `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.grok/skills`, `.opencode/skills` — it does **not** scan `skills/`, and it does not scan the personal root directly. Both destinations only become visible after `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh` links them into `.agents/skills/`. So a create action that only calls `writeFileSync` produces a file that never appears on `/skills` — the feature would look broken on its own success screen.

There is currently **zero** `child_process` / `execSync` / `spawnSync` usage anywhere in `openthrottle-developer`, so running sync from a route action introduces the app's first subprocess. Task 1 settles that before anything is built.

## Scope decision: no git, no PR, in this plan

The ask says the repo destination is "to be committed and in a PR". This plan takes that as describing *where the file lands and what happens to it next*, and stops at a correct file on disk plus a synced, discoverable skill. Driving `git` and `gh` from a route action is a materially different, privileged surface (branch creation, staging, push credentials, remote state) and deserves its own plan rather than riding along here. The success state should hand over the exact next commands. **If you want the PR automated in this same effort, say so and it becomes a fifth task** — the seam (a `.server.ts` module already shelling out, per task 1) will be in place either way.

Also out of scope: editing existing skills (already shipped on `/skills/$slug`), tag-vocabulary or availability wiring for the new skill, and DB ingest — `projectSkills` refreshes on the next ingest run, exactly as the edit path documents.

## Verification

`/skills/create` must beat `skills.$slug` in flat-route matching (static segment wins, but confirm — a regression here 404s or renders the detail page). End with the real thing: create a skill in each destination, confirm it appears in the `/skills` list under the right source badge (`Personal` vs `OpenThrottle`), and confirm `sync.sh --check` still passes and `git status` shows an uncommitted `skills/<slug>/` for the repo case and **nothing** for the personal case.
summary: New /skills/create route that authors a SKILL.md in the react-router-editor from a seeded frontmatter scaffold, and writes it to either the personal tier (~/.openthrottle/skills) or the repo (skills/), then syncs so it is discoverable.
title: Create-a-skill route: /skills/create

author: visormatt
description:
# Target a repository for /schedule runs

## Problem

A scheduled agent job (`/schedule` in openthrottle-developer, `scheduled_agent_jobs` in Postgres) has no notion of *which repository* it runs against. The only targeting knob is a free-text `cwd` column:

- `databases/migrations/082_create_scheduled_agent_jobs.sql` — `cwd TEXT NULL`, "Process cwd for the agent CLI; null falls back to WORKSPACE_ROOT ?? process.cwd()".
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.constants.ts` — `resolveScheduledAgentJobCwd()` (explicit cwd → `WORKSPACE_ROOT` → `process.cwd()`).
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/schedule/components/ScheduleForm.tsx` — a bare `Working directory (optional)` text input, placeholder "Defaults to the workspace root".

Consequences: the user must know and hand-type an absolute host path; the path is never validated or ownership-checked; it is not host/container aware; nothing ties a run to a repository for provenance; and every schedule silently defaults to the one canonical checkout (which is also why `SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY = 1` — two CLIs in one cwd would fight over the git index).

The streaming chat path already solved exactly this. `StartConversationStreamInput.repositoryId` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.input.ts`) takes a registered repository checkout id, and the resolver (`conversation-stream.resolver.ts` ~L476-500) resolves it via `repositories.findByIdForUser(repositoryId, userId)` → `toContainerPath(repository.filesystemPath)`, requires a repository in production, and keeps a `DEV_CWD_ENV` escape hatch for development. **/schedule should adopt that same model.**

## Goal

Let a scheduled job target a registered repository checkout by id, resolve the cwd server-side from that checkout (ownership-checked, container-path-aware), snapshot the resolved path on each run for provenance, and replace the free-text working-directory input with a repository picker — without breaking existing rows that only carry `cwd`.

## Design

**Data model** (`repository_checkouts` from migration 078 is the target; `workspace_local_repositories` is the deprecated view over it):

- `scheduled_agent_jobs.repository_checkout_id UUID NULL REFERENCES repository_checkouts (id) ON DELETE SET NULL` + index. Nullable so existing rows lift cleanly.
- `cwd` stays, re-commented as the legacy/explicit-path fallback, and is deprecated in GraphQL (`@deprecated`, never removed — CLAUDE.md schema rule).
- Runs get provenance: `scheduled_agent_job_runs.repository_checkout_id UUID NULL` (ON DELETE SET NULL) and `resolved_cwd TEXT NULL`, so a run's history survives a later schedule edit or checkout deletion. Sibling of the existing `settings_snapshot` column from migration 087.

**Resolution precedence** (one shared helper, documented in one place):
1. `repository_checkout_id` → checkout `filesystem_path` → `toContainerPath(...)` (from `@openthrottle/openthrottle-agentic-utils`; identity on host-run flows, mount-aware under a containerized server — mirrors `workspace-editor-config.service` and the chat resolver).
2. explicit `cwd` (legacy rows / power users).
3. `WORKSPACE_ROOT` → `process.cwd()` (today's behavior, kept so nothing regresses).

**Where resolution happens.** The BullMQ payload is a self-contained snapshot built at scheduler-upsert / run-now time (`buildScheduledAgentJobPayload` in `scheduled-agent-job-scheduler.service.ts`), so it must carry both `repositoryCheckoutId` and the resolved `cwd`. Because a scheduler payload can be arbitrarily stale (a checkout can move or be removed months after upsert), the processor re-resolves from `repositoryCheckoutId` when present and treats the payload path as fallback — one indexed read per run, and a moved checkout keeps working.

**Ownership.** Resolve against the schedule's `owner_user_id` (already on the row) using the same `findByIdForUser` check the chat path uses, and validate at write time in the GraphQL service so a bad or foreign checkout id fails at create/update rather than at 3am.

**Concurrency.** Note (do not change) that `SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY = 1` exists because of shared-cwd git-index contention. Per-repository targeting makes raising it *possible*, but that needs per-repo keyed concurrency — explicitly out of scope, captured as a follow-up.

## Non-goals

- Raising worker concurrency or per-repository queue partitioning.
- Auto-provisioning a worktree per run (`settings.worktree` already exists; untouched).
- Removing `cwd` from the schema or GraphQL.
- Repository targeting for Ralph plan runs (tracked separately with the run-provenance work).

## Acceptance

- A schedule can be created and edited with a repository picked from the user's registered checkouts; no path typing required.
- The agent CLI actually spawns in that checkout's directory (verified in run output).
- Existing `cwd`-only schedules keep running unchanged.
- A run row records the repository and the exact resolved cwd; the run detail page shows both.
- Picking a foreign or unknown checkout id is rejected at write time with a clear message.
- `pnpm run check:local` green; `schema.gql` + `__generated__` committed.
summary: Let a scheduled job target a registered repository checkout by id instead of a hand-typed cwd: FK on scheduled_agent_jobs, server-side ownership-checked + container-aware cwd resolution, per-run provenance snapshot, and a repository picker in ScheduleForm. Mirrors the chat path's repositoryId model.
title: Target a repository for scheduled agent job (/schedule) runs

author: visormatt
description:
Make the developer-app command palette (⌘K / OpenThrottleCommander) consume the same navigation source of truth as the global sidebar, instead of a hardcoded subset in useCommanderOptions.

## Problem

`root.tsx` already feeds `GlobalLayout` from `dataNavigationV2` / `dataNavigationGuest` (`app/global/data/data.navigation.ts`). Commander groups come from a separate hardcoded list in `useCommanderOptions()`:

- Only five destinations today: Dashboard, Plans, Projects, Queues, Notes — missing Skills, Rules, Schedule, Usage, Settings/*, Docs, FAQ, Chats, and everything else already in the sidebar.
- Different icons than the sidebar (e.g. Plans uses MapIcon in the palette vs NotebookTextIcon in nav).
- Single "Navigation" heading vs sidebar groups Agents / Settings / Workspace (and Legal for guests).
- Ignores `disabled` and `beta` flags that `GlobalSidebarContent` already honors (`FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW` hides beta; `disabled` is muted unless `FEATURE_CHARLIE_PREVIEW`).
- Always uses the authenticated list, even when `GlobalLayout` is on `dataNavigationGuest`.

Adding a sidebar link today does not add a ⌘K row. That split will keep drifting.

## Goal

One navigation record drives both the sidebar and commander groups. Adding, disabling, or beta-flagging a link in `data.navigation.ts` is enough for both surfaces.

## Approach

1. **Pure mapper** (new util under `app/global/utils/`, not inlined in the hook): `Record<string, GlobalSidebarContentLinkProps[]>` → `CommanderGroup[]`.
   - Group heading = navigation section key (Agents, Settings, Workspace, Legal).
   - Item: `label` from string `children`, `onSelect` via `navigate(to)`, same lucide icon at commander size (`h-3! w-3!`).
   - Stable `id` from path (`nav-dashboard`, `nav-settings-agents`); special-case `to: '/'` (Chats) so it is not an empty slug.
   - Set `CommanderItem.value` to include label + path so cmdk filter matches "plans", "settings", or "/plans", not only the id.
   - Omit empty groups after filtering.
2. **Filter to match sidebar visibility**
   - Drop `beta: true` unless `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW`.
   - Drop `disabled: true` unless `FEATURE_CHARLIE_PREVIEW` (cmdk has no good "visible but unclickable" state; omitting is the palette equivalent of `pointer-events-none`).
3. **`useCommanderOptions` takes the same record `GlobalLayout` gets.** Root picks once: `const navigation = data?.user ? dataNavigationV2 : dataNavigationGuest` and passes it to both. Do not re-branch on auth inside the hook.
4. **Leave commander-only extras alone.** Empty-state UUID/search rows (`commander-empty-extras`) and the commented Actions group (Create plan / Create project) stay out of this mapper. Re-enable Actions later as a separate optional group if needed.
5. **No shared-package change unless required.** `CommanderItem` already has `onSelect` / `icon` / `value`. Do not add `disabled` to `@openthrottle/react-router-ui` just to hide rows — filter in the app mapper.

## Out of scope

- Empty-state extras, `commander-search` POST jumps, header search chrome.
- Keyboard shortcuts per item.
- Uncommenting the Actions group.
- Changing `data.navigation.ts` destinations themselves (this plan consumes it, does not redesign IA).

## Acceptance

- Authenticated ⌘K groups match enabled, non-beta (or beta-when-flag-on) entries in `dataNavigationV2`, grouped as Agents / Settings / Workspace.
- Guest ⌘K groups match `dataNavigationGuest`.
- Selecting a row navigates to that link's `to`.
- Adding a sidebar link in `data.navigation.ts` appears in the palette with no second list to update.
- Tests treat `data.navigation.ts` as SSOT (assert mapper output against the imported nav data + flags, not a duplicated id list).
- `docs/commander-and-search-entrypoints.md` updated so `useCommanderOptions` is described as derived from navigation data.
title: Derive OpenThrottleCommander groups from data.navigation

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

The /usage route's "Top skills" leaderboard (`UsageSkillUsage.tsx`, heading copy `SKILL_USAGE_COPY.leaderboardHeading`) is a dead end: every row is plain text. A developer who spots a skill that is heavily used, slow, or erroring has no way to jump to that skill, and `/skills/$slug` — which today loads only the on-disk SKILL.md (`readSkillFileBySlug`) — shows no usage signal at all. Usage analysis and skill authoring are the same loop, split across two disconnected screens.

## Primary user

Human developer in the openthrottle-developer app (skill author/maintainer). Secondary: agent operator judging whether an authored skill is actually being invoked and succeeding.

## Outcome

1. Each "Top skills" row links to `/skills/$slug` when a matching on-disk skill exists.
2. `/skills/$slug` renders a new usage component with that skill's stats over the last 30 days.

## Key constraints discovered during scoping

- **Not every usage row has a detail page.** `skillName` on skill_usage events includes third-party/plugin-namespaced ids (e.g. `vercel:deploy`); `/skills/$slug` slugs come from disk discovery (`discoverRepoSkills` → frontmatter `name` or folder name) under `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.opencode/skills`. Link ONLY names that match a discovered slug; unmatched rows stay plain text (no hopeful links into 404s). Slugs containing `:` must be `encodeURIComponent`-ed in the `to`.
- **No per-skill server query exists.** `skillUsage(start, end, scope, gitBranch, cwd)` returns whole-range aggregates. Filtering client-side would give the detail route a bySkill row but no per-skill daily series — add an optional `skillName` arg to the existing query instead of a new query.
- **`/skills/$slug` has no GraphQL today** — its `.graphql` document file is empty and the loader is filesystem-only. The `skillUsage` query is guarded by `SETTINGS_READ`; a user without that permission must still get the SKILL.md view (degrade to a notice, never a 500).
- **Load order matters.** The detail route already streams `runOptions` as a naked promise so the shell paints immediately; per-skill usage should follow the same deferred pattern.
- Recharts renders no geometry under jsdom (see `UsageSkillUsageChart`) — tests assert wrapper/markup, not ticks.

## Non-goals (v1)

- Per-skill filters (branch/cwd/scope) on the detail route — the /usage route keeps ownership of filtering.
- Range picker on the detail route; fixed 30-day window matching /usage.
- Backfilling usage for skills that no longer exist on disk.
summary: Make the /usage "Top skills" leaderboard clickable through to /skills/$slug, and add a per-skill usage stats component on the skill detail route (same aggregates as the leaderboard, plus last-used and a 30-day series), backed by a new optional skillName filter on the skillUsage GraphQL query.
title: Skill usage drill-down: link Top skills to /skills/$slug and surface per-skill stats

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

On `/settings/workspace`, the "Add a folder" dialog's Browse control does not feel like folder selection. Today (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/WorkspaceAddFolderDialog.tsx`, `.../hooks/useWorkspaceAddFolderDialog.tsx`, `.../actions/workspace.ts` → `browseDirectory`, server `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/workspace-settings/workspace-folders.{resolver,service}.ts`):

- The Browse control is a **text input**: the user must type an absolute server-host path before anything happens, then click "Browse" to list immediate subdirectories.
- Navigation is **drill-down only** — no seed/default path, no breadcrumb, no "up one level", and no way to add the folder you are currently *inside* (only its listed children).
- Entries carry **no signal** for which are git repositories or already registered.
- The whole Browse block is visually secondary, buried under discovered folders and the manual-path escape hatch.

## Key constraint (design-defining)

Workspace folders live on the **openthrottle-server host**, not the browser. Browser folder pickers (`<input type="file" webkitdirectory>`, `window.showDirectoryPicker()`) intentionally **do not expose absolute filesystem paths** — only folder names / relative subpaths — so they cannot produce a usable server path even on localhost. Therefore the "native OS folder dialog" path must be a **server-side** OS picker (macOS `osascript -e 'choose folder'`, Linux `zenity --file-selection --directory` / `kdialog`, Windows PowerShell `FolderBrowserDialog`) that returns the chosen absolute host path, gated behind a **same-machine / localhost** capability check. When the server is remote (or headless / no display), fall back to the improved in-app server-side directory picker.

## Chosen direction (user decision)

**Both, with fallback:**
1. **Native path** — server-side OS folder dialog when server==same machine as the browser; the dialog opens on the user's own screen and returns an absolute host path that flows straight into `addWorkspaceFolder`.
2. **In-app fallback** — a real interactive directory picker built on the existing `browseDirectory` infra: seeded from configured workspace roots (or home), breadcrumb + up-navigation (allowlist-guarded), select-the-current-folder, and per-entry `isGitRepo` / `alreadyRegistered` annotations.

## Constraints & conventions

- Code-first GraphQL in `openthrottle-server`; after schema changes run the server to regenerate `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel` and commit `__generated__`.
- Reuse the existing allowlist guard in `browseDirectory` (must resolve under `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKSPACE_ROOTS`); keep the same path-safety posture (`realpathSync`, absolute-path + NUL checks, symlink-resolved root containment) on any new resolver.
- Native picker resolver must never hang the request: bounded timeout, clean cancel (user dismisses dialog → no error toast, just no-op), and hard-disable when headless / no display / not same-machine.
- Permissions: read capabilities under `SETTINGS_READ`; the native pick + `addWorkspaceFolder` remain `SETTINGS_WRITE`.
- UI from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; keep the component/hook split (component-primitive-shape R6/R7) and section comments; copy in `data.copy.ts`.
- Tests: server service/resolver Vitest; client hook + dialog render tests using `component` + `userEvent`. Gate with typecheck + lint + test + build on `openthrottle-developer` and `openthrottle-server`.

## Out of scope

- Electron/desktop-shell native dialogs (no desktop shell today).
- Clone-repo flow changes (separate surface).
- Multi-select add.
summary: Rework the /settings/workspace "Add a folder" Browse flow so the Browse button actually launches folder selection — a native OS folder dialog when openthrottle-server runs on the same machine as the browser, falling back to an improved in-app server-side directory picker (seeded roots, breadcrumb + up-navigation, select-current-folder, git-repo/already-registered annotations) otherwise.
title: Fix & improve the Add-folder Browse flow (native + in-app server directory picker)

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Take the `# 👨‍💻 Agent CLIs (skip if present; otherwise prompt)` block in [scripts/setup_software.sh](scripts/setup_software.sh:75) — the `installCliIfNeeded` calls for claude / cursor-agent / codex / grok / opencode — and lift it into the OpenThrottle stack so an operator can **check → install → update** each CLI from the server, triggered from the developer app. New route: `/settings/setup`. Finite allowlist, so per-CLI we show: installed (with version) / not installed → Install, or Update.

## What already exists (reuse, don't rebuild)

- **Driver registry** `@openthrottle/openthrottle-drivers` → `ALL_DRIVERS` is the single source of truth for the CLI allowlist (`id`, `binary`, `binEnv`, `versionArgs`, `label`, `capabilities`). Driver modules: [packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/*.ts](packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/claude.ts), type in [types/index.ts](packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts), `defineDriver` in [registry/index.ts](packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/registry/index.ts). Install URLs do NOT live here yet — today they only exist inline in setup_software.sh.
- **Discovery** `discoverAgentClis` in [packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/agent-discovery.ts](packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/agent-discovery.ts) — derived from `ALL_DRIVERS`, probes availability + `--version` + models. This IS the "check" step, free.
- **Server** `agent-discovery` GraphQL module: [service](applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/agent-discovery.service.ts) (SWR cache, 60s TTL), [object](applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/agent-discovery.object.ts), [resolver](applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/agent-discovery.resolver.ts) (query `discoverAgentClis`, `@Permissions(PERMISSIONS.SETTINGS_READ)`). Add the install/update mutations here (or a sibling `agent-setup` module).
- **Developer app** settings routes are flat (`settings.mcp.tsx`, `settings.rollout._index.tsx`, …); nav entries in [app/global/data/data.navigation.ts](applications/openthrottle-developer/app/global/data/data.navigation.ts:155) under `Settings`. Live-output streaming precedent: `resources.conversation-stream.tsx` + graphql-ws.

## Phasing / shippability

The **read-only status view is unblocked** — it renders entirely from the existing `discoverAgentClis` query (SETTINGS_READ) and can ship without any of the security decisions below. So `/settings/setup` lands first as a "which CLIs are installed + version" page (task 5), and the **install/update controls are a gated add-on** (tasks 3–4, 6) layered on once task 1's owner gate clears. Tasks split accordingly so the security surface never blocks shipping the status page.

## Core design decisions (locked in task 1)

1. **Install metadata belongs on the driver registry** (leaf, dep-free) as an optional `install`/`update` descriptor, so setup_software.sh and the server both derive from ONE source and can't drift. All 5 agent CLIs are `curl | shell` installers today (the brew items — openjdk, terraform, maestro — are NOT agent CLIs and are OUT of scope). So v1 only needs a `curl-shell` method: `{ url, installerShell: 'bash' | 'sh' }`. Update = re-run installer, unless a CLI has a real self-update subcommand (research per CLI: `claude update`, codex/grok/opencode/cursor equivalents).
2. **The confirmation moves to the UI.** The shell's interactive `read confirm_install` prompt is dropped; installers must run non-interactively. The Install/Update button IS the confirm.
3. **Security surface = the human gate.** Running `curl -fsSL <url> | bash` on the server host is effectively remote-code-execution-on-demand. It must be: (a) locked to registry-defined commands for an allowlisted backend — the mutation takes only a `backend` string validated against `ALL_DRIVERS`, never a URL/command from the client; (b) gated behind a WRITE permission (SETTINGS_WRITE or a dedicated `AGENT_SETUP_MANAGE`), not SETTINGS_READ; (c) gated behind an env/feature flag, DEFAULT-OFF for hosted/multi-tenant deploys — this is a local-developer-machine feature. This is the owner-judgment gate and blocks the install/update tasks (2–4, 6), NOT the read-only status view (task 5).
4. **Execution model:** install/update is long-running with streamed output. Decide sync-mutation-returns-runId + graphql-ws subscription (mirror conversation-stream) vs a BullMQ job. Invalidate the discovery SWR cache on success so the UI re-reflects state. Watch the PATH gotcha: installers drop binaries in ~/.local/bin (or similar) — the server process's PATH must include the install target dir or post-install discovery won't see the new binary.

## Out of scope
- brew packages / maestro / python software in setup_software.sh.
- Auth/login for each CLI (install ≠ authenticated). Note it but don't build it.

## Validation
`pnpm run check:local`; regen + commit `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` and all `__generated__` after schema changes (server:dev boot → codegen → commit). Scaffold the route/components via `@tools/generators` (react-router), don't hand-write.
summary: Move the "Agent CLIs" install/update block from scripts/setup_software.sh into the OpenThrottle stack: server-side check/install/update for the finite allowlist of agent CLIs (claude, cursor-agent, codex, grok, opencode), exposed via GraphQL and driven by a new /settings/setup route in the developer app. Check comes free from the existing discoverAgentClis; the new work is install/update descriptors on the driver registry, a permission- and env-gated server executor with streamed output, and the UI.
title: Agent-CLI setup in-stack: /settings/setup install & update

author: visormatt
description:
Prepare the local Postgres stack for making the repository public: preserve the current working database on a recognizable named Docker volume (`postgres_data_dev_personal`), then switch compose to a fresh volume for a clean public/demo seed.

## Goals
- Take a named backup of the current Postgres data directory by freezing the existing Docker volume under a recognizable name (`postgres_data_dev_personal`).
- Update `docker-compose.yml` so the postgres service can swap between the personal and public volumes with a simple comment toggle (same credentials, ports, env, and Postgres 18 mount path).
- Bring up a fresh volume and apply migrations + minimal public-safe demo seeds (no personal plans, tokens, or private content).
- Document how to flip back to the personal volume without dump/restore drama.

## Non-goals
- Changing Postgres credentials, ports, or image config.
- Exporting a SQL dump (volume-swap only for day-to-day).
- Redesigning the seed generator beyond what’s needed for a minimal public demo.

## Approach
1. Stop postgres (compose down or stop) so the volume is quiescent.
2. Keep the existing `postgres_data` volume contents under the recognizable name `postgres_data_dev_personal` (either rename via Docker volume copy, or declare both volumes and copy data once).
3. In `docker-compose.yml`, declare both volumes; mount the fresh public volume by default; leave the personal volume mount commented with a clear label so swapping is one-line.
4. Start postgres on the empty volume → migrate → seed minimal demo data.
5. Smoke-check server/developer against the fresh DB; confirm personal data is unreachable and restorable by flipping the mount.

## Acceptance
- `docker-compose.yml` lists both `postgres_data` (or a clearly named public volume) and `postgres_data_dev_personal`, with comments explaining which is active.
- Same `POSTGRES_*` env and `/var/lib/postgresql` (PG18) mount path for both.
- Fresh DB has migrations applied and only public-safe demo seeds.
- Documented one-line swap path back to personal data.
title: Reset local Postgres for public repo (named volume swap + demo seeds)

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

The chat composer already has an `@`-mention autocomplete backed by a file/code-search provider. Add a parallel **`/skills`** slash-command autocomplete: typing `/` at the start of the draft opens a popover of available skills (slug + description), keyboard-navigable, and selecting one inserts `/<slug> ` at the caret. Submitting `/<slug> <args>` already flows verbatim through `submitTurn` (same path as commit aaf4c550's Run-skill dialog), so no new send mutation is needed.

## Architecture — mirror the `@`-mention pattern

The `@`-mention feature is a clean, layered pattern to copy almost 1:1. Reference symbols (repo-relative):

**Shared package `packages/react-router-chat`:**
- `src/file-mentions.ts` — pure trigger/parse: `FILE_MENTION_TRIGGER='@'`, `detectActiveMention(value, caret)`, `insertFileMention(value, anchor, caret, path)`, `parseFileMentions(message)`.
- `src/hooks/use-chat-composer-mentions.ts` — `useChatComposerMentions` state machine: stale-guarded async `runQuery`, `refreshMention` on change/caret-move, Arrow/Enter/Tab/Escape nav in `handleKeyDown`, `selectOption` insertion, post-insert caret via `useLayoutEffect`.
- `src/components/ChatMentionPopover.tsx` — absolutely-positioned `<ul role="listbox">`; options commit on **`onMouseDown`** (not click) so the textarea keeps focus. Hand-rolled, NOT shadcn `Command` — the focus-retention constraint is the key gotcha.
- `src/components/ChatComposer.tsx` — presentational `<TextArea>`; `onTextAreaKeyDown` calls `mentions.handleKeyDown(event)` first and bails if the popover consumed the key before Enter-to-send.
- `src/types.ts` — `ChatMentionProvider` (`onQueryFiles(query) => Promise<string[]>`, `emptyLabel`, `loadingLabel`), `ChatFileMention`, optional `ChatComposerProps.mentionProvider`.

**Developer app `applications/openthrottle-developer`:**
- `app/routing/home/demo/useFileMentionProvider.tsx` — fetches full listing once from a resource route, caches per-repo in a ref, fuzzy-filters client-side (cap `MAX_MENTION_SUGGESTIONS=50`).
- `app/routes/ide.files.tsx` — resource-route loader `/ide/files?repositoryId=&q=`.
- `app/routing/home/demo/useHomeComposer.tsx` — owns `draft`/`setDraft`; `onSubmit` forwards `/<slug> …` verbatim to `submitTurn`.
- `app/routing/home/demo/HomeComposer.tsx` — renders `<ChatComposer>` and passes `mentionProvider`.

## Skills data source

- **Filesystem (has descriptions — used first):** `app/routing/agents/data/discover-repo-skills.server.ts` `discoverRepoSkills(monorepoRoot)` walks `.agents/skills` > `.claude/skills` > `.opencode/skills`, reads `SKILL.md`, dedupes by slug. `RepoSkillEntry` (`app/routing/agents/data/repo-skills-registry.ts`) carries `slug`, `summary` (frontmatter description), `tags`, `source`, `disableModelInvocation`. Frontmatter parser: `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/parse-skill-frontmatter.ts`. NOTE `getMonorepoRoot()` returns null on a deployed app → fs discovery is local-checkout only (same limitation `@`-mention already has).
- **GraphQL (no description today):** query `projectSkills` → `ProjectSkillObject` (schema.gql ~line 1888) exposes `slug`, `source`, `sourceUrl`, `tags`, `staticDisableModelInvocation` but **not** description. `skillAvailability` gives per-context effective disable-model-invocation flags. Canonical merge pattern in `app/routes/skills._index.tsx` loader: disk discovery for slug+summary+tags, merge GraphQL flags on top.

## Decision (locked)

**Both, staged:** ship the filesystem-backed provider first for parity with `@`-mention; add a follow-up to expose skill `description` over GraphQL so the menu works in deployed environments too.

## Gotchas
- The current `@` detector treats `/` as an ordinary path char; the slash trigger must be **anchored to the start of the draft** (or start-of-line), distinct from `@`'s scan-back-to-boundary.
- Options must commit without blurring the textarea (mousedown-commit), same as `ChatMentionPopover`.
- Respect `disableModelInvocation` / `skillAvailability` — a model-disabled skill is still user-invocable via `/`, so surface it but consider a visual marker; don't silently drop.
- After GraphQL codegen changes: boot `openthrottle-server:dev` to regen `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then run codegen-graphql/codegen-react-router and commit `__generated__` + schema.gql.
- Use `@tools/generators` for any new component/route rather than hand-writing.
summary: Add `/skills` slash-command autocompletion to the chat composer, mirroring the existing `@`-mention/code-search flow. Filesystem-backed provider (SKILL.md descriptions) first; GraphQL description field as a follow-up for deployed environments.
title: Chat composer: /skills slash-command autocomplete

author: visormatt
description:
## Why

A new OpenThrottle user lands on empty pages that say little more than "No data yet." Every empty page is a wasted first impression. Instead, each empty page should **sell the feature by teaching it** — show a new user what the feature is, what they could use it for, how we use it internally, and the fastest path to their first win.

Start with three routes: **Rules**, **Schedule**, and **Plans**. Each gets a prominent `XxxxxOnboarding` component that renders in the genuinely-empty (new-user) state.

## Current state (verified 2026-08-15)

- **Rules** (`app/routes/rules._index.tsx`) — mature pattern: always-on `RulesIntroduction` (thin heading + one-line description) + `RulesTable` whose `DataTable emptyState` renders the terse `RulesEmpty` (icon + CTA, branches on `isFiltered`).
- **Plans** (`app/routes/plans._index.tsx`) — same mature pattern: `PlansIntroduction` + `PlansTable` -> `PlanTasksEmpty` (branches on `filtered`).
- **Schedule** (`app/routes/schedule._index.tsx`) — the outlier: inline `GlobalHeading`, an inline `jobs.length === 0` dashed-border paragraph, a plain shadcn `Table` (`ScheduleTable`, no `emptyState` slot), **no** `ScheduleIntroduction`, **no** `ScheduleEmpty`, **no** `schedule/data/data.copy.ts`.

So the existing `Introduction` (always-on header) and `Empty` (terse in-table) components stay. The new `Onboarding` component is a distinct, richer teaching block shown only to genuinely-new users.

## Design decisions

1. **Distinct from Introduction and Empty.** `Introduction` = always-on header. `Empty` = terse in-table state used for the *filtered -> no results* case. `Onboarding` (new) = the rich sales pitch shown only when the list is empty **and** unfiltered (a true new user, not an empty search).
2. **Shared layout, per-feature copy.** Build one presentational `FeatureOnboarding` layout primitive plus a typed copy contract, so the three pages (and future ones — Prompts, Queues, Personas, etc.) read as one consistent system. Each feature supplies a copy object; no feature-specific copy lives in the layout.
3. **Content sections** (from the request): an eyebrow/icon + title + one-line tagline, **What it is**, **What you could use it for** (concrete use-cases), **How we use it internally**, a numbered **Quick start**, and a primary CTA ("Create your first ___").
4. **Copy lives in `data/data.copy.ts`** per the repo convention; Schedule needs this file created.
5. Purely presentational — **no GraphQL / schema / codegen** changes.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Fanning the pattern out to every other empty page (Prompts, Queues, Personas, Notes, PRs, Dashboard, etc.). This plan proves the pattern on three routes; a follow-up plan rolls it across the app.
- A dismiss/"don't show again" preference or feature flag. v1 is purely presence-driven (empty + unfiltered).

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint,typecheck,test` green, plus a live dev-server screenshot of each of the three empty pages as a new user.
title: Onboarding empty-states: turn empty Rules / Schedule / Plans pages into teach-me-fast sales pitches

author: visormatt
description:
Three `packages/react-router-*` libraries carry structure that is NOT part of the canonical `@tools/generators:folders` shape. Bring them into line: the only sanctioned top-level folders inside `src/` are `components/`, `config/`, `data/`, `hooks/`, `utils/` (each with its own `__tests__/`), plus a root `types.ts` and a single barrel `index.ts` (and the existing `index.css`). Specs live in the nearest `__tests__/`.

## Canonical shape (source of truth)
`tools/generators/src/generators/folders/` — template tree + `CANONICAL_ROUTING_SUBTREE.md`. Allowed per area: `components/ config/ data/ hooks/ utils/`, each with `__tests__/`; root `types.ts`; `config/defaults.ts`, `utils/formatters.ts`, `utils/parsers.ts` are canonical seed files. No other top-level folders.

## Ground truth gathered during planning
- All THREE packages are source-first (`main`/`types` -> `./src/index.ts`); consuming apps' Vite transpiles them. No `build` target to worry about; `dist/` is stale output — ignore it.
- Every EXTERNAL consumer imports via the package barrel only. No deep subpath imports (`.../catalog`, `.../tabs`, `.../env`, etc.) exist in `applications/` or other packages. So only the barrel + intra-package relative imports must be rewired.
- Validation per package: `pnpm nx run <project>:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`. There is NO `build` target on these source-first libs — use a consumer app (`openthrottle-developer`) `:typecheck`/`:build` as the integration check, and `pnpm nx run monorepo:knip` for dead-export drift.

## Scope
1. `@openthrottle/react-router-rollout` — dissolve `src/catalog/`.
2. `@openthrottle/react-router-testing` — flatten `src/*.ts` modules into subfolders, specs into `__tests__/`, keep one root barrel.
3. `@openthrottle/react-router-ui` — dissolve `src/tabs/`.

Constraints: no public API (barrel export) changes — same named exports out of each package `index.ts`. Preserve `@public` JSDoc tags so Knip keeps exports. Alphabetize barrel exports/object keys where order is immaterial (repo style). Conventional commits with `Plan-Id:`/`Task-Id:` footers; commit per task.
title: Conform three RR packages to the generator folder shape (drop catalog/, tabs/; flatten testing root)

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

On the Developer `/usage` route, the **Top skills** leaderboard has an **Outcomes** column and an **Avg duration** column that always render `—`. The read path is fully built end-to-end — the gap is purely on the ingest (write) side.

### What already works (do NOT rebuild)
- **Schema**: `SkillUsageBySkillObject.{outcomeCount, successCount, abandonedCount, errorCount, avgDurationMs}` — `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/skill-usage/skill-usage.object.ts`.
- **Aggregation**: `SkillUsageEventsService.listOutcomeStatsBySkill()` reads the `skill_usage_outcomes` table, computes success/abandoned/error counts + `AVG(duration_ms)`, and joins onto the start-count leaderboard by `skill_name` — `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/skill-usage-events/skill-usage-events.service.ts`.
- **Mutation**: `recordSkillUsageOutcome` resolver validates + persists outcomes — `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/skill-usage/skill-usage.resolver.ts`.
- **UI**: `UsageSkillUsage.tsx` renders both columns via `skillUsageOutcomesLabel` (`N/M`) and `skillUsageAvgDurationLabel` (`—` when null); tooltip already explains "no opt-in outcome reported" — `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/usage/`.

### Root cause
Both columns are driven by the `skill_usage_outcomes` table, which is empty:
- **Start events** (the Invocations column) are captured **automatically** by the `PreToolUse:Skill` + `UserPromptExpansion` hooks → `.claude/hooks/skill-usage-capture.cjs` → neutral `.agents/hooks/skill-usage/lib.cjs`.
- **Outcome events** (which carry `outcome` + `duration_ms`) come **only** from `.claude/hooks/skill-usage-outcome.cjs`, a **manual CLI helper**. Nothing invokes it automatically; it appears as an optional opt-in completion step in exactly one SKILL.md (`skills/ot-plans/SKILL.md`). Result: `outcomeCount=0` → Outcomes `—`; `avgDurationMs=null` → Avg duration `—`.

### The three missing pieces
1. **No automatic outcome emission** at skill completion. The harness has no clean per-skill "finished" signal for inline skills (a skill loads instructions into the turn; its work interleaves with the rest of the turn). Candidate signals: `Stop` / `SubagentStop` (correlate the open skill-start(s) in the session) or `PostToolUse:Skill` (accurate duration only for subagent-backed skills).
2. **No duration source.** Start events store `occurredAt`, but nothing remembers `(session_id, skill_name, tool_use_id, started_at)` so a completion can compute `duration_ms = finish − start` and correlate precisely.
3. **No JSONL→server drain.** The fail-open fallback writes `.cache/skill-usage/{events,outcomes}.jsonl` but nothing flushes them to OT — flagged "Future (not built)" in `lib.cjs`. Manually-emitted outcomes can be stranded locally when the server was down.

## Goal
Outcomes and Avg duration show real data for skills we author with **zero manual steps**, preserving the existing guarantees: fail-open, never block a Skill call, privacy-safe. Absent outcomes for third-party / uninstrumented skills remain a valid, accepted state (the UI already communicates this).

## Constraints & prior art
- Fail-open always: never block a Skill call; swallow errors; exit 0.
- Keep the tool-neutral architecture: shared logic in `.agents/hooks/skill-usage/lib.cjs`, thin per-tool adapters under `.claude/hooks/*`; mirror the adapter test pattern in `skill-usage-claude-adapter.test.cjs`.
- Related existing skill-usage plans: base `d3759118` (PreToolUse/Skill hook → JSONL → OT persist → UI) and future/paid `91679bbf` (configurable privacy). This plan extends the base with the outcome/duration feed; keep the privacy seam intact for `91679bbf`.
- Plans/tasks live in OT only; commit per task with `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers.

Each task carries its own acceptance criteria in `requirements`.
summary: The /usage "Top skills" leaderboard renders Outcomes and Avg duration as "—" because the skill_usage_outcomes table is never populated automatically. The full read path (schema, aggregation, UI) already exists; the gap is ingest. Fill it with an automatic, fail-open outcome+duration capture path (choose Stop/SubagentStop vs PostToolUse:Skill via a spike), session-scoped start-state to compute duration, and a JSONL→server drain so buffered records reach OT.
title: Usage → Top skills: populate Outcomes & Avg duration

author: visormatt
description:
# Defer slow loader data on Developer home + dashboard

## Problem

Navigating into `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx` (home composer) and `dashboard._index.tsx` feels sluggish because each route **blocks its entire render** on slow GraphQL work in the loader. React Router waits for the loader to fully resolve before it will transition, so the shell (heading, sidebar, nav chrome) is held hostage by data that only a sub-tree needs.

Two concrete offenders:

- **`_index.tsx`** — the loader does `Promise.all` of **five** discovery queries (`loadDiscoveredModels`, `loadAgentClis`, `loadDriverEndpointModels`, `loadRepositories`, `loadPersonas`). `loadDiscoveredModels` / `loadDriverEndpointModels` probe locally-running model servers (Ollama, etc.); cold, that is the slow path. Nothing paints — not the "What would you like to build today?" hero, not the conversation sidebar, not a disabled composer — until all five settle. Only the toolbar (`reconcileChatToolbarState`, `buildModelGroups`) actually needs `models`/`personas`/`repositories`.
- **`dashboard._index.tsx`** — worse: the loader `await`s `GetDashboardDocument` and **then sequentially** `await`s `GetDashboardGithubStatsDocument` (a GitHub API round-trip). Two serial network calls block the intro banner and the "This Week's Activity" chart, neither of which depends on GitHub stats.

## Approach — deferred (streamed) loader data

Move the slow work off the critical render path so the **shell paints instantly** and slow data **streams in** behind Suspense fallbacks.

**Idiom (important):** this app is on **react-router 8.0.1**, where the `defer()` helper has been removed. The modern equivalent is to **return naked promises** from the loader (Single Fetch serializes/streams them) and consume them in the component with `React.Suspense` + `<Await resolve={promise} errorElement={…}>` + `useAsyncValue()`. Streaming SSR is already in place — `entry.server.tsx` uses `renderToPipeableStream`, so deferred promises flush progressively. No `future` flags or `defer()` import needed.

### Per-route strategy

**Home (`_index.tsx`)**
- Keep the loader signature returning an object, but return the composer-data bundle as a **promise** instead of awaited values. The hero heading and the conversation sidebar (`useConversationList` is a client hook — already independent of the loader) render immediately.
- The composer/toolbar sub-tree — everything that consumes `models` / `personas` / `repositories` via `reconcileChatToolbarState`, `buildModelGroups`, and `capabilitiesForChatOption` — moves under `<Suspense fallback={<composer skeleton, disabled>}><Await>`. Because reconciliation needs all three lists together, bundle them into one awaited `Promise.all` promise (not three independent awaits) so the toolbar reconciles atomically.
- Fallback: a disabled composer skeleton reading e.g. "Discovering models…" so the input frame is visibly present instantly.

**Dashboard (`dashboard._index.tsx`)**
- First, stop the serial waterfall: fire `GetDashboard` and `GetDashboardGithubStats` **concurrently**.
- Return two independent deferred promises so the "This Week's Activity" chart streams as soon as the dashboard query lands, without waiting on the slower GitHub call. GitHub-dependent cards (PR time-in-state, PRs by author) get their own `<Suspense>` boundary with skeletons.
- The intro banner + grid scaffold render synchronously.
- **Error handling:** `dashboard._index` calls `executeGraphqlWithAuth` **without** a try/catch, so a deferred promise can reject. Each `<Await>` must supply an `errorElement` (inline per-section error) so a GitHub-stats failure degrades that card instead of throwing the whole route to the ErrorBoundary. (The home helpers already catch → `[]`, so those promises resolve rather than reject — but still guard defensively.)

## Skeletons / fallbacks
Use `Skeleton` from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`. New skeleton components follow repo conventions: one component per file under the route's `components/` folder, section comments, component-only exports (copy/data in a sibling `data/` folder if any). Inventory: composer-loading skeleton (home), dashboard activity-chart skeleton, dashboard PR-cards skeleton.

## Gotchas to watch
- `Route.ComponentProps['loaderData']` will now carry `Promise<…>` fields; `HandleData` (used by the breadcrumb `handle`) becomes promise-shaped — the breadcrumb returns a literal string so it still typechecks, but confirm.
- Existing route tests (`app/routes/__tests__/dashboard._index.test.tsx`, home `_index` tests) assert on resolved content and mock loaders returning plain objects. With deferral they must switch to async `findBy*` queries and add fallback-state assertions. Keep the repo test conventions (`component` not `screen`, `userEvent`).
- Don't over-defer: the shell + anything cheap stays synchronous. Only the genuinely slow discovery/GitHub work is deferred.

## Out of scope (note as follow-up)
The **root loader** (`root.tsx`) also runs on every navigation (health probe + `me` query, already concurrent) and contributes baseline transition latency. Not part of this plan — flag as a possible follow-up if transitions still feel slow after these two routes are deferred.

## Verification
- Dev server, navigate home ↔ dashboard ↔ home: shell must paint immediately, with skeletons visibly streaming into real content. Verify via the in-app browser preview tools (console/network clean, screenshot the streamed state).
- Gates: `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` on `openthrottle-developer` (plus codegen unaffected — no GraphQL schema change).
title: Defer slow loader data on Developer home + dashboard for instant page transitions

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

`/ot-loop <planId>` is the skill we want driving plan execution. It already works interactively in Claude. The gap is the **programmatic path**: everything that today defaults `--prompt` to `/agents-ralph`, and in particular the **BullMQ plan-run flow**, where the prompt is not a CLI flag at all but the first layer of a composed prompt string.

## Current state (verified 2026-08-24)

**The rename is a work-in-progress on disk.** `skills/ot-loop/SKILL.md` is a byte-identical copy of `skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md` — its frontmatter still reads `name: ot-claude-loop`, and its description still says "the user runs /ot-claude-loop". Both directories exist; `skills/ot-loop/` is untracked. `skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md` has one uncommitted line added (the "`$planId` is the first (and only) argument … throw an error immediately" guard).

**`/agents-ralph` is the default in five independent constants** (no single source of truth):

| Location | Symbol |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.constants.ts:10` | `DEFAULT_PLAN_RUN_RALPH_PROMPT` |
| `packages/openthrottle-agentic-ralph/src/config/index.ts:13` | `DEFAULT_PROMPT` |
| `tools/workflows/src/config/load-workflow-ralph-config.ts:40` | `DEFAULT_RALPH_PROMPT` |
| `tools/workflows/src/config/messages.ts:35` | `--help` text |
| `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plan.input.ts:247` | GraphQL field description |

Plus a hardcoded string literal at `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.round-trip.ts:159` (`prompt !== '/agents-ralph'`) that bypasses the constant, and the seeded JSON in `databases/migrations/098_adopt_plan_run_worktree_verbose_defaults.sql:32`.

**How the BullMQ path actually composes the prompt** — this is the crux. The queue worker does *not* shell out to `workflow-ralph`; it runs the in-process orchestrator in `@openthrottle/openthrottle-agentic-ralph`. `buildOrchestratorBasePrompt` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-ralph/src/utils/orchestrator.ts:75-105`) concatenates:

```
${context.prompt}            ← "/agents-ralph" today
${foreignWorkspaceLayer}
${injectedContext}           ← plan + tasks pulled from Postgres
${WORKFLOW_PROMPT_SHELL_COMMAND_GUARDRAIL}
Plan-Id: <id>. [Task-Id: <id>.] Use the plan and tasks above … When you complete a task output <ralph:task-complete>TASK_UUID</ralph:task-complete>.
```

`tools/workflows/src/bin/ralph.ts:135-140` builds the same shape for the CLI path. That whole string is handed to the agent CLI as a single `-p` prompt.

**So the prompt is a slash command sitting on line 1 of a multi-KB prompt, with the plan context as its trailing text.** `/agents-ralph` takes no arguments, so nothing depended on how the CLI binds that trailing text. `/ot-loop` takes `$planId` as its first and only argument — and the skill now throws if that value isn't a plan/task id. If the CLI binds `$planId`/`$ARGUMENTS` to the remainder of the prompt (the injected plan block), or drops the remainder once it expands the command, the run breaks. **Nobody has verified which happens, per driver.** That is task 1 and it gates the design.

Note also that `promptLayer: 'file'` (`--prompt-file`) already exists as an alternative: it reads a SKILL.md, strips YAML frontmatter, and inlines the body — no slash expansion, no argument binding. It may be the correct mechanism for the programmatic path.

## Non-goals

- Changing the per-task discipline itself. `skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md` § The loop is the canonical statement; three places restate it deliberately (`agents-ralph`, `ot-workflow-orchestration/runner.workflow.js`). This plan renames and re-points, it does not rewrite the discipline.
- Deleting `skills/agents-ralph`. It is fed to agents as a standalone prompt by design and stays as the file-layer / non-Claude fallback unless task 2 concludes otherwise.
- Touching the `/loop`-driven interactive path beyond the rename.

## Definition of done

A plan queued from the Developer UI with untouched defaults runs `/ot-loop` (or its resolved equivalent), the agent receives the plan context intact, tasks flip through `IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED`, and the run output stream shows it — verified on a real run, not just unit tests.
summary: Finish the ot-claude-loop → ot-loop rename and make /ot-loop <planId> the default plan-run prompt across the CLI, the UI and the BullMQ orchestrator — including the argument-passing problem the slash-command prompt layer introduces.
title: Switch plan runs from /agents-ralph to /ot-loop (incl. the BullMQ path)

author: visormatt
description:
Create a new hand-authored, repo-specific skill `skills/ot-onboarding/SKILL.md` whose job is to onboard a person (or agent-driven session) onto OpenThrottle end-to-end: confirm the OT MCP is installed/configured and healthy, then walk them through the basics of the system — the mental model, the core apps, keyboard shortcuts, workflows, and the wider skill catalog. The "kitchen sink" orientation skill new users invoke first.

## Why
OpenThrottle has a lot of surface area — a plans/tasks SSOT in OT, an Nx+pnpm monorepo, a NestJS GraphQL server, several React Router apps, a growing catalog of skills (`skills/` + managed `.agents/skills/`), Workflow/Ralph orchestration, and MCP tooling. There's no single guided on-ramp. New users (and fresh agent sessions) rediscover setup and conventions ad hoc. `ot-onboarding` is the front door: one skill that verifies the environment is wired correctly and then teaches the essentials with pointers into the deeper skills.

## Scope / behavior
1. **MCP install + health gate first.** Detect whether the `openthrottle-mcp` server is configured for the current agent (`.mcp.json` / per-tool config), run the `health` tool, and if it's missing or unhealthy, guide the user through install/auth using the existing runbook (see the "Stale in-session OT MCP" / AUTH.md guidance) rather than silently proceeding. Fail loudly with the exact remediation.
2. **System basics tour.** Explain the OT mental model (plans/tasks are the SSOT, created via MCP not Markdown), the monorepo shape (`applications/`, `packages/`, `tools/`, `databases/`), and how to run the core dev servers via Nx (`openthrottle-server:dev`, `openthrottle-developer:dev`) — linking to CLAUDE.md / MONOREPO.md instead of duplicating them.
3. **Keyboard shortcuts + workflows.** Surface the shortcuts and everyday workflows a new user needs (agent keybindings, the `/loop` recurring runner, Workflow multi-agent orchestration, the Ralph loop, `/github/*` skills) so they know what levers exist.
4. **The wider skill catalog.** Teach how skills work here (authored `skills/` vs managed `.agents/skills/`, fan-out via `skill-sync`, how to invoke a skill), and point at the handful of skills a newcomer should know first (`ot-plans`, `openthrottle-generators`, `openthrottle-folders`, `skill-sync`).
5. **Wire it in.** Follow the repo's skill architecture: author under `skills/ot-onboarding/`, run `skill-sync` to fan out to `.agents/skills` + `.claude/skills`, register it in `skills/README.md` / `skills/AGENTS.md`, and pass the skill-sync `--check` drift gate.

## Non-goals
- Not a replacement for CLAUDE.md/MONOREPO.md/CONTRIBUTING.md — it orients and links, it doesn't re-document.
- No new tooling, generators, or MCP tools — pure skill authoring + wiring.

## Definition of done
`skills/ot-onboarding/SKILL.md` exists with correct frontmatter (`name`, discoverable `USE WHEN` description), covers the five areas above, is fanned out by `skill-sync`, registered in the skills README/AGENTS index, and passes `skill-sync --check`. Invoking `/ot-onboarding` (or the trigger phrases) produces a coherent guided on-ramp.
title: Author an `ot-onboarding` skill: get new users set up on OpenThrottle

author: visormatt
description:
# Rebuild openthrottle-website index route from new landing mockup

## Goal

Replace the current minimal home page (`applications/openthrottle-website/app/routes/_index.tsx`, which renders only `OpenThrottleProductGetStarted` + footer) with a full multi-section landing page built from a new static HTML mockup (delivered by the owner). Preserve the current page as a separate `landing-simple` route so nothing is lost and we can A/B or fall back.

## Source mockup

A self-contained `index.html` mockup (hero + 4 content sections + footer) is the design reference. It ships its own CSS vars (`--ink #12141a`, `--paper #f3f0ea`, `--red #e10600`, `--signal #1a6b5a`), Google Fonts (Syne display + Figtree body), an animated grid backdrop, an inline SVG "arc" hero visual, IntersectionObserver reveal-on-scroll, and a `plan → task → run → commit` narrative. **We translate this into our stack — we do not copy its raw CSS/fonts/scripts.**

Sections in the mockup:
1. **Header nav** — brand wordmark + links (How it works / Surfaces / GitHub).
2. **Hero** — full-viewport, grid backdrop + arc SVG, `OpenThrottle` wordmark (red "Throttle"), headline "From idea to shipped commit — with agents you can trust.", lede, two CTAs (View on GitHub / Get started locally).
3. **Why it exists (promise)** — 2-col: title + lede on "one substrate for planning and agentic execution".
4. **How it works (flow)** — 4 numbered steps: Plan / Execute / Remember / Trace.
5. **Surfaces** — dark section, 3-col: MCP / Developer app / Ralph loop.
6. **Close (self-host)** — 2-col: copy + CTAs + a terminal code block (`./scripts/setup.sh` etc.).
7. **Footer** — reuse existing `GlobalFooter`.

## Translation constraints (our stack)

- **React Router v8 + Vite + Tailwind v4**, SSR on. Route files under `app/routes/` via `flatRoutes`.
- **shadcn** from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` (e.g. `Button` with `variant="brand"`). Reuse `OpenThrottleClipboard`, `OpenThrottleLogo` where they fit.
- **Existing design tokens only** — map the mockup's `--ink/--paper/--red/--signal` onto our shadcn tokens: `--red` → `--brand` (`hsl(0,100%,50%)`), ink/paper → `foreground`/`background`/`card`/`muted`. Must work in **light AND dark** (theme.css defines both).
- **Existing fonts** — the app intentionally ships **no external font stylesheet** (CSP is self-only + nonce; dead Google Fonts preconnects are commented out in `root.tsx`). Do **not** introduce Syne/Figtree or any Google Fonts. Use the current font stack. Preserve the mockup's *typographic hierarchy* (large tight display headings, uppercase kickers) with Tailwind utilities on the existing stack.
- **CSP-safe** — no inline `<style>`/`<script>` without the nonce. The animated grid, reveal-on-scroll, and reduced-motion behavior become: CSS utilities in `app/styles.css` (or component classes) + a small app-local React IntersectionObserver hook. No raw `<script>` like the mockup uses.
- **Folder placement** — landing-specific building blocks go app-local under `app/routing/home/` (`components/`, `data/`, `hooks/`) per the openthrottle-folders convention, not the shared `react-router-ui` package (these are website-only). Copy strings live in a `data/` file, not hardcoded in components.
- **Generators first** — scaffold every new component with `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-website --folder=routing/home --name=...` (batch via comma-separated names). Keep the generated section comments and exported Props interfaces.
- **Preserve loader/meta** — the new `_index.tsx` keeps the existing loader (`introduction`, `repo`), `meta` (SITE_TITLE, canonical, OG/Twitter), and `ErrorBoundary = GlobalErrorBoundary`.

## Out of scope
- No new external fonts, analytics, or GitHub-stars fetch (stars stay `0` / gated as today).
- No changes to the shared `react-router-ui` product components beyond optional reuse.
- No copywriting overhaul — carry the mockup's copy across as the starting content.

## Definition of done
- `/` renders the new multi-section landing; `/landing-simple` renders the old page.
- Lint + typecheck + tests green on `openthrottle-website`; dev/build smoke verified in light and dark.
- No external font/script requests; CSP report-only stays clean.
summary: Rename the current home route to landing-simple, then rebuild / as a multi-section landing page translated from a new static HTML mockup into our React Router + shadcn stack (existing tokens, no external fonts).
title: Rebuild openthrottle-website index route from new landing mockup

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Give developers a one-command way to get the exact, machine-specific instructions to register the OpenThrottle MCP server **globally** (user scope) in both Claude Code and Cursor — without hand-editing paths.

Running the script from the repo root prints two blocks, each with `<OPENTHROTTLE_ROOT>` replaced by the absolute path to the repo checkout on the current box (the same path `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` lives under).

## Behavior

The script:

1. Resolves the repo root absolutely — `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with a `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd` fallback so it works even outside a git checkout. This value replaces every `<OPENTHROTTLE_ROOT>` occurrence.
2. Prints a Claude Code section headed with a prompt like:
   `To install the OpenThrottle MCP globally for Claude Code please run:`
   followed by the `claude mcp add-json openthrottle-mcp --scope user '{...}'` command (block A below).
3. Prints a Cursor section that tells the user to add the JSON block to their `~/.cursor/mcp.json` to enable it globally across all IDE instances, followed by the JSON (block B below).

### Block A — Claude Code

```
claude mcp add-json openthrottle-mcp --scope user '{"args":["<OPENTHROTTLE_ROOT>/scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh"],"command":"bash","description":"OpenThrottle (OT) plans knowledge base (Postgres + GraphQL). Plans, tasks, notes, commit links, activity, output stream, semantic search, health.","env":{"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY":"${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}","API_URL":"${OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_EXTERNAL}","API_URL_INTERNAL":"${OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_INTERNAL}","OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN":"${OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}"}}'
```

### Block B — Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`)

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openthrottle-mcp": {
      "command": "bash",
      "args": ["<OPENTHROTTLE_ROOT>/scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh"],
      "env": {
        "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}",
        "API_URL": "${API_URL}",
        "API_URL_INTERNAL": "${API_URL_INTERNAL}",
        "OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN": "${OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Critical implementation detail

Only `<OPENTHROTTLE_ROOT>` is substituted. Every `${...}` env placeholder must be printed **literally** — these are variables the MCP launcher/tooling resolves at runtime, not at print time. Emit the blocks via a single-quoted heredoc (`cat <<'EOF'`) or otherwise disable shell expansion, then inject the resolved root path (e.g. a post-pass `sed "s|<OPENTHROTTLE_ROOT>|$ROOT|g"`). Do not let the shell expand `$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `$API_URL`, etc.

Note the two blocks intentionally differ: block A (Claude) uses `${OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_EXTERNAL}` / `${OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_INTERNAL}`; block B (Cursor) uses `${API_URL}` / `${API_URL_INTERNAL}`. Preserve each verbatim.

## Placement & invocation

- Script lives at `scripts/print-mcp-install.sh` (bash, `chmod +x`), matching the `scripts/*.sh` conventions (`set -euo pipefail`, comment header).
- Add a `package.json` root script alias (e.g. `mcp:install-instructions`) so it can be run as `pnpm run mcp:install-instructions` from the repo root.
- Pure stdout, no side effects — it only prints instructions; it never edits `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or runs `claude mcp add-json` itself.

## Out of scope

- Automatically writing to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or executing the `claude mcp add-json` command.
- Windows / non-bash shells.
summary: A repo-root-invokable script that echoes copy-paste install instructions for the OpenThrottle MCP — a `claude mcp add-json` command for Claude Code (user scope) and a `~/.cursor/mcp.json` block for Cursor — with `<OPENTHROTTLE_ROOT>` replaced by the repo's absolute path on the current machine.
title: Add a script that prints global MCP install instructions (Claude Code + Cursor)

author: visormatt
description:
Port `docs/marketing/scripts/05-connect-ot-mcp.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

This is the first Season 1 short whose subject is not the product's UI. Six of its eight beats are a terminal and a text editor; only the 0:44 payoff is in the browser. Every flow recorded so far (01, 03, 04, 21) lives entirely inside the dashboard, so this one does not merely add beats — it asks the pipeline for a capability it does not have.

## Gate 1: the runner cannot record a terminal or an editor

`runner/actions.ts` implements exactly thirteen verbs — `click`, `dwell`, `highlight`, `hover`, `moveTo`, `navigate`, `press`, `scrollTo`, `select`, `type`, `waitFor`, `waitForUrl`, `zoomTo` — and every one of them drives a Playwright page. `runner/run.ts` launches `chromium` and captures a CDP screencast of that browser. There is no verb, and no capture surface, for a shell or for VS Code.

That is not an oversight to patch casually: the pipeline chose Playwright over screen capture precisely because macOS screen capture hangs on an interactive permission grant and records the whole desktop (see the spike README). Re-opening that decision for one short would re-open it for the whole channel.

Three ways out, and this must be decided before any flow is written:

- Type the terminal and the editor **in the browser**, the way captions and cards are already typeset there — an HTML surface styled as a shell and as an editor pane, driven by the existing `type` and `press` verbs. Consistent with the pipeline's existing "typeset it in the recording browser" precedent, and it makes the on-screen text scannable by `video-scan` for free.
- Reshoot the script around `/settings/mcp`, which already exists (`settings.mcp._index.tsx`, `settings.mcp.$connectorId.tsx`) and is a real product surface. Changes what the short teaches.
- Add a real terminal capture path. Highest cost, re-opens the settled recorder decision, and puts arbitrary desktop content in frame.

## Gate 2: the command's own output fails the leak scan

The 0:00 and 0:09 beats put the output of `pnpm run setup:mcp-instructions` on camera. `scripts/setup_mcp-instructions.ts` resolves the repo root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and prints `${root}/scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh`, and it names the client config files as `join(homedir(), '.claude.json')` and `join(homedir(), '.cursor', 'mcp.json')`.

Every one of those is an absolute `/Users/<name>/…` path, and `scan/rules.ts` rule `home-path` is `severity: 'error'` — "a home directory leaks a username and the shape of someone's machine". The single most important thing this short asks the viewer to copy is the exact string the publish gate is built to reject. This is not a scan tuning exercise; the frame genuinely should not ship a real machine's paths.

## Gate 3: the script's happy path does not happen on the recording machine

`setup_mcp-instructions.ts` checks whether the `openthrottle-mcp` node is already registered and, when it is, prints `✓ already installed, nothing to do.` instead of the install block. On any machine that can record this short, OT MCP is already installed — that is how the recording gets a seeded database in the first place. The beat as written cannot be captured by simply running the command.

## What already exists and needs no work

- The payoff surface: `/plans` (`plans._index.tsx`) renders the plans list, and the demo fixture seeds enough plans that a new one arriving at the top reads clearly.
- `scripts/setup_mcp-instructions.ts` is pure stdout with no side effects, so it is safe to run repeatedly while iterating.
- The `type` verb supports per-character pacing, which is what a believable terminal beat needs.

## Constraints

- 63 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; any rewrite of a beat must re-validate against `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` and the `short` budget in `docs/marketing/format.json`.
- A flow may not invent a step the script does not describe, and a script may not describe UI that does not exist. Whichever gate resolution is chosen, the script and the flow end up agreeing before recording.
- Never point a flow at real data or a real machine's configuration.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.
summary: Port docs/marketing/scripts/05-connect-ot-mcp.md to a recorded flow, and settle how a terminal-and-editor short is captured by a browser-only runner without failing the home-path leak gate.
title: Build the 05-connect-ot-mcp screencast flow

author: visormatt
description:
## Goal

Rename the openthrottle-developer product area from `scheduled-jobs` to `schedule` end-to-end in the UI layer: routes, URLs, feature folder, components, nav, tests, and internal links.

**Destination changed:** original draft targeted `jobs` / `/jobs/*`; ships as **`schedule` / `/schedule/*`** so the short path matches the product area after Calendar moved to `/calendar`.

## Scope (confirmed)

- **In scope:** Full UI rename + free the `/schedule` path.
  - **Prerequisite:** Remove leftover calendar redirect modules at `app/routes/schedule.*` (they currently forward `/schedule` → `/calendar/*`). Calendar stays at `/calendar` only.
  - Routes: `app/routes/scheduled-jobs.*` → `app/routes/schedule.*` (keep `$jobId` / `$runId` params)
  - URLs: `/scheduled-jobs/*` → `/schedule/*` (hard cutover — **no** redirects from old paths in v1)
  - Feature folder: `app/routing/scheduled-jobs/` → `app/routing/schedule/`
  - Components / props / testids: `ScheduledJob*` / `ScheduledJobs*` → `Schedule*` where they name the product area (e.g. `ScheduledJobsTable` → `ScheduleTable`, `ScheduledJobForm` → `ScheduleForm`, `ScheduledJobRunsTable` → `ScheduleRunsTable`)
  - Form helpers: `parseScheduledJobForm` / `ParsedScheduledJobForm` → `parseScheduleForm` / `ParsedScheduleForm`
  - Nav link in `app/global/data/data.navigation.ts` (`to: '/schedule'`, label → `Schedule`)
  - Route titles/breadcrumbs/copy that say "Scheduled Jobs" → "Schedule"
  - All co-located `.graphql` files move with routes; GraphQL **document** filenames follow route names
  - Route/component tests moved and path/assertions updated
  - Regenerate React Router `+types` / codegen after renames
- **Out of scope:** GraphQL schema / NestJS API rename.
  - Keep server types/ops as `ScheduledAgentJob*` / `scheduledAgentJob*`
  - Keep client fragments that mirror schema semantic naming if they map onto API types — prefer aligning **UI** fragment aliases only when they are local names not coupled to shared docs. Do **not** rename `ScheduledAgentJobObject`, mutations, or DB tables in this plan.
  - Leave design docs under `docs/` unless a link path breaks; update only if they hardcode `/scheduled-jobs` URLs that agents/users follow.
  - Do **not** change the Calendar product area (`/calendar`, `routing/calendar`).

## Current inventory (developer app)

### Blocking legacy redirects (must clear first)
- `schedule._index.tsx`, `schedule.calendar.tsx`, `schedule.create.tsx`, `schedule.$eventId.tsx` — calendar leftovers redirecting `/schedule/*` → `/calendar/*`

### Routes (+ graphql + tests) — source
- `scheduled-jobs._index.tsx` (+ `.graphql`, test)
- `scheduled-jobs.create.tsx` (+ `.graphql`, test)
- `scheduled-jobs.$jobId._index.tsx` (+ `.graphql`)
- `scheduled-jobs.$jobId.edit.tsx` (+ test)
- `scheduled-jobs.$jobId.runs.$runId.tsx` (+ `.graphql`, test)

### Feature folder `routing/scheduled-jobs/`
- components: `ScheduledJobsTable`, `ScheduledJobRunsTable`, `ScheduledJobForm`, `RunDetail`
- data: `parse-form`, `data.run-status`, `data.run-detail`, `data.drivers`
- utils: `format-when`, `format-usage`, `format-duration`
- tests: `ScheduledJobRunsTable.test.tsx`

### Other references
- `app/global/data/data.navigation.ts` → `/scheduled-jobs`
- Comment in `routing/queues/components/QueueJobLogConsole.tsx`

## Approach

1. Delete legacy `schedule.*` calendar redirect routes so `/schedule` is free.
2. `git mv` routes + feature folder first (preserve history).
3. Rename symbols/components/file basenames in the moved tree.
4. Sweep remaining `/scheduled-jobs` string links and imports.
5. Update nav label/path to Schedule / `/schedule`.
6. Run `codegen-graphql` + `codegen-react-router` (or affected) so `__generated__` and `+types` match new route modules.
7. Fix tests; run developer `lint`/`test` for touched suites.
8. Grep to prove zero leftover `scheduled-jobs` UI paths/symbols (excluding intentional GraphQL/codegen names).

## Acceptance

- No calendar-only `schedule.*` redirect modules remain; `/calendar/*` still works.
- App serves `/schedule`, `/schedule/create`, `/schedule/:jobId`, `/schedule/:jobId/edit`, `/schedule/:jobId/runs/:runId`.
- Sidebar navigates to `/schedule` with label "Schedule".
- No remaining developer-app imports or links under `scheduled-jobs`.
- API still uses `ScheduledAgentJob*` unchanged.
- Tests green for moved suites.

## Deferred (separate follow-up tasks)

- Add `/scheduled-jobs/*` → `/schedule/*` permanent redirects
- Audit docs/skills for `/scheduled-jobs` URL leftovers
- GraphQL/API rename `ScheduledAgentJob*` (breaking)
title: Rename developer UI scheduled-jobs → schedule

author: visormatt
description:
## Problem

Running OpenThrottle **fully in Docker** (`docker compose up --build` on a fresh Postgres volume) never runs the two bootstrap steps that a host-based `scripts/setup.sh` performs:

- `pnpm database:bootstrap-default-user` -> creates the login user (`developer-a4b71f@atlasworks.example` / `FullThrottle2026!`) with admin/user/viewer roles. Without it there is **no account to log into** the developer/admin apps.
- `pnpm database:bootstrap-service-accounts` -> provisions the `openthrottle-mcp` and `workflow-ralph` bearer tokens (`OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN`). Without them the MCP server and Ralph worker **cannot authenticate**.

In Docker, the `migrations` one-shot service applies schema + migration `045` (service-account **rows/roles/permissions** only, NOT credential tokens, NOT the login user). And a fully-Docker user has no host pnpm/node toolchain to run `pnpm database:bootstrap-*`. Result: a schema-complete but **unusable** stack.

## Decision (locked — see Task 1)

Postgres + Redis are moving to **real, shared instances** in the near future, so we deliberately **require human intervention** and ship **no secrets in the repo**. The design optimizes for one thing: the human steps must be short, explicit, and exactly documented — identical whether the DB is the local Docker Postgres or a future shared instance.

1. **Env-provided deterministic credential.** When `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` / `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN` are set in `.env`, the service-account bootstrap **upserts** a credential whose hash matches the provided token (idempotent) instead of minting a random one and printing it. This relocates the human touch point from a mid-flow copy-back to a **single up-front `.env` edit**, and the token flows to the MCP/worker runtime automatically via compose. The mint-and-print path is preserved for the host `setup.sh` flow when the vars are unset.
2. **Explicitly invoked, never automatic.** Bootstrap runs as a **manual, documented one-time command** (`docker compose run --rm bootstrap`), NOT as an automatic `depends_on` of `server`. `docker compose up` must never silently provision a (possibly shared) database.
3. **No committed secrets.** `.env.default` ships only empty placeholders + a documented token-generation command. The default login password is a known dev constant only; docs show how to override it for shared/real installs.

## Goal

A fully-Docker user (or an admin provisioning a shared instance) follows a short, exact, copy-pasteable procedure to get a usable stack: generate token -> paste into `.env` -> run one bootstrap command -> log in and authenticate the MCP/worker. Works the same for local and shared DBs. The host `setup.sh` path and the mint-and-print behavior for host installs stay intact.
